author: lucos-site-reliability[bot]
body:
Third and final piece of `docs/incidents/2026-08-08-time-ipv6-subnet-collision.md`, following lucas42/lucos#281 and lucas42/lucos#284.

**Why a third PR:** I pushed this while lucas42/lucos#284 was being reviewed, and it auto-merged before the commit landed. Same mechanism as last time, an hour apart — see the note at the bottom.

## What this changes

`lucos-code-reviewer` asked for one specific edit when re-applying the calibration test on "What Was Tried That Didn't Work": the standalone **"A rollback recipe I asserted without testing"** paragraph retells, in narrative form, what Stage 2 already covers in full technical detail — the failing command, the label mechanism, the working replacement, the `docker network inspect` proof. Their read was that it is the one paragraph saying twice what is already said once, and that folding it into the synthesis keeps the insight without the duplication.

Agreed, and done. The section is back to **four distinct lessons plus one synthesis**, none of which duplicates another.

Two further changes while in there:

- **The synthesis now sits at the end of the section**, after the Arithmetic entry. It opens "three of the errors above", and it previously sat above one of the three.
- **The synthesis carries `lucos-architect`'s three additions**, which are new content rather than tidying:
  - Predictions about *procedures* are the higher-stakes half of untested prescriptions. A bad value fails immediately in front of the person typing it; a bad recovery step fails only in the state it was written for — mid-incident, after the destructive action, with no other route back.
  - **The hypothesis about why the rollback would fail was also wrong.** The worry was container reattachment to a network with a new ID; Compose never got that far. Recorded deliberately, because the tempting lesson — that reasoning harder finds these — is false. Rehearsing finds them, and works precisely because you cannot know in advance which assumption is broken.
  - The generalisable form: **enumerate what the *recovery* depends on, not just what you are changing.** The pre-flight proved the network could be created and said nothing about whether CircleCI could deploy or primary DNS was serving, both of which the recovery needs.

## On the repeat

`lucos` is unsupervised, so reviewer approval merges within minutes. Requesting a review is effectively requesting a merge, and I twice pushed follow-on commits to a branch whose review I had already asked for. My earlier instruction fix said "don't mark ready while a thread is live", which didn't cover this case because lucas42/lucos#284 was never a draft. I'm replacing it with the general rule: **once you request review, the branch is frozen — further changes go in a new PR.**

@lucos-code-reviewer — this is your requested edit, plus architect's additions. Nothing else is outstanding on this report from my side.

author: myinisjap
body:
The three single-task transition endpoints all guard against moving a task with a live run — `MoveLabel` (`handlers/tasks.go:512`), `Approve` (`:593`), and `Reject` (`:653`) each call `rejectTransitionWhileRunLive` and return 409 when the active run is `pending` or `running`.

`Bulk`'s `"move"` branch does not (`backend/internal/api/handlers/task_bulk.go:165`):

```go
switch body.Action {
case "move":
	err = h.engine.Transition(ctx, id, body.ToLabel, workflow.TriggerHuman, actor, body.Note)
```

`grep -rn "rejectTransitionWhileRunLive" internal/api/handlers/` returns only the three `tasks.go` call sites.

### Why it matters

`engine.Transition`'s CAS unconditionally sets `active_agent_run_id = NULL` (`internal/workflow/engine.go:214`) — that's deliberate, per the architecture note that "`UpdateTaskLabel` always sets `active_agent_run_id = NULL` in SQL, so every transition implicitly unlocks dispatch."

So a bulk move over a task with an in-flight run **silently releases the dispatch lock**. The next dispatcher sweep sees an unlocked task in an agent-triggerable state and starts a second run against the same worktree. When the original run finishes, its cleanup can then clear the *new* run's lock — precisely the scenario #244 hardened the single-task endpoints against.

This is reachable from the UI: the board's multi-select bar posts to this endpoint (`components/board/TaskCard.tsx:230` → `runBulk`).

### Fix

In the `"move"` case, load the task and run the same guard, recording a per-id failure in `bulkResult` rather than transitioning:

```go
case "move":
	task, gerr := h.q.GetTask(ctx, id)
	if gerr != nil { err = gerr; break }
	if runIsLive(ctx, h.q, task) {
		err = fmt.Errorf("task has a live agent run")
		break
	}
	err = h.engine.Transition(ctx, id, body.ToLabel, workflow.TriggerHuman, actor, body.Note)
```

`rejectTransitionWhileRunLive` currently writes the 409 to the `ResponseWriter` directly, so this needs a small refactor to split the predicate from the response — worth doing since the bulk path needs per-id results anyway.

A regression test asserting that bulk-move over a `running` task leaves `active_agent_run_id` intact would pin this.

_Imported from https://github.com/myinisjap/agent-task-editor/issues/333_

### What changed

## Code Review (reviewer agent)

Reviewed the diff against the issue description (#333: bulk "move" bypasses the live-run guard).

### Findings

- **No medium/high/critical issues found.**
- The fix matches the suggested approach exactly: `rejectTransitionWhileRunLive` was split into a pure predicate `taskRunIsLive(ctx, task) bool` plus a thin `rejectTransitionWhileRunLive` wrapper that writes the 409 for the single-task endpoints (MoveLabel/Approve/Reject — all three still call the wrapper, verified via grep).
- `task_bulk.go`'s `"move"` case now: loads the task via `GetTask`, calls `taskRunIsLive`, and on a live run sets `err = errRunLive` and records a per-task `bulkResult` failure instead of transitioning — leaving `active_agent_run_id` and `label` untouched. Non-live tasks in the same batch still succeed (batch isolation preserved).
- `bulkErrorMessage` adds an explicit `errors.Is(err, errRunLive)` branch returning the same message as the 409 single-task response; ordering in the switch doesn't shadow other cases (verified).
- `sql.ErrNoRows` from `GetTask` for a nonexistent id in the move path correctly falls through to the existing "task not found" mapping — behavior-preserving for that edge case.
- New tests added, all passing:
  - `TestTasks_Bulk_Move_RunningRun_Refused` — running-run task refused (207, per-task error, label/lock unchanged), other clean task in the batch still moves.
  - `TestTasks_Bulk_Move_PendingRun_Refused` — narrower #244/#333 pending-run window also guarded.
  - `TestTasks_Bulk_Move_WaitingHumanRun_Allowed` — confirms guard is scoped only to pending/running, not waiting_human (no over-blocking regression).
  - `TestBulkErrorMessage` extended with an `errRunLive` case.
- Docs/spec updated consistently and accurately: `AGENTS.md` (handlers package), `docs/api.md` (409 for label PATCH, per-task refusal note for bulk), `openapi.yaml` description, `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased] > Fixed`.
- Frontend `runBulk` (BoardPage.tsx) already generically surfaces per-task bulk failures (`results.filter(r => !r.ok)`), so no frontend change was needed and the fix integrates end-to-end without further wiring.

### Verification performed independently
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `gofmt -l .` — no output (clean)
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `go test ./... -count=1` (uncached) from `backend/` — all packages PASS, including the four new/updated tests run individually with `-v`.

### Conclusion
Implementation is correct, complete, matches the task's suggested fix, is well-tested with regression tests pinning the exact bug scenario, and docs are accurate. No issues above low severity found (none noted at all, actually — clean implementation).


### Commits

- [bug] Bulk "move" bypasses the live-run guard, re-opening the #244 double-dispatch window (safety-net commit)

author: elockenvitz
body:
The editor's left pane
UniversalNoteEditor's notes list is a w-72 flex sibling. At 390px that leaves roughly 100px for the editor, which is not a narrow editor — it is no editor. It becomes a full-screen overlay on a phone, absent from the layout when closed, with a menu button in the editor header as the way back in and an X rather than a collapse-left chevron to dismiss it. A chevron on a full-screen overlay reads as navigation, not dismissal.

The editor pane also gains min-w-0: without it a long note title would push the flex child past the viewport instead of truncating, which is the usual cause of a page that scrolls sideways for no visible reason.

The list table
Its six columns are percentage-width, so at 390px they do not overflow, they crush — a 35% title column is 136px and the remaining five share 250px. Notes are text, not figures, and nothing here gains from column alignment the way a price grid does, so below sm each note is a card: title, a two-line preview, and source, type, shared state and date on one line beneath. The table is unchanged and gated to sm:table.

Typecheck at baseline, 996 tests passing, production build clean.

Two operator statements from 2026-08-09, put where the decisions they bear on
are actually made rather than left in a session.

The Linux ABI is essential to Ken's practical value; without it the target
audience would treat Ken as a toy or a curio. That is a statement about what
Ken is, not a scheduling preference, so it outranks convenience arguments in
sequencing. Recorded in 10-linux-abi-completion.md section 3 with the

dependents of RT-BACKEND-MODULE-SPLIT through a single-file chain with no

Two consequences stated there. Latency on this program is a real cost, so an
ordering argument that buys a saved rebase and spends program latency must be
presented with both sides visible. And "works in the interpreter" is not the

author: maylortaylor
body:
## Why

A show on 2026-08-08 streamed from a venue with a weak uplink. OBS connected,
published for 20–60s, dropped, and reconnected — repeatedly, all night:

```
23:49:34 closed: EOF
23:50:20 closed: EOF
23:51:44 closed: EOF
23:54:27 closed: read tcp ...: i/o timeout
23:55:39 closed: EOF
```

MediaMTX was also logging frame starvation (`part duration changed from 233ms to
801ms`, `segment duration changed from 2s to 3s`).

Every reconnect tears down and rebuilds the HLS muxer, which viewers experience
as the stream dying — so the reconnect is more costly than the stall that caused it.

## What

Raise the global `readTimeout` from its 10s default to 30s, so a brief stall no
longer kills the publisher session.

## Scope — deliberately narrow

This helps **only** the `i/o timeout` close reason. A connection torn down
outright closes with `EOF` and reconnects regardless. In the sample above that's
4 of 5 drops, so **encoder bitrate is still the real lever** on a bad uplink
(that stream was pushing 8.1 Mbps peak / 5.3 Mbps average at 1080p).

One key changed on purpose — this was applied ahead of a live show, and fewer
edits meant less risk.

## Validation

Ran the edited config through the real image before applying:

```
docker run --rm -v candidate.yml:/mediamtx.yml:ro bluenviron/mediamtx:1.18.2
→ "configuration loaded from /mediamtx.yml"
→ RTMP/HLS listeners opened, no new deprecation warnings
```

Auth block and `runOnReady` verified intact.

## Note

`deploy.yml` does `rm -rf ~/stpetemusic/n8n/mediamtx` and re-copies from the
repo, so any hot-patch applied directly to the box is reverted on the next
deploy. This PR is what makes the change stick.

## Follow-ups found while investigating (not in this PR)

- **`Go Live Notify` has never fired.** `runOnReady:` calls `curl`, but the
  `bluenviron/mediamtx` image is distroless: `exec: "curl": executable file not
  found in $PATH`. Zero executions in 48h despite ~15 stream starts. Same class
  as bug #9 in `.claude/infrastructure.md`. Suggested fix: move the trigger to
  the existing `Stream Watchdog` workflow (already runs every 60s), with a
  cooldown so a flapping connection can't spam FB/IG.
- `deploy.yml`'s secret substitution is a blind string-replace and writes secret
  values into the config's *comments*, not just its config lines.
- `N8N_API_KEY` is empty in the production `.env` — the n8n public API returns 401.

## 문제

npm 설치자는 launchd 상주를 얻을 방법이 없었다. 등록 스크립트가 `scripts/install-launchd.sh` 하나뿐인데, 이 파일은 배포 대상(`files`: bin·dist·README)에 없다. 제품 정의는 "맥 상주 서버 + launchd 영구화"인데 대표 설치 경로는 포그라운드 실행만 주었고 `Ctrl+C`면 죽었다.

## 변경

- `src/server/daemon.ts` 신설 — plist 생성(`buildPlist`)·등록(`register`)·해제(`unregister`). 경로는 `process.execPath` + 설치본 `dist/server/main.js`에서 얻어 npm 전역·npx·소스 실행 모두에서 맞는 값이 들어간다. 경로의 XML 특수문자는 이스케이프
- `bin/kaivo.js` 흐름 3분기 — ① 포트 살아있음 → 브라우저만 ② 비어있음 → 상주 등록 1회 질문 ③ 거절·비대화형(`isTTY` false) → 종전 포그라운드
- 거절은 `~/.kaivo/daemon-declined`로 기억해 다시 묻지 않는다
- 등록 후 기동이 확인되지 않으면 등록을 되돌린다 (그대로 두면 `KeepAlive`가 재시작 루프)
- 빌드: `outfile` → `outdir`로 `dist/server/{main,daemon}.js` 두 파일 생성

## 선택하지 않은 안

- `postinstall` 자동 등록 — 동의 없이 데몬을 심는 것
- 서브커맨드 단독(`kaivo daemon install`) — 존재를 아무도 모른다

## 검증

- `npm run typecheck` 통과
- `npm test` **95/95 통과** (daemon 4건 신규)
- `kaivo` 실행 시 "이미 실행 중" 분기 exit 0 확인

## 한계

등록 분기는 이 머신에서 end-to-end로 돌리지 못했다 — 9011을 기존 launchd가 물고 있어 첫 분기에서 빠져나간다. 실검증은 publish 후 다른 머신에서.

author: novusedge
body:
Fixes BOT-348. Pairs with botspot-org/locus-core#25, which must deploy first.

Mikael's blog showed `above_footer` in the plugin while the database held `bottom_of_page`. This is the plugin half of the fix, and it also reworks how placement actually gets applied.

## The reported defect

`normalize_platform_settings()` checked the platform's placement against `["auto", "footer", "manual", "bottom_of_content"]`. The rest of the plugin used `bottom_of_content | above_footer | bottom_of_page | manual`; `auto` and `footer` existed nowhere else. A value outside the stale list became `null`, `array_filter` dropped the key, and the plugin kept its local value with no error and no log line. All three inbound paths funnel through that one function. `fe0ea70` (BOT-277) introduced the list and the vocabulary changed afterward without it.

## Why the names changed too

`above_footer` and `bottom_of_page` were never two placements. Both rendered inside `the_content`, then a `DOMContentLoaded` script walked 13 CSS selectors looking for a footer and moved the node before or after the first match. A theme that positions its own components — Mikael's does — got a result nobody chose, and when nothing matched the appendix silently stayed mid-content behind a `console.warn`.

So the vocabulary is now `in_content | end_of_page | manual` plus an optional CSS anchor, and `end_of_page` renders server-side at `wp_footer`. No JS, no guessing. The selector list is deleted. The anchor is the deliberate way to ask for a specific position, and it relocates against exactly one user-supplied selector.

**This moves live pages.** Sites currently on `above_footer` will see the appendix land below the footer instead of above it. The anchor field is how to put it back. Worth listing the affected domains before release so it reads as expected.

## Changes

- Canonical vocabulary in `Bspt_Options`, with legacy values migrating on read and write, so an upgrading site's stored `above_footer` resolves correctly instead of falling back.
- The allowlist now migrates instead of rejecting. An absent key still means "keep the local value", so a payload that omits a setting cannot clobber it.
- `push_platform_settings()` sends settings to the platform on admin save, so a site admin's change reaches the dashboard. Last write wins.
- `end_of_page` renders at `wp_footer`; the anchor script is the only JS left and only runs when a selector is configured. A missed anchor leaves the appendix at the end of the page and marks the node `data-bsa-anchor-missed`.
- Three-mode settings UI with the anchor fields, shown for End of page.
- The `bspt_settings_dashboard_locked` read-only lock is gone. Both sides write now, so the plugin UI stays editable.
- The plugin ignores a `settings.updated` event whose `site_domain` does not match this site. A payload without that key is still applied, so this build works against an older core.

## Notes for review

Two things came out of implementation rather than the plan. The settings screen saves through AJAX to `handle_save_settings`, so `register_setting()` alone would have shipped anchor fields that render but never persist — the admin JS needed the wiring too. And a site with no API key configured is not a failed push, so `push_platform_settings()` distinguishes skipped from rejected rather than showing a failure notice on every save of an unconnected site.

## Testing

120 tests passing, phpcs clean. New coverage for the legacy migration table, the allowlist fix, anchor sanitization, the render-mode decisions, and the site-scope check.

Hook ordering has no automated coverage — nothing in this repo can simulate WordPress firing order. The double-render and page-builder paths were traced by hand in review and are on the manual verification list, along with each placement mode in a browser.

author: nbeerbower
body:
Adds the first 1.14 protocol packet, and fixes four port bugs that were kicking **every** client.

> **Depends on `gn.hml` [#4](https://github.com/Yotis-Studios/gn.hml/pull/4).** Without those two codec fixes this server still rejects every connection. Merge and release gn.hml first, then bump the lock here.

---

## `GAME_NUM_PLAYERS` (115) — host-asked, server-clamped roster size

The client's lobby roster stepper was offline-only, because every client derived `numPlayers` from the map it was sent — so a host changing it alone disagreed with the whole lobby about which slots exist.

**The host asks; the server decides.** The request is clamped to `num_bases`, to a minimum of 2, and to an even number, and a **new** packet carrying the clamped value is broadcast to everyone *including the asker*.

Rebuilding rather than relaying is the design, not an implementation detail. Relaying the incoming packet would tell the other clients what was *asked for* rather than what was *agreed*, and a request that hit a bound would leave the host one step ahead of the lobby — the exact disagreement the packet exists to remove. It also means a client that is out of date, modified, or simply wrong cannot push the lobby into a state no map can satisfy.

Even-ness is not cosmetic: team play halves the roster and the client rounds nowhere, so an odd count is a silently mismatched team.

`set_num_players` already existed — it emits the `numPlayers` IPC event GameRouter lists lobbies with. It simply had no packet reaching it.

## The clamp moved into `game.set_num_players`

Trying to write a test for it is what found this. The bounds were in `packet_handler`, so `set_one_v_one` and the map load reached `set_num_players` **without** them — and testing three lines of arithmetic needed a `PacketHandler`, a `ConnectionManager` and a `MockServer`.

Order matters, and there is a test pinning it: **cap first, then even.** A request for 7 on a five-base map caps to 5 and rounds to 4; the other order gives 6, which that map cannot seat.

## Four port bugs

All JavaScript idioms that mean something different in Hemlock. All invisible to type checking and borrow checking.

| # | bug | assumed JS behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `connection.uid` **throws** on a missing field | JS yields `undefined`, so `x.uid != null` was the natural "is this a reconnect?" test |
| 2 | `remove_connection` indexed with `null` | JS tolerates `arr[null]` |
| 3 | `attack_damage: null` could not be serialised | JS sends null happily |
| 4 | booleans could not be serialised | fixed properly upstream; the local workaround here is reverted |

**Bug 1 rejected every client that had never connected before.** **Bug 2 hid bug 1** — while every client was being kicked, every kick threw again in the disconnect handler on the way out, and the second error buried the first in the log.

Bug 3's fix is safe as a number because the client only reads `attackDamage` when `suddenDeath` is set, and `sudden_death` defaults false.

## How they were found

The client would not connect and it was not obvious which end was at fault. Pointing it at a **bare `ws` server** — twenty lines of Node, no game logic — it connected immediately. That single run eliminated the client, its async plumbing and the test harness, and left this repository.

**Hemlock reports the top-level call site, not the throwing line** — all six bugs reported `server.hml:27`. They were located by inserting a `print` marker before every statement and seeing which was last.

## Tests

`test/game_roster_test.hml` — five tests for the clamp, **proven able to fail**: removing the even-ness line makes two of them fail with `Expected 5 to equal 4`.

Full suite: 4 suites, 0 failed.

And end to end against the real GameMaker client:

```
[nettest] connected; mainClient=0 host=0
[nettest] roster after shrink: 2
[nettest] clamp round trip OK: asked 99, server agreed 4
NET TEST OK
```

Protocol reference lives in the client repo at `docs/protocol/PROTOCOL.md`.

author: poindexter12
body:
Second part of the Scorecard remediation (with #36).

## osv-scanner.toml
`GO-2026-5932` (`x/crypto/openpgp` — deprecated by design, **no fixed version exists at any x/crypto release**) cannot be fixed by bumping: the module enters the graph transitively via the terraform-plugin-sdk chain, and `go mod why` + govulncheck confirm the package is never imported nor reachable. This checks in a documented, code-reviewed exception instead of a UI dismissal. **Verification pending**: after merge, the next Scorecard run on main will show whether its embedded osv-scanner honors the config — if it doesn't, the alert stays open with this file as the documented rationale.

## paths-ignore removal (lint.yml, test.yml)
Prep for making `lint` and both `test (…)` jobs required status checks on `main`: a path-filtered workflow never runs on a docs-only PR, so its required check would stay pending forever and block the merge. Cost: docs-only PRs now run ~2–3 min of CI. The fuzz/scheduled workflows keep their filters (not required checks).

author: jomcgi
body:
Follow-up to #4555, which set the key in the wrong object.

The process still reported `SSRF_ALLOWED_NETWORKS=[]` and registration kept failing. The chart emits this key into **both** the gateway ConfigMap and the gateway Secret, and the deployment's envFrom order is `[gateway-secret, gateway-config, context-forge]`. Kubernetes applies envFrom sources in order, so the ConfigMap default shadows the Secret value.

`MCP_REQUIRE_AUTH` worked earlier only because it exists solely in the Secret.

A CIDR allowlist is not sensitive, so config is the right home regardless.

Verified: `helm template` now emits the key exactly once, in the ConfigMap, with the intended value.

author: njrini99-code
body:
The new-message recipient search had three unchecked reads, and every one of them landed in the **same empty state** — which is worded as a claim about the team, not about the query.

A failed roster read gave `playerIds = []` and returned early, so a coach searching their own full roster saw **"No players on your team yet"**, or "No players found" for a name that is right there. A failed team read left the player with no coaches in the list, indistinguishable from a team that has none. Neither suggests trying again, so the person stops — and the message never gets sent.

The empty state now distinguishes the two: *"Couldn't load players — something went wrong looking that up. Please try again."* The genuine answers are untouched, and both still say exactly what they said.

The bare `catch {}` that swallowed everything now records what it caught and sets the same flag.

### Found by tsc, not by me
I set the failure flag and forgot to render it — which would have shipped the identical silent empty state with extra bookkeeping. Exactly the bug class this PR fixes, committed while fixing it.

- `npm run lint` 0 · lint-ratchet 0 · `tsc` 0 · `npm run build` 0 · suite **3647 passed**

body:
## Outcome

Builds one bounded main-process index for Quick Open, multi-format search, links, tags, citations, rename previews, and graph data.

Closes the acceptance criteria in `workplan/items/unified-workspace-index.md`.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --runInBand` — 109 suites, 1,280 tests passed
- `npm run quality:static` — passed
- `npm run wp:check` — passed
- `npm run ci:local` — 5/6 stages passed; required Electron E2E could not launch in the locked local macOS desktop (`Process failed to launch`)
- hosted `@required @workspace-index` Electron workflow added as the merge gate

## Design notes

The index atomically publishes complete refreshes, reuses unchanged extraction, falls back to deterministic verification without recursive watchers, preserves the last complete result on cancellation, and exposes explicit file/content/yield budgets.

author: danielbaldwin47
body:
Closes #135.

The live tier read the project as a given, and #119 §B found four failures that were all
the same habit. Each is now something the suite builds.

- **`a_still_lands`** took whatever image the pool listed first and named no bin, so a
  duplicated pool-root name was ambiguous. It now passes the listing's bin verbatim, and
  picks an entry Resolve types `Still` — a PNG *sequence* is a 27-frame clip with a `.png`
  path, and asking one for 90 frames is not the one-time Out write the test is about.
- **`render_queue_exports`** rendered whatever timeline the test before it left current,
  which after the locked-track probe was an empty locked one with no mix on it. A new
  `a_known_cut` fixture builds a short cut with a master mix under it, makes it current,
  and puts the director's timeline back — the same fixture serves the OTIO round trip and
  the dissolve import, which were comparing a concert-length edit shot by shot.
- **`locked_track_footgun`** met the name it had created on the run before. A
  session-scoped sweep deletes the previous run's timelines first, and the probe now puts
  Resolve back where it found it and deletes its own empty cut.
- **Scene scan** took the shortest clip in the pool — in this project a PNG sequence with
  no cuts — so the half of #34 it exists for passed vacuously every run. Per the ticket's
  branch: **the live box's pool was checked and holds no flattened Monkfish render**, only
  raw continuous angles, so the suite generates its own clip (four solid colours a second
  apart, three cuts) and imports it into a scratch bin it deletes afterwards.
  `RESOLVE_MCP_SCENE_SCAN_CLIP` stays as the override for a project that does have an edit
  to scan, and is documented as unset on the live box. Finding no cuts is now a failure
  rather than a skip.

`tests/live_state.py` holds what the tools under test cannot build — the sweep, the
generated clip, the name predicate — so the ticket's seam line holds: every decision
(which names are the suite's own, what happens when Resolve is sitting on one, what
command builds the clip, what an env var naming a missing clip means) settles in
`tests/test_live_state.py` against the fakes.

## Resolve crashed on the first live run

Worth reading before merging. The sweep's first live run took Resolve Studio 21.0.3 down:
it switched off a leftover timeline, deleted it, and Resolve logged `Internal undo error 3`
and wrote a crash dump inside the autosave the deletions triggered. The project survived —
`2026-06_Zinc_and_Monkfish` was intact after a restart — but the run did not, and neither
did the 34 tests that errored at setup, because a dropped handle answers `None` for every
method rather than raising.

So the sweep no longer moves off before deleting. The timeline Resolve is sitting on is
reported as `kept`, and `restore_current()` leaves the session on a cut the suite did not
build so the next run's sweep can take the leftover instead of it surviving forever. Two
consecutive full runs confirm the cycle: the first swept 13 and kept none, the second the
same.

## Scope beyond the four bullets, and why

- `resolve/timeline.py`'s `_timelines` is now `timelines_of`. The sweep needs the same
  enumeration, and CLAUDE.md forbids reaching for a symbol through a module that merely
  imports it — a private cross-module import is worse than naming it.
- The probe searches the whole pool rather than its root folder. Every real project keeps
  footage in bins, so the probe skipped on the machine it guards, and the footgun went
  unmeasured. This was observed live, not guessed: the test skipped on one run and passed
  on the next depending on what the listing returned.
- `restore_current()` prefers a cut the suite did not build. Putting a leftover back would
  make it permanent — it is current, so the sweep skips it, and the run after finds it
  current again.

## Review

Two-axis `/code-review` against `origin/main`, Standards and Spec as parallel sub-agents.

**Standards — no hard violations.** `CONTEXT.md` updated in the same PR for the new module,
the seam split honoured, `timelines_of` imported from its defining module, the
`getattr(x, "Method", None)` guard matching the existing dropped-handle idiom in
`resolve/apply.py`. Four judgement calls, all taken:

1. *Fake fidelity* — `FakeMediaPool.DeleteTimelines` recorded a refused delete in
   `deleted_timelines`, so the attribute no longer meant what its name said. Now recorded
   only once the refusals are past. (Pre-existing for the current-timeline refusal; the new
   knob made it visible.)
2. *Speculative Generality* — `a_known_cut` yielded a `durations` field nothing read.
   Dropped.
3. *Primitive Obsession* — the fixture returned `dict[str, Any]` for a two-field concept
   while the same diff introduced `Swept` as a NamedTuple. It is now `KnownCut`.
4. *Data Clumps / Speculative Generality* — `seconds` travelled through both hard-cut
   functions and was never overridden. Dropped to a module constant.

A fifth (mild Feature Envy in `sweep_suite_timelines(pool, project)`) was noted and left:
it is inherent to this repo's wrapper style over the foreign API.

**Spec — the four bullets are implemented; two real bugs found and fixed.**

1. The session fixture called `current_project` *outside* its own `try`, so a Resolve that
   is up with no project open would raise `NoProjectOpenError` and error every test at
   setup — precisely the shape the fixture's docstring says it exists to prevent. Moved
   inside the guard, with the teardown skipped when no project was reached.
2. `LOCKED_TRACK_PROBE` reported `put_back` as false when no timeline was open, so the test
   failed for correct probe behaviour *and* leaked `resolve-mcp-lock-probe` — the leftover
   this ticket exists to stop. "Nothing to put back" now counts as put back, the sweep
   assertion is conditional on a timeline having been open, and the comment says why the
   next run's sweep is the right place for that rare leak.
3. The still test's `if still["bin"] is not None` guard never fired — the listing's bin is
   a `str`, `""` for the pool root. Passed unconditionally now, matching `a_source_clip`'s
   documented "verbatim, not `or None`" rule from #122.
4. *Seam* — the scan-clip selection decision (env override vs generate, and what a variable
   naming a missing clip means) lived only in the live file. Extracted to
   `named_scan_clip()` with fake-tier tests, which is what the ticket's seam line asks for.
5. *Documented default* — the negative pool finding is now stated in `CONTEXT.md`, not just
   in a docstring.

Two spec notes accepted without change: `a_known_cut`'s audio-fallback branch delegates to
`validate_cut`, which is itself fake-tested, and the scope items above are justified in
their own section.

Fix diff re-checked as a focused pass; no new review.

## Test record

- **Fake tier** — `uv run pytest -m 'not live'`: 1481 passed, 0 failed.
- **mypy strict** — clean, 167 source files. **ruff** — clean.
- **Live tier** — Windows 11, DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.0.3.7, python.org CPython 3.12.10,
  project `mcp-tests-zinc`: **29 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed**, run three times. All six
  tests this ticket touches pass, including the scene scan finding real cuts. The eight
  skips are dependency- or human-gated, not state: `beat_this`/`panns_inference`/the
  analysis extra not installed, four opt-in env vars, and one that needs a marker placed by
  hand in the GUI.

The live tier ran in `mcp-tests-zinc` rather than the client project, per the ticket's own
note about scratch cleanup — and, after the crash above, because a sweep that deletes
timelines does not belong in a client project unattended.

## Known follow-up, not fixed here

`test_a_range_render_covers_the_frames_it_was_given` still skips with "The open timeline is
too short to render two ranges out of". It needs a timeline of 13s or more and reads
whichever one is current, so an earlier build test leaves a 108

author: danielgolden
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **Chat** view in the sidebar where signed-in users can ask natural-language questions about their own imported MacroFactor food-log data and get streamed answers from an LLM.

Closes #10.

## Provider decision

**OpenRouter** (Deepseek V4 Flash Latest, `~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest`) over Replicate. Full reasoning documented in [this comment on #10](https://github.com/danielgolden/macrofactor-dashboard/issues/10#issuecomment-5228627809). Short version: OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible (drop-in for the Vercel AI SDK), streams via SSE, supports tool/function calling, bills per-token, and has built-in provider failover — all a better fit for text chat than Replicate's per-second GPU model.

## How it works

- **Client:** `useChat` from `@ai-sdk/react` in `ChatView.tsx` handles message state, streaming, loading, and errors. Transcript + composer built with existing shadcn primitives (`Textarea`, `Avatar`, `Button`, `Card`, `ScrollArea`).
- **Server:** `POST /api/chat` uses `streamText` with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(5)` to allow up to 5 tool-call rounds. `GET /api/chat` returns persisted history.
- **Data grounding:** 4 server-side tools (`listFoods`, `getFoodByName`, `getFoodLogEntries`, `getDateRange`) query Supabase, all scoped `.eq("user_id", userId)` via Clerk's `auth()`. The LLM never controls `userId` — it's baked into the tool closures — so cross-user leakage is impossible by construction.
- **Persistence:** New `chat_messages` table (RLS-isolated) stores visible `user`/`assistant` messages. Loaded on mount, saved after each exchange via `onFinish`. Intermediate tool-call frames are not persisted (they re-query live data each turn).

## Security measures

- Per-user in-memory rate limiting (20 req/min) in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` — first layer behind the provider-level weekly cap.
- Message array capped at last 20 messages sent to the LLM; newest user message truncated at 8000 chars. Bounds cost per request. Full history still persisted.
- Clerk `auth()` guards on both `POST` and `GET`.
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is server-only (no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix), never shipped client-side.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `supabase/add_chat_messages.sql` | New `chat_messages` table + RLS policies. **Run this migration before deploying.** |
| `src/lib/chat-tools.ts` | 4 tool definitions + Supabase query implementations |
| `src/app/api/chat/route.ts` | `POST` streaming + `GET` history, with rate limit and payload caps |
| `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` | In-memory sliding-window rate limiter (20 req/min per user) |
| `src/components/ChatView.tsx` | Chat UI (transcript + composer) |
| `src/lib/views.ts` | New `chat` view entry |
| `src/components/Explorer.tsx` | Renders `ChatView` for `view === "chat"` |
| `.env.example` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` placeholder |
| `package.json` | Adds `ai`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/react`, `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm` |

## Setup required

1. **Run the migration** in the Supabase SQL editor: `supabase/add_chat_messages.sql`
2. **Set the env var** in Vercel: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (create a key at https://openrouter.ai/keys)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Provider decision (OpenRouter vs Replicate) documented on issue #10
- [x] New **Chat** tab visible in the sidebar for signed-in users
- [x] Chat UI renders with the placeholder example question in the empty composer
- [x] User can send a message and receive a streamed response
- [x] Response is grounded in the signed-in user's own imported data
- [x] "No data yet" state handled
- [x] API key stored securely (server-only env var)
- [x] Rate limiting + payload caps to bound cost abuse

## Test plan

- [ ] Run the Supabase migration
- [ ] Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `.env` and Vercel
- [ ] `npm run dev` → sign in → import a MacroFactor export → click **Chat**
- [ ] Send the placeholder question; confirm a streamed, grounded answer
- [ ] Confirm tool-call chips appear during tool execution
- [ ] Refresh the page; confirm history is restored
- [ ] With no data imported, confirm the "no data" state with an import prompt
- [ ] Send >20 messages rapidly; confirm 429 rate limit

author: giovaneguimaraes
body:
## T-104a — `validation-core` no formato-alvo

Primeira migração depois do piloto (T-103). O `validation-core` foi escolhido de propósito por ser o package trivial da fila — puro, sem I/O, sem `db` para injetar: se o formato do `subscription-core` não generalizasse, descobriríamos aqui e barato.

**Generalizou.** 1 função por arquivo + barrel + testes fora de `src/` + Jest/ts-jest funcionaram sem fricção.

### O que mudou

`src/` passou de 3 arquivos-balaio (`dates.ts`, `money.ts`, `categories.ts`) para **8 arquivos de uma função/constante cada**; `index.ts` virou barrel puro; os testes saíram de `src/**/*.test.ts` para `tests/unit/tests/`, um por arquivo de `src/`.

**Nenhum call site precisou mudar** — o barrel preservou os 8 símbolos exportados com as mesmas assinaturas (incluindo os parâmetros default `field = 'amount'`). O único ajuste fora do package foi um comentário no `portfolio-core` que citava `src/dates.ts`, arquivo que deixou de existir.

### Nenhuma regra de validação mudou

Ponto bloqueante da tarefa, verificado duas vezes de forma independente: o executor e o revisor compararam o corpo de cada função linha a linha contra a `main`. Todos idênticos, incluindo as invariantes sensíveis — calendário real em `isValidIsoDate` (T-043), máx. 2 casas em `isValidMoneyAmount` (T-052) e o `toLocaleLowerCase('pt-BR')` de `normalizeCategory` (que o `db/src/migrations.ts` usa numa migração de DADOS — o caso unicode `SAÚDE`/`saúde` segue coberto).

### Testes

- `validation-core`: **36 testes**, cobertura **100%** em statements/branches/functions/lines. Os 33 originais foram todos preservados (o revisor conferiu caso a caso); os 3 extras cobrem o branch do parâmetro default `field`, que ficou descoberto ao separar as funções do arquivo-balaio, e a constante que ganhou arquivo próprio.
- Raiz: `pnpm test` verde — server **452** (preservado), web 451, subscription-core 131, demais cores inalterados. `pnpm build`, `pnpm lint` e `pnpm format:check` verdes.
- Armadilha da T-097 (falso verde build × runtime) checada dos dois lados, e reproduzida pelo revisor: `require('@vetor-wallet/validation-core')` resolve após o build, e a suíte do server segue verde **com o `dist/` do package apagado** — prova que o alias do Vitest aponta para o `src`.

### Calibragem para a T-104b em diante

- Divergências do piloto declaradas de propósito no `CLAUDE.md` do package (seção "Onde este package DIVERGE do piloto"): sem `db` injetado, sem `setupTests.ts`, sem `moduleNameMapper`, sem Stryker — nenhuma delas faz sentido num package puro.
- **Achado útil**: separar funções que compartilham uma constante expõe branches de parâmetro default que antes ficavam cobertos incidentalmente por outro teste do mesmo arquivo. Os próximos executores devem rodar `--coverage` cedo, não só no final.

body:
### Motivation

- Establish a provider-neutral News & Catalyst foundation that can associate market-moving headlines, events, and catalysts with symbols while keeping external provider integrations replaceable and provider secrets out of the client.
- Surface news and catalysts alongside existing Market Data, Watchlist, Portfolio, and Research workspaces without changing existing Supabase ownership or market-data boundaries.
- Provide an honest demo/local adapter and UI scaffolding that clearly labels illustrative content and avoids fabricating live events or timestamps.

### Description

- Added strongly typed, provider-neutral domain models and validation for news articles, sources, categories, sentiment, impact, events, catalysts, company summaries, queries, and saved-news notes under `src/features/news`.
- Implemented a replaceable `NewsService` boundary with an isolated demo adapter (`demoNewsService`), deduplicated cached hooks (`useNews`, `useSymbolNews`, `useMarketNews`, `useCatalysts`, `useSymbolCatalysts`, `useCompanyNewsSummary`), and a small AsyncStorage-backed saved-news notes service for authenticated users.
- Built the News UI surface including reusable presentation components (article card, catalyst card, saved news list), the News workspace (`/news`) with Market/Watchlist/Portfolio/Company/Catalyst/Saved views, a symbol-specific route (`/news/[symbol]`), and lightweight Dashboard and Research navigation links that use existing market and investment providers for context.
- Updated documentation to describe the News/Catalyst architecture, demo adapter constraints, security boundaries, and next steps by modifying `CHANGELOG.md`, `PROJECT_SPEC.md`, and `README.md`; created the following key files: `src/features/news/{types.ts,validation.ts,hooks.ts,index.ts,services/*,components/*}`, `app/(tabs)/news.tsx`, and `app/news/[symbol].tsx`.

### Testing

- Ran `npm run format` and formatting completed successfully with Prettier. 
- Ran `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, format:check) and the suite passed after implementing ESLint/TS fixes. 
- Ran `git diff --check` and found no diff-check issues. 
- Performed credential and client scans (searches for service-role keys, OpenAI keys, broker secrets, and duplicate Supabase constructors) and verified no privileged credentials were introduced and the single Supabase client remains in `src/lib/supabase.ts`.

author: gacafly
body:
## What this is

Guard-rail PR accompanying the fix for the broken production deploy pipeline.

## Root cause (verified by reproduction)

- **#486** bumped `typescript` 5.9.3 → 7.0.2 (root). TypeScript 7 **removed** the tsconfig `baseUrl` option, so `tsc -b` fails with `TS5102` → every `CI` and `Deploy (Firebase Hosting + rules)` run on `main` since 2026-08-08 23:46 fails at the Build step.
- **#483** did the same in `/functions` (and left duplicate `typescript`/`globals` keys in `functions/package.json`; the last key, `^7.0.2`, wins).

Reproduced locally: pinning `typescript` back to `~5.9.2` makes both `npm run build` (543+167 sitemap URLs, prerender OK, JSON-LD OK) and `functions` `tsc` build pass.

## This PR contains

1. `scripts/fix-typescript-pin.mjs` — one-shot repair script (pin + dedupe) for anyone who prefers fixing forward instead of reverting.
2. `.github/dependabot.yml` — ignore `typescript` semver-major bumps in `/` and `/functions` so this can't recur.

## Required maintainer action (2 clicks, can't be automated — token lacks lockfile write path)

1. Open **#486** → click **Revert** → merge the revert PR.
2. Open **#483** → click **Revert** → merge the revert PR.
3. Merge this PR.

Order doesn't matter. After the reverts land on `main`, the `Deploy` workflow will go green and ship to https://flygaca.com automatically.

*Note: the live site is currently fine — it's still serving the last good deploy (Aug 8). Only new deploys are blocked.*

author: chadjw
body:
## Summary

`syncRoadmap` treats a named `Blockers:` entry as a status signal: any feature whose blocker is not yet `done` gets proposed as `blocked`. But the two fields mean different things:

- **`Blockers:`** is *informational* — it documents a dependency relationship.
- **`Status: blocked`** is *semantic* — "actively waiting on something we can't influence right now".

Conflating them silently flips every item added with `Blockers: <sibling-planned-item>` to `blocked` on the next sync, even when the dependency is just normal queue position within the same milestone. In one observed milestone, 13 of 46 newly added items had to be reverted by hand.

Blocker inference is now **cascade-unblock only**: a feature already marked `blocked` returns to `planned` once all of its blockers reach `done`. The bogus `→ blocked` proposal is gone.

## The bug, still live on `main`

`packages/core/src/roadmap/sync.ts` before this change:

```ts
if (feature.blockedBy.length > 0) {
  const blockerNotDone = feature.blockedBy.some(...);
  if (blockerNotDone) return 'blocked';   // ← corrupts planned features
  if (feature.status === 'blocked') return 'planned';
}
```

## Tests

The existing test that *codified* the bug (`proposes blocked when blocker is in-progress`) is replaced by three tests covering the corrected semantics:

- dependent and blocker both `planned` (the reproduction case)
- blocker `in-progress`, dependent `planned`
- dependent already `in-progress` with an un-done blocker

Verified these are real regression tests — against the unfixed `sync.ts` **2 of 19 fail**; with the fix **19/19 pass**. Cascade-unblock coverage is retained.

## Verification

- `packages/core` roadmap suite: **525 passed**, 1 skipped
- `packages/cli` roadmap/MCP suites: **109 passed**
- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/core`: clean
- prettier: clean
- No caller or test anywhere in the repo asserted a sync-produced `blocked` transition

## Provenance

The fix was authored on `fix/manage-roadmap-planned-blocked-corruption` (2026-06-04) but never had a PR opened, so the bug stayed live. Rebased onto current `main` here; the only conflict was signature drift — `inferStatus` became `async` upstream — resolved by keeping the async event-sourced signature and applying the corrected blocker logic on top.

author: os-project-manager
body:
Fixes #6696

## 问题

`packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts` 里 `describeHighPrivilegeBits` 的 JSDoc,拿平台自己的 `member_default` 当"裸 `'*'` 通配符本身不算高权限"的举例。#5491(PR #6684)按维护者裁定(2026-08-07)把平台基线收窄为 explicit-allow 之后,该集合**完全不带 `'*'` 条目**了,于是这句举例指着一个已经不是那个形状的集合。照着去找的读者一无所获,进而怀疑的是规则本身,而不是这句举例。

**规则没错,也没动。** `describeHighPrivilegeBits` 从不读 `member_default`,它评估调用方递进来的任意集合;ADR-0090 D5 断言原样保留,实现一行未改。

## 前提复核(在 `origin/main` @ `c32944d67` 上量的)

不是照抄 issue,而是拿**真实的 `defaultPermissionSets` 数组**跑真实谓词量出来的 —— 因为"用另一个同样失效的举例替换失效举例"是同一个缺陷再犯一次,本 lane 今天已经为这个形状关掉过 #6628:

```
=== member_default ===
  has '*' entry:         false          ← 前提成立,举例确实失效
  describeHighPrivilegeBits             -> null
  describeAnchorForbiddenBits(everyone) -> null

=== viewer_readonly ===
  ships:                 yes ("Viewer — Read-Only")
  has '*' entry:         true
  '*' value:             {"allowCreate":false,"allowRead":true,"allowEdit":false,
                          "allowDelete":false,"allowTransfer":false,"allowRestore":false,
                          "allowPurge":false,"viewAllRecords":false,"modifyAllRecords":false}
  '*' 非 read 的 true 位:  []            ← 名副其实的只读
  systemPermissions:     null
  describeHighPrivilegeBits             -> null   ← 确实不是高权限
  describeAnchorForbiddenBits(everyone) -> null   ← 确实可绑 everyone
  describeAnchorForbiddenBits(guest)    -> "a '*' wildcard grant (guest bindings admit explicit objects only)"
```

最后一行是意外收获:`viewer_readonly` 比 `member_default` 当年更适合做这个举例 —— 同一个集合把这句话的**两半同时演示**了,everyone 可绑、GUEST 层恰恰因为通配符被拒。

## 改动

一处注释,7 增 5 删,外加一个 changeset。有两点是刻意的:

1. **D5 的形状描述必须跟着放宽。** 原句是"a **read/create/edit-own** baseline ... 正是这个形状",而 `viewer_readonly` 是**只读**的。只换名字不动形状,等于把一个失效举例换成另一个失效举例。故改为 "a read — or read/create/edit-own — baseline"。
2. **#2753 的历史保留**(issue 明确要求),改写成 "the then-wildcard-carrying default baseline",让时态在新增的 `#5491` 从句旁边不产生歧义。

同一段 JSDoc 后面还有第二处 `member_default` 提及(`allowExport` 那句),已复核**仍然为真**(该集合确实不带 `allowExport`,且 everyone 可绑),故逐字节未动。

## 验证

- **验证方向,先说清楚:此处没有可用的"红"方向,如实报告。** 这是注释,没有任何断言读它;`packages/spec` 下不存在覆盖 `high-privilege.ts` 的 prose pin(该函数的行为 pin 在 `plugin-security/src/audience-anchors.test.ts`,它测行为不测文案),因此把改动回退不会让任何测试变红。此处不发明一次性的源码文本正则。真正有证伪力的检查是上面那次探针:若 `viewer_readonly` 没有通配符、或不是只读、或不可绑 anchor,探针会当场说出来 —— 它正是用来挡"同一个缺陷再犯一次"的。
- **Lane 准入(acceptance 逐字节不变):** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` → **10/10 绿**,含 `check:authorable-surface`(任何 schema 接受的键集未移动)与 `check:docs`。
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` → 绿(TEST_DEBT 未动:未触碰任何测试文件,58 files / 266 errors 原样)。
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` → **346 test files passed / 8877 tests passed**,exit 0。
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` → OK(6362 文件);改动文件另做了越过该 gate 的控制字符自扫描,干净。

## 参考文档触达结论(本次要求测的那一项)

**不触达 `content/docs/references/`。** `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts:186` 是 `if (!entry.name.endsWith('.zod.ts')) continue;` —— 生成器只遍历 `.zod.ts`,而 `high-privilege.ts` 不是。全文 grep `content/docs/` 对该 JSDoc 的特征句零命中,`check:docs` 亦无任何待重生成产物。所以本次属于今天两类测量中的**不触达**那一类(与 `.describe()` 字符串触达相反,与 TSDoc `@example` / authorable key 的 JSDoc 不触达一致)。⛔ 无生成产物需要提交,也未手改任何生成输出。

## Changeset 判断(要求逐条论证的那一项)

**加了,`@objectstack/spec: patch`。**

`packages/spec` 的 `files` 是 `["dist", "json-schema", "liveness", "prompts", "llms.txt", "README.md", "src/**/*.zod.ts", "CHANGELOG.md", "api-surface", "spec-changes.json"]`。`high-privilege.ts` 不是 `.zod.ts`,**源文件本身确实不随包发布**。但结论不能停在这里:构建后实测

```
$ grep -rln "high-privilege by itself" packages/spec/dist/
dist/security/index.d.ts
dist/security/index.d.mts
dist/security/index.js.map
dist/security/index.mjs.map
```

`dist` 在 `files` 里,所以**这段文案是随 npm 包发布给使用方的**,编辑器悬停 `describeHighPrivilegeBits` 读到的就是它 —— 也就是说被误导的不只是本仓库读者。

先例支持同一条线:最贴近的结构同类 `8ad609c69`(`packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts`,同为非 `.zod.ts` 的纯 JSDoc 改动)带了 patch changeset,其结语正是 "Documentation only — no implementation changed, and the doc comment ships in the package's `.d.ts`"。近期六个同类里四个带 changeset。

非 breaking,故不需要 ADR-0087 disposition 标记。

## 范围

严格限于 issue。过程中发现同一处失效举例在 `plugin-security/src/audience-anchors.test.ts:65` 的测试名里还有一份(以及 line 103 的弱实例),按 Prime Directive #10 **另行归档为 #6842**(observation-class,`finding`,无 `pm:queue`,未指派),未在本 PR 修 —— 它在另一个包,且本卡是 `domain:spec-surface`。该 issue 里也记了更值得 triage 的那一层:目前没有任何机制把"文案声称集合 X 是形状 Y"关联到 `defaultPermissionSets` 实际发布的内容,所以 #5491 一改,三处文案同时静默失效而没有一个 gate 动。

body:
## 概要

これ以降の変更を **すべて PR 経由** で進めるための土台として、GitHub Pages の **PR プレビュー配信** を整備し、あわせて公開ページを最新の **v19** に更新します。

このブートストラップ PR だけは「仕組みの導入」と「v19 の取り込み」を同時に行います（この PR 自身が新しいプレビュー機構で v19 をプレビューできるようにするため）。以後の変更は単一目的の PR として出し、それぞれにプレビューが付きます。

## 変更内容

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`**（新規）: `main` への push（PR マージ）で、サイトを `gh-pages` ブランチのルートへ本番配信。PR プレビュー（`pr-preview/`）は `clean-exclude` で保護。
- **`.github/workflows/preview.yml`**（新規）: PR を開く/更新するたびに `gh-pages` の `pr-preview/pr-<番号>/` へプレビュー配信し、PR に URL を自動コメント。クローズ/マージで自動削除（`rossjrw/pr-preview-action`）。
- **`index.html`**: v19 に更新（アプリ本体はアップロードされた v19 をそのまま採用。JS は `node --check` 済み）。
- **`README.md`**: 開発・プレビューの流れと、一度だけ必要な設定を追記。

## マージ後の URL

- 本番: `https://shuzon.github.io/complex-song-metronome/`
- プレビュー: `https://shuzon.github.io/complex-song-metronome/pr-preview/pr-<番号>/`

## 一度だけ必要な設定（メンテナ操作）

プレビュー/本番の URL が実際に表示されるには、以下が一度だけ必要です（ツールから設定変更はできないため手動でお願いします）:

1. リポジトリを **Public** にする（無料 Pages に必須）。
2. **Settings → Pages → Source = Deploy from a branch**、Branch = **`gh-pages`** / **`(root)`** で保存。
   （`gh-pages` ブランチは最初のワークフロー実行時に自動作成されます）
3. Actions の push が権限エラーになる場合は **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions** を **Read and write** に。

## 確認

- ワークフロー YAML は構文チェック済み。
- `versions/`（バージョンアーカイブ）は `.gitignore` 済みで本 PR には含まれません。
- 配信対象は `index.html` + `.nojekyll` のみ（`_site` にステージ）。

author: carloshgalves
omaraljarrah
body:
## Summary

`merge` compared two numeric constraint literals by building a `big.Rat` from each. A rational has to
materialize the value, and `big.Rat.SetString` refuses outright once the decimal exponent passes
roughly 1e6 — while `ir.NewBigVal` validates through `big.ParseFloat`, which holds the exponent
separately and accepts far more. Two legal, equal bounds could therefore reach the IR intact and
still fail to compare: the helper fell back to exact string equality, so `minimum: 1e1000001` against
`minimum: 10e1000000` came out as an `openapi/conflicting-redeclaration` warning on a document with
no conflict, and anyone compiling with `--fail-on warning` got a failed build out of it.

`annotation/decimal.go` already compares bounds exactly and without materializing them — it splits a
literal into sign, significant digits, and the power of ten the leading digit carries, then orders
those. That comparison is now exported as `annotation.BigValEqual` and used by both keywords that
need it: `minimum`/`maximum` through `boundConflictDetail`, and `multipleOf` through
`multipleOfConflictDetail`. Both misreported the same pair, so both are fixed and covered. `merge` no
longer imports `math/big`.

There is a cost side too. Building a rational for `1e1000000` allocates several hundred kilobytes of
digits and takes around 20 ms, and the old comparison did that twice for every redeclared bound.
Reading the literal instead is constant work in the exponent.

This changes only how two magnitudes are compared. Which of two disagreeing branches wins is
untouched — the first declaration still wins, and #10 stays open on whether they should be
intersected instead.

## Test plan

- `annotation`: `BigValEqual` driven directly over one value in two spellings and over pairs that
  genuinely differ, at magnitudes both above and below what a rational will hold, each asserted in
  both directions. A separate case pins the answer for a literal the reader cannot order.
- `merge`: both conflict helpers driven over the same literals, every one built through
  `ir.NewBigVal` so the rows are inputs a schema can actually produce. The test they replace used
  `"not-a-number"`, which `ir.NewBigVal` never returns, so it exercised the string fallback only on
  an input that could not reach it.
- `schema`: the end-to-end allOf tables gain the equal past-range pair for both keywords (must stay
  silent) and a genuinely differing past-range pair for both (must still be diagnosed, naming both
  literals) — so the fix cannot be mistaken for silencing every magnitude that large.
- Restoring the old rational-based comparison reddens all three levels.
- Full gate green: `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`, `go build`, and the 100% coverage gate.

Closes #287

author: sethbacon
body:
## Why

`terraform-suite-ui` has run zizmor for a while and reports **zero** findings. Pointed at the rest of the suite it reported **141, eighteen of them High**. The one repo with the linter is the one with nothing to find — that gap is the whole argument.

It earned its keep on the first run: it caught **eight** `actions/checkout` calls in the new `signature-replay` workflow persisting a cross-repo PAT into `.git/config`, inside a job that uploads an artifact.

## Result: 141 → 14, 18 High → 1

| rule | before | action |
|---|---|---|
| `artipacked` | 81 | `persist-credentials: false` where the job never writes to git |
| `template-injection` | 34 | step outputs moved out of `run:` into `env:` |
| `unpinned-uses` | 3 (High) | SHA-pinned |
| others zizmor could fix safely | — | applied |

## The part that would have broken things

**`--fix=safe` applied nothing.** zizmor classes every `artipacked` fix as *unsafe*, because it cannot know whether a later step needs the credential.

Running `--fix=all` and pushing would have broken **releases, wiki sync, translations and swagger doc sync across four repos** — nine checkouts whose jobs genuinely push:

| job | why it keeps its credential |
|---|---|
| `swagger-docs-sync` | pushes regenerated docs to the PR head |
| `wiki-sync` (×2) | pushes the wiki |
| `translate` (×2) | opens the translations PR |
| `goreleaser` / `publish-release` (×4) | publish releases |

Each is annotated inline. They were found by checking every job for git writes **before** trusting the fixer, not after it broke something.

## Accepted, not silenced

`.github/zizmor.yml` lists `github-app` on the release-please workflow, with the reason.

zizmor tips to add `permission-<name>` inputs so the App token stops inheriting blanket installation permissions. **That exact change has already been made in this suite and reverted** — the installation does not hold the permission requested, so `create-github-app-token` returns `422` and release-please stops running at all. Re-narrowing has to start from auditing what the installation actually grants.

Anything **not** in that file still fails the job, so a new finding of any kind is caught.

## Not a required check yet

What remains — `excessive-permissions`, `secrets-inherit`, one `dangerous-triggers`, one `superfluous-actions` — is a real enumerated backlog, not an accepted one. This is promoted to required once that reaches zero.

A required check that is red on day one is one everybody learns to scroll past, which is the failure this entire batch has been about.

author: tknatwork
body:
Closes #47, closes #48 — the two coverage gaps from the typings 1.133.0 bump (#46), implemented against **measured** Figma behaviour, not the docs.

## Motion variables (#47)
- `write_variables` accepts `resolvedType: EASING | TIMING`. EASING values are `{ type, easingFunctionCubicBezier?, easingFunctionSpring? }` (14 type values; the validator lists them in its error — Figma's own arrives truncated). TIMING values are plain ms.
- Reads emit a stable defensive-copy wire shape for `MotionEasing` (`NormalizedSpring` carries only `{bounce}` — measured).
- Lint: `LEGAL_SCOPES` pins both types to `ALL_SCOPES`. Measured: motion variables are created with ALL_SCOPES and **Figma rejects `set_scopes` on them entirely** — so the previously fail-open lookup now fires `scope-legal-for-resolved-type` on impossible snapshots instead of skipping.
- 3 new tests (legal-silent / impossible-scope-fires-as-error / structured values survive the dedupe keyer).

## Video export (#48)
- `save_screenshots` gains `MP4 | GIF | WEBM` with `fps` (per-format literal sets), `quality` (MP4/WEBM), `loopCount` (GIF), `videoConstraint` (SCALE 0.5–4 literal set / WIDTH / HEIGHT) — batch defaults + per-item overrides; `.mp4/.gif/.webm` extensions infer format; video items get a **120 s** bridge budget instead of the 30 s default.
- **Deliberately not offered on `get_screenshot`** — that tool returns base64 into the model's context; video belongs on disk.
- Plugin: dedicated `exportAsync` call path (the `ExportSettings` union excludes video settings), fail-closed validation, `clip` ignored for video.
- The leader RPC special-case threads all new fields — the silent-drop trap called out in the code map.
- Measured: Figma rejects video export of non-animated nodes with *"Cannot export node as video"*; that error is reported **per item**, documented in the schema.

## Gates
Plugin typecheck clean · plugin build passes · server **49/49** tests.

**Known remaining validation:** a live e2e of the new schema fields needs the MCP server restarted (the session-hosted server runs the previous build), and a genuinely *animated* file to produce a real video — neither existed in this session. The plugin-side semantics were measured directly instead.

author: oresoftware
body:
## Summary

- replace raw substring privacy checks with repository-reference boundary matching
- preserve fail-closed checks for exact HTTPS, SSH, JSON, Markdown, and plain `owner/repository` identities
- avoid false positives when a private repository name is only a prefix of a longer public repository name
- use the same matcher in preflight, existing README remediation, and post-write verification
- add focused regression tests for the production prefix-collision shape

## Root cause

The 62-organization v2 rollout passed credential validation, all existing tests, and `.github` existence preflight, then stopped before any write because a private repository identity was a prefix of a legitimate public repository name. Raw substring matching treated the longer public reference as a disclosure.

## Validation

- source and regression test compile locally
- exact private HTTPS/SSH/JSON references still match
- longer public suffixes do not match
- both files remain below the repository's 400-line contract
- branch contains only the publisher change and focused regression suite

## Rollout

After CI passes and this PR is merged, start a fresh bounded issue #615 challenge and require all 62 organizations to be verified before declaring completion.

Relates to #615, follows #1229 and #1241.

author: oyatubacarl
body:
## What changed

- Adds a source-only snapshot of the committed local `main` state.
- Removes Git-tracked video, audio, virtual environments, downloaded models and dictionaries, temporary renders, local backups, and generated deployment output.
- Adds stronger `.gitignore` rules and `GIT_STORAGE_POLICY.md` to prevent the repository from growing through generated binaries again.
- Keeps application source, lesson data, scripts, documentation, and canonical images.

## Why

The local `main` had advanced 1,888 commits beyond GitHub and those commits introduced about 12.27 GiB of raw blob data, including about 6.16 GiB of media and two virtual-environment dictionary files over 100 MB. The existing history could not be pushed safely as-is.

This branch starts from the existing GitHub `main` and condenses the committed local result into one reviewable source-only commit.

## Safety and impact

- The original local history is preserved in `backup/local-main-before-github-sync-20260809`.
- Production files in the local working directory were not deleted.
- Existing uncommitted work was not staged or included.
- Media remains in its canonical local production folders and published services; this PR only removes it from Git tracking.

## Validation

- Source-only tree: 3,651 files, about 0.40 GiB.
- New objects relative to GitHub `main`: 3,185 blobs, about 645 MiB raw.
- Files over 100 MB: 0.
- Forbidden media/model/archive extensions: 0.
- Common private-key and token signatures: 0.
- Canonical blobs match committed local `main` for:
  - `index.html`
  - `taco_course_mockup/app.html`
  - `taco_beat/index.html`
  - `vocab_sources/app.html`
  - `gasflare_minimal/gas/コード.js`
- Git connectivity check passed.
- Push dry-run passed before publication.

## Follow-up

Merge only after reviewing the large source snapshot. Before realigning the active local `main` with the merged GitHub branch, preserve or commit the current mixed working-tree changes.

author: chrismichaelps
body:
## Summary

- add immutable dimensioned cost entries, workspace price tables, rebuildable CAS rollups, and subtree budgets
- enforce budgets at work entry and sandbox provisioning boundaries, with sandbox lifetime metering
- expose signed cost reporting, rollup reads, budget grants, and workspace pricing over typed REST/OpenAPI routes
- add `budget.granted` and `budget.exhausted` events plus `budget_exhausted` and `unpriced_model` protocol errors
- accept ADR-0030 and update the public architecture, changelog, and README
- complete the existing event replay filter tightening by rejecting unknown event types

## Why

ACP could coordinate work but could not attribute or bound the resources that work consumed. Raw usage facts now remain durable and independently priceable, while derived subtree rollups make admission checks bounded by spawn depth instead of subtree size.

## Impact

Operators can set workspace pricing and per-work budgets. A budget on a parent bounds its descendants. Claims, transitions into running, and sandbox provisioning fail with `budget_exhausted` once any enclosing limit is consumed; already-running work is never interrupted. Attested cost reports require a `cost.report` worker assertion.

## Validation

- 161 test files passed; 1,042 tests passed and 17 existing tests skipped
- TypeScript typecheck, ESLint, tracked-file Prettier, file-size, environment-example, route-inventory, and OpenAPI drift gates passed
- production Docker self-dogfood passed the recovery quickstart, SQLite/Postgres backup and restore, two-replica HA, SQLite edge, and HA edge scenarios

author: zyron249
body:
Closes #139.

## Security rationale
Validator anti-double-sign safety must survive ambiguous append/fsync/close outcomes. Previously an I/O failure could escape before the in-memory reservation was installed, leaving the same running process able to attempt a conflicting choice for the same `(height, round)`.

This change fail-stops the `SigningJournal` instance after any reservation persistence uncertainty. Only restart/replay can re-enter signing. No consensus rule or signature primitive changes.

## Adversarial/regression evidence
- Injected failure immediately after append: current journal rejects every later signing reservation.
- Injected failure immediately after fsync: current journal fails closed; restart reloads the durable first choice and rejects a conflicting one.
- Existing restart double-sign tests remain intact.
- Local full Node suite: **166/166 passed**.
- Typecheck: passed.
- `npm audit --audit-level=high`: **0 vulnerabilities**.
- Independent Python light-client suite: **11/11 passed** using the hash-pinned `coincurve==21.0.0` wheel.

## Remaining risk
Real power-loss/ENOSPC and HSM/remote-signer failure drills on release hardware remain pre-mainnet operational gates. This PR specifically closes the in-process ambiguity window; it does not claim those external gates are complete.

author: raysyhuang
body:
## The bug, found by verifying the live deploy

After #59 deployed, the **first** open of the live site showed the *previous* shell — no pull-to-refresh element, no pipeline section, old hero text. Only the **second** load showed the new one.

```
load 1: ptrPresent=false  funnelRows=0
load 2: ptrPresent=true   funnelRows=4
```

The service worker was doing exactly what I wrote it to do — cache-first shell with background refresh — and that behaviour is wrong for this app.

## Why it matters more than it looks

For a dashboard opened once each morning from an iOS home screen, a cache-first document means **every deploy costs one stale session**. And that stale session is precisely when you'd be checking whether the deploy landed — in this case you'd have opened it looking for the pull-to-refresh you just asked for, and not found it.

## Fix

Navigations go **network-first with cache fallback**, matching `data.json`. Offline still works — a failed fetch falls back to the cached `index.html`.

Sub-resources stay cache-first, which is correct: css/js are versioned by `?v=`, so a fresh document always requests the right ones and a stale asset can never be served against a new document.

## Caveat, stated plainly

This takes effect from the **next** deploy onward. The currently-installed v14 worker will still serve one cache-first document before v15 takes over — inherent to fixing a service worker with a service worker. So expect one more stale first-open, then never again.

author: sringram96
body:
## The encounter

The Gnawing no longer stands at the end of the hall trading blows. It holds one of three **reaches** — `far`, `mid`, `close` — and **every score it survives brings it one nearer**. There is nothing past `close`, so a thing at `close` that survives your hand arrives, and arriving ends the run.

```
far ──score, survived──▶ mid ──score, survived──▶ close ──score, survived──▶ dead
 └──────────────── score, killed: it never moves ────────────────┘
```

The fight is a count the player reads off the picture rather than a health bar: three attacks, and the third had better kill it. The count is never printed — the thing is unmistakably larger every turn, and the intent at each reach says what the next step means, ending at `close` with the plain statement that this is the last turn there is.

## State owns the distance

`CombatState.approach` is seeded by `beginCombat` and moved only by the reducer. `resolve()` decides in one pass — before a frame is drawn — how far it moved, whether it arrived, and whether that killed you. `reached` is terminal, and nothing subtracts: contact is not a large blow that happens to equal your health. A dead enemy never advances, which is the only reason killing it at `close` is survivable.

`REDUCE → SAVE → PRESENT` is intact. `app.ts` derives what to play from the two authoritative states alone; no rule is duplicated in a timer, a callback or a CSS class.

## Presentation

`SCORE` grows a strike and an answer:

```
0    the chosen dice confirm
190  relics that contributed
330  marked faces
395  the arm draws back
440  and goes in
480  full extension — bright frame, damage number and frame-kick together
580  rest
700  an uncomfortable pause, then it gathers itself
772  hard cut to the next authored reach
790–1050  (contact only) three discrete enlargements, held
```

Nothing interpolates between reaches. Idle motion is one pixel on an interval that divides evenly into nothing. `settle()` mid-sequence lands on the authoritative final state; `prefers-reduced-motion` skips straight to it.

Every stable condition is renderable from the save — reloading after `far → mid` paints `mid`, and reloading after contact paints the thing on top of you. Only `.struck`, `.gathering` and `.settling` are transient.

## Tuning

64 HP, and **no damage at all on the way in** — it cannot bite you from down the hall. A first-timer wins 91% of the time and 83% of them watch it move at least once; 10% are reached.

Two run-level gates are re-based and one is added. The first fight used to take 18–24 HP off every run on the way past and the boss inherited that; it now costs nothing unless it costs everything, so a first-timer reaches the fork nearly whole. The gap between the stair and the deep way is now asserted directly, so the fork keeps its meaning under any future retuning.

## Art

**Not authored here, and not authorable here** — `CLAUDE.md` § *No art in the polish sweep* is still in force. The encounter runs on the existing `gnawing` sprite staged at the three reaches, which is mechanically complete but does not look authored at `close`.

The four plates it wants are specified in `docs/art-reference/masters/crawling-one/BRIEF.md` and recorded under `## HUMAN ART REQUIRED`. `npm run art` builds them the moment they land and prints a placement line per pose; integration is five steps and no new code. The supplied mock-ups are kept in `supplied/` as the look to hit.

## Gates

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm test` | 119 passed (was 96) |
| `npx playwright test` | 89 passed (was 78) |
| `npm run balance` | all gates green |
| `npm run build` | 45.5 kB js / 14.5 kB css |
| `npm run art` | no-op; runtime art unchanged at 2.44 MB |

New: `test/unit/approach.test.ts` (the rule), `test/browser/approach.spec.ts` (the picture agrees with it — the ladder grows, the reach survives a reload, the strike reads before the advance, contact is discrete, reduced motion lands on the same state).

Retargeted rather than weakened: assertions about *taking a blow* moved from the Gnawing to the Marrow, which still throws one.

author: ofuhrer
body:
Adds a checksum-pinned regional analysis campaign over the canonical compact REA archive.

The workflow builds reviewed GeoJSON/grid masks, independently cross-checks compact GRIB messages against sealed receipts and full-domain hourly Parquet evidence, publishes regional hourly counts, and reduces freezing-rain, freezing-drizzle, and combined icy-liquid event catalogues.

Local validation: compilation, Ruff, mypy, 152 tests with 79.62% coverage, benchmark, diff checks, and wheel inspection. The workstation-global pip check retains known unrelated package conflicts; the clean Balfrin candidate environment reports no broken requirements.

Balfrin acceptance: one-month run and byte-identical restart passed; all 248 months and 181,152 hours passed; full array wall interval 10 minutes 9 seconds; reducer 24 seconds; independent full-output verification 2 minutes 54 seconds. The permanent regional products are 34.3 MB and all 24 independent reconstruction checks pass.

Acceptance evidence is recorded in docs/acceptance/2026-08-09-regional-analysis.md.

body:
## Summary

- Port the Puppeteer v25.5.0 PWA APIs together with the CDP pipe transport required to exercise them.
- Forward connection headers, avoid unnecessary user-agent overrides, track dialogs handled by other CDP connections, and tolerate OOPIF teardown during frame fan-out.
- Align the default Chrome feature flags and WebMCP behavior with Chrome 151.
- Refresh the generated Puppeteer API reference and API coverage documentation to v25.5.0.

The upstream tests were translated to RSpec with their names and ordering preserved. The PWA fixtures are byte-identical to the upstream assets. Detached text visibility coverage was already present on `main`, so it was not duplicated.

Closes #405.

## Validation

- Issue #405 related suites: 137 examples, 0 failures
- `spec/integration/oopif_spec.rb`: 17 examples, 0 failures
- `Page#expose_function`: 14 examples, 0 failures, 3 existing pending examples
- RuboCop on all 28 changed Ruby files: 0 offenses
- `bundle exec rake rbs && bundle exec steep check`: no type errors
- Regenerated API JSON matches the upstream Puppeteer v25.5.0 artifact exactly
- Tested with Chrome 151.0.7922.77

The full suite was also exercised (1,296 examples). Of the 11 failures observed, seven reproduced unchanged at the base commit with Chrome 151, two were environment/external-site dependent, and one extension test passed when rerun alone. The single regression introduced by this branch was fixed and its related suites were rerun successfully.

author: brocla
body:
## Why

Compressing `Why I Believe Flyer.pdf` reported **0.00% for every step**, with nothing in the panel explaining it. Four of the five steps genuinely had nothing to do (no XMP, no `/Metadata`, no `/Thumb`, no JavaScript, ~80-byte content streams). The fifth — image downsampling — did have an opinion, but it was invisible.

`plan_one` has three outcomes and the report only carried two:

| Outcome | Reported as |
|---|---|
| `Replace` | bytes saved in the results table |
| `Skip(reason)` | the skipped-images notice |
| `Leave` | *(nothing)* |

`Leave` means "this image is already at or below the target DPI, so downsampling it would only lose quality." That's the step working correctly, but for an image-only PDF at a sensible resolution it makes the whole panel read as a broken tool.

## What

- `OptimizationReport` gains `images_at_target: u32`, tallied from `PlanResult::Leave`.
- Kept **separate** from `skipped_images` on purpose: "nothing to do" and "we couldn't handle this" are different signals, and merging them would turn reassurance into an apparent limitation.
- The panel surfaces the count and names the lever that would change it — lowering the target DPI. Not hypothetical: this file at `target_dpi 50` compresses **79.63%** (2,949,723 → 600,857 bytes).
- The notice quotes the DPI the report was produced at, not the live slider value, since the slider stays interactive after a run.

## Tests

- `recompress_images_leaves_low_dpi_image_untouched` now asserts `at_target == 1` alongside the existing "not a skip, byte-for-byte identical" assertions.
- Two frontend tests: the notice renders with its count and its remedy, and it keeps quoting the run's DPI after the slider moves.
- `cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1`: 248 passed. `npm test`: 233 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: sethbacon
body:
## Why

`terraform-suite-ui` has run zizmor for a while and reports **zero** findings. Pointed at the rest of the suite it reported **141, eighteen of them High**. The one repo with the linter is the one with nothing to find — that gap is the whole argument.

It earned its keep on the first run: it caught **eight** `actions/checkout` calls in the new `signature-replay` workflow persisting a cross-repo PAT into `.git/config`, inside a job that uploads an artifact.

## Result: 141 → 14, 18 High → 1

| rule | before | action |
|---|---|---|
| `artipacked` | 81 | `persist-credentials: false` where the job never writes to git |
| `template-injection` | 34 | step outputs moved out of `run:` into `env:` |
| `unpinned-uses` | 3 (High) | SHA-pinned |
| others zizmor could fix safely | — | applied |

## The part that would have broken things

**`--fix=safe` applied nothing.** zizmor classes every `artipacked` fix as *unsafe*, because it cannot know whether a later step needs the credential.

Running `--fix=all` and pushing would have broken **releases, wiki sync, translations and swagger doc sync across four repos** — nine checkouts whose jobs genuinely push:

| job | why it keeps its credential |
|---|---|
| `swagger-docs-sync` | pushes regenerated docs to the PR head |
| `wiki-sync` (×2) | pushes the wiki |
| `translate` (×2) | opens the translations PR |
| `goreleaser` / `publish-release` (×4) | publish releases |

Each is annotated inline. They were found by checking every job for git writes **before** trusting the fixer, not after it broke something.

## Accepted, not silenced

`.github/zizmor.yml` lists `github-app` on the release-please workflow, with the reason.

zizmor tips to add `permission-<name>` inputs so the App token stops inheriting blanket installation permissions. **That exact change has already been made in this suite and reverted** — the installation does not hold the permission requested, so `create-github-app-token` returns `422` and release-please stops running at all. Re-narrowing has to start from auditing what the installation actually grants.

Anything **not** in that file still fails the job, so a new finding of any kind is caught.

## Not a required check yet

What remains — `excessive-permissions`, `secrets-inherit`, one `dangerous-triggers`, one `superfluous-actions` — is a real enumerated backlog, not an accepted one. This is promoted to required once that reaches zero.

A required check that is red on day one is one everybody learns to scroll past, which is the failure this entire batch has been about.
