author: alitocodework
body:
## Problema

3 alertas 🔴 falsas en el grupo de Telegram en una sola tarde (08/08, 16:51 / 18:20 / 19:21 hora Cuba) con la plataforma respondiendo perfectamente.

## Diagnóstico (medido, no hipótesis)

- En las ventanas de alerta, **nginx no registró NI UNA conexión de los runners** — las sondas ni llegaron al servidor.
- No es fail2ban: única jail `sshd`, 0 baneados hoy.
- El `access.log` muestra la **lotería por corrida**: el runner `57.154.5.65` sondeó 22 min sin fallo, la corrida que lo reemplazó no aparece nunca en el log (gap de ~35 min = su alerta), luego `130.131.255.214` pasa, luego otro gap, luego `13.83.166.226` pasa. **El borde de Hostinger dropea la IP de ~la mitad de los runners de Azure** mientras el resto del mundo (check-host desde 6+ países, verificado hoy) llega sin problema.
- La sonda de control del 05/08 no cubre este caso: google/github sí le responden al runner bloqueado, así que el workflow concluye "servidor caído".

## Fix

Tras las 3 confirmaciones en rojo y antes de avisar, se pide **segunda opinión a check-host.net** (nodos neutrales, API pública sin key, contrato verificado hoy):

- Algún nodo recibe el 200 de la página de estado → **el bloqueado es el runner**: alerta suprimida, contada en el log de la corrida (`N suprimidos por veredicto externo`).
- Ningún nodo la ve → **caída real**: la alerta sale, ahora diciendo que está confirmada también desde fuera.
- check-host no responde o no da veredicto → **se avisa igual**: ante la duda, nunca se calla una alerta.

Validado: YAML parsea, `bash -n` limpio, y el parseo jq probado contra la respuesta real de la API (`[[1, t, "OK", "200", ip]]` por nodo).

author: gwenphalan
body:
Follow-up to #230, which pinned the lattice backdrop with a `position: fixed` layer. That fixed the
scrolling, and testing it on a real device exposed the rest.

## The requirement

`.notes/01-todo/ui.todo.md` named this as a second effect that might or might not need addressing, in
the owner's words:

> A second mobile-only effect rides along and may be part of what reads as "scrolling": a collapsing
> address bar changes `documentElement.clientHeight` mid-scroll, the `ResizeObserver` fires, and the
> vertical phase is rewritten — so the lattice shifts under the content even where the attachment is
> honored. Whether the fix has to address this too depends on what the reproduction shows.

The reproduction now exists, so this is the answer to that conditional: it does.

## Why

**This was confirmed on hardware, not reasoned.** The owner loaded #230's branch on her own iPhone
over the LAN and reported that the backdrop holds still during normal scrolling — so the fixed layer
worked — but that the lattice still jumps in exactly two situations: when Safari's address bar is
pulled back down, and on a resize.

That is `GraphBackground` reading `documentElement.clientHeight`. On iOS Safari that value tracks the
address bar, so retracting or expanding the bar fires the `ResizeObserver`, `--grid-phase-y` and
`--grid-bold-phase-y` are rewritten, and the lattice slides under stationary content.

That evidence also settles an argument that could not be settled any other way. The competing theory
was that the root's containing block is sized to the large viewport, making `clientHeight` constant
across a bar collapse and the whole effect imaginary. It is not constant. The observer fires.

**The fix removes the measurement rather than guarding it.** `GraphBackground` no longer reads
`clientHeight` and no longer writes the two Y variables; the stylesheet uses a literal `0` for the Y
term of every lattice layer.

Guarding the observer against height-only changes was the alternative, and it would have kept the
rendering pixel-identical. It was rejected because the vertical measurement has no referent to begin
with. Horizontal centering does: the shell's content column is `mx-auto max-w-[92rem]`, so the
viewport centerline *is* the content centerline, and phasing a lattice line onto it makes the grid
look deliberately placed against real content. Vertically, on a backdrop pinned to the viewport
behind a scrolling page, "a lattice line on the viewport's vertical midpoint" aligns with nothing at
all. Keeping a decorative measurement and adding a condition to stop it misbehaving leaves a guard
that reads as arbitrary to the next person; deleting it means the address bar has nothing to move.

The visible cost is a one-time shift of the lattice's Y origin — at most 20px on the fine tier and
120px on the bold one — against a grid that repeats every 40px and 240px. Not identifiable without a
before/after comparison.

## What else this removes

`graph-background.tsx`'s doc comment carried a hedge on the `clientWidth`-over-`innerWidth` choice:
the scrollbar-gutter rationale was "the design rationale, not a tested guarantee", because headless
Chromium uses overlay scrollbars and cannot reproduce it. #230's browser verification measured it in
a real headed Chromium on a Linux host with classic scrollbars — `clientWidth` 1265 against
`innerWidth` 1280, a 15px gutter, and a `position: fixed; inset: 0` probe measuring 1265, matching
the `clientWidth` basis. The hedge is no longer accurate, so it is gone.

The same comment previously justified `clientHeight` as "the *viewport* height rather than the content
height, so this fires on real viewport changes only and never thrashes against page growth." That
premise is exactly what turned out to be the bug on iOS, so the comment now records why height is
deliberately not measured.

## Scope

- `packages/ui/src/components/graph-background.tsx` — stops reading `clientHeight`, writes two
  variables instead of four. `latticePhase`/`boldLatticePhase` are unchanged.
- `packages/ui/src/styles.css` — Y term of each lattice `background-position` becomes `0`; no
  `var(--grid-*-phase-y, …)` remains.
- `packages/ui/test/graph-background.test.tsx` — Y assertions dropped, X assertions untouched, the
  viewport helper is width-only.
- `apps/web/e2e/grid-phase.spec.ts` — the Y assertion is gone; the width and bold-cell assertions
  stay, so the spec still pins that a real browser's `ResizeObserver` on `documentElement` delivers.

## Verification

- **On the owner's iPhone, against this branch**: address bar pulled back down mid-page, and a device
  rotation. The lattice holds still through both. This is the only check that tests what the change
  is for.
- **Desktop, in a real browser at 1280 wide** (`apps/web` `/` and `/about`, `apps/cflop` `/`).
  Horizontal centering measured rather than eyeballed: `--grid-phase-x: 0px`,
  `--grid-bold-phase-x: 40px` at `clientWidth: 1280`, so a fine line lands exactly on the 640px
  column centre, and the nearest bold lines sit at 520 and 760 — centre exactly mid-cell, 120px from
  each, which is the documented intent. `--grid-phase-y` and `--grid-bold-phase-y` both read empty.
  A height-only resize (900→700) left both X variables untouched; a width resize (1280→1000)
  recomputed them to 20px/140px with the same midpoint relationship at the new centre.
- **The Y-origin shift does not crop the grid awkwardly.** Zoomed on the top edge of each route: no
  bold line or row of intersection dots is clipped at the viewport top; the edge cuts cleanly through
  fine-grid cells. Frosted header and footer still read as glass with the lattice through the blur,
  and the backdrop still holds still on scroll.
- `pnpm check` 62/62 · `@unimatrix/ui` 41/41 + typecheck + prettier · `@unimatrix/web` 51/51 unit,
  9/9 smoke including the updated `grid-phase.spec.ts` · `@unimatrix/cflop` 697 unit + 6/6 smoke ·
  `check:stale-comments` 5337 comment lines across 471 files, no stale identifiers ·
  `check:coverage-drift` all 30 floors passing.

## What was not verified

Nothing was tested on Chrome for Android — the device evidence is iOS Safari only. The desktop resize
behaviour above was measured through Playwright viewport changes against the running dev server
rather than by dragging a real OS window.

author: rickcrawford
body:
`RequestEnricher` was declared in the initial commit, documented in three places, and never implemented or invoked in the entire life of the Rust tree (`git log -S` returns exactly one commit).

## Why delete rather than wire

Wiring it produces a **subtler lie than leaving it**. `enrich` returns `PluginResult<()>`, so it has no in-band output at all; its only output channel is a type-erased `ctx` whose concrete type is `RequestContext`, which lives in an internal, unpublished crate. An out-of-tree implementor cannot name the type it would need to downcast to, so the only legal thing it can do with `ctx` is ignore it. That is one grade worse than `AuthProvider`'s `&mut ()`, because at least that trait has a return value.

Every sibling has real output: `ActionHandler` returns `ActionOutcome` and gets `&mut Request`, `AuthProvider` returns `AuthDecision`, `PolicyEnforcer` returns `PolicyDecision`, `TransformHandler` gets `&mut BytesMut` plus a typed context.

**The niche is already served properly.** `IdentityResolverHook`, `MlClassifierHook`, and `AnomalyDetectorHook` are dispatched in `request_phase`, live in the same public crate, run early and annotate, and take **typed** public context views (`RequestContextView`, `RequestSnapshotView`) returning typed verdicts. That is the shipped answer to the GeoIP and UA-parsing use case; a second type-erased version would be strictly worse.

And there was no dispatch point to wire into: no config surface (zero `enricher` keys in any YAML or JSON, and `BundleHookKind` has no variant), and no typed registration channel (`EnricherPluginRegistration` does not exist).

## What went with it

`PluginKind::Enricher`, the trait's only registration slot. Left in place, an operator could submit an enricher registration, watch it appear in `/metrics` as `kind=enricher` and in the extension inventory, and never have it load. `ExtensionHookKind::Enricher` follows, having become unconstructible.

## The test is a compile-time ratchet

`every_plugin_kind_has_a_typed_build_path` walks every `PluginKind` through an **exhaustive match**, so it fails pre-fix as a compile error rather than a runtime assertion. A runtime formulation cannot both enumerate the variants and detect a missing one; this way a sixth kind cannot be added later without a typed channel.

## Also in here

It now matches. `docs/extension-bundles.md` added to the `docs/README.md` index, where it was missing despite being the most important extensibility doc. And a dangling promise in `request_phase.rs` telling operators they could override `canonical_url` "from a request enricher upstream" is gone, since nothing could ever have done that.

author: sethbacon
body:
## Why

`terraform-suite-ui` has run zizmor for a while and reports **zero** findings. Pointed at the rest of the suite it reported **141, eighteen of them High**. The one repo with the linter is the one with nothing to find — that gap is the whole argument.

It earned its keep on the first run: it caught **eight** `actions/checkout` calls in the new `signature-replay` workflow persisting a cross-repo PAT into `.git/config`, inside a job that uploads an artifact.

## Result: 141 → 14, 18 High → 1

| rule | before | action |
|---|---|---|
| `artipacked` | 81 | `persist-credentials: false` where the job never writes to git |
| `template-injection` | 34 | step outputs moved out of `run:` into `env:` |
| `unpinned-uses` | 3 (High) | SHA-pinned |
| others zizmor could fix safely | — | applied |

## The part that would have broken things

**`--fix=safe` applied nothing.** zizmor classes every `artipacked` fix as *unsafe*, because it cannot know whether a later step needs the credential.

Running `--fix=all` and pushing would have broken **releases, wiki sync, translations and swagger doc sync across four repos** — nine checkouts whose jobs genuinely push:

| job | why it keeps its credential |
|---|---|
| `swagger-docs-sync` | pushes regenerated docs to the PR head |
| `wiki-sync` (×2) | pushes the wiki |
| `translate` (×2) | opens the translations PR |
| `goreleaser` / `publish-release` (×4) | publish releases |

Each is annotated inline. They were found by checking every job for git writes **before** trusting the fixer, not after it broke something.

## Accepted, not silenced

`.github/zizmor.yml` lists `github-app` on the release-please workflow, with the reason.

zizmor tips to add `permission-<name>` inputs so the App token stops inheriting blanket installation permissions. **That exact change has already been made in this suite and reverted** — the installation does not hold the permission requested, so `create-github-app-token` returns `422` and release-please stops running at all. Re-narrowing has to start from auditing what the installation actually grants.

Anything **not** in that file still fails the job, so a new finding of any kind is caught.

## Not a required check yet

What remains — `excessive-permissions`, `secrets-inherit`, one `dangerous-triggers`, one `superfluous-actions` — is a real enumerated backlog, not an accepted one. This is promoted to required once that reaches zero.

A required check that is red on day one is one everybody learns to scroll past, which is the failure this entire batch has been about.

author: juliantellez
body:
**What.** The memory file read back recognises the skills mark in every file and drops what sits under it, a level whose stored context already carries a swept index is cleaned the next time it renders, and a note appended to the end of the workspace memory file is kept as workspace context instead of being filed under the index's mark and dropped.

**Why.** A build before the index moved wrote it into the session's own memory file. Read back by a later build that only knew the mark in the outer file, the whole index was swept into session context, stored as though the operator had typed it, and rendered again on every turn from then on, permanently. Found in the 9 August architectural review.

Three scenarios in `features/skills.feature`, each mutation checked red then green: the old ordering fails the appended note scenario, removing the healing fails the swept context scenario.

Closes #190

The realtime socket's own vocabulary was rendered straight to the user, and `closed` was coloured with `--destructive`.

So a socket that had simply not connected yet announced itself **in red** beside "Recent activity", and again as a red value under "Live updates" — a resting state dressed as a failure, on the first screen anyone opening a workspace sees. For someone evaluating the product, that reads as "this thing is broken."

The feed is still correct when the socket is down; it just stops updating on its own. That's a caution at most, so `closed` drops to muted and the three states get words instead of transport terms:

| socket | shown |
|---|---|
| `open` | live |
| `connecting` | connecting |
| `closed` | not live |

Also: environment rows showed three bare numbers (`2 · 1 · 1`) whose meaning lived in a `title` attribute. Hover text is invisible on a dashboard, so the columns get a label once, in the box-score idiom the rest of the surface already uses.

author: arsfeld
body:
Third slice of Mydia Server, following #373 (skeleton and contract gate) and #374 (scan and browse). The Flutter player can now play a real file from Mydia Server at original quality, with subtitles.

Slice 3 was split in two. This is **3a**: streaming candidates, byte serving, remux, subtitles. **3b** is HLS sessions, quality caps and start position.

## Why playback next, and how much of it this delivers

The original design ordered a throwaway spike first, to answer the streaming unknowns before crate boundaries hardened. That spike never happened, which left streaming the largest unproven part of the design.

Reading `player_screen.dart:840-853`, the player takes the direct path when the first streaming candidate is `DIRECT_PLAY`, `REMUX` or `HLS_COPY` and the quality rung is Original. Per `candidates.ex:101-127`, the first candidate is one of those three in every branch except a transcode-needing codec with no variant string. So after this slice essentially every file in a library plays at original quality. Quality selection and that residual case are 3b.

## What landed

- **`mydia-streaming`**, a new crate: codec compatibility, RFC 6381 codec strings, the ordered candidate list, the fMP4 remux pipe, and subtitle conversion. All ported from Elixir modules that already had test oracles.
- **`mydia-library`** gains file ranking and sidecar subtitle discovery.
- **`mydia-db`** gains an `external_subtitles` table.
- **`mydia-api`** resolves `streamingCandidates` and the `MediaFile` playback fields.
- **`mydia-server`** serves bytes under `/api/v1/stream/...` with HTTP range support, and subtitles under `/api/player/v1/subtitles/...`.

The SDL contract gate stayed green throughout, so the schema never drifted.

## Two auth transports

`player_screen.dart:893-916` sends different things depending on pairing mode: password mode sets an `Authorization` header with an access token, claim-code mode appends `?token=` with a media token. Both are accepted, from either transport. Accepting only one would have broken half the installs while passing every unit test.

## A bug this surfaced in the Elixir server

`lib/mydia/subtitles/extractor.ex:251-253` passes the requested subtitle format straight to ffmpeg's `-f`, so a VTT request becomes `-f vtt`. ffmpeg only knows `webvtt`:

```
Requested output format 'vtt' is not known
```

The player's `MediaFileFragment` always requests `url(format: VTT)`, so embedded subtitle extraction fails on every install today. Not caused by this PR and not fixed here; it wants its own change against the Elixir app.

## Deliberate divergences from the Elixir server

None touch the GraphQL surface, so slice 4's conformance suite stays exact. Recorded here because that suite is built separately and a red assertion there would otherwise look like a bug.

| Divergence | Elixir | Mydia Server | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sidecar subtitles | Not discovered at all | Found during the scan | Near-universal in self-hosted libraries. Seed the conformance corpus without sidecars |
| VTT muxer | `-f vtt`, which ffmpeg rejects | `-f webvtt` | See above |
| External subtitle conversion | Serves the file unchanged, labelled with the requested content type | Converts to the requested format | Elixir hands back SRT bytes under `text/vtt` |
| Track belonging to another file | 403 | 404 | 403 confirms the track exists |

## Testing

Ported logic is table-driven against the existing Elixir tests. Media is synthesized with ffmpeg `testsrc` at test time; no binary fixtures. Remux output is verified by probing it rather than by exit code, since ffmpeg exits 0 on plenty of output nobody can play. The ffmpeg child is proven dead by pid after its stream drops.

`server/crates/server/tests/playback.rs` reads `player/lib/graphql/fragments/media_file_fragment.graphql` off disk and runs it against the server, so editing the player's fragment fails this suite rather than drifting silently.

Full gate green: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`.

## Still outstanding

The slice is not finished until someone points the real Flutter player at Mydia Server and plays a file, including a seek and a subtitle track. Synthesized `testsrc` media does not substitute for that, and it is the step that actually retires the streaming risk.

author: benzn-tech
body:
`tests/unit/test_multichannel_probe.py` imports numpy through `scripts/multichannel_probe.py`. CI installs `psycopg`, `pgvector`, `PyJWT`, `boto3` and `pytest` — **not numpy**. The module fails to *import*, so pytest reports a collection error and **the whole suite is red**.

It passed locally because the local harness runs `uv run --with numpy`, which quietly supplied a dependency CI does not have.

## Verified against CI's actual dependency set, not the convenience harness

```
without numpy:  ERROR tests/unit/test_multichannel_probe.py
                Interrupted: 1 error during collection
with numpy:     2251 passed, 1 skipped
```

## Install rather than skip

`pytest.importorskip` would have turned CI green without running the tests. **A test that is skipped in CI is decorative** — it would have gone on "passing" while the thing it guards was broken. numpy is a genuine dependency of the script; the deployed lambdas get it from the VAD layer and are unaffected.

## My mistake made it worse

**#333, #334 and #335 were all merged while showing `MERGEABLE/UNSTABLE`** — which is exactly "checks are failing but the merge is allowed". Earlier in this same session I waited for `CLEAN` before merging and should have kept doing that.

**`UNSTABLE` is not a yellow light.**

author: cjkjellander
body:
Adds continuous capture-and-decode, printing each decode to stdout as it
arrives, and puts it under supervision.

```
sh0tcaller_sup          one_for_one, intensity 3    (was one_for_all/0)
└── sh0tcaller_ft8_sup  simple_one_for_one — empty at rest
    └── sh0tcaller_ft8_monitor   started on demand, transient
```

```erlang
sh0tcaller_ft8_sup:start_monitor().     %% or start_monitor(Dir)
sh0tcaller_ft8_sup:stop_monitor().
```

```
   UTC   dB    DT    Hz  message
224800  -14   0.4  1508  CQ EA8DNB IL18 a1
224800   -6   0.6  1701  DL1UDO PV8AJ FJ92
224815   -8  -0.4   512  CR5VP IU8QTW JN70
224815  -10   0.1  1640  PV8AJ EC5M IM98
```

## Design

**The monitor process does no work itself.** Capturing blocks for a whole
15 second cycle and decoding takes seconds more, so a linked capturer
loops over cycles and hands back paths, and each decode runs in its own
process. The server only routes results and prints, so it stays
responsive, no cycle is missed while a decode is in flight, and a decoder
crash is reported rather than fatal.

**`ft8_sup` is empty at rest by design.** Starting the application must
not start capturing — that would seize the radio from anything else using
it, including the test suite, which starts the application. Monitoring is
an explicit action.

**The top supervisor's generated defaults are gone.** `one_for_all` with
`intensity => 0` meant any child crash brought the whole application
down; it now restarts the failing subtree.

## Cycle alignment fix

A capture ends exactly on the next cycle boundary, so waiting for "the
next" boundary afterwards skipped a cycle every time — a 50 second run
produced one cycle instead of three. A cycle that has only just begun is
now joined and the remainder recorded, and trimming rather than
overrunning keeps the following capture on the boundary so the reopen
latency cannot accumulate.

Verified rather than assumed: jt9 decodes a 40 ms-short file identically
to the full-length one (12 decodes either way). Consecutive cycles are
now captured back to back.

## Tests

12 passing. The new `sh0tcaller_ft8_SUITE` needs no radio and covers the
two places where a silent mistake is expensive: the WSJT-X filename
convention, where getting it wrong makes jt9 report every decode as
`000000`, and the jt9 output parser, where dropping lines is
indistinguishable from a quiet band. `sh0tcaller_SUITE` gains the
supervision tree assertions; the monitor lifecycle case skips rather than
fails where no radio is attached.

Verified on Erlang/OTP 29.0.5 against a Burr-Brown PCM2901 USB codec.

author: say828
body:
## 요약

S6 확률과 통계의 **02단원 확률변수와 분포(126~131강)**를 작성합니다.

| 강의 | 제목 | 구조 |
|---|---|---|
| 126 | 확률변수와 분포함수 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 127 | 베르누이와 이항분포 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 128 | 포아송분포와 기하분포 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 129 | 연속확률변수와 확률밀도 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 130 | 정규분포 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 131 | 지수분포와 감마분포 | 5 / 15 / 13 / 6 |
| 문제집 | 02. 확률변수와 분포 | 48문항 |

## 121강에서 남긴 숙제를 갚았습니다

121강 문제 5에서 "한 점의 확률은 0인데 구간은 양수"라는 구조를 던져 놓고 넘어갔습니다. 129강 문제 1이 그 답입니다.

| $h$ | $P(a<X\le a+h)$ | 그 값 $/h$ |
|---|---|---|
| $10^{-2}$ | 0.003321975301 | 0.33219753 |
| $10^{-4}$ | 0.000033467014 | 0.33467014 |
| $10^{-8}$ | 0.000000003347 | 0.33469524 |

왼쪽은 0으로 가는데 오른쪽은 수렴합니다. 37강에서 도함수를 정의할 때와 같은 수법입니다.

## 여섯 분포를 하나의 그림으로

흩어진 목록이 아니라 세 갈래가 모두 감마에서 만나도록 배치했습니다.

- 베르누이 → 이항 → 포아송 → 지수 → 감마
- 베르누이 → 기하 → 음이항 → 감마
- 이항 → 정규 → 카이제곱 → 감마

131강 문제 4에서 `Gamma(1/2, 1/2)`의 밀도가 129강 심화 3에서 $Z^2$의 밀도로 유도한 값과 소수점 여덟 자리까지 일치하는 것을 확인합니다. $\Gamma(1/2)=\sqrt\pi$가 그 일치를 만듭니다.

## 앞 과목 도구가 실제로 쓰인 자리

| 도구 | 어느 강의 | 쓰인 곳 |
|---|---|---|
| 이항정리 (20강) | 127 정규화, 128 가법성 |
| 지수급수 (54강) | 128 포아송 정규화 |
| 미적분학의 기본정리 (49강) | 129 $F$와 $f$ |
| 부분적분 (50강) | 131 감마함수 재귀 |
| 극좌표 변환 (104강) | 130 가우스 적분 |
| 변수변환 야코비 (105강) | 129 변환 공식 |
| 라그랑주 승수법 (113강) | 130 최대 엔트로피 |

## 검산에서 잡아 고친 것

- **127강 문제 4**: `argmax`가 3, 공식 $\lfloor(n+1)p\rfloor$가 4를 줘 불일치. $n=7,p=0.5$는 $(n+1)p$가 정수라 **공동 최빈**이었고 $P(X{=}3)$과 $P(X{=}4)$의 차이가 정확히 0이었습니다. 공식의 예외를 그대로 교재로 삼았습니다.
- **127강 문제 5**: 연속성 보정이 중심($k{=}25$)에서 340배 좋아지지만 **꼬리($k{=}20$)에서는 오히려 나빠집니다**. 보정 전후 오차를 나란히 놓았습니다.
- **128강**: $n{=}3,\lambda{=}3$이면 $p{=}1$이 되어 예외 발생. "한 조각에 2회 이상" 계산은 항상 0을 내던 죽은 코드였고, 제대로 세우니 기대 조각 수가 **0.369 → 0.00045로 $1/n$ 감소**하는 것이 드러나 포아송 극한의 엔진을 수치가 직접 설명하게 됐습니다.
- **131강**: 합성곱 누적 로직이 잘못돼 $r{=}5$에서 2배 틀렸습니다. 또 $\Gamma(1/2)$를 격자로 적분하면 $t^{-1/2}$ 특이점 때문에 오차가 $3.0\times10^{-3}$이었고, 그게 문제 4의 카이제곱 대조까지 어긋나게 했습니다. 치환 $t=u^2$으로 특이점을 없애니 오차가 $2.2\times10^{-16}$이 됐고 **열세 자릿수 개선**을 그대로 교재로 실었습니다.

## 검증

- verify.py: 8문서 전부 통과. 강의 6개 모두 `(5, 15, 13, 6)`, 문제집 48문항, 규약 위반 0
- cmpout.py: 코드 검산 출력과 주석 완전 일치 (126강 59줄, 127강 56줄, 128강 58줄, 129강 52줄, 130강 48줄, 131강 68줄)
- pipescan.py 0건, 엠대쉬 0건
- 문제 유형 지도 준수: 126~131강 모두 계유해

## 인덱스 갱신

- `확률과 통계/index.md`: 집필 현황, 02단원 링크, Page Tree
- `Lecture/index.md`: 과목 줄 "121~131강 집필", Page Tree
- `00. 학습 순서와 커리큘럼/index.md`: 진행 문장과 과목별 표

author: joshrandall8478
body:
The three C++ patches in `home/joshr/niri/` are unified diffs against
particular files at a particular release. That release was a fact this
repository depended on and had no way to state: `pkgs.noctalia` followed
nixpkgs, so a bump would have arrived as a failed `patchPhase` in the middle of
some unrelated `nix flake update`. Loud and before activation — but it blocks
the whole rebuild, and the fix is a patch rebase, which is not the errand
anyone was on.

## The change

`noctalia.nix` now overrides `src` on the patched derivation, and two lines at
the top of its `let` are the only place this repo names a version:

```nix
noctaliaVersion = "5.0.0-beta.7";
noctaliaHash = "sha256-9RlJNIy2DFVm9SB2vwGEBsbHc1r3dIB+K+b+nd6Bdho=";
```

Overriding `version` alone would not have held. nixpkgs builds the tag as
`"v${finalAttrs.version}"` but the `hash` beside it is a literal, so the next
package bump would have paired our tag with the new release's hash. Replacing
`src` outright is what makes the pin real. `tag` rather than `rev` matches
upstream's packaging; the hash is what actually pins the content, so a moved
tag fails loudly instead of quietly building something else. Both values are
nixpkgs' own for this release.

## Why this release is worth pinning to

v5 is a beta shipping roughly weekly — beta1 through beta.7 landed across five
weeks. One commit already on upstream `main`, the tree-wide uppercasing of
float literal suffixes (`1.5f` → `1.5F`), is on its own enough to break two of
the three patches:

| patch | line it deletes | upstream `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `noctalia-clock-shadow-offset.patch` | `constexpr float kShadowOffset = 1.5f;` | `… = 1.5F;` |
| `noctalia-lock-transition.patch` | `const float w = cardWidth(s, orientation) + innerPadX * 2.0f;` | `… * 2.0F;` |
| `noctalia-user-media.patch` | no float literals in any removal line | anchors intact |

A deletion line has to match character for character, where context lines get
some fuzz — so those two fail the moment a release carrying that commit reaches
nixpkgs.

## Only the patched side is pinned

`noctaliaSourcePatches = false` exists to stay on the binary cache and skip
compiling a Qt/C++ project. Overriding `src` there would defeat exactly that
and cost `laptop-niri` a local build for a version it has no patches to
protect.

The cost of the asymmetry is that the two hosts can drift onto different
releases, and `noctalia config validate` is what reports it: it runs against
whichever package the host selected, so a generated key that the laptop's newer
stock package has renamed fails the laptop's build. That is the prompt to move
the pin, not a reason to remove it.

Note this pins the *source*, not the recipe — `buildInputs`, meson flags and
the wrapper still come from nixpkgs. That keeps their packaging fixes, and is
also why the gap is not meant to sit here for a year.

## Moving it later

Change the version, set the hash to `lib.fakeHash`, build once, copy the hash
out of the error — then rebase the patches, which is the real work.
`noctalia-lock-transition.patch` is 21 hunks across six files in
`src/shell/lockscreen` and `src/shell/osd`, both of which upstream changes
weekly.

## Docs

`MANUAL.md` gains a **The version pin** subsection under "The shell: waybar or
noctalia" covering all of the above, and the version table above it now says
that its `pkgs.noctalia` row is nixpkgs' version rather than this repo's. No
table-of-contents change — that file does not list `####` headings.

## Testing

`nix` is not available in this container, so **this has not been evaluated or
built**. `nixos-rebuild build --flake .#gamestation-niri` is the real check; if
the hash is wrong it fails immediately and prints the correct one.

What was checked instead: the hash and version were read from nixpkgs'
`pkgs/by-name/no/noctalia/package.nix` three times over independent URLs (the
locked rev, its full-length form, and `master`) and all three agree — nixpkgs
`master` is still on beta.7, so this lands before the break rather than after.
The patch/upstream comparisons in the table above are line-by-line reads of the
current upstream sources. The edited `.nix` file was checked for balanced
strings, brackets and interpolations with a small Nix lexer verified against
deliberately broken copies; that is structural, not a parse.

FEATURE: `Nembra Capture / first private ES80 truth`
LANE: adversarial Final GO durable-publication truth
PARENT: #1508 exact `48849a76861713eef2fafa92c70378a07617e842`
HEAD: `e5075161442df70ac90e4dcb22057f9b62115d33`
STATUS: DRAFT / EXPECTED-RED / tooling-only / PHYSICAL NO-GO

This child mechanizes blocking review `4890492295` without touching flagship #833 or any app/BLE path.

## Exact defect reproduced
#1508 correctly stages + fsyncs + byte-verifies before an atomic no-replace rename. But after `publisher(staging, output)` succeeds it marks the transaction published, clears the staging reference, then performs parent-directory fsync and final-byte verification. Any exception in those post-rename steps returns NO-GO while leaving the authoritative final path present with bytes that already say `decision: GO`.

The new focused regression injects a failure on the **second** `os.fsync` call (the parent-directory fsync after the file has already been renamed) and requires:
- the invocation raises/fails;
- `FinalGO.json` is absent after failure;
- no staging residue remains.

The current #1508 implementation is expected to fail that assertion because it only unlinks the staging path when `published == false`.

## Required green recovery
A green successor must retract the authoritative destination after a post-rename failure when it can prove the destination is still the exact file it published, fsync that removal when possible, and treat any unprovable cleanup as an explicit ambiguous/quarantined state that cannot be consumed as Final GO. Do not reduce this to caller exit-code discipline: the durable artifact itself must not survive a failed publication transaction while self-describing as `decision: GO`.

No accepted subject binding, candidate/signing logic, install handoff, ResearchAdmission, BLE policy, or physical procedure is changed by this expected-red child. No Xcode job is required for this one-file adversarial test.

**FIRST REAL ES80 CAPTURE REMAINS NO-GO / DO NOT RUN.**

Opens Gate C10 (compiler release qualification) and lands its first two packets.

## What is here

| Commit | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `ff5be86` | The C10 execution plan, written against `f12ecec` |
| `100d0f7` | Owner rulings OD-1…OD-6 + three methodological amendments |
| `f7e2f0c` | **C10-0** opening inventory and qualification freeze |
| `7cfa59e` | **C10-P** — DEV-213 repaired and closed |

## The sequencing question the plan opened with

The position line read as *"C9 Part B blocks C10"*. The roadmap does not say that anywhere: §4.5
admits "blocked on second-artifact evidence" as one of three permitted explicit statuses, WP-C10.7
requires C0–C8 plus the mandatory native path, and the Core v1 Compiler Stable class requires "C7,
C8, and C10". C9 is excluded in three independent places. **OD-1 rules that C9 Part B does not block
C10**, and nothing in C9's history is rewritten.

## What C10-0 found

- **F3** — six open deviations (DEV-156/157/159/160/161/162) exist only in `COMPILER-STATE.md` and own
  no heading in `KNOWN-DEVIATIONS.md`. A C10.7 check reading only the ledger would not see them.
- **F2** — "Known open, at a glance" listed 2 deviations; population A has 32.
- **F1** — `target-matrix.json` names **four** targets. `x86_64-apple-darwin` is tier-3, packaged with
  an archive and both installers, and exercised by **no CI job**. C10-Q may not claim tier-3.
- **F6** (positive, measured) — every inherited AS8 mutation result is FRESH: 12/12 authority files and
  13/13 control suites hash identically at `e7bb95d` and at the baseline.
- **F5** — the corpus README cited a `cargo test --test c6_corpus_cases` target that has never existed.

## The one behaviour change: DEV-213

The LSP cached one whole-package analysis **per open URI** and invalidated per URI, so a rename in one
open file left every sibling's analysis carrying the old name and `workspace/symbol` answered with
both. Now invalidated per **package**.

**The test was proved able to fail before its pass was believed** — with the sweep disabled it fails
with `["alpha_symbol", "renamed_symbol"]`, the defect's exact signature; the control was removed and
the restore verified byte-identical. AS8's test is polarity-flipped, not deleted, exactly as its own
assertion message instructed.

## Still owed

- **DEV-012** — seven features need a person in a real editor. An autonomous session cannot produce
  MANUAL evidence. `C10-P-LANGUAGE-SERVICES.md` §3 specifies the sitting.
- Owner adjudication of 8 deviations whose last heading does not settle them.
- Owner ruling on whether ONNX timings enter the C10-E workload set (recommendation: exclude).

## Review focus

CI on this PR is the point — the compiler change is confined to `src/lsp/`, and this is the first
multi-platform run over it.

## 개요

밥상 스튜디오를 "메뉴 공지 도구"에서 **한식뷔페 가게 운영 전반을 관리하는 앱**으로 확장합니다. 생각할 수 있는 운영 기능들의 기본틀(입력·목록·요약이 동작하는 상태)을 전부 만들었고, 기존 메뉴 공지 기능은 그대로 유지됩니다.

## 새 화면 구성 (5탭 내비게이션)

- **홈 `/`** — 대시보드: 오늘 현황 4카드(오늘 메뉴 등록 여부 / 오늘 매출 / 재고 부족 품목 수 / 오늘 예약 건수·인원) + 이번 달 매출−지출 간이 손익. 최상단에 "오늘의 메뉴 공지 만들기" 대형 버튼.
- **메뉴 `/menu`** — 기존 메뉴 공지 작성 화면 그대로 이동 (기능 변경 없음)
- **매출 `/sales`** — 일별 점심/저녁 매출·객수·메모 입력(같은 날짜는 덮어쓰기, 날짜 선택 시 기존 값 자동 로드), 이번 달 합계, 최근 7일 요일별 미니 차트
- **재고 `/inventory`** — 품목 등록(분류/수량/단위/최소 수량), +/− 버튼으로 수량 조절, 최소 수량 이하 시 부족 표시 + **발주 목록 텍스트 복사**(거래처 채팅에 붙여넣기)
- **더보기 `/more`** — 예약 / 지출 / 직원 / 메뉴 히스토리 / 설정
  - **예약 `/reservations`** — 단체 손님 기록(날짜·시간·인원·연락처), 다가오는/지난 예약 구분, 바로 전화
  - **지출 `/expenses`** — 분류(식자재/인건비/임대료/공과금/기타)별 기록, 이번 달 분류별 합계
  - **직원 `/staff`** — 명단·역할·연락처(바로 전화)·급여 메모

## 구현 노트

- `CollectionStore` 범용 CRUD 계층 추가(`lib/storage/collection.ts`) — 5개 모듈이 공유하며, 추후 Supabase로 옮길 때 이 계층만 원격 구현으로 교체하면 됩니다.
- 새 타입 5종(`SalesRecord` `InventoryItem` `Expense` `StaffMember` `Reservation`)과 상수(지출/재고 분류) 추가, 금액 포맷 유틸(`lib/format.ts`) 분리.
- 기존 규칙 유지: 한글 주석, 명시적 타입, 매직 넘버 상수화, 터치 영역 44px+, 모바일 우선.
- README에 화면 구성과 **데이터가 현재 기기(브라우저) 안에만 저장된다는 안내** 추가.

## 검증

- `npm run lint` / `npm run build` 통과 (10개 라우트 정적 생성)
- Playwright 실브라우저 검증: 매출 저장→월 합계·차트 반영, 재고 부족 알림·발주 복사 토스트, 지출·예약·직원 등록, 대시보드에 전 모듈 집계 표시(오늘 매출 1,470,000원 / 재고 부족 1개 / 예약 1건 12명 / 이번 달 차액 +1,150,000원) 확인

author: shigechika
body:
Closes #39.

## Summary

`pr-gate.yml`'s admission logic lives entirely inside an
`actions/github-script` block (plain JS), which the bash/jq-only
`tests/run_all.sh` harness cannot exercise. `CLAUDE.md` previously
documented this as "verified by reasoning plus a real PR," with no
automated coverage — and that gap let two real bugs through before
being caught late by `/code-review` or an advisor pass, not by any test
(see PR #38): an unrestricted same-repo-PR trust check that would have
let anyone bypass the gate on a public repo, and a legacy-`private`-
boolean-vs-`visibility` gap for GitHub Enterprise "internal" repos.

Adds `tests/test_pr_gate.mjs`, run by `tests/run_all.sh` alongside the
existing bash suites (extension-dispatched: `.sh` via `bash`, `.mjs` via
`node` — no npm dependency, `ubuntu-latest` ships Node already and this
repo has no `package.json`). It extracts the real `script:` block from
the committed `pr-gate.yml` at test time — the same principle
`extract_run()` already applies to `ai-review.yml`'s `run:` block, never
a hand-retyped mirror — and runs it against mock `github`/`context`/
`core` objects across the full trust-decision table: fork vs. same-repo,
public/private/internal base repo visibility, first-party bots,
release-please branch ordering, and closed/reopened actions (49
assertions total).

## Proof the harness isn't vacuous

Confirmed with real mutations, not just a green run:

- Reverting `isTrustedSameRepoPR`'s `visibility` guard to always-true →
  **8 FAILs** (the exact public-repo gate-bypass class fixed in #38).
- Shifting the `script:` block's base indentation (simulating a
  structural YAML reflow) → **4 FAILs**, including a new "exactly one
  script block" assertion added specifically for this, since
  `extractScript` takes the first `script: |` match and would otherwise
  silently test stale/wrong content instead of failing loudly.
- A YAML nuance worth recording so a future reader doesn't "fix" this
  away: shifting a single content line one space *deeper inside* the
  block is **not** an extraction break. YAML literal block scalars
  preserve indentation beyond the block's base level as literal
  content, so the pure-JS extractor and the PyYAML cross-check both
  correctly treat it as real script content, not a shared blind spot.
- Confirmed against a real CI log that PyYAML actually runs in the
  `unit-tests` job (no `pip`/`setup-python` step there — `ubuntu-latest`
  ships it) rather than silently skipping, so the PyYAML cross-check is
  a live CI guard, not dead code.

## Scope

Test-coverage-only — `pr-gate.yml`'s actual trust logic is untouched by
this PR. Because of that, `pr-gate-selftest.yml` running clean on this
PR tells you nothing new about the gate's behavior; the mutation runs
above are the actual evidence this harness works, not the selftest.

## Verification

- `bash tests/run_all.sh` — 49 passed, 0 failed
- `actionlint -shellcheck=` — clean
- `python3 scripts/lint-embedded-shell.py` — all pass
- `node --check tests/test_pr_gate.mjs` — syntax OK

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (`unit-tests`, `actionlint` jobs)
- [ ] `pr-gate-selftest.yml` runs clean (expected, but not evidence of
      the harness's correctness — see Scope above)

A potential risk: Maybe including GMP impacts the other test results? I think that this makes sense - if you wanted to try to reproduce my results, that would be the procedure to follow, even though due to time constraints I couldn't follow it myself.

author: sirfoxworththethird
body:
The three visualisation findings from the UX review — `TL-1`, `ST-1`, `REL-1` — plus a flake fix. These were the ones I expected to hold up under measurement, and they did.

## The pacing curve has a scale and its chapters (`TL-1`)

Narrower than filed: the chart already drew gridlines and already said *"point size = scene length"*. Two things were genuinely absent. Nothing named the **scale**, so a height meant nothing; and 58 events ran in a row with no way to tell which **chapter** a spike belonged to — the question you bring to a pacing chart.

The five tension levels are now labelled (Calm → Climactic) in a gutter drawn *outside* the scrolling plot, so it stays put while you pan. Each chapter start gets a faint numbered rule.

## The structure board shows proportion, not just sequence (`ST-1`)

A beat sheet exists to answer "does Act 2 sag?", and a flat list of equal-height rows cannot. `buildBeatSheet` now measures the acts as well:

- A band above the list divides the book's chapters between the acts at widths proportional to their share, with the conventional 25 / 50 / 25 drawn as dashes to compare against.
- An act begins at the chapter of the first beat placed in it, so the division is read off the writer's own tagging rather than assumed. Until Act 2 *and* Act 3 each have a beat there is no division to draw, and the board says so instead of guessing.
- Each row carries a dot at the beat's position along the book, measured by chapter **rank** so sparse chapter numbers don't stretch an act and beats sharing a chapter coincide — which is what makes a climax and a resolution both crammed into Ch. 22 visible as two dots in one place.

## The relationship graph survives its own example (`REL-1`)

The cause was one line. Every character went onto a fixed four-column grid — 880 × 1920 for a cast of 45 — so `fitView` zoomed out to swallow the height, the connected characters knotted in the top third, both side thirds stayed empty, and a grid slot said nothing about who knew whom.

New `src/features/relationships/graphLayout.ts`: a deterministic Fruchterman–Reingold layout. Relationships pull, pairs within a cutoff push, connected groups are shelf-packed (tallest first, rows centred) towards a landscape shape, and characters with no relationships at all are gathered into a block of their own rather than scattered through the grid. Seeded off a phyllotaxis spiral, so the same cast always gives the same picture.

Two things found while building it that weren't in the finding:

- **The repulsion cutoff earns its place on its own.** Without it, a chain of fifteen characters drew its links half again as long as a chain of five's — mean link length 227 → 272 → 306 as the chain grew. With the cutoff it is 208 flat. The same relationship drawn at two lengths depending on cast size makes the one thing distance is supposed to mean unreadable.
- **Hiding edge labels below a legibility threshold was a regression by itself.** `fitView` on a *twenty*-character world lands at 0.33, so labels would have silently never appeared for most users. A note in the corner now says "Zoom in to read the relationship labels" rather than leaving a reader to conclude the graph has none.

Three controls followed: **Tidy up** re-runs the layout and discards hand-placed positions; **Focus** draws one character's neighbourhood at one or two hops with a count of what is shown; edge labels drop below the zoom at which they are legible.

## Also

Fixed a real race in `e2e/collectiveItem.spec.ts` — it clicked Save and reloaded immediately, beating the async Dexie write. It passed on an idle machine and flaked under load. Waiting for the editor to close is the signal the write committed.

## Testing

Every new spec was mutation-checked: each fix was reverted and the test confirmed to go red.

- `remove the repulsion cutoff` → red · `back to the four-column grid` → red · `focus filter does nothing` → red · `tidy up keeps hand positions` → red · `labels never hide` → red
- `ruler never renders` → red · `dots all at one place` → red · `shares all equal` → red · `drop the out-of-order guard` → red · `zero-count act keeps a range` → red

One turned up a vacuous assertion: the sparse-chapter-numbering test still passed with chapter rank replaced by chapter number, because the fixture's chapters happened to be numbered 1–22. Fixed the test before trusting it.

- Unit: **1603 passing**, 115 files
- e2e: **205 passing**, no flakes, run at the tip of this branch
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean

## Docs

`docs/GUIDE.md` gains *How the book divides* under Structure board and *Keeping a large cast readable* under Relationships. Screenshots: `55-structure-proportion.png` and `56-relationship-focus.png` added, `45-structure.png` and `10-relationships.png` refreshed. `docs/ux-review.md` marks `ST-1` and `REL-1` fixed with what each turned out to be.

author: kayatlanyardhealth
body:
Docs only. Items 3 and 4 from `docs/soc2-readiness-checklist.md` "What to do first".

## Item 4 — corrected, not fixed

I originally graded CC8.2 ❌ on the basis of a "At least 1 approval" line that contradicted the live branch protection setting.

Re-verified: **the enforced control was already accurately documented.** `CLAUDE.md:324` and Information Security Policy §8 both state required approvals = 0 as a deliberate position with named compensating controls. The contradicting line lived in a personal instructions file outside the repo — never an audit artifact. Corrected there separately.

Checklist row regraded ❌ → ⚠️ with the correction recorded inline.

**No approval-count change, and none should be made.** GitHub forbids self-approval and `enforce_admins` is on, so requiring one approval would lock the sole engineer out of merging entirely.

## Item 3 — the inventory was already complete

A full sweep — dependency manifests across all four packages, every outbound HTTP call in `services/`/`agents/`/`queues/`/`scripts/`, frontend SDKs, CI workflows — found **zero missing subprocessors**.

What it did surface is now recorded in `vendor-management-policy.md`:

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| §3.1 Completeness | Five parties that receive data but are **not** vendors, with the reason each fails the test |
| §3.2 Built but not enabled | Libretto Cloud, Retell AI — complete code paths, no prod credentials |
| §3.3 Dead | Stripe, AWS Textract, Stedi, DocuSign/Salesforce |
| §3.4 Credential provenance | Gmail and Firecrawl — open decision |

**The test applied:** does this party process Lanyard or customer data *on Lanyard's behalf*? Payer portals fail it — Aetna is the counterparty an application is submitted *to*, which is the business transaction itself. CAQH passes it, because Lanyard holds an organizational account and pulls credentialing data *from* them. That asymmetry is stated explicitly in §3.1.

Padding the inventory is not harmless: every row implies an attestation an auditor can request, and there is no Libretto SOC 2 report to produce for a service that isn't switched on.

## §3.4 is deliberately unresolved

`GMAIL_*` (4 vars) and `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` are live in production with no code path. Rather than revoke, the evidence for each is recorded and the decision is left open — per the instruction to establish why a credential exists before removing it. Firecrawl in particular may be legitimately required by monitors configured outside this codebase.

## Incidental finding

`@aws-sdk/client-textract` is a production dependency that is never constructed — Claude vision replaced it. Dead weight in both the install and the vulnerability surface. Not bundled here.

## Remaining on item 3

Not code: download and file the current attestation for each Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendor, and resolve §3.4.

author: mendestrading21
body:
Le lot 406 a montré que `myCapital` et `myTradesEquity` ne sont écrits nulle part, et a suivi **une** conséquence (la courbe d'équité jamais affichée). **Ce lot suit la seconde — et elle est plus grave.**

**Aucun code, aucun gardien, aucun test.** Dossier de rang 1.

## D'abord borner : y a-t-il d'autres accesseurs orphelins ?

```text
vx-entities.js — clés LUES par un accesseur      11
                 clés ÉCRITES                     9
                 LUES mais JAMAIS écrites          2   → myCapital, myTradesEquity
```

**Exactement deux.** Et sur les 8 pages servies, un seul module les consomme : `portfolio_page.py`. Périmètre du dossier 406 **confirmé et clos**.

## La conséquence non suivie

```javascript
portfolio_page.py:718   cash: E().capital() || 0,  simulated: false
```

`capital()` vaut **toujours `null`** → le `|| 0` **convertit une absence en zéro**, envoyé à `/api/portfolio/team` et **déclaré réel** (`provenance='REAL'`).

Trois lignes plus bas, le fichier écrit lui-même la règle qu'il enfreint :

```javascript
portfolio_page.py:727
/* … « Manquant/insuffisant » n'est jamais présenté comme zéro. */
```

## Ce que ce zéro change — mesuré

Moteur exécuté deux fois sur les **mêmes** positions :

```text
mesure          cash = 0        cash = 50 000    verdict
equity          4 100           54 100           DIFFÈRE
hhi             0.5003          0.0029           DIFFÈRE  (×170)
issue_gardien   True            False            DIFFÈRE
```

La page **affiche** ce chiffre : `if (risk.hhi >= 0.66) → « Concentration très élevée (HHI …) »`.

**Le seuil est-il franchi ? Oui :**

```text
1 position    HHI cash=0  1.0     → ALERTE   | cash=50k 0.0015 → aucune   ★ FABRIQUÉE
2 positions   HHI cash=0  0.5003  → aucune   | cash=50k 0.0029 → aucune
4 positions   HHI cash=0  0.3019  → aucune   | cash=50k 0.0073 → aucune
```

**Avec une seule position déclarée, le terminal affiche « Concentration très élevée (HHI 1) »** — un artefact du `|| 0`, pas une lecture du portefeuille. Le blob actuel porte 2 positions, donc l'alerte ne part pas aujourd'hui ; **mais le HHI affiché reste faux d'un facteur ~170**, servi comme mesure réelle.

## Une conséquence qui n'atteint PAS l'écran — dite quand même

`team_view` conclut **toujours** « pas de gardien (cash/monétaire) » (`ROLE_TARGETS[GOALKEEPER]=(1,1)`, `if snapshot.cash > 0` jamais vrai). Mais la page **ne consomme pas** `d.team` — `team` n'y est que le nom de la vue « Synthèse ». Calculé, **pas affiché**.

## Trois issues, aucune engagée

1. Ne pas envoyer un zéro pour une absence.
2. **Alimenter `myCapital`** — même décision que le volet 1 du 406, règle les deux d'un coup. **Recommandé.**
3. A minima, masquer le HHI et son alerte quand le cash est inconnu.

## Portée

Chiffres issus d'une exécution directe de `risk_engine`/`stress_tests` sur des positions **fabriquées pour la mesure** — c'est la méthode qui est démontrée, pas le portefeuille du trader. `beta` et `pire_stress` ressortent `None` faute d'entrées : leur sensibilité au cash **n'est pas affirmée**.

## Vérifications

- Anti-doublon : `total 100 · actifs 0`. `pwd` vérifié avant toute mesure.
- **Aucun fichier touché** — moteurs exécutés en mémoire, sans serveur. SW : `td-shell-v187`.
- Snapshot des 22 fichiers runtime avec contrôle d'apparition ; écart final **aucun**.
- Suite : **2864 passed / 0 skipped**, inchangée.

author: siddanta-ar1
body:
Finishes the monk that was dropped into the welcome screen locally, and takes the structure (not the styling) from the reference onboarding.

## The monk

It was a static `<Image>` pointing at the **429 KB animated WebP built for the landing page**. React Native does not reliably play animated WebP, so the figure stood still or animated depending on the device — and the file was a second, untracked copy of an asset the repo already has.

**Not the 3D route either.** `components/3d/Character3D` reaches for `@react-three/fiber`, which on React Native needs **`expo-gl`** — a native module that is **not in the shipped APK**, so no OTA update can add it, and EAS builds are unavailable until 1 September. A 3D figure cannot reach a single existing install right now; eleven images and a timer reach all of them. `Character3D` is also a box-and-cylinder placeholder rather than a monk, so nothing finished is being set aside.

Frames are extracted from the **committed** keyed WebP — the same output the landing page uses, which is what stops the app and the site showing differently-cut versions of the same figure. `tools/extract-monk-frames.py` does it, because the existing `build-greeting-monk.py` starts from a source `.webm` that is not in the repository and so cannot regenerate anything a year from now.

**Eleven files for a twenty-frame loop.** The animation is a ping-pong, verified rather than assumed: frames 19..11 are bit-identical to frames 1..9 (one pair differs by 2.2 mean absolute, where genuinely different frames differ by 7.2). Storing all twenty would store nine files twice, so the component walks the index back down. **264 KB against 429 KB, with more control.**

Every frame is mounted and switched by **opacity** rather than swapping one image's `source`. A source swap decodes on the fly and the first pass through the loop shows a blank beat at each new frame; mounting pays the decode once, up front.

Reduced motion is honoured — checked *before* the first tick, so the sway never plays a frame for someone who asked not to see movement, and it holds frame 0 (the rest pose the sway departs from) rather than something caught mid-movement.

## The step shape

Adapted, not copied. The reference's purple chrome and profile form belong to a social app; two things are worth taking.

**Progress becomes discrete marks, current one held as a lozenge.** A bar cut into equal segments reads as one thing partly filled, which invites "how much is left". Marks read as a short list of places — which is what five screens are. Same ink, held longer; no second colour needed.

**Back moves from the top-left corner into the footer, beside the action.** It is the control someone reaches for while already holding the phone to press Continue, and a top-left target on a tall screen is a two-handed reach for a one-handed decision. It takes its own square rather than a share of the button, so no screen's action gets narrower — including `PermissionsScreen`, whose footer stacks a caption under its button.

## One thing deliberately changed

The welcome screen's comment said the reticle carries the whole identity — *"no Buddha, no temple, no lotus"* — and the monk contradicts it. That reasoning still holds everywhere else, and the reticle still opens the alignment rehearsal two screens later, where it is about to mean something. The first screen has a different job: to greet whoever opened the app. The comment now says that rather than describing a screen that no longer exists. **Worth a second opinion — it is a deliberate reversal of a documented decision.**

## Not included

Left uncommitted in the working tree, deliberately:

- `package.json` additions (`three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei`, `expo-gl`) and `components/3d/` — they cannot ship over OTA, per above.
- `components/map/SiteMap3D.tsx` and `components/map/SitePlan.tsx`, which `require('@/assets/greeting-monk.webp')` — **that asset is untracked**. Committing those files without it would break the bundle, the same way the narration `.opus` files did.

## Verification

Typecheck clean; lint has no new problems (the setState-in-effect the rule caught is fixed by deriving the frame rather than storing it). Ping-pong sequence asserted numerically. Composition checked by rendering both screens at 390×844 with the real palette and a real frame.

Part of #556 — **the predecessor**, one of two additions the epic proposed that the source design document did not contain, and the one it called *the funniest possible institutional memory: the institution outlives the hero.*

> **Precedent**
> *This file continues one opened for Bendrel, Sub-Subprocessor Robot Monk, last recorded at level 19.*

## Every piece was already here and unconnected

The roster holds many characters. The caseload, commendation and specimen ledgers deliberately span all of them — *"a new character starting over must not erase the record"* — so a new hero opens a service record onto a filing cabinet full of somebody else's arithmetic. **Nothing anywhere said whose.**

That is the whole feature. Not a simulation of a retired character, not a ghost, not a mechanic. One line, filed under everything it explains.

## Seniority, not recency

"Predecessor" suggests the previous one, and the roster does keep a recency order. This uses the **highest level** instead, for the same reason that decides which of two overlapping eras is current in #566: recency moves. A player switching between two characters would see the citation swap every time, which reads as the institution changing its mind rather than as a record. Ties resolve alphabetically, so key order cannot decide it either.

## The citation claims no ending

A character in the roster has not retired, died, or been dismissed — **they have not been loaded lately**, which is not a fate and must not be written as one. The line states a name, a race, a class and a level, because that is what the sheet holds, and a test forbids the vocabulary of an ending.

The roster is read at render, and a failed read costs one line rather than the document — the same arrangement every ledger here already has with storage.

## Verification

`npm run quality` clean — **1000 tests / 93 files / 56 node gates**, 164 e2e, 9 PWA.

Four mutations, all killed: the current hero admitted as their own predecessor (usually the highest level in the roster, which is exactly why it must be excluded rather than assumed away), the lowest level winning, ties left to key order, and the citation inventing a retirement.

The service record's structural line bound moved 20 → 21, and the maximal-file test caught that it had to — it failed at 20 until the fixture was given a roster, which is the assertion doing its job rather than quietly accepting a lower total.

author: 99yash
body:
## Where this change sits

The outbox write path (ADR-0005 durable domain-event publication) is now owned by the @alfred/assistant/triggers module, alongside the existing in-process trigger-consumer bus (publishDomainEvent).

## Why this change is needed

Triggers already owns the in-process domain-event broadcast (publishDomainEvent, consumer registry). The outbox write (publishEvent, the realtime SSE relay substrate) is the same publication contract at a different scale. Co-locating both behind one module interface (triggers) simplifies the dependency graph and closes the gap between the two publication paths — a single verb `publishEvent` covers both in-process and durable publication, distinguishing them only in the transport choice (tx vs. untransacted).

## What this change does

- Deepen `packages/assistant/src/triggers/index.ts` with `publishEvent(args: PublishEventArgs<K>): Promise<void>` — validates the payload against the kind's Zod schema before writing the `events_outbox` row
- Add `PublishEventArgs<K>` type — discriminated union over `tx: DbTransaction` vs. `untransacted: true`, enforcing the author's intent for atomicity
- Delete `packages/api/src/events/publish.ts` (functionality folded into triggers)
- Delete `packages/api/src/events/types.ts` (re-export of @alfred/contracts/events; direct imports use @alfred/contracts/events)
- Repoint `packages/api/src/backend.ts` to re-export `publishEvent` and `PublishEventArgs` from `@alfred/assistant/triggers` (facade preserves public surface)
- Repoint all 11 source importers (agent, knowledge, triage, conversations, connections, composition) to `@alfred/assistant/triggers`
- Repoint 5 internal type-only imports (outbox-reaper, outbox-relay, replay, user-events-bus) to `@alfred/contracts/events`
- Move `packages/api/test/events/publish.test.ts` to `packages/assistant/test/triggers/publish.test.ts` (DB-backed, runs in assistant test:db)
- Regenerate module-architecture-baseline.json + oxfmt

## Preserved behavior

- @alfred/api/backend surface is byte-identical (re-export facade maintains the same export list)
- All callers reach publishEvent through the same import path they already use (@alfred/api/backend or direct @alfred/assistant/triggers import)
- The outbox invariants (row insertion, payload schema validation, atomicity with domain writes, retention policy) are unchanged
- Triggers remains a zero-outgoing-edge leaf — zero new package edges, no cycles

## Tests

- DB-backed api test:db suite: 1946 pass, 0 fail
- DB-backed assistant test:db suite: 62 pass, 0 fail (includes moved publish.test.ts)
- Architecture check: clean (41 package edges, 82 assistant-module edges, 0 package SCCs, 0 module SCCs, triggers is a leaf)

## Design invariant

Durable domain-event publication is owned by the @alfred/assistant/triggers module; the outbox write path (publishEvent) and in-process broadcast path (publishDomainEvent) coexist under one interface, and callers from any module reach them through the published index.

## Vocabulary ledger

Removed: @alfred/api/events module (events/publish.ts, events/types.ts), from-events import paths in 11 source + 5 type-only + 1 test file
Added: publishEvent + PublishEventArgs on @alfred/assistant/triggers index
Net call sites learning: 0 (all repointed; no new callers)
New package edges: 0 (@alfred/assistant → @alfred/db pre-exists, legal per ADR-0089 L30)

## Why
The MCP bridge now has an immutable GHCR packaging path, but Coolify still needs a dedicated pull-only deployment definition that can start safely before OAuth, database, or bridge activation is configured.

## Change
- add `docker-compose.mcp.prebuilt.yml` with exactly one `mcp` service
- pull only `ghcr.io/diazpmatt-cmd/ai-edge-os-mcp:${MCP_IMAGE_TAG}`; never build on the Hetzner host

- default `DAB3C_ENABLED=false` and `DAB3C_KILL_SWITCH=true`
- allow the container to become healthy through `/healthz` while all activation/OAuth/database values remain unset
- preserve non-root image execution and add `no-new-privileges` plus dropped Linux capabilities
- add a focused GitHub Actions validator that proves one-service/pull-only/external-network/fail-closed defaults

## Safety
- no deployment
- no domain
- no OAuth configuration
- no database creation or migration
- no credentials or secret values
- no customer-facing behavior
- bridge remains disabled and kill-switched by default

## Next after merge
Create one isolated Coolify application from this compose file using the verified immutable MCP image. First prove `/healthz` with the bridge disabled. Only then provision/configure the tenant-independent control database and OAuth boundary, activate `/mcp`, and connect the ChatGPT custom app.

### Summary

A second-router simulator for the testbed: an FRR speaker in an LXC on the transit link that peers with both MWAN speakers in the iBGP AS and announces the prefix it owns. author: os-project-manager
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6881
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6762

**Paired 「spec-surface sweep」卡（#6243 模型）** —— 两条同类问题：**已发布的 `.describe()` 说明不足**。
属性上方的 TSDoc 块**不进生成器**，只有 `.describe()` 会进 `content/docs/references/**`，所以这两处直接决定参考文档里那一格渲染出什么。

按条目 checklist 复核，两条彼此独立、可分别裁决。

---

## 条目 1 —— #6881：`ExecutionContextSchema.preserveAudit` 没有 `.describe()`

**锚点（实测）**：`packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts:356`（卡上写 ~`:356`，实测一致）

- [x] **Before** —— 裸声明 `preserveAudit: z.boolean().optional(),`，语义只写在上方 `:329-355` 的块注释里，于是 `content/docs/references/kernel/execution-context.mdx:69` 渲染成 `| **preserveAudit** | boolean | optional |  |`，**描述列为空**。
- [x] **After** —— 补上 `.describe()`，参考行不再空白；措辞按 **#6640 收窄后**的契约。

**口径对齐的两处已合入站点（读过，不另造第三种拼法）**：

| 站点 | 借用的词汇 |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` — `FieldSchema.readonly`（PR #6823） | 「Exempt on the UPDATE path ONLY」、「On INSERT the exemption does NOT apply (#6640)」、whitelist = 审计/时间戳族 + 作者声明的业务 `readonly` 字段 |
| `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` 的 callout（同一 PR #6823） | 「CREATE is stripped earlier, at the DataProtocol ingress，whose only exemption is `context.isSystem`」、「the server logs a `WARN` … the strip still applies」 |

即落到描述里的规则：**豁免仅在 UPDATE 路径成立；INSERT 侧只认 `context.isSystem`，非 system 的 create 请求即便携带 `preserveAudit`，字段仍被剥离并记 WARN。**

---

## 条目 2 —— #6762：`rls.zod.ts` `using` 的 `.describe()` 既 under-promise 又指向正在退役的方言

**锚点（实测）**：`packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts:358`（打标记后现为 `:364`）

- [x] **Before** —— 「One of the **four** compiler-supported forms: `field = current_user.< prop >`, `field = 'literal'`, `field IN (current_user.< array >)`, or `1 = 1`.」两个方向都不准：比实际编译的**窄**，且四种拼写全是 **SQL 方言**（ADR-0058 D1 定其为过渡态，`sqlPredicateToCel` 标 `@deprecated`）。
- [x] **After** —— 改为按**编译器实际下推的形态**描述，用规范 CEL；SQL 拼写降格为「过渡桥接」而非定义。

### 须实测：门实际接受什么（不照抄卡上的清单）

我自己跑了 `isSupportedRlsExpression`，**实测 ENFORCES**（远宽于「四种」）：

| 形态 | 样例 | 结果 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `==` 对上下文值 / 字面量 | `organization_id == current_user.organization_id` / `status == 'published'` | ENFORCES |
| `!=` | `region != null` | ENFORCES |
| `<` `<=` `>` `>=` | `amount > 100`、`amount <= 100` | ENFORCES |
| `in` 对 `current_user.*` 数组 | `assigned_to_id in current_user.team_member_ids` | ENFORCES |
| `in` 对**内联字面量列表** | `status in ['draft', 'pending']` | ENFORCES |
| `&&` / `\|\|` | `a == 1 && b == 2`、`a == 1 \|\| b == 2` | ENFORCES |
| 裸 allow-all | `true` | ENFORCES |
| 传统 SQL（经桥接） | `=` → `==`、`IN` → `in`、`1 = 1` | ENFORCES |

**实测 FAILS CLOSED**：SQL 的 `AND` / `OR` / `NOT IN` / `IS NULL` / `LIKE`、算术 `amount + 1 > 2`、子查询、跨对象 `record.a.b == 1`、裸真值字段 `is_active`、取反 `!is_active`、空串。

> ⛔ **没有换一个新的固定计数。** 「四」换成「八」是同一个缺陷。描述改为讲**形态**（哪些算子、可否组合），把「数目」这件事整个去掉；pin 里还有一条断言明确禁止再出现固定计数。

`||` 与内联字面量列表这两项是本次实测的**增量发现**（issue 正文只提到 `&&`），已写进描述。
CEL 拼写与同文件 PR #6729 落下的 `check` `@example`（`status in ['draft', 'pending']`）一致。

---

## Lane admission —— acceptance 逐字节不变

`domain:spec-surface`。`.describe()` 不参与 parsing；无任何 key / 类型 / 枚举成员 / refinement / 默认值移动。**证据**：`gen:schema` 之后

```
$ git status --porcelain packages/spec/authorable-surface packages/spec/json-schema.manifest packages/spec/authorable-defaults packages/spec/authorable-surface.base.json
  (空 —— 零 diff)
🔒 authorable-defaults/ verified against upstream — 1308 default(s) unchanged (#4666).
```

（`packages/spec/json-schema/` 是 `.gitignore:61` 的构建产物，不进版本库；已确认其磁盘内容确实随本次改动重生成。）

## 生成产物（两条同乘一次重生成）

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:docs` 后**恰好**两个受版本控制的文件变化，**各一行**，无附带 churn：

```
 content/docs/references/kernel/execution-context.mdx | 2 +-
 content/docs/references/security/rls.mdx             | 2 +-
```

均为生成器产出，未手改；`content/docs/releases/` 未触碰。

## 验证 —— 方向在跑之前先预测

两条都是**正向内容**断言，pin 读回 schema 上的 `description` 并断言其必须承载的实质。

| 反向臂 | 预测 | 实测 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A. 把原描述原样放回**（`git checkout origin/main --` 两个 zod 文件） | RED | **RED，13/13**。条目 1 的 7 条全部对 `''` 失败（正是「空单元格」缺陷本身）；条目 2 的 6 条对旧 four-forms 串失败，含「不得再出现固定计数」那条抓到字面量 `four`。 |
| **B. anti-vacuity：两处都设为 `.describe('')`** | RED，且须由**非空臂**抓到 | **RED，13 failed / 46 passed**。两条目的「is present and non-empty」臂各自触发；而条目 2 的「does not re-close the set」臂**未**出现在失败列表里 —— 它在 `''` 上**空洞通过**，这正是非空臂存在的理由。 |

**按 idiom 而非逐字断言**：改写自由（用 `toMatch` 交替式），丢失实质不自由。
pin 覆盖检索时**同时搜了转义正则拼法**（`toMatch(/…/)`）而不只字面量（#6854 的教训）—— 两处此前均无既有 pin。

门的**行为**半边不重复 pin：`packages/formula/src/rls-predicate.test.ts:46-67` 已经钉住 `isSupportedRlsExpression` 的红/绿线，本 PR 只钉「散文与之相符」，避免同一事实两处钉。

## 结果

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` → **348 files / 8967 tests passed**（合入 `origin/main` 之后、以及加标记之后各复跑一次）
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` → 通过
- `pnpm lint`、`check:generated`、`check:docs`、`check:authorable-surface`、`check:api-surface`、`check:spec-changes`、`check:upgrade-guide`、`check:skill-refs`、`check:doc-authoring`、`check:docs-audit-scope`、`check:adr-anchors`、`check:nul-bytes` → 全部 exit 0
- **`test-typecheck-debt.json` 账本（#5286 ratchet）**：前后均为 **58 file(s) / 266 error(s)**，文件 sha256 `b5e1c38e…` **逐字节未变** —— 两处新 pin 不带 tsc 错误。

## 范围 —— 刻意留在范围外的相邻问题，已立卡 #6919

⛔ 只有这两条修复，无搭车。相邻问题**已作为正式 GitHub issue 立卡：#6919**（未指派；`finding` + `domain:spec-surface`，无 `pm:queue` —— 观察类归档，不进派发池）。不是 PR 评论：合入后评论就不再是任何人会看的地方。

**#6919 记录的是同一句话的两处副本**，其中一处是我在复核期间新实测到的，且**已发布**：

| 位置 | 是否进生成器 | 现状 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `rls.zod.ts` 属性级 TSDoc（`:296-354`） | ❌ 不进（`gen:docs` 只渲染 `.describe()` 与模块级 docblock） | 「Exactly four forms compile」「no support for AND/OR/NOT、`=` 以外的比较算子」 |
| `rls.zod.ts:79` **模块级** docblock | ✅ **进** —— 逐字渲染到 `content/docs/references/security/rls.mdx:79` | 「A small, fixed expression grammar (equality, set-membership, always-true)」 |

第二行是本 PR **没有**动、但值得分诊优先看的一处：合入后 `rls.mdx` **同一张渲染页**上会同时有 `:79` 的旧三项说法和 `:174` 已改正的 `using` 行 —— 自相矛盾落在**已发布面**上。之所以仍未动它：派发卡把条目 2 限定为 `.describe()` 字符串，改它会额外改动一个已发布页面、超出本 PR「恰好两文件各一行」的证据面。按纪律记录、交分诊，不自行扩面。

**本 PR 就近做了一件事：给 TSDoc 那段打 `⚠️ STALE` 标记，不是重写。** 改之前两处一致地错，改之后会互相矛盾 —— 而读源码者（常是 AI，ADR-0033）先撞上的是那段更长、更像权威的语法规范。标记把「两条互相矛盾的断言」降级为「一条断言 + 一句诚实警告」，指向 #6919，一行成本，不破坏 per-item 复核模型。重写那 60 行语法规范散文（连同 5 条 SQL 方言 `@example`）是 #6919 自己的卡。

实测确认标记不进生成器：加入后 `content/docs/references/**` **零 diff** —— 这也再次印证了 TSDoc 那半是观察类。

author: 00o-sh
body:
### Description

Follow-up to #865 (Renovate presets), covering two things: clearing the open Dependabot alerts on `main`, and adding automatic PR labeling.

#### 1. Security — remediate transitive vulnerability alerts

All 10 open Dependabot alerts were for **transitive** dependencies (nothing imported directly is vulnerable), which Dependabot can't auto-fix on a pnpm project. Fixed via `pnpm.overrides` (in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, where this repo keeps pnpm settings):

| Override | Fixes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dompurify@<3.4.13 → 3.4.13` | 2 moderate + 2 low | `monaco-editor` bundled `dompurify@3.4.8`; this aligns it with the `3.4.13` we already ship directly. |
| `ip-address@<10.3.1 → 10.4.0` | **1 HIGH** + 1 moderate | `composerize-ts → ip-cidr` pulled `ip-address@7.1.0` (SSRF `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr`). `ip-cidr`'s usage is compatible with v10 — verified by tests. |

This clears **6 of 10 alerts, including the only HIGH**. Verified locally: `pnpm audit` drops 10 → 4, the full unit suite (**1216 tests**) passes, `pnpm typecheck` passes, and the docker-run→compose converter (the sole `ip-address` consumer) passes.

**Deliberately not fixed** (no safe/available fix — documented for follow-up):
- **unhead** (2 moderate + 1 low): the whole `@unhead` family is on `1.11.20` via the deprecated `@vueuse/head`; the fix is in `unhead@2.x`, a major that restructured the `@unhead/*` packages and needs a real migration (`@vueuse/head` → `@unhead/vue` v2). The vulnerable APIs (`useHeadSafe`/`makeTagSafe`) are **not used anywhere in the app**, so these aren't in the execution path.
- **elliptic** (1 low): the advisory's patched `6.6.2` isn't published on npm yet (latest is `6.6.1`).

#### 2. CI — PR labeler (`.github/workflows/pr-labeler.yml`)

Tags every PR from its changed files so triage/filtering works off labels:
- **area/type**: `ci`, `docker`, `dependencies`, `renovate`, `i18n`, `ui`, `tools`, `tests`, `documentation`, `cloudflare`, `scripts`, `assets`, `build`;
- **per-tool**: `tool:<name>` for each `src/tools/<name>/` a PR touches (capped at 12 — a wider sweep just gets `tools` to avoid label spam);
- **size**: one mutually-exclusive `size/*` label (XS…XL) from lines changed.

Missing labels are created on demand with stable colors/descriptions, and the machine-owned namespaces (`tool:*`, `size/*`) are reconciled on each `synchronize`. It uses `pull_request_target` so PRs from forks get labeled too — safe here because the job only reads the changed-file list via the API and never checks out or executes PR code. Validated with `actionlint`. (Because `pull_request_target` runs the workflow from the base branch, labeling starts once this is merged to `main`.)

### Additional context

Reviewers may want to confirm comfort with the `ip-address` major override (7 → 10 in a transitive tree); it's covered by the converter's unit tests and the full e2e/visual-regression suite that dependency PRs trigger.

author: jmerritt0119-blip
body:
## The waste

Her 63-part scan billed **189 Opus requests and returned nothing usable**.

Every part was retried to exhaustion whether or not it had already produced a catalog. A part cut off near the end — holding nearly all of its evidence — was thrown away and re-run twice more at full price.

## Measured against her actual archive

3,739,755 characters, Opus 5 pricing, prompt caching counted:

| | requests | cost | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| What actually ran (`xhigh`, 3 attempts) | 189 | **~$76** | nothing |
| Same scan, `high` effort, 1 attempt | 63 | ~$13 | full catalog |
| After the merged fixes (30k parts) | 125 | ~$21 | full catalog |

The 3× retry multiplier on top of the `xhigh` regression is what turned a ~$13 job into a ~$76 one that produced zero output.

## Fix

A failed attempt is now checked for usable content **before another one is paid for**. If the reply already contains incidents or messages, it's kept and the loop stops. Retries only happen when there's genuinely nothing to salvage — which is what they were for.

The part is still reported as incomplete so she can top it up, and `mergeScanResults` deduplicates by date and content, so re-running a salvaged part **cannot double-count her evidence**.

## Note on chunk size

Halving parts to 30k (#40) makes the scan *more* expensive per run — 125 requests instead of 63, ~$21 vs ~$13 — because per-request overhead is paid more often. It buys reliability: a dense part can no longer blow the output ceiling deterministically. Worth it given a deterministic failure previously cost the entire scan, but it is a real trade and should be a deliberate one.

author: muaz787
body:
## Summary

Removes the **"How should calls be answered?"** mode selector from the Call Handling page — it was a no-op. Per your request I also **audited every other section**; it was the only dead one.

## Why it was dead

The three mode options wrote `profile.mode` (and `overflow_enabled`), but **nothing reads those at runtime**:
- `routing_engine.evaluate()` doesn't branch on `mode` (only names it in a docstring).
- No webhook / mid-call tool / assistant code consumes `mode` or `overflow_enabled`.

So selecting a mode saved a setting no behavior acted on. It was leftover scaffolding from the phased plan, and next to the new **"Call routing is on/off"** toggle it looked like a control while doing nothing. Two options were also misleading (e.g. "only when busy… via carrier forwarding" is a customer-side carrier setup the app doesn't configure).

## Audit of the remaining sections (all kept — all functional)

| Section | Wired to | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Call routing on/off toggle | `/activate` `/deactivate` → `routing_enabled` → assistant tools | keep |
| Transfer destinations | encrypted destinations feed the engine + transfer webhook | keep |
| Where should calls go (default / urgent) | `default_destination_id`, `urgent_destination_id` in `routing_engine.evaluate()` | keep |
| Routing rules | `rules` (priority/match/destination) in the engine | keep |
| Test it (simulate) | `/simulate` → the engine, no call placed | keep |

## Changes

Removed the Mode card JSX + its `MODES` constant, `modeState`, and `saveMode`. The profile is still created lazily on first real config (setting a default/urgent destination or adding a rule), so no behavior change. `Profile` type keeps `mode?`/`overflow_enabled?` (still valid API fields).

Frontend-only; **lint + typecheck clean**.

## Rollout / Rollback

- Merge → Vercel redeploys the page. No backend change.
- Rollback: revert the merge commit.
