## Summary

Playtest observations B1–B6. **The reference PNGs named in the prompt (`image1`…`image10`) never arrived** — there is no `artifacts/` directory in this container, nothing matching those names anywhere on disk, and the prompt `.md` came through twice byte-identical with no embedded images. So B1 and B2 are untouched, B3 and B6 are done only as far as they can be without artwork, and **no founder art was guessed at or deleted**.

| # | Item | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **B4** | Diamond claim survives Blaze restart | **FIXED** (2 root causes) |
| **B5** | Magic mushrooms look wrong | **FIXED** |
| **B6** | Smoke Lounge anticipation banner | **PARTIAL** — built + gated on L1/L2/L3; "replace entirely" needs image10 |
| **B3** | Band spacing, GM logo right | **PARTIAL** — GM shifted right; image7 insert blocked |
| **B1** | Wrong flaming diamond art | **BLOCKED** — needs image2 |
| **B2** | World-info tab fill | **BLOCKED** — needs image3/4/5 |

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Other: art correction + two new regression gates

## Changes

### B4 — two separate bugs, each reproduced by a failing test first

**(a) A same-frame race — the founder's "often via candle bounce".** A candle and a diamond can be touched on the *same physics frame*. The pickup set `visible = false` immediately and `_crash()` set `visible = true` immediately, so whichever Area2D the physics server reported **second** won:

```
candle  -> _crash() -> token.visible = true    (restored)
diamond -> pickup   -> area.visible  = false   (claimed again)
```

The restore is now deferred to strictly after every collision callback for the frame, with a `_crash_pending` guard closing the same hole from the pickup side. Note the in-isolation reset already tested green — which is exactly why this needed a test that reproduces the *reported* sequence.

**(b) The Blaze entrance was consumed permanently.** `blaze_portal_used` / `secret_door_used` were written by `mark_side_entrance_used()` and cleared **nowhere in the codebase** — not on death, not on `full_wipe_restart`, not on `boss_contact_restart`, not in `reset_session`. The first Blaze run on a level killed that entrance for good. `reopen_side_entrances()` now runs on every fresh-attempt path; the once-per-visit rule still holds inside a run, so this does not reintroduce the "kept falling back in while fleeing the Tax Collector" problem.

### B5 — the mushrooms were throwing a runtime error on every spawn

`magic_mushroom.gd` and `weed_leaf.gd` still carried ColorRect-era placeholder code (`sprite.color`, `sprite.size`) against scenes that have used a real `Sprite2D` for a long time. A Sprite2D has neither property, so every spawn threw *"Invalid assignment of property or key 'color'"* and **aborted the rest of `_ready()` on that line**. Those two were the last placeholder-era stragglers.

The 40px pickup art was separately a low-contrast smudge; redrawn from the silhouette in — wide domed cap **overhanging** a separate stem, dark keyline, cream spots. The Blaze backdrop mushrooms (an ellipse on a rectangle) got the same treatment.

### B6 — anticipation banner

New **SMOKE LOUNGE / CHILL OUT AHEAD** banner, placed late in each course, guaranteed on L1/L2/L3. It owns its placement rather than competing for a landmark lattice slot — anything in that lattice is *dropped* when it cannot clear a floor gap, so whether the callout appeared was a function of each course's gap layout.

`br_smoke_lounge_car.png` is deliberately **left in place**: without image10 there is no way to know that is the banner meant by "replace entirely", and deleting founder artwork on a guess is the failure mode to avoid.

### B3 — GoldMine moved right

Slot order *is* the layout, so GM moved from third of seven to second from last: the right-hand end of the band.

## Checklist

- [x] Verified in real Godot 4.3 headless runs, not by code reading
- [x] 12 gate suites ALL PASS, including 2 new (`blaze_claim_reset`, `blaze_lounge_banner`)
- [x] Security sentinel 18/18; sprite-alpha clean
- [x] Logo constraints respected: no white outlines, purple band only, no gap placement
- [x] Forest BG system not reopened; no video work; no B.AI
- [x] No hardcoded paths or platform-specific assumptions

## Known gaps

- B1, B2 and the artwork halves of B3/B6 are waiting on image2, image3/4/5, image7 and image10.
- `icp_contract` fails in the dev sandbox only (needs a live ICP canister; the proxy blocks it).

## Stage 4 — ORÍKÌ News + Intelligence Update Engine

This stage makes ORÍKÌ a living intelligence platform rather than a static catalogue.

### Implemented

- Adds a dedicated **NEWS** application section.
- Adds News to the main application navigation and landing page.
- Adds News categories: Breaking, New Releases, Models, Tools, Research, Business and Africa.
- Adds news cards, filtering, source links and related Intelligence.
- Adds latest AI news to the Dashboard.
- Adds a structured `data/news.json` source of truth for the news cache.
- Adds a public RSS/Atom feed scanner using Python standard-library tooling only.
- Monitors public feeds from OpenAI, Google, Google DeepMind, Hugging Face and arXiv AI.
- Detects release-oriented stories and creates conservative **AUTO-DETECTED** AI candidates.
- Automatically places detected candidates into the Intelligence catalogue while retaining their source URL and detection metadata.
- Preserves detected candidates between scans.
- Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs daily and can also be triggered manually.
- When new information is found, the workflow creates a dedicated update branch and **ONE review PR** against `main`.
- The automation never merges the PR automatically.
- No API keys, paid news service or backend are required for the initial implementation.
- Existing Stage 3 Intelligence architecture remains intact.

### Review model

Public source → ORÍKÌ scanner → news/candidate update → GitHub PR → Commander review → Commander merge.

The automated candidates are intentionally conservative and marked `AUTO-DETECTED`; the PR is the human approval gate before the live catalogue changes.

This is the single Stage 4 implementation PR. Do not merge automatically.

author: cjimti
body:
Closes #1220

## What this delivers

An insight is a claim, and a delivered claim removes the reader's reason to check it. When the platform can query the subject of a claim for itself, it now says so: an insight whose linked catalog entity resolves through the query provider to an available table is delivered carrying the queryable identity of that entity.

```json
{
  "source": "insights",
  "ref": "i-9f2c",
  "text": "The orders table holds 1,140 rows for FY25.",
  "reference": "mcp:insight:i-9f2c",
  "entity_urns": ["urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:trino,iceberg.retail.orders,PROD)"],
  "verifiable": {
    "urn": "urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:trino,iceberg.retail.orders,PROD)",
    "query_table": "iceberg.retail.orders",
    "connection": "primary"
  }
}
```

The marker rides the payload rather than the transport, because the platform cannot detect what is consuming it. It appears on every surface that delivers an insight:

| Surface | Where the field lands |
|---|---|
| `search` insight hits | `knowledge.Hit.Verifiable` |
| `fetch` of `mcp:insight:<id>` | `knowledge.Document.Verifiable` |
| `memory_context` enrichment block | the insight entries' `verifiable` |

It asserts that the claim's subject is one query away — not that the claim was checked, and not that it is true. An insight linked to several entities names the first that resolves; a claim needing more than one table to settle is not the checkable shape this is for.

## Contract

The field is additive and absent whenever nothing resolves. An insight linked to no entity, an entity the query provider cannot see, a noop provider, and the operator opt-out all deliver exactly the payload they always did — absent, never an empty block. A plain memory record never carries it: a note is not a claim about the warehouse.

Config, default on per the platform's `*bool` convention (nil = enabled):

```yaml
knowledge:
  verifiable_insights: true   # set false to deliver insights with no marker
```

**The marker is topology, so it honors the persona connection boundary (#1108).** An insight about a dataset on a connection the caller's persona may not reach is still delivered — an insight is not connection-scoped, and reading a colleague's conclusion about a warehouse you cannot query is the point of shared knowledge — but it carries no marker, and that connection is never probed on the caller's behalf. The hit is not counted as withheld, because nothing about the record was hidden.

## Cost

Resolution shares one implementation with the review path's observed-entity block, extracted from `internal/admin/insightobs` (#1219) into `internal/tableavail` rather than copied.

- **A page costs one pass.** All of a page's distinct entities resolve together, so an entity claimed by several insights is looked up once, not once per hit.
- **No `COUNT(*)`.** Delivery asks through the new optional `query.LocationResolver` capability (*where* an entity is queryable), implemented by the Trino adapter as `ResolveLocation`, instead of `GetTableAvailability` (which also runs `COUNT(*)` where `enrichment.estimate_row_counts` is on). The admin review path, which reads the estimate, is unchanged.
- **Concurrent callers share one lookup.** An expiring entry no longer turns N active sessions into N warehouse queries for one table.
- **Bounded at 2s per pass**, well under the search fan-out's 5s per-provider budget, so a slow warehouse costs a delivery its marker rather than the record or the arm's whole budget.
- **A negative answer expires in 30s** against a positive answer's 5 minutes, because a query adapter reports a transiently failed describe and a genuinely absent table in the same shape. An answer computed after the budget expired is not remembered at all.

## Two fixes on the same path

**A `memory_context` reference that never dereferenced.** The block stamped every knowledge-dimension record with `mcp:memory:<id>`, a handle `fetch` always declines — insights resolve from a different store, so that reference pointed at nothing for anyone. It now publishes `mcp:insight:<id>`, and only for an applied insight: the push path is persona-scoped rather than caller-scoped, so it delivers other people's records without knowing whose, and applied is the only status whose handle is certain to resolve for the reader. Anything else is delivered with no reference rather than one that answers not-found.

**A byte budget that under-counted.** `recordSizeEstimate` now charges the new field, so `enrichment.memory_context_budget_bytes` bounds what it says it bounds. A DataHub URN is long enough that omitting it let a page of marked insights overshoot the operator's cap by roughly half again.

## Structural change worth a look

`personasForRolesFunc` moves from `pkg/platform` to the existing `internal/platform/iam` identity seam, where role-to-persona membership belongs. This is not otherwise part of the feature: `pkg/platform` sat exactly at the frozen package-size budget (9598 of 9600 LOC, flat for 20+ commits), so adding a config key required freeing the room. `TestPlatformGodObjectBudget` likewise refused a Platform field for the resolver, which is why each delivery surface builds its own from the query provider it already holds.

`testdata/allowed_internal_imports.txt` is regenerated for the new seam's edges (`internal/tableavail -> pkg/query` and its four consumers).

## Verification

`make verify` green end to end.

Integration tests exercise the real assembled system rather than hand-built inputs:

- `pkg/toolkits/search/verifiable_integration_test.go` — the search toolkit's tools on a real `mcp.Server` behind the real tool-call middleware, driven by a client over an in-memory transport, over the real `knowledge.Router` and `InsightsProvider`. Covers marked, unresolvable, no-verifier and noop-provider cases across both `search` and `fetch`.
- `pkg/middleware/verifiable_insight_chain_test.go` — the `memory_context` surface through the real middleware chain. The resolver is deliberately **not** handed in: the test supplies what an operator supplies (a query provider and the toggle) so the constructor branch that is the only production wiring is on the path under test.
- `internal/platform/searchfed/verifiable_insights_test.go` — proves the toggle and provider actually reach the insights provider through the federation assembly.

Unit coverage for the connection boundary (search and fetch), the budget arithmetic, the negative TTL, the expired-budget rule, single-flight (under `-race`), and the adapter's no-count path.

## Review history

An adversarial review raised ten findings. Eight are fixed in this branch — the connection-boundary leak and the budget under-count were the two that mattered, both introduced here. Two were considered and kept:

- **The 64-lookup-per-pass bound.** That bound is what stops one read becoming hundreds of warehouse queries. The marked prefix is deterministic (hit rank order, so top results mark first), the remainder fills in on a later read, and an absent marker is the documented degrade rather than a claim of unverifiability.
- **Three caches over one provider.** Sharing one instance requires a Platform field the god-object gate forbids. With row estimation no longer requested, the duplicated cost is a catalog lookup per surface, and each cache deduplicates and remembers in its own right.

author: stuart-jjj
body:
## Summary
- The self-consumption deadband handoff was a single hard 50W threshold with no hysteresis. body:
# Sprint 9 — Delayed Lifecycle ⏱️

## Overview
Adds built-in spawn/destroy/respawn scheduling on coroutines for entity lifecycle management.

## Feature Breakdown

### T1: `DestroyAfter(TimeSpan delay)` on Entity
- Schedule delayed entity destruction using coroutine system
- Cancelable before delay expires via `CancelDestroyAfter()`
- Auto-cancellation on manual destroy to prevent memory leaks
- Throws on negative delays for safety

### T2: `SpawnAfter<T>(Vector2, TimeSpan)` on EntitySystem
- Schedule delayed entity creation at a specific position
- Returns Guid for cancellation tracking
- Cancelable via `CancelSpawnAfter(Guid)`
- Game-time-aware timing (pauses with game)

### T3: `RespawnAt(Vector2, TimeSpan)` on Entity
- Configure one-time respawn behavior
- Auto-triggers after entity destruction
- Cancelable via `CancelRespawnAt()`
- `HasPendingRespawn` property for state checking

- All tests passing ✅

author: behindthedash
body:
## Outcome
`worktrail-skill-dispatch` now detects an unwritable `CODEX_HOME` before launching a Codex child process and prints the exact remediation, instead of the failure surfacing only after `codex exec` starts (a read-only PATH-alias warning).

## Business or User Value
Anyone dispatching an SDD workflow subagent through Codex (the `worktrail-skill-dispatch` adapter, used when the host has no native `Skill(...)` capability) gets an immediate, actionable error — set `WORKTRAIL_CODEX_HOME` or pass `--codex-home` — instead of a confusing mid-run warning discovered after the child process already started.

## Route Selected
F — Defect Repair. (classify.py's organic pick was F=3 vs C=2; an automatic handoff-recommended override briefly moved it to G based on the brief's `change-kind: delta` frontmatter, but `src/worktrail/router/skill_dispatch.py` has no owning openspec/docs spec, so Route G's "locate the current spec" precondition doesn't hold — routes.md explicitly routes unspecced code through F's direct fix-branch path instead. See run record decisions.)

## Epic / Feature / Specification
none (unspecced code, direct fix-branch per routes.md §F)

## Behavior Before
`skill_dispatch.py main()` resolved an explicit `--codex-home`/`WORKTRAIL_CODEX_HOME` override (or fell through to the inherited/default `CODEX_HOME`) and launched `codex exec` unconditionally. If that directory wasn't writable by the nested Codex app-server, the failure only surfaced after launch as a read-only PATH-alias warning from Codex itself.

## Behavior After
Before launching a Codex child (and only for `--agent codex`, skipped on `--dry-run`), the dispatcher resolves the CODEX_HOME that will actually govern the child (`resolve_codex_home`) and checks write-permission bits on the nearest existing ancestor (`codex_home_write_remediation`) — never opening any file under that path. If unwritable, it prints the exact path and the remediation (`WORKTRAIL_CODEX_HOME` or `--codex-home`) to stderr and exits 1 without launching Codex.

## Scope
- Add `resolve_codex_home()` and `codex_home_write_remediation()` to `skill_dispatch.py`.
- Gate the existing `subprocess.run` call on the new preflight check.
- 10 new regression tests.

## Non-Goals
- No change to `build_command()`, provider identity, or the explicit override precedence (`--codex-home` > `WORKTRAIL_CODEX_HOME` > inherited `CODEX_HOME` > default `~/.codex`).
- No change to non-Codex providers (claude/opencode) — preflight is guarded to `agent == "codex"`.

## Implementation Summary
- `resolve_codex_home(codex_home_override)`: same precedence the dispatcher already uses to build `child_env`, exposed as a pure function.
- `codex_home_write_remediation(path)`: walks up to the nearest existing ancestor of `path` and checks `os.access(ancestor, os.W_OK)`; returns a remediation string or `None`. Never calls `open()` on anything under `path`, so credentials already stored there are never read.
- `main()`: after building (but before running) the Codex command, calls the preflight; on failure prints the remediation to stderr and returns 1 without calling `subprocess.run`.

## Security and Authorization Impact
None. The check only inspects filesystem permission bits on directory paths (never file contents), and only for the Codex provider's own working-directory resolution — no new credential handling, no new external calls.

## Data or Migration Impact
None.

## UI Validation
n/a (CLI-only change)

## Tests and Evidence
| Acceptance criteria (from brief) | Test |
|---|---|
| Detects unwritable CODEX_HOME before launch, Codex only | `test_preflight_blocks_launch_when_codex_home_not_writable`, `test_preflight_does_not_run_for_non_codex_agents` |
| Reports exact remediation incl. safe persistent-home suggestion | `test_write_remediation_flags_a_read_only_ancestor` |
| Focused regression test | `CodexHomePreflightTests` (10 tests) |
| Provider identity unchanged / preserve explicit override path | existing `test_codex_home_environment_override_is_passed_to_child`, `test_explicit_codex_home_takes_precedence`, `test_codex_home_override_is_not_applied_to_other_providers` (all still pass, unmodified) |
| Avoid probing or exposing credentials | `test_write_remediation_never_opens_files_under_the_path` (patches `open()` to raise if called) |
| Preflight skipped on `--dry-run` | `test_preflight_does_not_run_for_dry_run` |

Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q` → 3030 passed, 1 skipped, 137 subtests passed.

## Scope Completeness
All 5 run-record `scope-review` items recorded `complete` with evidence (see run record `go-20260808-211542`); no item deferred or out-of-scope.

## Pre-PR Test Gate
`PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m worktrail.orchestrator.orchestrate check` → PASS (3030 passed, 1 skipped, 137 subtests; `GOLDEN OK (toy-spec.golden.txt)`).

## Performance Impact
Negligible — one `os.path.exists`/`os.access` walk (at most a few `stat` calls) added to the Codex dispatch path only, before process launch.

## Deferred Work and Handoffs
none

## Risk Assessment
**critical** (per `go:risk-critical` label, applied by the deterministic classifier). This is a text-signal false positive, not an assessment of the actual diff: the brief's own constraint prose ("avoid probing or exposing credentials") matched the `secrets` risk regex, which triggers on prose mentions and has no diff awareness (documented behavior in `classify.py`, not a bug — see the `RISK_SIGNALS` comment). The actual diff touches only filesystem-permission-bit checks on a local CLI's working-directory resolution; no secrets, auth, or data paths are touched. Carrying the label as computed rather than self-overriding it, per policy.

## Rollback Plan
Revert this PR. The preflight is additive and only short-circuits before `subprocess.run` for the Codex provider; reverting restores the previous unconditional-launch behavior with no other side effects.

## Auto-Merge Eligibility
**Ineligible** — `go:no-automerge` applied (protected "secrets" text signal → `require_human_approval` + `never_automerge` gates from classify.py, carried through by the pre-PR gate as `AUTOMERGE LABELS: go:risk-critical go:no-automerge`). Requires human merge.

## Summary

Ports the AI system from `cms.intubemedia.com@5c6ad5d` (PRs #55/#56 there) into this CMS **without touching Bainsla branding, data, Redis db5 or env**: `/ai-center` page, `/api/ai`, `/api/ai/reports`, `src/lib/ai/*` (gemini, context, analytics, reconciliation, copyright-priority), sidebar entry for admin/company/client, and `npm run test:ai`.

Bainsla-specific adaptations:

- AI safety prompt says `read-only Bainsla Music CMS AI` instead of the InTube one. Everything the AI answers comes from the tenant-scoped Redis/cache context — no new YouTube sync, no mutations.
- **Cron-name collision fixed.** Both repos' installers wrote `/etc/cron.d/cms-copyright-scan`, so the intubemedia deploy silently overwrote Bainsla's copyright cron (it currently points at `/var/www/cms-frontend`). This repo now writes `cms-bainslamusic-copyright-scan` + `/var/log/cms-bainslamusic-copyright-scan.log`, so the two tenants can't clobber each other.
- New `scripts/run-ai-report.sh` + `scripts/install-ai-report-cron.sh` → `/etc/cron.d/cms-bainslamusic-ai-report`, calling `http://127.0.0.1:3190/api/ai/reports` daily at 15:05 UTC with `x-cron-secret`. Deliberately a standalone cron rather than reusing intubemedia's `install-cms-data-sync-cron.sh`, which would have enabled stats/revenue/sheet syncs here too and reused the shared cron filename.
- `createSystemNotification` now returns `boolean` so the report route can roll back its `ai_report_delivery:<date>:<id>` dedupe key when storage fails.

Whitelist Excel import is now preview-then-confirm:

```ts
parseChannelSheetPreview(file) -> { valid, duplicates, invalid }
```

It reads the sheet with `{ header: 1 }` so *every* cell (header row included) is scanned, keeps only a UC id / channel URL (`/channel/UC…`, `/@handle`, `/c/…`, `/user/…`) / bare `@handle` — a `watch?v=` link no longer counts — dedupes, and reports skipped rows with their line number. Nothing hits `/api/copyright/whitelist` until the admin presses **Confirm and whitelist**.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:compliance` all pass. `npx eslint` on the touched files is clean except the pre-existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on the copyright page's `loadAll()` effect.

The Gemini key is only read server-side from `GEMINI_API_KEY` (`src/lib/ai/gemini.ts`, `import "server-only"`) and is set directly in the server's `.env.local` — not in the repo, the client bundle, or any response.

author: vrwarp
body:
`Student.firstName` holds `Benson “蔡秉洲”` — first name and nickname joined — and the kiosk passed that field straight through to `{{firstName}}`. So the curly quotes and a second script went onto the `xl` line that exists to be read across a room, and being long, took the shrinker with them: once one line cannot fit, `labelRender` scales the whole block, so one child's second name costs every line on their sticker.

Nobody chose that. The token was a pass-through of a field whose shape had been decided elsewhere, for a different reason, and no comment in the printing path had ever mentioned nicknames.

## Why it went unquestioned

A false claim in the docs. `docs/planning-center.md` said Planning Center composes a display name as `first_name “nickname” last_name` and that Tally "follows that exactly, so the name on a roster row is the name on the profile page."

Planning Center does no such thing. It keeps the two fields apart and composes neither into its own `name` — a person with `first_name: "Benson"` and `nickname: "蔡秉洲"` comes back as `name: "Benson Tsai"`. That is what a real API response shows, and what this repo's own simulator has always emitted (`tools/pco-simulator/src/handler.ts`, `personResource`).

The composite is Tally's own convention. It earns its place on a roster row, because `searchName` is built from it and either spelling then finds the child — which matters in a bilingual congregation. It never earned a place on a sticker; the profile-page argument for putting it there was not true.

## What changed

- `{{firstName}}` resolves through `splitFirstName` → `Benson`. `{{nickname}}` joins the token list → `蔡秉洲`, so a gathering that wants both puts them on two lines at two sizes rather than one line at one.
- Token resolution moves to `src/kiosk/printing/tokens.ts` so it can be tested — `index.ts` imports WebUSB and a `?worker`, neither of which exists under vitest, and this rule is worth more than a mock of the transport. `index.ts` re-exports `tokenValuesFor`, so the module's surface is unchanged.
- The nickname resolves to `''` rather than absent, the same distinction `SPARSE_SAMPLE_VALUES` draws: empty is what a kiosk that looked and found none sends. Both read as nothing through `fillLabelTokens`, so a `{{nickname}}` line disappears for the children who have none.
- The label editor's full preview sample gains a nickname. Neither sample had one, which is why a leader could not have seen this before Sunday.

Nothing on the roster, in search, or in write-back changes.

For Benson, the default template goes from `Benson “蔡秉洲” T` — long enough to shrink the whole label — to `Benson T` at full `xl`.

## Docs

`docs/planning-center.md` now states what the API actually returns, and says plainly that the composite is Tally's convention rather than quietly deleting the wrong sentence — the belief that Tally was mirroring the profile page is what put the composite on labels in the first place.

A second paragraph blamed the double-render (`Benson “蔡秉洲” “蔡秉洲”`) on Planning Center rendering, when it is `displayFirstName` composing twice on the next read. The split-before-write invariant it argues for was always right; only the reason was wrong.

`docs/label-printing.md` gains a **Names with two halves** section, and the note that `{{nickname}}` is empty for most children so its line wants **Only if filled in**.

## Tests

author: fredriksknese
body:
Batch 4-0b of `docs/PRODUCTION-PLAN.md`. Unblocked by #30, which captured the Session Request this is measured against.

## The defect

For a Session Request or Session Created, i2pd covers packet bytes 16..64 — header bytes 16-31 (source connection ID and token) plus the 32-byte ephemeral key — in a **single 48-byte ChaCha20 pass**, zero nonce. This repository did two things wrong there:

* `ObfuscateEphemeralKey` restarted the keystream, XORing the key with bytes 0..32 where i2pd uses 16..48.
* The send paths called `EncryptLongHeaderInPacket`, which stops at byte 16 — so the source connection ID and token went out **in the clear**, and the receiver, which has always unmasked 0-31, hashed a header the sender never built.

## The evidence came first

The question was decided before a line of production code changed, by decoding #30's captured packet with an implementation independent of this repository (Python `cryptography`, not `SSU2HeaderEncryption`):

```
i2pd: one 48-byte pass over bytes 16..64  ->  payload Poly1305 tag VERIFIES
this repo: two restarted keystreams       ->  tag fails
```

**A verifying tag is not a claim about one field.** The AD is the 32 plaintext header bytes and the Noise hash covers X and the protocol name, so every byte of both had to match what i2pd hashed. The recovered plaintext is `DateTime(0x6a77a32d) + Padding(26)`, and header bytes 24-31 carry the token our own Retry issued.

`Ssu2SessionRequestVectorTest` then runs that packet through the production receive path. It was **confirmed red first**, with `AEAD authentication failed`.

## The fix

`ObfuscateEphemeralKey` takes keystream bytes 16..48; the four Session Request / Session Created send and parse paths use `EncryptLongHeaderComplete`. Composing the two reproduces i2pd's single call byte for byte — 48 bytes fit in one ChaCha20 block and both halves use the zero nonce.

**The 16-byte form is untouched**, per the constraint session 4 derived from the TokenRequest vector: TokenRequest, Retry and PeerTest are correct as they are, and the Retry path #29 proved against the real peer does not move.

## It was one defect, not two

As 4-0 predicted, this was also batch 3-3's unexplained C#-to-C# AEAD failure. The 3-3 loopback fixture goes `sent=1` → `sent=2`: Bob logs `SessionRequest received and validated` and answers with a Session Created.

Alice then drops that reply — `Unknown packet type 160`. That is a **separate** defect, recorded as batch **4-0h** and not fixed here: the type peek trial-decrypts with `k_header_2 =` the intro key, which is right for a Session Request and wrong for a Session Created, whose k_header_2 is `HKDF(chainKey, "SessCreateHeader")`. So `HandshakeCompletesOnACleanChannel` stays quarantined, failing one message later for a named reason.

## Recorded, not fixed

* **4-0i** — i2pd's handshake payload is SSU2 blocks (`00 0004 <ts> | fe 001a <pad>`); `BuildRequestPayload` writes a bare timestamp and both readers read one back. The captured plaintext is the reference.
* **4-0j** — `SendHolePunch` uses `Host.GetMyStaticKey()` where an intro key belongs, and masks 0-15 where receivers unmask 0-31. Unverified, and labelled as such.
* The PeerTest builder shares `ObfuscateEphemeralKey`, so its bytes 32-63 moved too. Not a regression: it writes an obfuscated key at the offset its own parser reads as AEAD ciphertext, so the two never agreed and nothing tests the pair. Folded into 4-0j.

## One quarantined test was deleted rather than un-quarantined

`SessionRequestObscuresItsSourceConnectionIdAndToken` asserted that bytes 16-31 are masked by calling the 16-byte primitive directly — but that primitive was never the defect; the Session Request path calling it was. Keeping it would have meant a test that passed throughout the defect's life. The assertion now lives on the message, against i2pd's keystream, in `OurSessionRequestMasksBytesSixteenToSixtyFourAsOnePass`.

## Verification

```
dotnet build -c Release i2p.sln   0 errors
UNIT                              293 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped   (was 288)
quarantined                       5 red, unchanged set
```

author: danstiner
body:
Per-spurt playout instrumentation for the receive path: playout latency from AudioTrack timestamps, underruns counted against a spurt-start baseline, concealment ticks for audible gaps, and per-speaker jitter-buffer depth — published as a `StateFlow` and logged alongside the existing `capture:` line.

Nothing consumes the flow yet. The log line is the only production consumer; the stats pages are the stated destination and the shape was cheap to get right now.

## Verified on a Pixel 7a (Android 17), against a local Mumble 1.5.915 server

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| Periodic mid-spurt sample | 11–12 samples per 12 s spurt at ~1.00 s cadence — the `WRITES_PER_SAMPLE` path, which no device run had reached before |
| Stale-timestamp guard | Never fired: zero `latency=n/a` in ~45 samples across four 3 s inter-spurt gaps, so `MAX_TIMESTAMP_AGE_NANOS = 1s` is correctly sized here |
| Underrun baseline | AudioTrack underran at every spurt start (`disabled due to previous underrun` ×9); all correctly absorbed into the baseline and published as 0 |
| Per-speaker depth | Real per-session values — 0 at end-of-spurt, 140–320 ms mid-spurt |
| Playout latency | 130–187 ms, median ~152 ms |
| `concealedTicks` | 0 in every sample — never exercised non-zero on hardware; unit tests only |

The AudioFlinger line earned its keep on first contact with a device:

```
track: buffer=3848f (asked 3848f) rate=48000 | device: burst=128f rate=48000 | quantum=480f
```

The track buffer is 80 ms — `getMinBufferSize` returns it, so the 2-quantum floor never binds — and the quantum is 3.75 device bursts, i.e. misaligned. With ~150 ms measured latency that is a tuning target, deliberately not addressed here.

## Fixes found while reviewing

- **The branch did not compile.** `67f42e0` gave `AndroidAudioOut` a `Context` for its debug log and clobbered the Hilt constructor doing so; the transport lambda bound positionally to `newCapture`. This is what CI has been failing on. Had it compiled it would have been worse than a build break — `newCapture` defaults to `{ null }` and `call` to `NoVoiceCall`, so push-to-talk capture and telecom registration would have silently vanished. Commits `67f42e0`..`d45ffd9` still do not build individually; the fix is on top rather than rebased in.
- **Two surviving mutants**, both mutation-verified. `underruns = underrunBaseline?.let { 0 }` was green across the whole suite — nothing moved the platform counter between the baseline read and the publish. And deleting `writesThisSpurt = 0` was green too: it does not stop sampling, it latches the counter above the threshold so the loop publishes on *every* write instead of every hundredth, a 100x rise in map allocation and string formatting on a `THREAD_PRIORITY_URGENT_AUDIO` thread.
- **Log consistency** with the `CaptureStats` sibling: formatting moved to `PlayoutStats.summary()`, logged at debug and ungated, so the numbers are readable off a release build.

## Known gap

`concealedTicks` counts only partial quanta (1..479). A speaker that comes up dry on a *whole* quantum ends the spurt instead, which neither counter registers. Observed once in a 12 s stream — depth collapsed 12480 → 960 with `underruns=0 concealed=0` and no platform underrun — and not reproduced on a second run, so it is a one-off hiccup, but the metric gap is real regardless of how often it fires.

Verification: `assembleDebug assembleRelease testDebugUnitTest verifyShippedGroups` green, 35/35 host C++ tests green.

author: kgarg2468
body:
Phase 2 (PR-16): human-authored epistemic status — **accepted / disputed / resolved / superseded** on lab-visible annotations. Transitions are never inferred; every one is a person's judgment on the record. - **Storage:** fields on the annotation row (`status`, `supersededBy`, `statusSetAt`, `statusSetBy`) — one value per note, needed for every card drawn, so an adjacent table would re-ask a question the margin query already answered. History lives in two new reference-only ledger variants, `annotation.status_set` and `annotation.status_cleared` — two variants, not one with an optional field, so a reader that forgets the optional can't report a verdict the lab retracted. - **Who:** the PI, or anyone who has presented a session about this paper (`canApprove`, called not restated). The note's author is deliberately excluded — an author recording that the lab accepted their own critique is the exact failure this permission exists to prevent. - **Private/withdrawn notes carry no status**, both sides: `setStatus` refuses them, and reads decide the audience off the annotation each time — flipping private takes the verdict off the wire in the same instant. The row is not cleared (the lab's ruling isn't the author's to erase by changing their mind about the audience), so re-sharing restores it. - **Supersession is a citation:** target constrained at write to lab-visible top-level notes on the same paper (zero extra reads to resolve — the target is already in the result set), re-checked with `isStillShared` on every read, redacted honestly ("Superseded · by a note that is no longer shared"). - **UI:** a word-mark in the type badge's micro-caps, full ink, no pill — under the note, above the marks, in the order the three things happened. The control rides an existing query's `canSetStatus`; Superseded opens a menu of exactly the notes the server will accept. Flagged follow-ups: briefs/digests/synthesis don't read status yet (the brief's carried-over section is the highest-value consumer — "unresolved" is now a stored fact); outcomes-that-settle and notes-marked-resolved are the same event in two unlinked places; only direct supersession cycles (A↔B) are refused; no status-history panel yet (`events` lacks a `by_annotation` index). Verification: lint, `tsc --noEmit`, `typecheck:convex`, full vitest (privacy guard included), build — all green on current main. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

 The PR adds human-authored epistemic statuses to lab-visible annotations, including persisted provenance, ledger events, permission checks, supersession references, and status controls in the annotation UI. - Stores accepted, disputed, resolved, and superseded states on annotations. - Restricts status changes to PIs and presenters of sessions that have begun. - Records status-set and status-cleared events. - Redacts supersession citations when their target is no longer shared. - Adds transition, rendering, and presenter-standing tests.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | convex/annotations.ts | Adds status projection and mutation logic; the presenter-standing fix now excludes scheduled and cancelled sessions consistently on both read and write paths. | | lib/epistemic/status.ts | Defines the status vocabulary, rendering helpers, transition validation, and lifecycle predicate that grants standing only for live, ended, or synthesized sessions. | | lib/epistemic/status.test.ts | Covers status coherence and verifies that scheduled and cancelled sessions do not confer presenter standing. | | convex/schema.ts | Adds annotation status fields and immutable status-set and status-cleared event variants. | | app/(app)/app/library/[paperId]/read/_components/epistemic-status.tsx | Adds status display and controls using the server-provided authorization result and valid supersession candidates. | | app/(app)/app/library/[paperId]/read/_components/annotation-card.tsx | Integrates the status line and control into annotation cards. |

author: carbon-teq
body:
## What changed

- Start GRPO actor-update telemetry only after TRL finishes rollout generation,
  reward scoring, zero-gradient filtering, and active-sampling refill.
- Keep the phase idempotent across gradient-accumulation microbatches for the
  same optimizer step while preserving cross-step overlap detection.
- Retain rollout timing for every candidate batch and actor timing only for the
  selected training batch.
- Prepare the coordinated Posttrain 0.3.4 patch release and update the living
  OLMo 3 qualification plan.

## Why

The released OLMo 3 canary passed the corrected Qwen 3.5 LoRA actor/sampler
parity gate, then requested a second candidate batch during active sampling.
Posttrain had opened actor-update telemetry when the first candidate rollout
returned, so the refill was incorrectly classified as a concurrent actor
update and the run failed before optimization.

TRL owns the real boundary in `_prepare_inputs`: it returns only after candidate
generation, filtering, and refill have produced the retained batch. The adapter
now opens actor telemetry at that boundary.

## Developer impact

OLMo 3 and other active-sampling GRPO runs can refill zero-gradient groups
without a false actor-update overlap. Observatory phase durations also
distinguish rollout work from forward/backward optimization correctly.

body:
v3.62.2. A trace of the whole information flow against the product model, then the smallest change that fixes what was actually broken.

## The headline: most of the model is already implemented

I traced each item before touching code. Seven of them are already done and tested — details in the table below. **The two genuine violations were both in the Brand Book**, and one of them was worse than a duplicate.

## What was broken

### Brand name — a control that discarded your typing

`brandName` read `detective.clientName || project.name` and `setBrandName` wrote `project.name`. **Two different fields.** On any project where the client had answered chapter 01, the box showed their answer, accepted an edit, renamed the project underneath, then re-rendered the client's answer over the top. No error, no toast, nothing to notice.

Now read-only with a route to the Brief. `setBrandName` and its `renameProject` wiring are deleted rather than left looking functional.

### Colours — a second authoring home for the canonical palette

Name, hex, add, remove. It wrote the real `palette`/`paletteTokens` through `setPaletteTokens`, so it was never a second *store* — it was a second *home*, which is the rule `bookContent.js` exists to hold.

**Naming was the one thing it could do that the Colour bench could not.** So naming *moved* to Colour, beside the hexes it names, through the same single writer. Deleting the editor without moving it would have removed the only way to name a colour anywhere in the app.

The swatch, name and hex still **show** in the book — an output surface has to display what it will print; it just may not be where the value is decided.

## Trace results — what was already correct

| Item | Status | Canonical source, traced |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Identity consumes the Brief | **Already done** | `briefWords.js` — resolve-never-copy. `BRIEF_WORD_SOURCES` maps voice→`toneOfVoice`, promise/proof→`messaging*`, personality→`brandAsPerson`. Effective value shown, override on type, nothing copied. |
| 2 · Artboard left, tool right, live | **Already done** | `design-artboard-column` + `design-edit-column`, `editable`, on all four sub-screens. Preview screen was removed for this reason. |
| 3 · Mark concepts + existingAssets | **Already done** | `logoConcepts[]`; `existingMarks` reads `detective.existingAssetsFiles`, gated to `rebrand`/`extend`. |
| 4 · accessibilityNeeds → Color | **Already done** | `contrastTargetFor(detective)` → `strict` raises AA→AAA. Threaded to rows, health score, pass-pairs and Fix so they can't disagree. |
| 5 · Type hierarchy | **Already done** | `typeSpecimen.js` — Display/Heading/Subhead/Body/Caption at real px, brand colours, on paper. Fallback warnings intact. |
| 6 · strategyAttributes seeded | **Already done** | `strategySeed.js` — 3 of 4 spectrums mapped; High-end↔Affordable deliberately unmapped (no price axis) rather than bent onto formality. |
| 7 · `project.positioning` | **Already done** | Own field, never `project.brief`. Pinned by `positioningOwnership.test.js`. |
| 11 · competitors → Research | **Already done** | One-tap competitor pins from the brief. |

author: arvindhkumarss
body: ## Root cause Commits were writing correctly to git, but reload fetched JSON from **GitHub Pages**, which is served with `Cache-Control: max-age=600`. After a partial save, a reload within that window could show empty/stale balance and pending credits — even though the data was already on `main`. Worse, the next commit merged against that stale in-memory snapshot and could overwrite good remote data. ## Fixes - When a PAT is configured, load data from the **GitHub Contents API** (authoritative, no Pages CDN cache) - Pages fallback uses `cache: 'no-store'` + cache-bust query params - Every write path refreshes from git first, then merges - Balance footprint shows `live from GitHub` when API-loaded ## Transactions tab Read-only cumulative view of all unique committed transactions: - Mapped apartment credits - Expenditures (with category) - Interest - Pending credits still awaiting tags Filter + **Reload from GitHub** button included.

author: jcosta33
body:
A freshly added Dutch Oven ran `damping = 0.0005` while the Damp knob's **reset target** and `DEFAULT_PARAMS.damping` both said `0.3`. Because `addDevice` pushes the descriptor value to the engine at add time, 0.0005 was what a new instance actually sounded like. This moves the descriptor and the Rust constructor to 0.3, leaves `DEFAULT_PARAMS` and the panel knob where they are, and empties the census exemption that recorded the disagreement.

The knob's *readout* was never part of the disagreement, and an earlier revision of this PR said it was. The knob displays the stored value through `Math.round(v * 100)`, so an old device read **0%** and agreed with the engine. That agreement is why nobody found this by looking: 0.0005 and a true zero are the same three characters on screen. What disagreed with the descriptor and the constructor were the two *reset/default* declarations — `ProofChamberState.ts:47` and `ProofChamberPanel.tsx:809`. Both now pinned by execution in `proofChamberDampingDefaultGrid.spec.tsx`: at 0.0005 the cell reads `0%`, at 0.3 it reads `30%`.

Closes #1546

## What the change measures

Stimulus: a unit impulse into the plate at `mix = 1`, everything else at its constructor value, 4 s at 48 kHz. The figure is 6–12 kHz band power against 400–1200 Hz band power, taken over an early window (0.55–1.0 s) and a late window (1.5–3.0 s) of the same tail. The two bands have different widths, so the absolute number is a yardstick rather than a flatness measure; what carries the claim is how it moves between the two windows.

| damping | early 0.55–1.0 s | late 1.5–3.0 s | HF loss across the tail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.0005 (what shipped) | +5.10 dB | **+0.21 dB** | 4.88 dB |
| 0.15 | +3.47 dB | −3.46 dB | 6.94 dB |
| **0.3 (this change)** | +1.21 dB | **−8.45 dB** | 9.66 dB |
| 0.5 | −3.14 dB | −18.28 dB | 15.15 dB |

At the value the Dutch Oven shipped, the 6–12 kHz band was **louder than the midrange two seconds into the tail**. At 0.3 it sits 8.45 dB below it.

This table was measured here rather than taken from #1546, and #1546's own table is **not** corroboration for it. That table is not reproducible under this method or under the independent 8th-order Butterworth harness review ran against it: its early column is nearly flat where both methods swing 7–9 dB, its stimulus differs, and its arithmetic is internally inconsistent (4.20 − 2.07 = 2.13, listed as −2.14, under an inverted sign convention). The issue's *conclusion* stands on the evidence measured here; its numbers should not be cited.

Two render digests move as a direct consequence, and both are re-measured in the same commit as the constructor edit rather than widened or deleted:

* `plate_parameter_surface.rs::UNTOUCHED_PLATE_DIGEST` — `0x9107053e51407165` → `0x15ca3842cec55de2`
* `algorithm_switch_parameter_retention.rs::UNTOLD_INSTANCE_DIGEST` — `0xdd9383f3187eb942` → `0xaf2403b19139eb46`

**Confinement.** Forcing `damping` back to `0.0005` at head — nothing else touched — and restoring both constants to their pre-change values makes both digest tests pass again: `cargo test -p proof-chamber --test plate_parameter_surface --test algorithm_switch_parameter_retention` exit 0, 14 and 13 tests, 0 failed. The entire digest delta is the damping change; nothing else moved.

## The bandwidth filter directly above it: it stays

The line above the damping seed is `bandwidth_filter: OnePole::new(1.0 - 0.9995)`, whose coefficient is numerically the same 0.0005. The issue asked whether both filters had been switched off from the same Dattorro bring-up row. They had not, and the reasoning is now written beside the line in `proof_chamber.rs`.

**Topology.** `left_damp` and `right_damp` sit inside the tank's recirculating path, so their coefficient compounds once per circulation — hundreds of times across a three-second tail. That is why 0.0005 there is still measurable (4.88 dB of HF loss above) and 0.3 is a different reverb. `bandwidth_filter` sits on the input, ahead of the diffusers, with no feedback around it, and is applied exactly once per sample. Measured by driving the real `OnePole` at DC and at Nyquist, its worst-case attenuation anywhere below Nyquist is **0.0087 dB** — the tail's HF loss is more than a thousand times that. The same literal in the two positions is not the same amount of filtering.

**No contradicted claim.** `damping` contradicted its own reset target and the module default — `ProofChamberPanel.tsx:809` and `ProofChamberState.ts:47`, both 0.3 — and that contradiction is what made it a defect rather than a preference. `bandwidth` has no reset target, no module default, no descriptor entry, no `set_param` arm and no control, so there is nothing for it to contradict. The user-facing treble control on this path is the output stage's 12 kHz `high_cut`.

**The paper does not separate the two, and an earlier revision of this PR claimed it did.** Table 1 reads:

```
 bandwidth = 0.9995        High-frequency attenuation on input; full bandwidth = 0.9999999
 damping   = 0.0005        High-frequency damping; no damping = 0.0
```

Both rows list a near-neutral preset value and name their own neutral extreme, and §1.3.5 gives both filters the same recommended range 0.0 to 0.9999999. `"1 = all-pass"` does not appear in the bandwidth row — "all-pass" in the paper refers to the diffuser lattices. So `0.0005` is the paper's choice too, the transcription was correct, and "one literal is the paper's choice; the other was the paper's bypass" was wrong. The claim is withdrawn from the source comments, the descriptor comment and this body. The split rests on the two legs above; the case for moving `damping` is a product case — it contradicted its reset target, that reset target was the only route back to an off-grid value, and it does not render like a plate — not a claim that the paper was misread.

**Enforced on the running engine, not on the source text.** `proof_chamber::tests::the_input_bandwidth_filter_has_no_audible_authority_on_the_running_engine` constructs the engine, renders a block, reads `self.bandwidth_filter.coeff` back off it, and measures the real `OnePole`'s magnitude at DC and at Nyquist — then repeats after writing every name in `param_names()` across its range. The first revision of this guard parsed the constructor literal instead, which proves nothing about the engine: this file's own `left_damp: OnePole::new(0.3)` is a dead literal, because `process()` overwrites `.coeff` every block. M6b below is the mutation that exposed it.

## 0.3 is on the knob's grid — checked by reading it back

`RotaryKnob.quantize` snaps every write onto `min + round((raw − min) / step) × step`, and the Damp knob is `step={0.001}`, so an off-grid value is left behind permanently by the first nudge of the control.

`0.3` being on that lattice is not something to settle by inspection — `300 × 0.001` is `0.30000000000000004`, and it is only `toPrecision(15)` inside `quantize` that pulls it back. So `proofChamberDampingDefaultGrid.spec.tsx` renders the real panel and reads the numbers back out of it, comparing with `Object.is`:

* the Damp knob's `aria-valuenow` is exactly `0.3`, and its cell reads `30%`;
* at the old default the same knob reads `aria-valuenow="0.0005"` and a cell of `0%` — the invisibility, pinned;
* ArrowUp from the shipped default sends exactly `0.301`, and ArrowDown from `0.301` sends exactly `0.3` — the same bit pattern the device booted with;
* alt-click reset from `0.62` sends exactly `0.3`;
* and the same walk from `0.0005` lands on `0.002` then `0.001`, never back on `0.0005` — the failing case, kept so the walk above is not vacuous.

The other legs are welded where they live, each read back rather than restated: `declaredDefaultConsensus.spec.ts` compares descriptor, module declaration and panel reset literal; `proofChamberParamMapClosure.spec.ts` gains a `damping` row comparing `DEFAULT_PARAMS` against the Rust constructor literal it parses out of t

author: gruberchris
body:
Two of the three remaining M5 items.

The audit log
-------------
Authorization decisions are recorded inside Auth::require -- the one function every check funnels through, whether it came from a REST route, an MCP tool, the change-stream upgrade or a vector endpoint. audit.mode selects off, denials (default), writes or all.

Emitted from the check rather than from each route, for the same reason the check lives in one place: a log each handler has to remember to write is a log with holes in it, and nothing about a missing audit line says it is missing. A new route is audited by virtue of being authorized at all.

denials is the default because all writes one line per authorized operation, which on a read-heavy node is one per request -- a real cost an operator should opt into. off would mean nobody gets the event they actually want. search and watch count as reads at the writes level: one ranks documents and the other observes them, and an auditor asking what changed does not want either.

Authentication is not in this stream. A failed login is not an authorization decision -- there is no principal yet -- and mixing them would make "denied" mean two things in one stream. It is counted as kimmy_auth_failures_total instead.

An unknown mode fails at startup: a typo would otherwise produce a server that records nothing, which looks exactly like a server nobody has attacked.

Records go to the kimmy::audit tracing target so they can be routed separately, and carry user, action, db, collection, decision and unauthenticated -- the last distinguishing "root did this" from "the server was started with authentication disabled".

Richer metrics
--------------
Uptime, request and response-class counters, storage size, and counters for authorization denials, authentication failures, rate limiting and backups served.

The three specific counters are derived from the response status in one middleware rather than incremented where the refusal happens. Each of those statuses has exactly one source -- 401 from credentials or tokens, 403 from ApiError::forbidden which only RBAC returns, 429 from the limiter -- so deriving them means a new route is counted by existing, where a counter beside a check is one somebody forgets to bump.

Counters render at zero rather than appearing on first use, so a dashboard shows "nothing has gone wrong yet" instead of "no data". Still no per-collection series: /metrics is unauthenticated and a series per collection would put the schema on it.

Latency histograms and oplog lag are deliberately absent and documented as such. A histogram needs buckets chosen from measurements that exist for the storage layer but not for end-to-end requests, and lag needs a peer's version vector the API layer does not hold. Both are worth doing and neither is worth guessing.

Driven on a live node: at mode=writes the two admin actions and the write were recorded, the refusal was recorded, and the find was correctly absent; at mode=denials the same traffic produced exactly one record. kimmy_authz_denied_total matched the single 403.

677 -> 687 tests.

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Problem

SSE clients can disconnect while `EventStreamService.publish` is mid-loop. The old code only caught `IOException`; a disconnect could surface as another runtime exception, and the removed/stale emitter was never dropped from the `emitters` set, so publish kept pushing to (and accumulating) dead connections. `completeWithError` could also throw `IllegalStateException` if the emitter had already completed.

## Fix

- In `EventStreamService.publish`, catch `Exception` (not just `IOException`) and remove the failed emitter from the set before completing with error.
- Wrap `completeWithError` in a try/catch for `IllegalStateException` so a concurrently completed emitter cannot abort the publish loop.
- Add `EventStreamServiceTest` with 2 tests: stale/errored emitter is removed from the set, and healthy emitters continue to receive events after one fails.

## Files changed

- `Backend/src/main/java/com/sandeep/eventrabackend/service/EventStreamService.java`
- `Backend/src/test/java/com/sandeep/eventrabackend/service/EventStreamServiceTest.java`

## Testing

- New `EventStreamServiceTest` (2 tests) passes — verifies stale emitter removal and that healthy emitters are still served.
- Existing `EventStreamTests` suite passes.
- Verified against the pre-existing backend compile-error workaround (stubs reverted; not part of this PR).

body:
## Summary

Adds five configurable libretro core options for the NicaiEmu core, following
the same registration/application pattern used by the sibling emulator cores:

| Option | Default | Choices | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audio Volume (%) | 100 | 100..0 step 10 | Master playback volume (maps to `NicaiMachine::set_volume`) |
| Key Auto-Repeat Delay (frames) | 10 | 0-60 | Frames a held key waits before auto-repeat |
| Key Auto-Repeat Period (frames) | 15 | 1-30 | Frames between repeat pulses |
| Touch/Pointer Input | enabled | enabled/disabled | Whether mouse/touchscreen taps reach the guest |
| CPU/HLE Debug Logging | disabled | disabled/enabled | Forwards debug-level core logs to the frontend log |

## Implementation

- New `libretro/options.rs`: option registration via
  `RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_SET_VARIABLES`, reading via `GET_VARIABLE`, change
  detection via `GET_VARIABLE_UPDATE`, and parsing with default
  fallback/clamping plus unit tests.
- `api.rs`: registers options in `retro_set_environment` and applies them on
  load, on runtime changes in `retro_run`, and after `retro_reset`; touch
  input gates the pointer poll.
- `constants.rs`: adds the variable environment command constants.
- `logger.rs`: adds `set_debug_logging` to toggle debug records in the log
  bridge.
- `nicaiemu_libretro.info`: advertises `core_options = "true"`.
- `README.md` and `docs/RetroArch-Core.md`: document the new options
  (Core Options section).

## Verification

- libretro crate: 15 unit tests pass; the real-content integration test
  (requires `NICAI_GAME_DIR`) is unchanged and ignored.
- Workspace tests: 32 (nicaiemu) + 43 (nicaiemu-core) + 15 (libretro) pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean (also
  enforced by the pre-commit hook).

author: cwisecarver
body:
> **This PR exists to run CI. It is not a request to merge.**
>
> A2 is unproven and stays off `main` until it is decided to work — the position `8453de3` took
> deliberately, and nothing here changes it. **Merging this would put `aaf6d82`'s
> `sqlite3_wal_hook` back on every tenant connection**, which is the specific thing that revert
> called out as most wanting removal. Leave it in draft.

Phase 2 **A2 — quorum replication**: ship WAL frames to N followers and gate a tenant's commit on
Q acks. Closes node-loss RPO from ~300 s to ~0, and it is the only thing that does.

**Off by default** (`REPLICATION_ENABLED`), like every other Phase 2 component. With the gate off,
nothing in the default hot path changes.

## Both design gates cleared, measured

- **A frame seam exists.** `sqlite3_wal_hook` is reachable from the loadable extension fathom
  already ships. Incremental WAL shipping works on **stock SQLite** — no libSQL, no engine swap,
  no NIF. The receive half too: byte-range deltas appended to a follower's `-wal`.
- **The ack cost is known.** Against the `hrana_rt_us` 127 µs baseline: healthy 2-of-4 = **96 µs**.
  With two stragglers, 2-of-4 = **185 µs** against 4-of-4 = **5 994 µs**.

**The result that should drive deployment:** a quorum skips the *slowest* replicas, so it buys
nothing unless a quorum's worth are near. Four equidistant followers ⇒ 2-of-4 tracked 4-of-4
exactly at every latency. Two near + two far ⇒ 2-of-4 at **1.6 ms** against 4-of-4 at **134 ms**.
Same replicas, **82×**. Placement is the decision; replica count is not.

## What's here

| | |
|---|---|
| `Protocol` | Explicit binary wire format — no `binary_to_term` on socket bytes. |
| `FollowerLog` | Pure accept/reject. Every way a follower can corrupt a shard is a branch here. |
| `Quorum` | Pure counting. `Q < N` enforced at construction **and** at boot. |
| `Shipper` / `Follower` | One socket per follower **node**, not per shard (millions of shards ⇒ millions of sockets otherwise). |
| `Session` | Commit-path integration. Per-shard serialization point, per-follower offsets. |
| `Promote` | Replica → primary. Standalone, **not** wired into cold open. |
| `Fleet` | Membership + liveness reporting. |

## The four bugs worth reading about

Found while finishing per-follower catch-up. Each ships with a test that fails without its fix.

1. **A follower that was already current got dropped from the quorum instead of counted.** The push
   list shrinks to the laggards while `Q` stays put, so `Quorum.new/2` refused `q >= n` *inside a
   tenant's commit* — a config guard firing on a per-commit subset.
2. **The deep one: a follower's reply almost always arrives while the session is idle**, so
   `handle_info`'s catch-all silently ate it. Consequences looked exactly like replication bugs and
   were not: a follower stuck one delta behind permanently if writes stopped, and a never-seeded
   follower whose seeding depended on whether its reply beat the quorum.
3. A late ACK was discarded even when drained.
4. `reconcile` read the generation off the record it already had, so a follower it had no record
   for — a late joiner — had its correction thrown away.

## Safety properties pinned by tests

- **A partial seed is never installed.** Chunks land in `.seeding` temps, renamed only on
  `seed_end`. An interrupted seed leaves *no* state, so the follower re-seeds — rather than a
  database missing pages that opens cleanly and reads wrong.
- **Promotion refuses when a live node holds the lease.** Two primaries is the one outcome worse
  than a stale one. The fence is the lease epoch; the old primary's pushes then get `:stale_epoch`.
- **A failed promotion cannot leak the lease** (released in an `after` — the shape of every lock
  leak AGENTS.md records in the coordinator).
- **Liveness never filters the per-commit push set.** A structural test reads `session.ex` and
  fails if it ever does — shrinking `n` is how bug 1 comes back.
- **`promotes writes that never reached storage`** is the one that matters: write rows, replicate,
  never flush, delete the primary's files, promote, read them back. Nothing asserted the RPO claim
  before this.

Every new test was run against the unfixed code and confirmed failing first. Anything touching the
quorum was run 8–10× — two of the four bugs above presented as ~50% flakes, and a single green run
would have hidden both.

## Known gaps, named not hidden

- **Promotion is not wired into cold open** — the actual RPO~0 payoff. `warm_or_cold_pull/2`
  validates a local copy by proving it *equals* the stored object; a replica is deliberately
  fresher, so it needs a different provenance story. Next piece of work.
- Followers are a static config list. No per-shard follower sets, no zone-aware placement.
- Chunked seeding bounds **memory**, not head-of-line blocking: one socket per follower node
  carries every shard.
- `docs/a2-quorum-replication.md` on `main` still asserts "There is no seam to ship a frame from",
  which both gates disproved.

## Verification

`mix precommit` green — **1497 passed**. `[skip-bench]` throughout: replication is gated off, so
the default hot path is unchanged.

49 files, +6762/−64.

author: irfndi
body:
Fixes #201

## Problem

An exit settlement's sell amount is fixed at creation and never reconciled with the live wallet balance. A concurrent entry consumed part of the wallet USDC the pending settlement still expected (41.91 USDC expected, 24.35 in wallet): every swap attempt failed simulation ("Swap simulation failed" — insufficient balance) 130 times, the job went terminal, and the orphan sweep could not recover it — `backedMints` includes open-position legs, and the two HYPE/USDC positions made ALL wallet USDC "position-backed" even though position liquidity lives in the position account. Result: $24.35 (25% of live equity) permanently stranded.

## Fix

1. **Settlement amount clamp** (`processSettlementJobs`): the sell amount is clamped to `min(job amount, live wallet balance)` before quoting. A partial balance persists through the retryable job (next attempt quotes what exists); a fully-consumed balance terminalizes with a clear error instead of looping; a failed balance read fails open; partial adapters fail open instead of defecting.
2. **Amount-aware sweep backing** (`sweepOrphanSettlements`): position backing no longer exempts a mint that has a stranded-terminal job — the terminal job's unspent balance proves the wallet-held excess was never sold, so the sweep revives it with the LIVE wallet amount. Active-job backing still suppresses (an in-flight job owns the mint).
3. **Entry prep reserves pending settlement claims** (`entry-prep-service`): the spendable balance subtracts non-final settlement job amounts per mint, so a new entry can no longer consume funds an exit settlement is about to sell. `EntryPrepLive` now takes `DbService` (wired through `buildLayer` and test layers).

## Verification

- New regression tests: processor clamps the quote amount to the wallet balance; zero-balance terminalizes without quoting; the sweep revives a terminal job despite position backing with the live wallet amount; entry prep rejects with `INSUFFICIENT_USDC_BALANCE` when a pending claim makes the USDC leg unaffordable.
- `bun run lint` clean; `bun run test` 123 files / 1610 tests pass.

## Summary by Sourcery

Reconcile autonomous exit settlements with the live wallet balance to prevent stranded funds and infinite retry loops.

Bug Fixes:
- Clamp settlement sell amounts to the current wallet balance when processing jobs, terminalizing settlements whose balances have been fully consumed instead of repeatedly failing swaps.
- Adjust orphan settlement sweeping so wallet-held excess for a mint is revived even when that mint is position-backed, while still avoiding double-selling mints with active jobs.
- Reserve pending non-final settlement job amounts from entry preparation spendable balances so new entries cannot consume funds that existing settlements expect to sell.

Enhancements:
- Wire database access into the entry preparation service and runtime to support settlement-aware balance calculations.
- Extend autonomous runtime and sweep logic with wallet and position awareness to better model live holdings at execution time.

Documentation:
- Document the settlement reconciliation behaviour and its safeguards in the unreleased CHANGELOG entry.

Tests:
- Add regression tests covering clamped quote amounts, terminalization on zero wallet balance, orphan sweep revival of terminal jobs with wallet-held excess, and entry preparation failures when pending settlement claims exhaust USDC balance.
- Update existing autonomous token and entry-prep tests to mock wallet balances and DB services required for the new reconciliation logic.

author: awdawmip
featheranalytics
body:
**Returning visitors are still broken and this fixes them.** Switching the server to `no-cache` fixed new visitors only — it cannot reach a cache entry a browser already holds under `immutable, max-age=31536000`, which is a year-long licence to skip revalidation. Not even a hard reload overrides it.

So anyone who loaded the site before that change keeps pairing year-old geometry with a fresh manifest, and sees the same holes in the map. I changed the header and called it fixed. That was wrong.

**The fix:** a cache entry is keyed by the whole URL, query string included. Appending `?c=1` makes every payload a URL no browser has ever held, so the poisoned entries are unreachable and expire unused.

- **Verified against the live bucket** — R2 serves the query form identically: 200 and the same headers for `tiles/`, `meta.json`, `zone_ids` and `boundaries.json`
- **Applied at the two choke points** every payload passes through, plus the three raw fetches that bypass them
- **Audited** — no fetch of a data URL is left unbusted
- **No export needed** — the payloads are unchanged, only the URLs asking for them

It is a constant, not a versioning scheme. Freshness is `no-cache`'s job now; this exists only to escape entries written before it.

author: surajverma
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to the reminders/calendar functionality, adding support for multi-day and all-day reminders, soft deletion (trash), and new endpoints for marking reminders as done and undoing. It also enhances the UI and API to handle these new fields, improves validation, and updates the documentation to reflect the new features.

**Reminders and Calendar Enhancements:**

* Added support for multi-day reminders with new fields: `start_date`, `start_time`, `end_date`, `end_time`, and `all_day` to the `reminder` table and API. This allows reminders to span multiple days and be marked as all-day events. 
* Implemented soft deletion (trash) for reminders using a new `deleted_at` field, with automatic purging of trashed reminders older than 7 days.
* Added endpoints to mark reminders as done, undo completion, and snooze reminders (`/api/reminders/<id>/done`, `/undo`), including permission checks.

**Validation and Utility Improvements:**

* Improved date/time parsing and validation with helper functions for time parsing, boolean conversion, and range validation, ensuring correct handling of start/end dates and times.
* Updated API endpoints for creating and updating reminders to use the new fields and validation logic, supporting both legacy and new data formats.

**Documentation and Configuration:**

* Updated `README.md` with instructions for enabling the shared calendar and configuring the weekly grid start day, and documented the new `calendar` feature toggle.

**Calendar UI and Data Handling:**

* Enhanced calendar event counting logic to display multi-day reminders correctly in the calendar view.
* Filtered out soft-deleted reminders from API responses to prevent trashed items from appearing in the UI.

These changes significantly improve the flexibility and usability of the reminders/calendar system, making it more robust and user-friendly.

author: rob-p
body:
Part of #1085 — its map-side half. The quant-side half landed with #1099.

**This is the first change out of this audit with an unambiguous end-to-end win.** 10M human fragments, reads path, `-p 16`, interleaved, warm-up discarded:

| | mean | sd |
| --- | --- | --- |
| develop | 28.845 s | 0.317 |
| this PR | **28.156 s** | 0.218 |

**−0.689 s (−2.39%), t = −5.28**, 95% CI −0.950 … −0.428, faster in **9 of 9 rounds**. Worth stating against the run of nulls in #1092: every other structural item measured |t| ≲ 2 with a CI straddling zero. This one does not.

It is also the size the microbenchmark predicts — dedup runs once per fragment, and at typical n the scan is 7–8× faster than allocating a map (8.2 ns vs 61.0 ns at n=4); ~50 ns × 10M ≈ 0.5 s.

## What changed

**Deduplicating raw mappings by transcript** allocated an `AHashMap` per fragment to handle what is typically 1 to 20 entries. Now a hybrid, split at the measured crossover:

| n / distinct | AHashMap | prefix scan | reused table |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 / 4 | 61.0 ns | **8.2** | 38.5 |
| 20 / 12 | 231.5 | **29.1** | 104.7 |
| 60 / 30 | 513.9 | **173.6** | 270.4 |
| 100 / 50 | 851.9 | **399.7** | 429.3 |
| 128 / 64 | 1325 | 752.3 | **586.7** |
| 160 / 80 | 1439 | 1004.5 | **591.5** |

`DEDUP_HASH_THRESHOLD = 112`, the midpoint of the crossing interval, with a `const` assertion that it stays in a range where both paths are reachable in a real run.

**`best_per_target`** allocated an `AHashSet` per call; it now scans the kept prefix in place, preserving both the survivor and the highest-coverage-first ordering.

## The part that took two attempts

The tie rule is load-bearing. The map replaced an entry only on a **strictly** greater score, so among equal scores on one transcript the first in arrival order survived — and those records carry different positions, so a different survivor shifts the fragment's bias and fragment-length weights.

My first attempt sorted by `(tid, score, ref_pos)`. Every `sample_data` check passed, and it **silently changed 55 equivalence classes** on 10M human fragments (407,855 vs 407,800) — small enough to miss, large enough to matter. Only the human-scale byte comparison caught it.

Both paths now apply the original rule, with a test asserting they agree on cases loaded with ties, negative-controlled by flipping the table path to `>=` (fails on a 2-mapping case).

Conversely the survivors' *order* is **not** part of the contract, which is worth recording: the map being replaced was seeded per process (`ahash` `runtime-rng`), and develop is byte-identical across separate runs regardless, so the order it yielded cannot be load-bearing.

## Scratch, not thread-local

`DedupScratch` is threaded through 4 signatures rather than held in a `thread_local`. On 200 mappings:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| threaded parameter | **768 ns** |
| `thread_local` | 839 ns |
| fresh allocation per fragment | 1468 ns |

Reuse is what matters most — allocating on demand is 1.9× worse — and the parameter recovers the remaining ~10% that the lazy-init check and `RefCell` borrow cost (a `HashTable` has a `Drop`, so a bare const-init TLS is not available). `QuantProcessor` already owns a `RecordScratch` from #1099, so it has a natural home; the two convenience wrappers that allocate their own `out` allocate a scratch too, which costs them nothing relative to what they return.

Hashing is `ahash` with fixed seeds. `hashbrown::HashTable` takes the hash from the caller and has no default hasher, so `std`'s SipHash is not reachable here.

## Verification

- `quant.sf` **byte-identical** to develop on 10M human fragments (407,800 eq-classes, 9,221,625 mapped)
- byte-identical on `sample_data` across plain / `--seqBias --gcBias --posBias` / `--softclip` / `--sketch`
- full suite, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, fmt clean

## Not touched

`cfg.chain.clone()`, which #1085 lists among "4 or more Vecs per fragment". `ChainConfig` is `{i32, i32, f32, usize}` — a ~24-byte POD copy, not heap traffic. Same false positive as the `PiscemStreamingQuery` item already withdrawn in that issue.

author: asiawright1122-boop
body:
把「账号里那个遗留 Cloudflare Pages 项目」从待确认项变成已记录事实。纯文档改动，`deploy-cloudflare.yml` 有 `paths-ignore: docs/**`，合并不会触发部署。

## 起因

`CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_DEPLOYMENT.md` 原本把三件事列为「到 Dashboard 里确认」，并警告「如果域名还指向旧 Pages 项目，那么即使 GitHub Action 成功执行了 `wrangler deploy`，公网访问的也还是旧站」。这个警告一直悬着没人回填结论。

2026-08-08 用只读查询查清了，结论写进文档。

## 查清了什么

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 绑定域名 | `u2tool.pages.dev`、`u2tool.com`、`www.u2tool.com` |
| 部署触发 | Git 集成，**不在** `.github/workflows/` 任何文件里 |
| `pages_build_output_dir` | `dist` |
| Pages 侧响应 | `/` 与 `/en/tools/` 均 404 |
| 实际服务生产的 | Worker |

那个警告**当前不成立**：公网访问到的是 Worker 的新站。判据是 `x-u2tool-html-cache` 响应头——`src/middleware.ts` 设的，Pages 产不出来。`www` 返回 200 且带该头，apex 301 到 `www`。

## 这个项目是坏的，不只是闲置

`pages_build_output_dir` 是 `dist`，但 Astro `output: 'server'` 产出的是 `dist/client` + `dist/server`。Pages 服务的 `dist/` 根目录里既没有 `index.html`，也没有 `_redirects`。

两个后果：每次 push 白烧一遍构建（Git 集成独立于 `deploy-cloudflare.yml`）；以及一旦 Worker route 失效，Pages 会静默接管这两个域名并对整站返回 404。

## 没有动任何基础设施

我一度打算「解绑自定义域名、保留项目」，查完 DNS 后放弃了。

`u2tool.com` 与 `www.u2tool.com` 都解析到 zone 的通用 anycast IP（`104.21.72.162` / `172.67.153.36`），而 Cloudflare 对已代理记录会隐藏 CNAME 链。所以**从公网无法区分**这两条记录是 Pages 绑定时自动创建的、还是独立记录。若是前者，解绑会连带删掉 DNS 记录导致整站解析失败——比原本要规避的风险严重得多。而手头令牌只有 `zone (read)`、没有 `dns (write)`，出问题无法自行回滚。删项目有同一个未解决的风险。

用一个不可逆且无法回滚的操作，去消除一个当前完全无害（被 Worker 完整遮蔽）的隐患，代价与收益不对等。因此文档把「先在 Dashboard 确认两条 DNS 记录各自来源」记为清理的前置条件，而不是在这里动手。

## 验证

- 全程只读查询，生产未受影响
- `pages download config` 在 `/tmp` 下执行以免覆盖仓库的 `wrangler.jsonc`，已清理并确认仓库工作区干净
- 文档里两处断言当场复验：`www` 带 `x-u2tool-html-cache`、apex 301

author: renesenses
body:
Forum — **Benjithom** (08/08) : *« Dans l'onglet favoris, catégorie Albums, la lecture ne se lance pas. Appuyer sur un album Qobuz ou sur l'icône lecture n'entraîne ni la lecture ni l'ouverture de l'album. Catégorie Titres, tout fonctionne. »*

## La cause

Un favori de service n'a **pas d'id local** : `streamToAlbum` ne lui donne que `source` et `source_id`. Or les deux gestionnaires de l'onglet Albums commençaient par exiger cet id :

```js
function navigateToAlbum(album) { if (!album.id) return; … }
async function playAlbum(album)  { if (!zone?.id || !album.id) return; … }
```

Ils sortaient donc **en silence**, sans erreur ni message — exactement le symptôme décrit.

Pourquoi les titres marchent : `playSingle` avait été rendue consciente du streaming (`if (st.source_id && st.source)` avant le repli sur `t.id`). L'onglet Albums n'a jamais reçu ce traitement.

**L'onglet Artistes a le même défaut**, non signalé jusqu'ici : `navigateToArtist` portait la même garde.

## Le correctif

- **Lecture d'un album distant** via `streaming_album_id`, que le serveur sait déjà traiter (`playback.rs:651` : il récupère les pistes auprès du service et les enfile).
- **Ouverture d'un album ou d'un artiste distant** par les stores `pendingStreamingAlbum` / `pendingStreamingArtist`, déjà utilisés par les raccourcis pour ce même besoin — plutôt que de réimplémenter dans les favoris l'affichage d'un album distant que `StreamingView` sait faire.
- Le chemin local est inchangé : la garde sur `album.id` reste, elle n'est simplement plus la première décision.

## Vérification

`npm run build` passe, sans nouvel avertissement. Le champ `streaming_album_id` est bien au contrat côté client (`api.ts:653`) comme côté serveur.
