author: aminsato
body:
Part of #5503 — **phase 1 of 4.** This PR defines the token layer only. It does not close the issue.

`ui/theme/` has `Colors`, `Typography` and `Theme` and **no radius concept at all**, so every rounded surface in the app spells its geometry out as a numeric literal: 384 of them across 23 distinct values, plus six different ways to say "fully round". This adds the missing layer and migrates a small, deliberately-chosen slice of call sites to prove the API works end to end.

**Zero visual change is the acceptance criterion for this phase**, and it is measured rather than asserted — see below.

Ports vultisig-ios#5040. The scale is the same one; the API is not, because Compose is not SwiftUI — the differences are called out where they matter.

---

## The scale

| Token | dp | Surface class | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` | 4 | progress tracks, skeleton bars | inferred |
| `sm` | 8 | small inline tags | inferred |
| `md` | 12 | list rows, compact containers | Figma — asset list row |
| `lg` | 16 | input fields, inner icon tiles | Figma — input, inner tile |
| `xl` | 24 | cards, banners, list containers | Figma — banner |
| `pill` | — | chips, search fields, capsules | Figma — 50 / 77 / 99 |

**There is deliberately no sheet token, and the scale stops at 24.** The two sheet frames in the design file measure 38 and 28, but both are stock design-kit components pasted into the file rather than authored Vultisig surfaces — 38 is Apple's iOS 26 sheet, 28 is Material 3's default. Neither is ours, and adding a step for them would encode a platform default as a design decision. A comment at the scale declaration records this so nobody "completes" the scale later.

### Where these came from

Read off rendered frames in Figma file `puB2fsVpPrBx3Sup7gaa3v`, section **"Main View (Mobile) - iOS 26"** — these were re-measured for this PR rather than taken from the iOS port:

- banner `68734:97487` → `rounded-[24px]`
- inner icon tile `68734:97489` and input field `26557:15834` → `rounded-[16px]`
- asset list row `51141:203613` → `rounded-tl-[12px] rounded-tr-[12px]`
- vault-type chip `rounded-[99px]`, coin logo `rounded-[50px]`, glass-close `rounded-[77px]`

Two caveats worth stating plainly:

1. **Radii are not Figma variables.** `get_variable_defs` on that section returns colours, fonts, a stroke width and `dimensions/3 = 8` — there is no authored radius scale to import. These values were measured off rendered frames.
2. **`4` and `8` are lower-confidence than the rest** — inferred from existing app usage and that `dimensions/3`, not read off a frame. Any outlier found during phase 2 should go back to the designer rather than be rounded to the nearest token.

Values are shared with iOS and Windows — identical numbers, units per platform.

---

## The token API

```kotlin
Theme.v2.radius.xl              // the token — reads like Theme.v2.colors.*
Modifier.clip(Theme.v2.radius.xl)
Modifier.background(color, Theme.v2.radius.xl)
Card(shape = Theme.v2.radius.xl)

Theme.v2.radius.md.size         // Dp, only where a Shape will not fit (Canvas, insets)
Theme.v2.radius.lg.shape.copy(...)   // derive partial corners from the token
```

**The token *is* a `Shape`.** That is the one design decision everything else follows from: a call site names neither a radius nor a corner geometry, so changing the app's corner shape is one line inside `Radii` instead of another 384-site sweep. It also means the token drops into `shape =`, `clip`, `background` and `border` with no wrapper and no `.shape` noise at the point of use.

`Radius.Fixed.size` stays for the cases a `Shape` cannot reach — a `Canvas` corner radius, an inset computed off the surface. `Radius.shape` is a `CornerBasedShape` rather than a bare `Shape` so partial-corner surfaces can `copy(...)` from the token instead of restating its number. Both have a call site in this PR; nothing ships unused.

### `pill` is `CircleShape`, and that is better than the iOS equivalent

iOS needs a clamping *bound* — a 100,000pt constant, measured to still produce a capsule at 5120×2880 — because SwiftUI clamps a large radius down to half the smaller dimension. Compose's `CircleShape` is `RoundedCornerShape(percent = 50)`, which is defined *relative to the surface*. It cannot stop being round no matter how large the surface gets, so the Android token needs no magic number at all.

The app's fully-round idioms (50, 70, 77, 88, 99, 100 dp and `percent = 50`) all collapse onto it.

---

## `CornerType` is replaced by the token type

`V2Container` had its own two-case corner vocabulary — `CornerType.Circular` and `CornerType.RoundedCornerShape(size = 12.dp)` — across 17 call sites. It is deleted; `V2Container` now takes `radius: Radius` directly, so there is one corner concept in the app rather than two. `Circular` → `pill` is identical by construction (both produce `CircleShape`), and each numeric site maps to its own step.

---

## Migrated sites — every one pixel-neutral

26 token references across 21 files, chosen so each site's current literal **already equals** the token's value. Nothing was re-valued.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `components/v2/containers/V2Container.kt` | `CornerType` | `radius: Radius`, defaulting to `md` |
| 17 `V2Container` call sites | `CornerType.Circular` ×10, `12.dp` ×3, `24.dp` ×2, `8.dp` ×2 | `pill` / `md` / `xl` / `sm` |
| `components/SignTonDisplayView.kt` | `RoundedCornerShape(4.dp)` | `xs` |
| `components/library/form/Form.kt` | `RoundedCornerShape(4.dp)` | `xs` |
| `components/errors/ErrorView.kt` ×2 | `RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)` | `lg` |
| `components/dapp/DappRequestBanner.kt` | `RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)` | `lg` |
| `components/v2/fastselection/…/FastSelectionModalContent.kt` | `clip(RoundedCornerShape(24.dp))` | `clip(xl)` |
| `screens/transaction/TransactionHistoryScreen.kt` ×2 | `CornerRadius(12.dp.toPx())` + `RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)` | `md.size` + `md` |
| `screens/cosmosstaking/CosmosWithdrawRewardsScreen.kt` ×2 | `RoundedCornerShape(topStart = 16.dp, topEnd = 16.dp)` | `lg.shape.copy(...)` |

Between them these cover every scale step the app uses, and every form a radius takes in Compose: `Card(shape =)`, `Modifier.clip`, `Modifier.background`, `Modifier.border`, a `DrawScope` corner radius, and the partial-corner case.

### Two of them fixed latent drift

Both are the bug class that no lint rule will ever catch, because it is invisible in the declaration and only shows at the call site:

- **`TransactionHistoryEmptyState`** drew its border on a canvas at `CornerRadius(12.dp.toPx())` and its background at `RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)` — two independent literals for one surface. The stroke would have stopped tracing the card the first time either moved. Both now read one token.
- **`CosmosWithdrawRewardsScreen`**'s docked footer restated `topStart = 16.dp, topEnd = 16.dp` in its clip and again in its border. Now derived once from `lg`.

### Deliberately not migrated

- **Sheets.** Out of scope entirely, not just out of phase 1 — the scale has no step for them.
- **Text inputs.** Figma says 16; the app's fields are at 12. Real drift, needs a designer call rather than a silent rounding.
- **Fully-round literals on unbounded surfaces.** See the clamping test below — converting one of those is a visual change, not a rename.

---

## How pixel-neutrality is proven

**1. Geometry, not eyeballs.** `RadiusTokenTest` (9 cases) asserts each token's `createOutline` is identical to the outline of the exact literal expression it replaced, pins the scale values and their ordering, and checks the derived partial-corner shape against the literal it replaces.

It also **measures the clamping bound** rather than assuming it, which is the rule phase 2 needs: a fully-round literal only collapses to a capsule while the surface's smaller dimension stays under twice the literal. `RoundedCornerShape(99.dp)` on a 320×240 surface draws 99, not a capsule — so migrating a fully-round literal is only safe o

body:
## Summary

- Register `Gateway.set_schema_updated_callback()` in `async_start` to write topology changes (binding, class promotion, circuit creation) back to the config entry within seconds instead of waiting up to 5 minutes for the polling fallback
- The callback is debounced (2s trailing) to coalesce bursts of topology events (e.g. a discovery scan processing many 1FC9 packets) into a single `async_save_client_state` call
- The existing polling loop is kept as a safety net (can be reduced to 15-30 min once the event-driven path is verified reliable in production)
- The debounce task is cancelled on unload to avoid racing with the unload's own save
- Guards on the existing `_skip_topology_sync` flag to ignore stale events during unload/reload

This implements Phase 4 Step 5, unblocked by ramses_rf PR 997 (event bus & handshake, shipped in 0.59.3).

#### Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: burst debouncing (3 events → 1 save), skip_topology_sync guard, debounce cancellation on unload
- [x] `prek run -a`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest` (1144 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures)
- [x] ha_sim_test R62: schema updates within 10s of device accept (event-driven, not 5-min poll), burst coalescing, both TRVs in final schema — 5/5 PASS

body:
💡 What:
- Extracted `BagDrawer` inner logic into a new `BagDrawerContent` component that is conditionally rendered only when `bagOpen` is true.
- Wrapped the `subtotal` calculation inside `BagDrawerContent` with `useMemo`.

🎯 Why:
- Previous implementation ran heavy hooks (`useQuery` for products, `useMemo` for `productMap`) on every application render cycle even when the drawer was closed.
- `subtotal` calculation (`bagItems.reduce`) ran unnecessarily on every re-render of the open drawer, even when the `bagItems` array did not change.

📊 Impact:
- Prevents unnecessary background execution of data-fetching and mapping hooks for a completely hidden UI element.
- Reduces O(N) overhead during the active render cycle of the drawer by caching the derived `subtotal`.

🔬 Measurement:
- Verify by opening and closing the Bag Drawer; behavior should be identical.
- Check React DevTools Profiler to confirm `BagDrawer` renders faster and `subtotal` does not recalculate unnecessarily when unrelated state changes.

author: ktngch
body:
## 概要

VM の対話シェルのプロンプトを [starship](https://starship.rs/) で装飾する。git のブランチ / 変更状態やランタイムのバージョンが一目で分かるようになる。

```sh
make shell
# VM 内
~/workspace/github.com/ktngch/sandbox-vm on  main [!] via  v24.19.0
```

VM の起動ごとに provision が走るので、明示的な有効化操作は要らない。

## 変更点

| ファイル | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `lima/provision/50-starship.sh` (新規) | starship の初期化を `~/.bashrc` に配線 |
| `lima/provision/mise.toml` | `starship` (1.26.0) を追加 |
| `lima/claude-code.yaml` / `Makefile` | provision エントリと `reprovision` の配線 |
| `README.md` | 「入っているもの」と構成ツリー |

apt パッケージの追加は無し。隔離設定 (`mounts: []` / `ssh.*`) には触れていない。

## 設計判断

**`~/.profile` ではなく `~/.bashrc` に書く** — CLAUDE.md 不変条件 #4（PATH は `.profile` 側で通す）の例外にあたる。プロンプトは対話シェルにしか意味が無く、`limactl shell -- cmd` のような非対話実行では `.bashrc` が冒頭 `return` するので影響しない。その旨をスクリプト冒頭のコメントに残してある。

**「中身を比較して差分があるときだけ書き直す」方式** — `40-aws-vault.sh` と同じ。マーカーの有無だけで判定する `10-mise.sh` 方式だと、後からブロックを直したときに既存 VM へ伝播しないため。

**mise のブロックより後ろに置く** — `mise activate bash` は評価時点で解決済みの `PATH` を `export` するので、この順序なら `command -v starship` が通る。sed で消して末尾に追記し直す実装なので、書き直し時も順序は保たれる。`command -v` ガードにより、`mise install` 失敗等で starship が無くても対話シェルは壊れない。

**`starship.toml` は同梱しない** — 既定のプリセットで足りるため。設定を入れたくなったら `mode: data` で `mise.toml` と同じ経路に載せられる。

## 検証

既存インスタンス (`claude-code`) で確認:

- `make validate`: OK、警告行なし（不変条件 #3）
- `make reprovision`: starship 1.26.0 インストール → `~/.bashrc` に配線
- 2 回目の `50-starship.sh`: 書き換えログ無し・ブロックの重複無し
- 対話シェル: `PROMPT_COMMAND=starship_precmd`、`STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND=_mise_hook_prompt_command` で mise の hook も保持される
- 非対話実行 (`bash -lc`): `node` / `claude` / `starship` がこれまで通り解決する

`make recreate`（yaml の provision エントリが新規ブート経路に載る）は、VM 内の `~/.claude` の認証情報が消えるため未実施。

body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the application to use a service layer pattern for data persistence and converts several features to use full-page Livewire components instead of traditional controllers and views.

## Key Changes

### Service Layer Introduction
- Created service classes for core entities:
  - `CurrencyService` - Handles currency CRUD operations with ISO code normalization
  - `UnitService` - Manages unit persistence
  - `CategoryService` - Handles product category operations with product count and deletion guards
  - `ExpenseCategoryService` - Manages expense categories with related expense checks
  - `CustomerService` - Handles customer data with image media management
  - `SupplierService` - Manages supplier data with image media management

- Services encapsulate business logic including:
  - Pagination with search filtering
  - Data validation and normalization
  - Media/image handling for customers and suppliers
  - Deletion guards (preventing deletion when related records exist)

### Full-Page Livewire Components
- Converted currencies management to full-page Livewire components:
  - `CurrencyIndex` - Replaces `currency/index.blade.php`
  - `CurrencyForm` - Replaces `currency/create.blade.php` and `currency/edit.blade.php`
  
- Converted units management to full-page Livewire components:
  - `UnitIndex` - Replaces `setting/units/index.blade.php`
  - `UnitForm` - Replaces `setting/units/create.blade.php` and `setting/units/edit.blade.php`

- Updated Livewire components to extend `layouts.app` with proper breadcrumb sections

### Controller Updates
- Removed `CurrencyController` and `UnitsController` (now handled by Livewire)
- Updated remaining controllers (`CustomersController`, `SuppliersController`, `CategoriesController`, `ExpenseCategoriesController`) to:
  - Inject service dependencies via constructor
  - Delegate persistence logic to services
  - Simplify validation and data handling

### Livewire Component Updates
- Updated all Livewire components to use service layer instead of direct Eloquent model access
- Refactored delete operations to use service methods with proper error handling
- Updated render methods to call services for data retrieval

### Routing Changes
- Updated `routes/web.php` to use full-page Livewire component routes for currencies and units
- Removed traditional resource routes for these features

## Implementation Details
- Services follow a consistent interface pattern with `paginate()`, `create()`, `update()`, and `delete()` methods
- Deletion guards return boolean to indicate success/failure, allowing UI to display appropriate messages
- Image handling is abstracted in services, removing duplication from controllers
- All components maintain existing permission checks via `Gate::denies()`

author: jefferis
body:
Three related fixes to `aedes_flytable_update()`, found while porting this function to `crantr` (`crant_seatable_update`).

## 1. Only write columns that can change

The change set is computed correctly (diffing across all read columns), but the write step pushed back the **whole** changed row. This function only ever changes `root_id`, `supervoxel_id` and `root_duplicated`; `point_xyz` and `status` are read (to resolve supervoxels / compute `good_status`) but never modified, yet were rewritten with identical values on every touched row — including the **human-curated `status`** column. Fix narrows the payload:

```r
mutable <- intersect(c("_id", "root_id", "supervoxel_id", "root_duplicated"),
                     names(updated))
```

`intersect(..., names(updated))` keeps the `update_dups = FALSE` path correct (no `root_duplicated` there).

## 2. Treat NA `root_duplicated` as FALSE in the diff

The scheduled Python updater only ever sets `root_duplicated` to `TRUE`, so unchecked rows read back as `NA`. Diffing `NA` against the freshly computed logical column flagged **every** not-duplicated row as changed. Coerce the stored column `NA -> FALSE` before diffing:

```r
rd <- as.logical(cands$root_duplicated)
rd[is.na(rd)] <- FALSE
cands$root_duplicated <- rd
```

Only genuine transitions (`-> TRUE`, or `TRUE -> FALSE`) are written.

## 3. Return what would be written

Previously returned `invisible(TRUE)` / `invisible(FALSE)`. Now returns, invisibly, a list capturing **both** write streams so nothing is hidden:

```r
list(updated    = toupdate,        # _id, root_id, supervoxel_id, root_duplicated (changed rows)
     serial_ids = serial_toupdate) # _id + newly assigned serial_id, or NULL
```

`serial_ids` is `NULL` unless serial ids were (or, under `dry_run`, would be) assigned — i.e. `NULL` in the default `update.serial_ids = FALSE` path. The `serial_id` block no longer early-returns, so the list is returned on every path.

**Note:** this changes the return contract (logical → list). `@return` doc and `.Rd` updated. Scripted callers branching on a truthy/`FALSE` return should switch to e.g. `nrow(res$updated) > 0`.

All internal-only; no signature changes.

author: malkreide
body:
## Problem

Der Skill liess sich bisher nur per Klonen und Kopieren einrichten. Der Upload-Dialog von Claude Desktop und claude.ai erwartet aber eine einzelne Archivdatei — und ein heruntergeladenes Repo-ZIP ist keine: es trägt `github-repo-skill-main/` an der Wurzel und README, CHANGELOG und CI mit sich.

## Änderung

**`github-repo.skill`** (57 KB, 19 Dateien) enthält `SKILL.md` und ausschliesslich das, was der Skill zur Laufzeit liest — `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`.

**`skill-manifest.txt`** hält den Paketinhalt fest, 1:1 zum Repo-Layout. Das ist Bedingung, nicht Bequemlichkeit: SKILL.md nennt seine Begleitdateien als `scripts/validate_repo.py` und `references/review-rules.md` — diese Pfade müssen im Paket unverändert auflösen. Wer beim Packen umbenennt, bricht SKILL.md, ohne dass im Repository etwas kaputt aussieht.

**`scripts/build_skill.sh`** baut reproduzierbar (fester Zeitstempel je Eintrag, `-X`, sortierte Reihenfolge). Gleiche Quellen ergeben ein bit-identisches Archiv — nur dadurch ist ein eingechecktes Binärartefakt im Diff beurteilbar und in der CI prüfbar.

**`scripts/validate_skill.py`** prüft das Repo als *Paket*, nicht als Repo:

| | Prüfung |
|---|---|
| P1 | Manifest wohlgeformt, alle Quellen vorhanden |
| P2 | Frontmatter mit `name` und `description` samt 1024-Zeichen-Limit — dieser Skill liegt bei 1001, der Upload wird bei Überschreitung abgewiesen und nicht gekürzt |
| P3 | Jeder von SKILL.md genannte Paketpfad steht im Manifest |
| P4 | Das eingecheckte Archiv ist inhaltlich deckungsgleich mit den Quellen |
| P5 | Relative Links lösen auch im Paket-Layout auf |

## Zwei Entscheidungen, die begründet sind

**Die CI prüft das Archiv VOR dem Build.** Danach verglichen wäre es gegen die Quellen geprüft, aus denen es soeben entstand — immer grün. Der Build läuft im zweiten Schritt trotzdem, sonst wäre er der einzige Code im Repo, den nie jemand ausführt.

**Kein Byte-Vergleich in der CI.** Das Archiv ist reproduzierbar, aber eine andere `zip`-Version auf dem Runner machte den Lauf ohne Codeänderung rot — genau die Fehlerklasse, gegen die Regel 8.1 in diesem Skill steht. Verglichen werden Dateiinhalte.

**`*.skill binary` in `.gitattributes`**, weil dieses Repo für alle Textformate `eol=lf` erzwingt. Eine einzige Zeilenende-Normalisierung machte das Archiv unlesbar — sichtbar erst beim Upload, nicht beim Commit.

## Geprüft

- `ruff check scripts/` und `ruff format --check scripts/` grün
- `python3 scripts/validate_repo.py .` → 0 ERROR (1 WARN: E5 Default-Branch, Artefakt des Feature-Branches)
- `python3 scripts/validate_skill.py` → grün
- Zwei aufeinanderfolgende Builds ergeben denselben SHA-256 (`2e22d62e…`)
- Negativtest: eine Zeile an `references/review-rules.md` angehängt → P4 meldet die Abweichung, Exit 1
- `unzip -t` fehlerfrei, entpacktes Paket enthält 19 Dateien mit gültigem Frontmatter

SKILL.md selbst ist unverändert.

author: llun
body:
## Problem

`NODE_ENV=production yarn migrate` dies partway through the publicId backfill:

```
  statuses: 22000/174526 (13%) - 22000 updated
Acquire connection error: Error: operation timed out for an unknown reason
    at async Promise.all (index 487)
    at async backfillPublicIds (migrations/20260808000000_add_public_ids.js:265:7)
migration failed with error: Knex: Timeout acquiring a connection. The pool is probably full.
```

`backfillPublicIds()` issued **one UPDATE per row** and fanned the whole `BATCH_SIZE` (500) out with `Promise.all`. knex's pool defaults to 10 connections, so ~490 of those queries sat in tarn's acquire queue and the entire batch had to drain inside a single 60s `acquireConnectionTimeout`. Against a 174k-row table on a remote database that is also serving traffic, the queue eventually outlives that timeout and the migration dies mid-run. `sweepMissingPublicIds()` had the same fan-out.

The `Promise.all (index 487)` frame in the trace is the smoking gun — index 487 of a 500-wide fan-out.

## Fix

Both loops now fold rows into a single `UPDATE ... SET "publicId" = CASE "id" WHEN ? THEN ? ... END WHERE "id" IN (...) AND "publicId" IS NULL` per 200-row chunk, awaited **one chunk at a time**.

- The backfill holds exactly **one** pooled connection at any moment. It cannot starve its own pool, and it leaves the database's connection budget to the app running alongside it.
- 200 rows is 600 bind parameters — under the 999-parameter floor of the most conservatively built SQLite, and far under PostgreSQL's 65535.
- Built through the query builder rather than `knex.raw` so the return value is knex's normalised affected-row count on every dialect.
- `else "publicId"` in the CASE is unreachable (the `IN` list restricts the statement to exactly the ids the CASE enumerates) but keeps the expression total and gives PostgreSQL a typed branch to resolve the otherwise-unknown parameters against.
- Much faster as a side effect: 174k rows go from 174k round trips to ~900.

`updated` now counts rows actually affected rather than rows attempted.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged — idempotency, the forward keyset walk, the self-healing sweep, the NULL-id skip, the converged-vs-stuck exit semantics and every log message are all as before.

## Resuming the failed production run

No manual repair needed. knex records nothing for a failed migration and `up()` is idempotent, so `yarn migrate` re-runs it: the walk restarts at cursor `''`, skips the ~22k rows that already have a `publicId`, and fills the rest.

## Verification

- `yarn run prettier --write .`, `yarn lint` (124 warnings, byte-identical to `main`), `yarn build`, `yarn test` (757 files / 8251 tests) all pass.
- Verified against a throwaway **PostgreSQL 17** with a deliberately hostile `pool: { max: 2 }` and a 5s `acquireConnectionTimeout` — the old code would blow that up instantly:
  - 2301 rows backfilled in **15 UPDATE statements** (was 2301)
  - **max 1 concurrent query**
  - 0 rows left with a NULL `publicId`, 2300/2300 distinct publicIds, v7 timestamps matching `createdAt`
  - NULL-id actor correctly skipped and reported
  - re-run preserved existing values
- New regression test `backfills in bulk statements instead of one query per row` asserts both the statement count and `maxConcurrentQueries === 1`. Confirmed it actually catches the regression: forcing `UPDATE_CHUNK_SIZE = 1` fails it with `expected 450 to be less than or equal to 5`.

No schema change, so no dump regeneration.

body:
The Toon World modal really was showing the whole Deck, and I said it wasn't.

## Three copies of one rule

The engine's card filter knew about `toon`. The picker's copy did not. Neither did the picker harness's. So "add 1 Toon monster" offered **every monster in the Deck** — exactly as reported.

My first look at it went wrong in the most ordinary way: I checked the picker, saw `dark-hole` excluded, and read that as the Toon filter working. It was `kind: 'monster'` doing it. The filter I thought I was testing had never run.

`matchesFilter` is exported now and the other two are deleted.

The harness had the same gap with teeth: `cardMatching` seeded a **non-Toon** into the Deck for Toon World's own test, so the moment the real filter started running, the harness reported the card as broken.

## How it was found

By auditing all seventeen items of the request against the shipped game rather than against my memory of having done them — 53 checks, one red, and it was the one I'd told the owner was already fine.

## Falsification earned its keep twice

Reinstating the drifted copy reddens the new pin **and** an older Magnet Warrior pin that the drift had been masking:

```
❌ the picker offers exactly the three Magnet Warriors — 6 of 6 in the Graveyard
❌ not the bird that was never one
❌ not a Ritual monster
```

author: mudream4869
body:
Second of the mobile read-only cleanup series. Independent of #289 — different files, either can merge first.

## Why

`/import` is a route-level redirect to `/books?import=1`, and vue-router resolves a redirect *before* `beforeEach` runs. So the guard only ever sees `library` — a route the mobile shell must keep reachable — and the name-based `MOBILE_BLOCKED_ROUTES` structurally cannot cover it. The import modal opens off that query alone, reachable from any link, deep link, or restored tab. The existing e2e case already noted this as a known hole.

Until now the only thing stopping it was `LibraryPage` folding `!readOnly` into `importModalOpen`. That is correct, but it left one arm of the mobile route policy living in a page component, where the next query-driven write surface would have to remember to repeat it.

## What changed

`stripMobileBlockedQuery` in `blockedRoutes.ts` (kept there so it stays importable without constructing a router — the unit tests run in a node environment with no `window`), called from the guard right after the route-name check, so the whole mobile route policy sits in one place.

It returns `null` when there is nothing to strip. That is load-bearing: a guard that redirected unconditionally would redirect to a location still matching the condition that triggered it, and loop. There is a test for exactly that, including feeding a stripped result back in.

`LibraryPage`'s own check stays — deliberate depth, not duplication — and the comment says so.

## Verification

- `npm --prefix frontend test` — 432 passed (4 new cases: stripping, preserving unrelated params including `mobile-shell-preview`, the no-loop null contract, no mutation of the input)
- `npm --prefix frontend run build` — `vue-tsc` clean
- `mobile-read-only.spec.ts` — 6/6 passed

The e2e case previously only asserted the modal was absent, which `LibraryPage` alone satisfies — it would have passed with the guard doing nothing. It now also asserts the query is gone, so a regression in the guard is visible.

Note: `mobile-multiselect.spec.ts` fails in my container, but it fails identically on unmodified `dev`, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

The pytest check in this project's own `ship:` config still carried a `--deselect`
for the old "install-helper flake". PR #306 diagnosed that flake as **argv
dependence** and fixed it at the source; the workaround outlived the cause.

A `--deselect` in a ship check is the same shape #306 removed: it makes the result

author: jaxywaxy
body:
Follow-up to #421, from the same 2026-08-09 scan.

## What was wrong

A standing subscription-scope **Owner** grant, absent from Bicep, rendered as a grey **"Unknown"** badge. `DriftClassifier` rated that same row **HIGH** — I ran it against the exact payload to confirm.

Three things were true at once:

1. The classifier was reachable only as a `DriftAgent` mixin, so its verdict went into the LLM prompt and **nowhere else**.
2. With no provider, no agent is built — so a keyless scan **never computed a severity at all**.
3. The drift table had **no severity column**, so there was nowhere for it to show even if it had been persisted.

Nothing about classification needs an LLM. `agent/classification.py` is policy tables with no client and no network. It was gated by an accident of where it lived.

## What changed

- **`classify_drifts()`** runs in the deterministic section of `analyze_drift.main` — after attribution (`_honour_attribution` reads `change_origin`) and before the analysis (so prompt and report agree). Each row gains `severity` and `category`.
- **`_build_drift_report()`** extracted, so classification and the LLM call cannot disagree about what a drift is.
- **A Severity column** in the HTML. The Origin badge could not carry this: a finding with no Activity Log entry has `origin` *and* `category` of `unknown`, so it greys out however serious the resource is. That's the same badge that was taught to honour `category` in an earlier round — the fix doesn't reach a row whose category is unknown too.

## The design call worth reviewing

**The two severities stay separate fields.** `change_origin.severity` is **provenance** — it defaults to MEDIUM whenever the Activity Log is silent, which is a statement about attribution confidence, not danger. `severity` is **risk**. Folding one into the other turns "we could not attribute it" into "it matters less".

I specifically did *not* teach `change_origin` about `details.privileged`, which would have been the smaller diff — that's the shape of the earlier defect where a provenance claim was applied to a declared-state fact.

The rejected cheap alternative was escalating on `privileged` inside `html_report`. That puts a risk heuristic in the render layer where nobody will find it, and only covers one field.

## Verification

- **1342 tests pass** (was 1331; +11). New file `tests/test_risk_severity.py`.
- Smoke-rendered a real 29-drift report: **6 critical / 15 high / 7 medium** now surfaced where rows previously carried no risk severity at all. The Owner grant renders a red HIGH chip beside its (correctly) unknown origin.

**Wiring is pinned, not just behaviour.** The unit tests call `classify_drifts` directly and would all still pass if nothing in the pipeline invoked it — which is precisely the bug being fixed. Source-inspection guards pin the call site, matching the existing pattern in `test_agent_availability.py`.

Mutation-checked, each caught by a different test:

| Mutation | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| Remove the call from `main()` | 3 wiring tests |
| Hide it behind `if agent:` | `test_it_runs_outside_the_provider_branch` |
| Stamp provenance severity instead of risk | 3 behaviour tests |
| Use the severity-**sorted** `_build_findings` against positional rows | 6 tests |

## Docs

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` gains the two-severity table and two invariants: *living in `agent/` does not make something LLM-dependent*, and *provenance must never soften risk*. (The pipeline-step list in `CLAUDE.md` is also updated, but that file is gitignored, so it stays local.)

body:
依赖 #903。为 CoreCronTaskService 增加单实例后台 worker，由 AppServices 自动启动；worker 支持停止、错误退避和旧服务替换停用，并按秒检查到期任务。

## Summary by Sourcery

引入一个基于 cron 的服务器任务调度服务，使用单个后台 worker，由应用服务容器自动管理。

新特性：
- 添加 `CoreCronTaskService` 实现，用于持久化 cron 任务、执行服务器重启和命令，并通过 interface crate 暴露契约。
- 暴露 `CronTaskService` 接口、模型和错误类型，用于跨各层管理服务器 cron 任务，包括列表、CRUD、启用/禁用以及临时（ad‑hoc）执行。
- 将 cron 任务服务接入全局 `AppServices` 容器，采用惰性初始化，并自动启动后台调度循环。

缺陷修复：
- 确保 cron 任务运行记录在额外的 cron 任务模型中存储具体的动作类型，而不是静态字符串切片。

改进优化：
- 为 cron 任务操作添加应用层错误映射，将 extra 层错误转换为稳定的 interface 错误枚举。
- 将 `ExtraCronTaskError` 标记为 `non_exhaustive`，以便未来向后兼容地扩展错误类型。
- 为应用层和接口层依赖添加 `chrono` 和仅用于测试的工具，以支持基于时间的 cron 调度和持久化测试。

测试：
- 添加类似集成测试的用例，用于验证 cron 任务持久化、服务器契约执行、输入校验以及调度器生命周期行为。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a cron-based server task scheduling service with a single background worker that is automatically managed by the application service container.

New Features:
- Add a CoreCronTaskService implementation that persists cron tasks, executes server restarts and commands, and exposes a contract via the interface crate.
- Expose a CronTaskService interface, models, and error types for managing server cron tasks across layers, including listing, CRUD, enable/disable, and ad-hoc execution.
- Wire the cron task service into the global AppServices container with lazy initialization and automatic startup of a background scheduler loop.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure cron task run records store the concrete action type instead of static string slices in the extra cron task models.

Enhancements:
- Add application-level error mapping for cron task operations from extra-layer errors into stable interface error enums.
- Mark the Extra CronTaskError as non_exhaustive to allow forward-compatible error expansion.
- Extend application and interface dependencies with chrono and test-only utilities to support time-based cron scheduling and persistence tests.

Tests:
- Add integration-style tests for cron task persistence, server contract execution, input validation, and scheduler lifecycle behaviour.

</details>

author: alexrinass
body:
Adds an opt-in `--init` flag and an interactive `[y/N]` prompt so `git flow init` can create the git repository when the current directory is not one, instead of always erroring out.

The non-repository gate in `cmd/init.go` becomes a creation decision: `--init` creates without asking, interactive stdin asks first, and everything else keeps today's error and exit code. Creation runs after configuration resolution rather than at the gate, because the created repository's initial branch must be the resolved git-flow trunk (`git init --initial-branch=<trunk>`) rather than an ambient `init.defaultBranch`; both paths then converge on the unchanged identity check, config save and branch creation, so the identity fast-fail and scope handling apply to a freshly created repository for free. Supporting pieces are `git.Init(dir, initialBranch)` in `internal/git/repo.go`, `(*Config).TrunkBranch()` in `internal/config/config.go`, `reopenRepo()` in `cmd/repo.go` (needed because `openRepo` memoizes the pre-creation "not a git repository" failure for the lifetime of the process), and the rename of `firstRunInteractive` to `stdinIsInteractive`. Coverage is 18 integration scenarios plus 3 unit tests: the flag, the prompt, both decline paths, the unchanged default outside a repository, the no-op inside one, the identity fast-fail, local/global/shared scope, nested subdirectories, and an invalid trunk name.

Closes #125

### Remarks

Three deliberate deviations from the literal transcripts in the spec:

- The "not a git repository" error keeps its existing exit code 3, not the 1 shown in the spec's transcript. The spec's normative text calls that path unchanged, and its Out of Scope section forbids changing existing behavior beyond gating creation. The interactive-decline path uses the same code, so every "no repository to work in" outcome reports one code.
- `Initialized empty Git repository in ...` prints after the "Initializing git-flow..." line, because the trunk has to be resolved before `git init --initial-branch` can run. Only the ordering of those two output lines differs from the transcript.
- AVH config import detection is skipped on the repository-creation path. It needs a repository handle that cannot exist yet, and a brand-new repository could only ever carry AVH keys from global or system config, which is not a repository being migrated.

Two review findings were fixed on the branch. `--shared --init` now honors the same pre-existing `.gitflow` guard as the in-repo path — `git config --file` merges into an existing file rather than truncating it, so stale keys previously blended into the new configuration and neither the refusal nor the `--force` requirement applied. And the declined-prompt message no longer reads as an internal probe failure ("failed to check if git repository: ...") when nothing failed and the user simply said no.

The docs commit also corrects a pre-existing error in the init manpage's EXIT STATUS table, which listed the wrong codes for "not a git repository", "already initialized" and "invalid options". That correction is documentation-only and unrelated to this change.

**Review focus:**
- `cmd/init.go:134-154` - the creation decision at the non-repository gate
- `cmd/init.go:307-339` - creation after configuration resolution, with trunk validation ahead of `git init`
- `cmd/repo.go:46-56` - `reopenRepo` and the memo priming
- `internal/config/shared.go` - `SharedConfigExistsIn` and the repo-less `--shared` probe

author: sanohiro
body:
Climb the alignc self-optimization ladder with measured rungs, plus the owner-decided default flip for emitted binaries. Every number below was measured on this branch before wiring.

## alignc itself

- **mimalloc as the `alignc` binary's global allocator** (binary-only; in-process library consumers keep the default allocator, while tests spawning the real binary exercise the shipped configuration). The compiler frontend is allocation-heavy: measured **~30% faster `check`** on both a 3.5k-line real package file and a 2k-function synthetic corpus — in every profile, including dev and untuned release. Build-subcommand wall time is LLVM/link dominated and unchanged.
- **Two-phase PGO in the versioned-release flow** (`release.yml`): instrumented dist build → examples + `pkg.db` check corpus → `llvm-profdata` merge → profile-use dist build. Measured locally end to end: PGO stacks a further **5–15%** frontend win on top of thin LTO + mimalloc (best case **−47%** against the untuned baseline). The profdata tool comes from the rustup toolchain (`llvm-tools` component + sysroot lookup), never a system LLVM whose profraw format can silently mismatch, and profile collection has a canary run without error suppression so a broken instrumented compiler fails the release instead of shipping a build-script-noise profile.

Ordinary `--release` builds stay untuned by design; only the tagged release pays the double build.

## Binaries alignc emits — rt-LTO defaults ON at release/fast (owner decision 2026-08-09)

Cross-arch evidence from `bench/rt_lto`: **2.9× (x86-64 Zen 3) / 2.10× (Apple Silicon)** on the string-predicate kernel, numeric control non-regressing (1.01×/1.04×), compile-time delta +1–2 ms. The CLI resolves an absent flag to ON for `release`/`fast` and OFF for `dev`/`small`/`tiny` (`align_driver::default_rt_lto`, owner-test-pinned for all five profiles); `--no-rt-lto` is the explicit opt-out, and explicit `--rt-lto` keeps its verb/profile guards. The library API is unchanged (`rt_lto: bool` stays explicit at every `emit_*` entry point). Recorded in guide 16 (en+ja), roadmap M14 Slice 2, and a new open-questions Settled entry; `bench/rt_lto`'s OFF arm now passes `--no-rt-lto` explicitly, and `per_unit_surface` pins the new contract in both directions (flagless release output equals explicit `--rt-lto`; `--no-rt-lto` restores the runtime call).

## Review

Two fresh adversarial rounds. Round 1 (mimalloc/PGO slice) found two P2s in the PGO pipeline — both closed as described above. Round 2 (full branch) found one P1 (a sibling copy of the rejection-text assertion in `rt_lto.rs` missed by the sweep — exactly the sibling-sweep class this repo's checklist now names) and two P2s (stale CLI help, stale bench header wording); all closed, `rt_lto` suite 9/9 green.

## Known pre-existing failure (recorded in HANDOFF, not caused or hidden here)

`per_unit_surface::emit_llvm_n1_has_no_banner_and_matches_whole_program` fails on `main`: the CLI emits `pkg.db.internal` static-constructor extern declarations into every program, including one with no database usage, while the library `emit_llvm` helper does not. The suite is outside the bounded CI gate, which is why it went unnoticed. Left for the `pkg.db` owner to decide (intended emission → update the parity test; leak → gate declarations on use).

author: pschmiedmayer
body:
### :recycle: Current situation & Problem

Repository conventions were never written down, so every repository drifted. 12 of 19 carried a CI badge, 3 a license badge, 1 REUSE, 1 a DOI, and 5 had no badges at all. Badge labels for the same workflow appeared as "Main", "CI", "Main Validation" and "Build and Test". Two repositories advertised DOIs belonging to an unrelated project, because the legacy Zenodo badge form renders a plausible badge in any repository it is pasted into.

This repository already centralizes the reusable workflows and the org-wide health files, so the convention and its check belong here as well. It must land and be tagged before the repository pull requests that consume it.

No related issue was identified.

### :gear: Release Notes

- Add `REPOSITORY_STANDARDS.md`, documenting required files, the badge block and its order, README structure, the `CONTRIBUTORS.md` shape, the copyright holder, and how private repositories differ.
- Add `repository-standards.yml`, a reusable workflow that enforces the standard. It takes no inputs and has no opt-out, and runs REUSE, the Markdown link check, and a surface job covering required files, `CITATION.cff`, `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, README structure, badges, releases and DOIs, the copyright holder, and repository settings. Settings are reported rather than failed, because a pull request author cannot change them.
- Add `self-standards.yml`, holding this repository to the same standard. It calls the reusable workflow by local path, so a pull request here is checked against the version it proposes rather than the version already released.
- Bring this repository into compliance: add `LICENSE.md`, complete `CITATION.cff` with `license`, `url` and `repository-code`, and give the README a badge block and the required Contributing, License and Citation sections.
- Rename the footer assets to `assets/footer-light.png` and `assets/footer-dark.png` with the alt text `Schmiedmayer Lab`. Neither the name nor the alt text describes which logos the image contains, so changing them later is a change in this repository alone.
- Set the copyright holder to `Schmiedmayer Lab and the project authors (see CONTRIBUTORS.md)` across 50 files.

Consumers call the workflow with:

```yaml
name: Repository Standards

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  standards:
    name: Check Repository Standards
    uses: SchmiedmayerLab/.github/.github/workflows/repository-standards.yml@v0.4
```

The asset rename is a breaking change for consumers. 17 repositories currently embed the previous paths and their images will 404 from the moment this merges until each repository's own pull request lands. Copying the assets under the new names instead of renaming them removes that window, at the cost of a follow-up that deletes the old pair.

### :books: Documentation

- Document the workflow in the README catalog and workflow reference, alongside every other reusable workflow, rather than in comments inside the workflow file.
- Document the standard itself in `REPOSITORY_STANDARDS.md`, including why a root `LICENSE.md` is required for GitHub and Zenodo license detection, why `REUSE.toml` carries no wildcard annotation, and why the concept DOI is used rather than a per-version DOI.
- Record that the footer wording `open-source organization` applies to this repository only, so it is not copied into a project.

### :white_check_mark: Testing

- `git apply --check` against a fresh clone of `main`
- `actionlint` with shellcheck across all 35 workflows
- `reuse lint`
- This repository against its own checker, with every rule passing
- The badge-target, CONTRIBUTORS/CITATION equality, and footer-asset rules exercised against known-good and known-bad inputs

The workflow is exercised end to end by `self-standards.yml` in this pull request's CI.

### Code of Conduct & Contributing Guidelines

By creating and submitting this pull request, you agree to follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/SchmiedmayerLab/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/SchmiedmayerLab/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/SchmiedmayerLab/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/SchmiedmayerLab/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

`V21-LEARNING-GROWTH-BRAIN-P0-V1`

Final product authorization proposal only. No Learning product implementation is authorized before an ordinary two-parent merge into trusted `main`.

## Fresh trusted base

`main@ebb839b10f8acb93f29ce9aec15ec9fa392293af`

This base already contains:
- Persona V2 implementation and its post-merge semantic repair;
- Model Brain V4 / LiteLLM replacement, merged + post-merge GREEN;
- Learning OSS route bootstrap, exact UI routes, and Presidio/OpenFeature/flagd license route closure.

## Exact complete implementation scope

Future implementation branch:
`product/v21-learning-growth-brain-p0-v1`

- exact changed paths: **143**
- canonical path-set SHA-256: `b7bed2fe518d71036ec23a73bc8b26c84833461a70f5a7b105e0de2b4d31b29c`

The obsolete 88-path target `cb3376971ba3900418e55e6468ee188cb4b6b22ce27788492f51450412e3ec10` is not implementation authority.

## Mature OSS ownership

- Langfuse + OpenTelemetry: traces, scores, corrections, datasets, annotations, experiments and prompt-version evidence.
- DSPy 3.3.0 + GEPA 0.1.1: optimization.
- Promptfoo 0.122.0: precomputed regression/evaluation only; no direct provider calls.
- APScheduler 3.11.3: scheduling; no Yance scheduler.

- OpenFeature server SDK 1.23.0 + flagd provider 0.16.0 + flagd-core 4.0.0: in-process/offline staged rollout; no daemon or Yance rollout DB/engine.
- existing Letta Agent SDK/runtime: Learning Coach.
- assistant-ui 0.15.1 + tool-ui v2026.2.13: Coach chat, approval, question and progress UI.
- Graphiti: relationship facts.
- Parlant: Journey/Goal.

## Complete UI rule

Backend-only completion is forbidden. The same package must provide a real top-level Learning entry and real runtime-backed surfaces for:
- Overview / Daily Review
- Learning Coach
- Evidence / Mistake & Success Library
- Proposals
- Experiments
- Rollout / Promotion / Rollback
- Privacy / Consent
- per-conversation “do not learn”

Fake/dead buttons are forbidden. Approval enters evaluation; it cannot directly deploy.

## Legacy retirement

The package must remove/de-authorize the old Yance Learning engine/scope authority/L1-L2-L3 preference authority/synthesis scheduler/direct governance mutation/promotion state machine/projection lease-retry-DLQ workflow and old SQLite-backed summary/quality authority from production.

Historical old Learning SQLite rows may remain dormant for data safety, but no production path may read, write, promote or inject them after cutover. Explicit user purge is handled through the new privacy boundary.

## Failure-first

After authorization merge, the first implementation commit must contain exactly the nine frozen Learning test paths and zero product code. It must establish causal RED for absent OSS runtime/dependencies/UI/privacy/rollout and still-active legacy Learning authority before product implementation begins.

Final implementation merge remains explicit owner approval gated after exact 143-path sealing, applicable Stage/Layered/ACV2/Learning Windows GREEN, and self-independent P0=0/P1=0.

No force push, rebase, amend, squash, temporary bypass, gate weakening, product release, publish or promotion is authorized.

body:
## Summary

- prepare package version 0.4.0 directly on the published and tagged 0.3.0 foundation
- add the approved shadcn semantic token-name contract for Card, Popover, charts, Sidebar, and radius
- replace the old Radix/CSS Variables alias with the 57-name Radix Themes custom-palette override contract plus 26 Larsen tokens
- keep CSS Variables as the independent generic 50-name contract
- preserve alpha in all six formats and retain HSL precision through serialization
- enforce contrast-safe shadcn primary/ring roles and Radix accent contrast while preserving the scale-first foreground chooser
- track the older palette audit as dated research and provenance, without reapplying its stale PROJECT or CHANGELOG edits
- expand release smoke to scaffold shadcn, Radix, and CSS Variables artifacts

## Release boundary

0.3.0 is published on npm and tagged from `2ee1ccb60e2f0e7a15acaa3b55f6dabe043386a3`. This branch is a direct descendant of that release.

This PR does not publish, tag, merge, or deploy 0.4.0. It prepares the backward-compatible minor feature release for review.

## Scope and compatibility

- shadcn: approved semantic token names and Larsen additions, not a promise that shadcn components work without separate Tailwind/runtime assumptions
- Radix: sRGB custom-palette override names and Larsen additions, not full Radix Themes runtime compatibility or deferred P3 blocks
- CSS Variables: unchanged 50-name generic preset
- no Tailwind, framework, component library, or JavaScript theme controller is added

## WCAG correction

- shadcn primary keeps the requested mode seed at 1.5:1 or higher; otherwise it uses the perceptually closest passing accent-scale step
- shadcn ring keeps the requested mode seed at 3:1 or higher; otherwise it uses the closest passing accent-scale step
- primary foreground is recomputed with the existing accent-scale-first, gray-scale-second chooser, with pure black/white only as the final fallback
- Radix accent contrast keeps the upstream value at 4.5:1 or higher against accent step 9; otherwise it uses the same scale-first chooser
- HSL and HSL Values retain up to four decimal places after integer rounding was found to move a 4.506:1 harmony pair to 4.486:1

The pre-change behavior and rollback boundary are recorded in `docs/plans/2026-08-09-wcag-correction.md`.

- full smoke from the exact tarball - dependency install and `next build` passed
- separate exact-tarball Radix/OKLCH/Biome app - 83 names per mode, no duplicates, alpha preserved, Next.js 16.3.0 production build passed, HTML and compiled CSS returned HTTP 200
- `npm publish --dry-run` passed
- GitGuardian security check passed

author: rivhome
body:
Makes `zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows-gnu` pass end-to-end on a non-privileged Windows host (no msys2, no admin / Developer Mode):

```
zig build        -> 90/90 steps, exit 0
zig build smoke  -> dumped emacs starts (native emacs.exe, no bash)
zig build check  -> 582 tests, 580 pass, 0 unexpected, 2 skipped
```

Six independent fixes, each small and platform-guarded (Linux/macOS/CI unchanged):

1. **bootstrap-dump: fall back to copy when symlinks are denied** (`10353df`). `PermissionDenied` on non-admin Windows; the `etc` link is covered by `EMACSLOADPATH` and the pdmp is copied via `copyFileAbsolute`.

2. **gnulib-time-rz: `Tm` must match the platform's `struct tm`, not glibc's alone** (`eb0abb7`). mingw's `struct tm` is the bare C99 9-int layout (no `tm_gmtoff`/`tm_zone`), so `mktime_z`/`localtime_rz` wrote 16 bytes past the caller's `struct tm` → `__stack_chk_fail` (SIGILL) on `encode-time`, e.g. while byte-compiling `icalendar-ast`.

3. **native `emacs.exe` launcher** (`dbe8ff4`). The installed `emacs` was a `#!/bin/sh` script, not runnable on Windows without bash. Added a Zig launcher (resolve own dir → `temacs --dump-file=bootstrap-emacs.pdmp <args>`); `build.zig` installs it on Windows, `smoke` invokes `emacs.exe`.

4. **w32 `new_child`: guard the slot scan against an empty child list** (`391540a`). `child_proc_count==0` made `child_procs + (count-1)` underflow — UB that zig cc traps as a panic during `make-pipe-process`.

5. **run-check: force `LC_ALL=C`** (`9f17493`), like the dump/compile/smoke tools, so UTF-8 test inputs decode identically on every host (`character-test-string-width` failed under a zh-CN locale).

6. **bignum: use the GMP `long` ABI for the `*_ui`/`*_si` entry points** (`8bd7670`). They took `i64`/`u64`, but GMP passes `signed/unsigned long` (32-bit on LLP64 Windows); zig read a 64-bit register whose high 32 bits were undefined, so `-1` (`0xFFFFFFFF`) became `+4294967295` — corrupting any arithmetic that promoted a negative fixnum to a bignum (e.g. `(* -2 big)` = `0xFFFFFFFE*big`). `c_long`/`c_ulong` (32-bit Windows, 64-bit LP64) matches the ABI; an internal `mpz_set_u64` keeps the one `>32`-bit caller (the double mantissa in `mpf_set_d`).

All commits are functional, small (largest is the launcher at ~120 lines net), and keep the Unix paths unchanged.

author: arklual
body:
След в логе оборвался ровно на снятии статуса узла и до конца списка не дошёл.

Причина в самом выражении: версия читалась прямо в поле структуры, а соседнее поле звало `outdated()`, который лезет за тем же замком. Временный страж живёт до конца **всего** выражения — то есть до конца литерала структуры, — поэтому второй захват приходился на живой первый. Обычный мьютекс не реентерабелен: поток вставал навсегда.

Это объясняет оба симптома разом:

- пока команда была синхронной, она вставала в главном потоке — окно замирало наглухо;
- когда она ушла с главного потока, вместо замирания получились белый раздел «Проекты» и вечные скелетоны в настройках удалённых: команда просто не отвечала никогда.

Тест проверяет это в отдельном потоке с ожиданием — он обязан падать, а не висеть, иначе утащил бы весь прогон.

author: unional
body:
Refs #48. Closes the gap that stopped the 1.2.2 release after it had already cut a tag.

## How far the last run got

```
ℹ  Found git tag v1.2.1 associated with version 1.2.1 on branch main
ℹ  Found 7 commits since last release
ℹ  The next release version is 1.2.2
✔  Created tag v1.2.2
✘  Failed step "publish" of plugin "semantic-release-vsce"
```

Everything upstream now works — federated login, `vsce verify-pat --azure-credential`, and publisher authorization via the managed identity's Azure DevOps profile. It failed at the very last step:

```
ExecaError: Command failed with exit code 1:
ovsx publish --packagePath mac-shortcut-mapper-1.2.2.vsix --azure-credential
error: unknown option '--azure-credential'
```

## Cause

`semantic-release-vsce` 6.0.10 shells out to the **vsce and ovsx CLIs** and passes `--azure-credential` to both. Open VSX is a different registry, run by the Eclipse Foundation, with its own token and no Azure credential concept — so turning on Azure auth for the Marketplace broke Open VSX publishing.

## Fix

6.0.25 replaced both CLIs with their APIs — *"use vsce and ovsx APIs instead of CLI commands"*. Confirmed by reading the installed 6.1.6 rather than trusting the changelog:

```js
import { publish as ovsxPublish } from 'ovsx';
await ovsxPublish(ovsxOptions);
```

No CLI, so no flag can reach ovsx.

`package.json` already permitted this (`^6.0.10`); only the lockfile was pinned four minors back. The large lockfile diff is that upgrade's transitive closure.

## Note on the tag

`v1.2.2` was created before the failure, so the next successful run resumes from there. semantic-release is idempotent about this — it will not try to re-cut an existing tag — but if anything looks confused about versions afterwards, that tag is why.

## Verifying

Three signals, all currently unchanged, that should move together:

| | now |
|---|---|
| Marketplace version | 1.2.1, last updated 18 May 2026 |
| Latest GitHub release | v1.2.1 |
| Issue #55 | open |

A green run is not one of them.

## Follow-up

With the APIs bundled, `pnpm add -g @vscode/vsce ovsx` in `release.yml` is now redundant. Left in place so this PR changes one thing.

author: sno2wman
body:
## What this adds

A page-level Storybook story for `/work/[work_id]/edit`. The page had no story before this change.

The story mocks the data that the `work/[work_id]` layout load returns (`WorkSchema` fields, `links`, `head`) and the sources that the page load returns. It reuses the shape of the sibling stories for `/work/[work_id]` and `/work/[work_id]/history`. All values are invented, and all dates are fixed ISO strings, so the story stays deterministic.

## What the stories cover

- **Member** — a plain member. The origin select stays disabled for every approved source.
- **Member With Pending Work** — the work waits for approval, so a member can change the origin.
- **Editor** — an editor can change the origin of every source, and gets the link that relists a source which is down.
- **Moderator** — a moderator also gets the delete button.
- **With Form Error** — the edit action failed, so the page shows the values that the server sent back.

`parameters.msw.handlers` answers the `/api/wiki/page` request that `GuidelineWarning` makes on mount. It also answers `/api/upload/origin` and `/api/upload/refresh`, because a reviewer can trigger both from the source table.

## Why this is needed

The source table on this page is the widest table in the app. It is `inline-block` with no width cap, and its origin `<select>` forces the column to an intrinsic width. The table pushes the page sideways. That is the same defect class as `/comments` (#984). A fix needs a story to compare against.

One mock source has no title, so its cell falls back to the raw URL. That URL has a query string. This is the content shape that makes the table widest, and the later fix must see it.

This pull request adds the story only. It does not change `+page.svelte` or any other production code.

author: jphilbrick10
body:
v0.22.0 failed on **all five** standalone-binary jobs:

```
FAIL: packaged web/data payload differs from current source:
missing=['bundle/_internal/one_link/web/dr_test.html']
```

`build_binary.py` deliberately withholds `web/dr_test.html` — a Double Ratchet self-test harness the daemon serves **unguarded** on the loopback UI — from every frozen bundle. The release-time payload verifier walks every source asset and demands each one be present. Both were right on their own terms; together they made a release impossible.

## It could only surface under a tag

| | |
|---|---|
| v0.21.0 tagged | 2026-07-31 |
| exclusion landed | **2026-08-05** |
| releases in between | none |

The verifier runs in `release.yml` and nowhere else, so the contradiction sat latent for four days and the next tag was the first thing that could expose it. Same shape as the TPM bench: a release-only path master never runs.

## Fixed as one source of truth

`build_identity.DELIBERATELY_UNPACKAGED` is read by the builder (what to filter) **and** the verifier (what not to expect), so they cannot drift again. The file still ships in the wheel and stays in `EXPECTED_STABLE_PACKAGE_DATA` — only frozen bundles withhold it.

**The gate stayed strict.** A bundle that *contains* the file is still refused — "must not ship" is the point. That made two fixtures wrong: they copied the whole source tree, staging a bundle that must never exist. Both now drop withheld files.

## The guarding test got stronger, not weaker

It grepped `build_binary.py` for two literals, and its own comment records why leniency there is fatal — an earlier version normalised backslashes and accepted a wrong value: *"a deliberately lenient assertion is a gate that cannot fail."*

Since the literals moved, it now **generates the spec**, **parses** the emitted `_FORBIDDEN` list (comparing values rather than fighting `repr()` escaping), and **executes the filter** to confirm `dr_test` is rejected while `index.html` is kept.

**Calibrated:** emptying `DELIBERATELY_UNPACKAGED` fails three tests.

## Why 0.22.1

`RELEASE_CHECKLIST` is explicit that a tag is not reused. Nothing was published under v0.22.0 — `publish tagged release` was skipped — but the tag exists and stays.

Full suite: **9470 passed, 260 skipped, 0 failed.** Shell rebuilt and re-pinned to UI hash `ac7ded38`; One Link relaunched on it.

author: girnarholdings
body:
## What & why

Extends `tridelphi expose` toward the **managed-cloud** shapes a vibe-coded app leaks — the ones that hit apps built on Next.js/Vite + a hosted database. Every invariant holds: native detectors are **pure file reads** (no subprocess/network), secret **values stay masked**, gating stays conservative, and every message keeps the honest static-read caveat.

The through-line is one honesty insight the tool now applies consistently: **some keys are public by design** (Firebase web key, Supabase anon key) and calling them leaks makes the tool cry wolf — the real protection there is server-side **Security Rules**, which this PR can now *also detect as wide open*.

## Changes

**Framework "public env" leaks (Category A) — `_detect_public_env`.** A secret behind a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` / `VITE_` / `REACT_APP_` / `PUBLIC_` / `EXPO_PUBLIC_` / `GATSBY_` / `VUE_APP_` / `NUXT_PUBLIC_` prefix is **inlined into the client bundle** and ships to every visitor. Provider-key-shaped value → `critical`; secret-named var → `warning`. The message is about the *prefix* (the real trap), and the committed-secret path (category F) now skips public-prefixed lines so each line yields one precise finding.

**More managed-cloud key shapes (Category A).** OpenRouter, Groq, HuggingFace, Replicate, PlanetScale, Supabase access token, Docker, Figma. OpenRouter's `sk-or-v1-` is matched before the OpenAI pattern, whose guard widens to `(?!ant-|or-)`, so a key is never double-reported.

**Supabase role nuance (Category A → note/critical).** A Supabase key is a JWT; `_supabase_role` decodes the payload (pure, defensive `try/except`): a `service_role` key in a bundle is `critical` (it **bypasses Row Level Security**), while an `anon` key is a `note` (public by design — protection is RLS, not hiding the key). Mirrors the Firebase fix.

**Open cloud data rules & public buckets (new Category G) — `_detect_open_cloud_rules`.** Firebase/Firestore/Storage rules that `allow … : if true` → `critical` (**completes the Firebase story**: the public-key note says "lock down Security Rules"; now we flag when they're open). A terraform world ACL (`public-read-write` / `allUsers`) → advisory `warning`, scoped to `.tf`/`.tf.json` only.

## Files
- `tridelphi/expose.py` — new secret patterns + OpenAI `(?!ant-|or-)` guard; `_supabase_role` + role branch; `_detect_public_env` (A) and `_detect_open_cloud_rules` (G); `_Surface.cloud_rules` + discovery; category-F `.env` de-dup; `CATEGORIES += G`.
- `tests/test_expose.py` — 9 new tests.
- `README.md` — expose table updated.

## Testing
- **9 new tests**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secret → A critical, masked, names the prefix, no F dup; suspicious public-env name → warning; Supabase `service_role` → critical, `anon` → **note**; OpenRouter **not** double-reported as OpenAI; malformed JWT never crashes; open `firestore.rules` → G critical; locked rules → clean; terraform `public-read-write` → G warning.
- Invariants still green: `test_native_path_spawns_no_subprocess`, deterministic SARIF, shape gate (category G included).
- Full suite **623 passed / 6 skipped**; `ruff` clean; repo self-scan **0/0** and `tridelphi expose .` all-clear; end-to-end confirms the new criticals gate (`--fail-on critical` → exit 1).

author: jameskilbynet
body:
Fixes the CLS regression: **P73 / CLS 0.647** on the homepage at 2026-08-09 07:58 UTC, against P91–93 / CLS 0 all morning.

The two measurements straddle the force-full rebuild — P93 was taken at 07:35, mid-rebuild, so it scored the *old* output; P73 at 07:58 scored the rebuilt site.

## Cause

`_resolve_css_path` did a bare `lstrip('/')` before the disk lookup. At the point the transformer runs, hrefs are absolute — `convert_to_staging.py` doesn't rewrite them to relative until "Prepare output for deployment", long afterwards. `lstrip('/')` doesn't touch a scheme, so the lookup became:

```
static-output/https:/jameskilby.co.uk/wp-content/.../header.min.css
```

which never exists. Query strings failed the same way.

Measured against the live homepage, holding the CSS on disk constant and varying only the href form:

| href form | sheets resolved | critical CSS |
|---|---|---|
| relative | 3/3 | 11,684 chars |
| **absolute (the actual transform-time state)** | **0/3** | **0 chars** |
| relative + `?ver=` | 0/3 | 0 chars |

This is the **same defect #146 fixed** in `html_transformer`'s stylesheet inliner. There are two copies of the resolver; only one was fixed.

## Why it costs CLS

It fails silently — an unresolvable sheet and a sheet with nothing above the fold both yield zero rules, and the caller can't tell them apart. Meanwhile `_convert_css_to_preload` defers those exact sheets.

So `header.min.css` (13.7 KB) and `content.min.css` (19.1 KB), which carry the above-fold layout, were loaded async with **none of their rules inlined**. The page paints, then reflows. The homepage's critical CSS came out at 4,302 chars against the 11,684 it produces once hrefs resolve.

## Why it surfaced now, not on 2026-08-08

Incremental builds seeded `static-output` from `public/`, where `convert_to_staging` had already made hrefs relative — so the resolver worked *by accident* and pages got their full critical CSS.

#148 made incremental builds seed from raw generator output, correctly and identically to a full build, which removed the accident. **Full builds have always produced the degraded output.** The divergence measured before #148 — 4,621 vs 12,058 bytes of critical CSS on the same page — was this bug all along, and the stale seed was masking it.

## No externalisation risk

`max_critical_css` (15,000) sits below `max_inline_critical` (16,384), so a harvested block can never cross the threshold that spills it into a separate render-blocking file. Larger critical CSS will not add a stylesheet request or push pages past the 5/5 budget.

## Does this change `public/`?

Yes. Every page's `<style id="critical-css">` block grows — roughly 4.3 KB → 11.7 KB on the homepage. That's the intended effect: the deferred sheets' above-fold rules land in the inline block where they prevent the shift.

## Tests

6 tests appended to `tests/test_extract_critical_css.py`; **5 fail without the fix**. Each href form, the invariant that form must not change output at all (the full-vs-incremental divergence), that a third-party sheet is still not mapped onto a same-named local file, and an end-to-end assertion that any sheet `_convert_css_to_preload` defers has contributed its above-fold rules first — a deferred sheet with no inlined rules is a layout shift by definition.

## Verify after merge

Watch CLS on the next Quality Checks run. Expect it back to ~0 and Performance back to the low 90s. If CLS stays high, the remaining shift is not stylesheet-driven and needs a different investigation.

fixes #28 

## What

  Clarify Path D as a self-hosted x402 service rather than a managed public endpoint on `agents.sera.cx`.

## Why

 Caddy has no `/x402/*` route and Docker Compose has no `x402-service`, but the public copy implied that `agents.sera.cx` provided a
  hosted x402 API. This change aligns the documentation with the deployed infrastructure without promoting unverified live payment flows
  to a public service.

## How

- Update the landing page, README, Concepts, Architecture, and deployment docs to describe Path D as local/self-hosted. - Document the localhost demo (`localhost:8402`) and explicitly state that `agents.sera.cx` does not host x402 endpoints.
- Link live-mode guidance to `x402-service/README.md` and `SECURITY-MODEL.md`, including the Base Sepolia E2E and explicit operator-
  approval requirements.
- Update `SECURITY.md` to reflect the current CDP facilitator integration and production-verification status.
- Add a Node built-in `node:test` regression test that verifies:
   - Caddy does not route `/x402/*`.
   - Compose does not deploy `x402-service`.
   - Public docs do not advertise `agents.sera.cx/x402`.
   - Path D includes self-hosting and live-readiness guidance.
 
 ## Smoke check

  - [x] `npm run build` passes
  - [x] `tools/list` returns the expected number of tools (55)

  Additional validation:

  - [x] `npm run typecheck`

  ## Notes for reviewers

  - Root cause: `docker-compose.yml` contains only static, gateway, and Caddy services; `agents-gateway/deploy/Caddyfile` routes only the
  gateway API surface and has no `/x402/*` matcher.

author: tjdwls101010
body:
## 무엇을 바꿨나

`promulgated_without_number` 와 `sitting_gaps` 를 게이트에서 보고값으로 내렸다. `sitting_gaps` 질의는 종류별 차수 규칙에 맞게 다시 썼다.

`readme.md` 의 상태와 "시작하기"를 채웠다.

## 왜

계획 7단계대로 실제 데이터에 감사를 돌렸더니 게이트 둘이 빨간불인데 **고칠 방법이 없었다.** 게이트는 "우리 수집이 틀렸다"만 담아야 한다 — 원천이 보장하지 않는 것을 등식으로 걸면 영구 빨간불이 되고, 늘 빨간 신호는 신호가 아니다.

**`promulgated_without_number`** — 원천을 다시 받아 확인했다.

```
2218525  announceDt='공포일자 2026-06-02' | announceNo='공포번호' | lawName='공포법률'
2215132  announceDt='공포일자 2026-02-19' | announceNo='공포번호' | lawName='공포법률'
2214602  announceDt='공포일자 2025-12-23' | announceNo='공포번호' | lawName='공포법률'
```

`<i>` 라벨만 있고 값 `<span>` 이 비어 있다. 공포일자는 있는데 번호가 없는 의안이 실제로 존재한다. 파서는 맞게 `None` 을 냈다.

**`sitting_gaps`** — 차수 매김 규칙이 종류마다 다르다는 것을 몰랐다.

```
윤석열정부의…국정조사특별위원회   회기 420  차수 1,2,3,4
                                  회기 421  차수 5
                                  회기 422  차수 6,7,8,9,10,11
```

특위·국정조사는 차수가 **임기 전체에 걸쳐** 이어진다. 상임위·예결위만 회기마다 1로 돌아간다(과방위 실측: 415회 1~6, 416회 1~6, 417회 1~9 …). 전부 "같은 회기 안에서 차수−1이 있는가"로 재던 질의는 회기 경계마다 오탐했다 — **70 중 42가 그것이었다.**

종류별로 갈라 28로 줄었지만 게이트로 되돌리지는 않는다. 남은 28도 "우리가 놓친 회의"와 "원천이 공개하지 않는 회의"가 섞여 있고, 우리는 원천의 트리가 열거해 준 id 만 알 뿐 열거되지 않은 회의가 열렸는지는 알 수 없다. **회의 완결성의 진짜 증명은 `meeting_bodies_missing`** — 열거한 id 를 전부 받았는가 — 이고 그건 그대로 게이트다.

## 영향

게이트가 8개에서 6개로, 보고값이 9개에서 11개로 바뀐다. 06번 7단계의 "게이트 9 · 조건부 1 · 보고값 5"라는 숫자와 어긋나는데, 그 숫자는 실측 전에 적힌 것이다.

## 검증

**일부러 망가뜨려 빨간불을 봤다** (계획 7단계). 각 시험은 트랜잭션 안에서 하고 되돌렸다.

| 망가뜨린 것 | 기대 | 실제 |
|---|---|---|
| 의안 한 행(가운데) | `bill_no_gaps` 1 | 0 → **1** |
| 가장 작은 의안번호 | 구멍은 그대로, 하한이 튄다 | gaps 0 유지 · min 2200001 → **2200002** |
| 한 회의의 발언 | `meeting_bodies_missing` 1 | 0 → **1** |
| 상임위 제2차 회의 | `sitting_gaps` +1 | 28 → **29** |
| 국정감사 회의 3건 | 그대로 (알려진 사각지대) | **28 유지**, `meetings_total` 2047 → 2044 |
| 명부 시드 없음 | `fail` 이 아니라 `skip` | **skip** |

두 값을 따로 둔 이유가 두 번째 줄에서 그대로 보인다 — 하한이 통째로 밀리면 "구멍"으로는 안 잡힌다.

**수집 중 스냅샷의 남은 빨간불 둘은 정상이다.** `dangling_alt_bills 106`(대안 의안을 아직 안 받았다) · `unresolved_retriable 9`(회의록 재시도 대상, 전부 `attempts=1`).

## What
The **Security** workflow's `Dependency audit` step (`pnpm audit --audit-level high`) has been failing on `main`, which is the last CI failure on the default branch.

## Why it failed
16 high advisories, all in **transitive dev/build-tooling** deps:
- `brace-expansion` (via eslint, vitest/coverage) — ReDoS/DoS
- `js-yaml` (via commitlint) — quadratic CPU
- `fast-uri` (via commitlint, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk>ajv) — host confusion
- `postcss` (via vitest) — path traversal
- `ip-address` (via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk>express-rate-limit) — octet parsing

## Fix
Refresh those transitive deps to patched versions **within existing semver ranges** (`pnpm update -r`). Lockfile-only change, no direct dependency bumps.

Result: `pnpm audit --audit-level high` now passes (exit 0). Remaining advisories are low/moderate only (4 low, 15 moderate).

## Verification
- `pnpm audit --audit-level high` → PASS
- `pnpm typecheck` → clean
- `pnpm test` → 107/107 pass
- `pnpm build` → OK

author: doyun-1999
body:
## 작업 내용

#116 코드리뷰에서 지적된 🟠 Major 2건을 반영한다. #116 이 그대로 머지돼 현재 `main` 에 남아 있는 문제다.

## 변경 이유

### 1. 세션 만료 이동이 실패하면 복구할 수 없다

```kotlin
// before
private suspend fun goToLogin() {
    sessionExpiredNotifier.consume()      // ← 먼저 소비
    redirectedToLogin = true              // ← 가드도 먼저 닫음
    runCatching { sessionRepository.clear() }
    val sent = navigationHelper.navigate(NavigationEvent.To(AuthGraphBaseRoute, popUpTo = true))
    if (!sent) Log.w(TAG, "Dropped session-expired navigation event")   // 로그만
}
```

`navigationHelper.navigate()` 는 `Channel.trySend` 결과를 그대로 돌려준다. 버퍼가 가득 차거나 채널이 닫혀 실패하면 로그만 남는데, **그 시점엔 만료 상태(`consume()`)도 가드(`redirectedToLogin`)도 이미 닫혀 있다.**

결과:
- `SessionExpiredNotifier` 는 `StateFlow` 라 같은 값을 다시 내보내지 않는다 → 통지로는 재시도 불가
- 다음 앱 진입의 `verifySession()` 은 `if (redirectedToLogin) return` 에서 빠져나간다 → 재시도 불가

**로그인 안 된 화면에 영구히 남는다.** #116 이 고치려던 바로 그 증상이다.

### 2. 콜드 스타트에서 세션 검사를 통째로 건너뛴다

```kotlin
val route = _startRoute.value ?: return@launch
```

`verifySession()` 은 `onStart` → `onAppEntered()` 에서 불린다. 콜드 스타트에서는 `onStart` 가 시작 목적지 판정(`resolveStartDestination()` 은 suspend)보다 먼저 오므로 `_startRoute` 가 아직 `null` 이고, 그 실행에서는 검사가 아예 일어나지 않는다.

## 주요 변경사항

**이동이 큐에 들어간 뒤에 소비**

```kotlin
val sent = navigationHelper.navigate(NavigationEvent.To(AuthGraphBaseRoute, popUpTo = true))
if (sent) {
    sessionExpiredNotifier.consume()
    redirectedToLogin = true
} else {
    Log.w(TAG, "세션 만료 이동 발행 실패 — 상태를 유지해 다음 진입에 다시 시도한다")
}
```

실패하면 만료 상태와 가드를 그대로 둬서, 다음 앱 진입의 `verifySession()` 이 다시 시도한다.

`sessionRepository.clear()` 는 발행 성공 여부와 무관하게 먼저 한다 — 죽은 토큰을 남겨둘 이유가 없고, 남기면 `isLoggedIn()` 이 계속 true 라 `verifySession()` 도 재시도하지 않는다.

**판정을 기다린 뒤 검사**

```kotlin
val route = _startRoute.filterNotNull().first()
```

## 리뷰 지적 중 반영하지 않은 것

> `verifySession()` launches a separate coroutine, so `syncTodaySteps()` can start before the session result is known.

**이미 방어돼 있다.** `SyncTodayStepsUseCase` 첫 줄이 세션을 확인하고 빠진다.

```kotlin
suspend operator fun invoke(...): StepSyncResult? {
    if (!runCatching { sessionRepository.isLoggedIn() }.getOrDefault(false)) return null
```

세션이 죽었으면 `tokenManager.clear()` 로 토큰이 지워져 `isLoggedIn()` 이 false 가 되므로, 걸음 수 동기화는 서버를 건드리지 않고 종료된다. 두 코루틴을 직렬화하면 걸음 수 동기화의 간격 제한(`STEP_SYNC_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`)이 세션 검사에까지 걸려 오히려 검사 빈도가 떨어진다.

## 스크린샷 / 영상

<!-- 로직 변경 — UI 없음 -->

## 리뷰어가 집중해서 봐줬으면 하는 부분

- **`clear()` 를 발행 실패 시에도 하는 게 맞는지.** 위 근거로 그렇게 뒀는데, "이동에 실패했으니 세션도 되돌린다"는 선택지도 있다. 다만 그 경우 죽은 토큰으로 계속 401 을 맞는다.
- **`filterNotNull().first()` 가 영원히 대기할 가능성.** `_startRoute` 는 `init` 의 코루틴이 반드시 값을 넣고(실패해도 `AUTH` 폴백), 안 넣더라도 `viewModelScope` 라 화면이 사라지면 취소된다. 문제없다고 봤는데 확인 부탁.
- **기기 검증 미완료.** 재현이 까다롭다 — `navigate()` 가 false 를 반환하는 상황(채널 버퍼 초과)을 실기기에서 만들기 어렵다. 코드 경로로만 확인했다.

## 체크리스트

- [x] 로컬 빌드 확인 (`:presentation`)
- [x] 셀프 리뷰 완료
- [ ] **기기 동작 확인 — 미완료**
- [x] 불필요한 로그/주석 제거

## 관련 이슈

<!-- #116 코드리뷰 후속 -->

author: levicobra
body:
## The repositioning

The page now opens on **"Palantir, government, AI."** and carries a dedicated Foundry / Gotham / AIP section *above* the general services:

- **Foundry development** — ontology design (objects, links, action types), Pipeline Builder and code repositories, incremental transforms and data health, Workshop apps
- **AIP with review gates** — AIP Logic bound to ontology actions, task-scoped agents, evaluation sets before deployment, write-back that records the approver. Deliberately the same standard the page already argues for elsewhere
- **Gotham & integration** — entity resolution and link analysis, data connection and sync health, permissioning and markings that survive an audit, handover documentation

Honolulu is put to work as a *reason* rather than an address: one time zone from **INDOPACOM, Pacific Fleet and U.S. Army Pacific**, which is what forward-deployed work actually needs.

## The status discipline is untouched — and extended

The file's header comment is explicit that no claim on this page may imply past performance. So a second capability note sits **inside** the new section stating plainly that there is **no Palantir engagement, no partner status and no certification** to point at, keeping the disclaimer adjacent to the claim rather than only at the bottom.

Nothing was added to the **Stack** list, which is framed as "what gets used, and where" — a usage claim. Palantir stays in capability framing until there's real delivery history to move it.

## Also

- Title, meta description and social text now name Palantir, so the page is findable by someone searching for it.
- Consulting gets **its own preview card** in the page's azure theme instead of sharing the hub's generic one — it's the link that goes to a prospect.
- Nav subtitle updated estate-wide (`Government · software · AI` → `Palantir · government · AI`), 10 files, no stale copies remaining.

## Two tooling problems surfaced while syncing

**`sync_nav.py` was not idempotent** — same class of bug as `apply_themes.py`. It grabbed the nav CSS from the source *starting at its comment banner*, but replaced the target *starting after* the banner, so every run left the old one and inserted a new one. Pages had accumulated **three** copies. Now anchors on the banner, which is idempotent and cleans up the existing duplicates. Verified: 3 → 1 everywhere, and a second run produces zero byte changes.

**`sync_satellite_nav.py` is broken, pre-existing and left as found.** It exits before writing anything, looking for `<div class="sitebar">` in mil — all 8 `sitebar` occurrences there are CSS; the element doesn't exist. mil's header markup has diverged from what the script expects. Repairing it means reconciling that markup against a generated 175 KB page, so I updated the three satellite files directly instead and flagged it rather than risking that page.

## Verification

- Page rendered in a browser at desktop and mobile widths: correct title and `h1`, no horizontal overflow at either.
- Estate-wide sweep: no duplicate nav banners, no raw ampersands in any `meta content`, no stale nav subtitles.
- New preview card verified at 1200×630 by reading the JPEG header.
