body:
Empilée sur #26 : cible `feat/image-socle-observabilite`, pas `develop`. GitHub la
recibleera seule quand #26 fusionnera.

Répond à FT-53 du backlog consommateur — les 7 dashboards du §8.3 et les alertes du §8.4 du
DAT. Le §8.3 précise que ces écrans vivent « dans le dépôt de la plateforme, pas ici » : c'est
donc entièrement du travail de ce dépôt.

## Les dashboards

Sept écrans, 51 panneaux, provisionnés en JSON versionné sous
`grafana/provisioning/dashboards/socle/`, regroupés dans un dossier « Socle ».
`allowUiUpdates: false` : ce qui est modifié à la souris ne survit pas au redémarrage, le JSON
reste la seule vérité.

Le §8.3 annonçait « Par service (×5) ». C'est **un** dashboard à sélecteur `$service` et non
cinq copies — cinq copies divergent, un sélecteur non.

Aucun écran ne nomme un service du consommateur. Le seul qui suppose des noms est « Métier »,
qui lit des compteurs applicatifs : sa convention de nommage est documentée dans un panneau de
texte en tête, et c'est signalé comme tel.

## Les alertes

De 7 à 15 règles. Budgets de latence par opération (ENF-01/02), remplissage disque à 80 et
90 %, cible injoignable, file de rebut, échecs d'authentification, sauvegarde absente.

Les écritures sont reconnues au **nom du span**, par convention, et non par une liste
d'opérations : inscrire ici les opérations d'un projet lierait la plateforme à ce projet.

## Trois exportateurs entrent dans l'image

`node-exporter`, `blackbox-exporter` et `postgres_exporter`. Les deux premiers étaient
explicitement exclus, avec des raisons écrites en tête du `Dockerfile`. **Ces raisons tenaient**
— vérifié : embarqué, node-exporter rapportait quatre systèmes de fichiers dont trois n'étaient
que des bind-mounts Docker, et la taille annoncée est celle de la VM, pas de la machine.

Ce qui lève l'exclusion : le disque à surveiller ici est `/var/lib/obs`, là où Prometheus, Loki
et Tempo écrivent — précisément un volume de conteneur. Sans lui, l'alerte disque n'avait
aucune source en mode image, et une alerte sans source est pire qu'absente. Le bruit est filtré
à la source (`--collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude`), et l'en-tête du `Dockerfile` a été
réécrit pour dire ce que l'image fait désormais, réserves comprises. Pour de vraies métriques
machine, node-exporter reste un service à part avec `pid: host` et `/:/host:ro`.

`postgres_exporter` ne démarre **que** si `DATA_SOURCE_NAME` est fournie : absent ou sain,
jamais en boucle d'échec.

## Cibles optionnelles : muettes, pas fausses

Trois alertes et deux dashboards dépendent d'un composant que la plateforme n'héberge pas.
Les jobs `postgres`, `rabbitmq` et `keycloak` se découvrent par fichier
(`prometheus/targets/`), à `[]` par défaut. Pas de cible, pas de série, donc **pas de fausse
alerte « service injoignable »** — ce qu'un `static_configs` pointant une cible absente aurait
produit en continu. Les règles existent et s'allument seules le jour du branchement.

## Deux défauts trouvés en recette

**Les sondes de la démo sonnaient en permanence.** Activer `blackbox-exporter` dans l'image
réveillait `blackbox-demo`, dont les cibles n'existent qu'en mode compose : deux `ProbeDown`
en continu chez le consommateur. Tant que l'exportateur était absent, le job tombait entier et
personne ne le voyait. Passé en découverte par fichier, vidé hors `DEMO_TARGETS=true`.

**`oneuptime_webhook_url` n'était jamais créé.** `alertmanager.yml` le référence pour le
receiver `page-oncall`, mais l'entrypoint ne créait que le webhook Slack.

## Recette

Sur l'image construite, pas sur les fichiers :

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| Sonde de santé | `healthy` |
| Processus | 12 actifs ; `postgres_exporter` absent, faute de DSN — attendu |
| Dashboards, via l'API Grafana | 7, UID conformes |
| Règles, via l'API Prometheus | 15 alertes |
| Cibles | 7/7 en *up*, aucune cible fantôme |
| Alertes qui sonnent | **aucune** |
| Empreinte | 341 Mio |

Vérifié aussi : `node_filesystem_size_bytes` ne rapporte plus qu'une série, `/var/lib/obs`, et
l'expression exacte de l'alerte disque évalue à 21,9 %. Et en injectant
`RABBITMQ_METRICS_TARGET=rabbitmq-inexistant:15692`, la cible est bien écrite puis vue *down* —
le mécanisme de découverte fonctionne de bout en bout.

## Écart assumé avec le DAT

Le §8.4 demande « Email + Telegram ». La plateforme conserve Slack et OneUptime, plus riches
pour l'astreinte. Écart assumé côté produit ; c'est le DAT qui sera aligné.

author: recondesigns
body:
One line in `AGENTS.md`. No code.

#63 is closed — the Figma file now matches what ships, and `ResultSlot` and `InputPad` bind their `width`/`height` to `Size/slot` and `Size/pad`.

That binding is the part that actually stops the drift recurring, and **it is invisible from the repo**. Before it existed, nothing on the canvas aliased those size variables, so changing one moved nothing and the file could sit out of step with the code indefinitely — which it did three times, each caught only when someone happened to open the file.

Worth writing down because from inside Figma the binding looks like an ordinary component property, so the obvious way to resize a variant is to unbind it first. Doing that quietly reopens the trap.

## Note

Touches `AGENTS.md`, as does #74. Different sections, so they merge cleanly in either order.

author: cryptoreporthub
body:
## Council glass B/B + tier-2 · Rogue attribution fix + one-time rebalance

### Why
The legacy fallback in expert_display.leading_expert_for_pick returned "quant" for any pick with no classifiable signals and no expert scores. Every such row was stamped expert="quant", and the weight replay (incl. archive rows) credited it - pinning quant at the 2.0 learned cap despite "Graded 0". That was the bug behind quant 2.00.

### Fixes landed directly on this branch
1. **Fallback -> Rogue** - internal/council/expert_display.py: unresolved picks now return ("rogue", "Rogue"); Rogue is NOT in CANONICAL_EXPERTS, never enters weights/scoring/pick generation.
2. **Attribution resolver** - internal/council/expert_attribution.py: all-failed paths resolve to ("rogue", "unresolved") and stamp rows explicitly.
3. **Archive hygiene (replay guard)** - internal/council/signal_expert.py expert_for_replay_row: bare stored expert stamp with no signal evidence -> "rogue", so replay never re-awards quant. Real signal evidence is untouched.
4. **Rogue tracking (weight-like %)** - internal/learning/weight_deltas.py: expert_graded_counts includes rogue · new build_rogue_stats() (count, share_pct, hit_rate, promotion_rule: hit_rate >= 0.55 & count >= 30 -> consider official) · new count_rogue_replay_rows() for fix-3 observability.
5. **Rebalance CLI** - scripts/rebalance_expert_weights.py: w' = 1 + 0.5(w-1), clamped [0.1, 2.0] (quant 2.00 -> 1.50), --dry-run/--save, emits weight_change trail (reason rogue_rebalance_attribution_fix), prints rogue replay-skip count. Run post-merge: python scripts/rebalance_expert_weights.py --save.
6. **UI B/B** - council.html: arc cards on real weight fields + Graded N + Rogue strip + cap note · tribunal_hero.html: instrument console (AVG ACC / WIN RATE meters, SIGNAL/RSI/STOCH/7D, variance floor) fed from /api/learning/stats, tier-2 change-driven flash/meters. No continuous per-card animation; prefers-reduced-motion respected.
7. **Checks/tests** - .github/scripts/check_templates.py context defaults; tests/test_rogue_attribution.py (fallback->rogue, replay guard, rogue not scored, rebalance math 2.00->1.50).

### Follow-up hunks (large files - exact anchors verified, not blind-edited)
These ship as byte-exact patches because the files exceed the in-session read cap; apply in your checkout (or ask to land via a focused job):

- internal/learning/routes.py (in _learning_snapshot() dict): add "rogue_stats": build_rogue_stats(), and extend the existing from internal.learning.weight_deltas import (...) block with build_rogue_stats.
- internal/learning/dashboard_context.py (fast_shell_dashboard_context()): add ctx["rogue_stats"] = build_rogue_stats() + the same import, so the Rogue strip renders server-side.
- static/js/cockpit_hydrate.js (186 KB): keep the SSR arc-card markup; if hydration re-renders .soulmap-constellation/soul-orb cards into it, port the council render to the new arc structure (anchor: SOUL_ORB_COLORS / soulTrendFromDelta).

### Evidence
- tests/test_rogue_attribution.py parametrized rebalance check: 2.0->1.5, 1.0->1.0, 0.4->0.7, clamp 3.0->2.0.
- Replay guard test: bare {"expert":"quant","correct":true} -> "rogue"; {"signal_source":"rsi_crossover","expert":"technical"} -> "technical".
- Rogue excluded from CANONICAL_EXPERTS (asserted).

author: chernistry
body: # User description Closes #3468. `tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py` compared the registered top-level CLI commands against `DOCUMENTED_COMMANDS`, a hand-typed `frozenset`. A command counted as documented the moment its name was typed into the set, and the failure message told the contributor to type it there. This derives the expected set from `docs/reference/cli-reference.md` on disk instead, and keeps the allow-list only as `UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS` - a map from command name to the reason it is not in the reference yet. ### Enforcement rules 1. Every registered top-level command must be documented in `docs/reference/cli-reference.md` or listed in `UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS`. 2. Documenting an exempted command fails the gate until its exemption is removed, so the exemption set shrinks as documentation lands. 3. Every entry in `UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS` must name a registered command and carry a non-empty reason. 4. A missing `cli-reference.md` fails the gate rather than degrading to "nothing is documented". ### What the reference is read as documentation `_parse_documented_commands` accepts the shapes the reference actually uses, and rejects mentions: | Shape | Read as | |---|---| | ``#### `bernstein run` `` | documents `run` | | ``## SPIFFE workload identity: `bernstein spiffe` `` | documents `spiffe` | | ``#### `bernstein voice` / `bernstein listen` `` | documents `voice` and `listen` | | `` \| `bernstein doctor` \| Run diagnostics. \| `` | documents `doctor` | | ``\| `--cli NAME` \| Any adapter from `bernstein adapters list`. \|`` | not documentation - a cross-reference inside a description cell | | ``## `bernstein pipeline` is covered in the workflow guide`` | not documentation - a pointer, not a section | Both directions are pinned by tests, because the extractor is the whole gate: a shape it cannot see produces an exemption nobody needed, and a mention it counts opens the gate for an undocumented command. ### Current state of the split 199 registered top-level commands: 140 documented in `cli-reference.md`, 59 exempt. Nothing is uncovered, and no exemption names a command the reference already documents. ### `scripts/regen_contract_drift.py` `regen_documented_commands()` is report-only and never writes. `contract-drift-autofix.yml` pushes regen output straight onto the source PR's head ref, so a fixture that appended `"": "Bot-added exemption"` would let an undocumented command go green with no human decision - the hand-typed allow-list this change removes, rebuilt by a bot. The fixture now reports on stderr and returns False; the workflow's existing tracking-issue path is where the choice between documenting and exempting is made. It reports every state the gate fails on - registered but undocumented, exempt but now documented, exempt but not a registered command, exempt without a reason - so a run cannot print "nothing to add" while CI is red on one of them. A missing or unreadable `cli-reference.md` refuses explicitly instead of substituting an empty string. The documentation-parsing rules are imported from the gate rather than duplicated, with a test asserting both read the reference identically. ### Verification Fail-before / pass-after, all run against this branch. The gate fires on a registered command with no documentation and no exemption (throwaway command added to the top-level group): ``` FAILED tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py::test_all_cli_commands_are_documented E Failed: New CLI command(s) detected that are neither documented in docs/reference/cli-reference.md nor listed in UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS: zzz-probe-undocumented ``` Documenting that command in `cli-reference.md` - and nothing else - turns it green, so the on-disk document is load-bearing rather than decorative: ``` 1 passed, 6 deselected ``` The shrink rule fires when an exempted command gains documentation (appending ``#### `bernstein serve` `` to the reference): ``` FAILED tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py::test_exemptions_are_not_already_documented ``` Phantom and empty-reason entries fire: ``` E Failed: UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS contains names that are not registered commands: adapters-empty-probe, zzz-phantom-cmd E Failed: UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS contains entries without a non-empty reason: adapters-empty-probe ``` Loosening the extractor's end-of-line anchor is caught: ``` FAILED tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py::test_parser_rejects_mere_mentions[mid-heading-mention] ``` The regen fixture reports and writes nothing: ``` [regen] UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS: 1 registered command(s) are neither documented in cli-reference.md nor exempt: zzz-probe-undocumented. [regen] This fixture does not patch itself: an exemption records a decision, and a bot-written one records none. ``` Suite: ``` uv run pytest tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py tests/unit/test_cli_command_registration.py tests/unit/test_regen_contract_drift.py -q 234 passed, 1 warning in 43.02s uv run ruff check tests/unit/test_readme_api_coverage.py tests/unit/test_regen_contract_drift.py scripts/regen_contract_drift.py All checks passed! uv run ruff format --check 3 files already formatted ``` ### Note on the test id The gate keeps the node id `test_all_cli_commands_are_documented`. `.github/workflows/contract-drift-autofix.yml` selects that node by name; renaming it made the drift probe exit `ERROR: not found` on every run, so the workflow reported drift unconditionally and could no longer detect real drift. Observed in run 31303712728 on this branch before the fix. ### Exclusions None. ### Review-bot findings acknowledged without a code change - `3743455570` - not reproducible. `scripts/run_tests.py --shard` (ci.yml:1582) runs the whole `tests/` tree, so the three exemption tests block the required `CI gate` on every code PR; `contract-drift-autofix.yml` is the auto-patch convenience, not a gate, and the states it omits are not bot-patchable. The half that was real - the regen script staying silent about them - is fixed in c7b87c79. - `3743455572` - a real property of `contract-drift-autofix.yml`, not introduced here. That job already runs the same test file under pytest and imports the PR's `src/bernstein/cli` tree with the same persisted write token, before this import is reached. Splitting analysis from the privileged push is a workflow change this PR does not otherwise touch. - `3743490249` - correct, and not closable from inside this diff. `contract-drift-autofix.yml` `paths:` does not list `docs/reference/cli-reference.md`, and `ci.yml` classifies `^docs/` as `docs_only`, which puts `test` in `DOCS_ONLY_SKIPPABLE` - so a docs-only PR that documents an exempted command runs neither the drift workflow nor the unit shards, and the shrink rule does not fire. Bounded rather than permanent: the stale exemption fails the next PR touching `src/` or `tests/`. The fix is one line in `paths:`, which belongs in its own change rather than an unreviewed CI trigger edit inside a test-only diff. --- --- # Generated description Below is a concise technical summary of the changes proposed in this PR: Replace the hand-maintained CLI documentation allow-list with an on-disk reference parser and explicit UNDOCUMENTED_EXEMPTIONS, enforcing coverage, exemption validity, an

## Summary
All 7 previously "coming soon" reports are now fully built, following real accounting practice:

- **Trial Balance** — net balance per account as of a date, correct Debit/Kredit column, with a balance-check.
- **Balance Sheet** — Assets vs Liabilities + Equity, Retained Earnings computed from cumulative Revenue-COGS-Opex. Liabilities honestly shows RM0 with a note (no AP/loan accounts modeled yet).
- **Cash Book Statement** — Terimaan/Bayaran ledger per bank with running balance.
- **Aging Report** — outstanding AR per job, bucketed by days since invoice (0-30/31-60/61-90/90+).
- **Bank Reconciliation Report** — book balance vs manually-entered statement balance, flagged reconciled/not (full itemized reconciliation would need a clearing-status field not yet tracked — noted honestly in the UI).
- **Sales Report** — invoices by department and customer for a year.
- **Installment Outstanding** — every unpaid installment across special-arrangement jobs, overdue ones flagged.

Also fixed the sidebar's Finance submenu clipping long labels like "Bank Reconciliation Report" — now wraps instead of being cut off by the sidebar's hidden overflow.

<!-- Link the issue. -->
Closes #

> **Blocked on publishing `@evinvest/uikit@0.9.0`.** The source side is done and verified; the lockfile cannot be regenerated until the version is on the registry. See *Before merging*.

Everything the temporary override supplied now ships in the package — the surface ladder, the AA fixes, and the palette referencing the semantic tokens rather than copying them. Two sources of truth for one colour is exactly what the upstream fix existed to end, so the copy goes.

## Verified, not assumed

I packed the current `lib` main locally and installed that build into this branch rather than waiting to find out after a publish.

- The guard fired first, naming all ten redundant tokens and the files to delete — the mechanism doing its job:
  > `@evinvest/uikit now ships these tokens itself: card, popover, secondary, muted, muted-foreground, primary, primary-foreground, destructive, destructive-foreground, border.`
- With the override removed, **every one of those tokens resolves exactly once**, from upstream. No leftover old/new pairs in the compiled CSS.
- `bg-main-card` and `bg-card` both emit `background-color: var(--card)`.
- The rendered dashboard is unchanged: one teal (`#2a9d8f`, 5 usages) and one solid fill plus the switch — identical counts to before the removal.

## Guards kept

Two of them outlive the override, retargeted at the installed package:

- the palette must **reference** the semantic tokens, not repeat them — the drift that left profile, settings and wallet on the old colour while the dashboard moved;
- the account-chip remote must import those tokens, and its theme import must stay **unlayered** — layering it hides the spacing scale, so fractional steps compile to nothing and the chip collapses.

Both describe failures that shipped once and neither announced itself. The third guard went with the override it existed to remove.

## Before merging

```
nix run .#publish -- minor        # in EV-invest/lib, needs a valid NPM_TOKEN
cd cabinet/frontend && npm install # regenerates the lockfile against 0.9.0
```

`package.json` already asks for `^0.9.0`; the lockfile still pins `0.8.0` and is deliberately left alone, so CI will fail until that `npm install` lands. I could not run the publish myself — `npm whoami` returns 401 and the token in `~/.npmrc` is expired.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-reviewed the diff
- [x] Docs updated if behavior changed — the surviving rationale moved into the guards

author: recondesigns
body:
Two tuning constants, both settled by playing at the machine rather than from the numbers. Nothing touches the game model, the store, or what gets recorded.

## The read-back starts at dot 4

Down from 5. **This adds exactly one read-back per round** — the one at dot 4 — because every read-back from 5 up happens either way. It is a single event, not a compounding cost:

| Cadence | Added per round |
|---|---|
| Fast | 3.7s |
| Normal | 4.0s |
| Relaxed | **4.5s** |
| Slow | 5.0s |

Set against what the grouping already saves on a twenty-dot round — **1:09 at Relaxed** — the trade is not close.

Where a player's memory actually gives out is a fact about the player, not something to derive from a "7±2" rule of thumb. The classic span is for digits recited in a quiet room; this is spatial positions on a TV, standing at a machine, with noise and fatigue. So it was set by playing.

## The in-group gap has a 160ms floor

A pure proportion breaks down at the fast end. `INTRA_GROUP_RATIO` put Fast's triplets at 350/3 = **117ms**, which ran together and could not be followed — the exact corner flagged as risky when #69 shipped, now confirmed at the machine.

| Option | Fast | Normal | Relaxed | Slow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ratio 1/3 (before) | 117 | 167 | 267 | 367 |
| **floor at 160ms** | **160** | 167 | 267 | 367 |
| ratio 0.4 | 140 | 200 | 320 | 440 |
| ratio 1/2 | 175 | 250 | 400 | 550 |

**The floor fixes only the cadence that is broken.** Raising the ratio instead loosens all four and hands back most of the grouping's saving to solve a problem only Fast has. Raising Fast's own 350 toward Normal's 500 would make Fast pointless.

It costs Fast about 5.6s across a twenty-dot round. That buys nothing if the numbers can't be told apart.

The in-group gap is also clamped to never exceed the boundary gap, which would invert the phrasing. Dead code at today's four cadences, and not dead the moment anyone adds one under 160ms.

## Where the time actually goes

For context, whole-round locked time at the new threshold:

| Cadence | 20 dots: flat → grouped | 12 dots: flat → grouped |
|---|---|---|
| Fast | 3:27 → **3:02** | 1:18 → **1:09** |
| Normal | 3:55 → **3:11** | 1:27 → **1:12** |
| Relaxed | 4:51 → **3:41** | 1:46 → **1:22** |
| Slow | 5:47 → **4:12** | 2:05 → **1:32** |

The grouping is where essentially all of the saving comes from; the threshold is a rounding error against it. Worth knowing before anyone reaches for the threshold to claw back time.

Those savings are exact regardless of voice — flat and grouped speak identical words, so speech cancels and only the gaps differ. The per-digit figure used elsewhere (558ms) was measured in a headed browser against real macOS voices, excluding the first utterance which carries engine warm-up.

## Verification

`pnpm lint` clean, `pnpm build` compiled and typechecked, `pnpm test` 96 assertions across 22 files passing.

Measured in a real browser:

- First read-back lands at **dot 4**; dots 1–3 stay silent and unlock in 610–628ms.
- Fast's triplets are **165ms** against a 354ms boundary, up from 117.
- Normal **171**, Relaxed **271**, Slow **371** — unchanged, which is the entire point of a floor over a ratio change.

**One caveat, not papered over:** `pnpm test` failed once on the first run after the edits, then passed four times in a row. The output scrolled before it was captured, so the failure is unexplained rather than fixed. Treat the suite as green but worth catching properly if it recurs.

## Note

Touches `AGENTS.md`, as does #73. Different sections, so they merge cleanly in either order.

author: anyulled
body:
💡 What
Replaced \`sessionGroups.flatMap((group) => group.sessions)\` with an optimized search approach using \`sessionGroups.find\` and nested \`group.sessions.some()\` internally, alongside nested iteration loops for static param and metadata generation.

🎯 Why
Using \`.flatMap()\` allocates a massive intermediate array in memory and forces a complete O(N) traversal of the nested object structure before \`.find()\` or \`.filter()\` even start executing. By using short-circuit \`.find()\` operations across the multi-level nested objects directly, we can avoid the memory bloat and breakout early once a tag match is found.

📊 Impact
- Saves large intermediate array memory allocations during SSR metadata resolution.
- Shifts lookup behavior from a strict O(N) iteration and array allocation constraint to best-case immediate short-circuiting on the first loop index match.
- Memory usage for tag static param generation avoids building temporary unified arrays.

🔬 Measurement
- View memory allocation footprint reductions using local profiling inside \`generateMetadata\`.
- Check elapsed time for \`generateStaticParams\` execution locally versus production.

author: tommasonardizzijp-art
body:
## Problema

Il delay tra pagine inbox era una lognormale **clampata**:

```python
delay = min(hi, max(lo, random.lognormvariate(0, 0.9) * mid))
```

Il clamp non scarta la coda, la **schiaccia sui bound**. Con i bound 10-40 il **45% dei delay finiva esattamente su due valori fissi**. Due picchi netti in un istogramma temporale sono una firma piu' riconoscibile di un delay costante: nessun umano ripete lo stesso intervallo al millisecondo trenta volte su cento.

Riscontrato sul campo: le due pagine della campagna `AV X @michele.carozza` distano **40,3s**, cioe' un clamp sul massimo.

Allargare il range da solo non basta — col clamp a 10-60 resta il 28% sul massimo. Serve il troncamento per riestrazione.

## Misura su 4000 campioni (massa nell'1% estremo del range)

| implementazione | sul minimo | sul massimo |
|---|---|---|
| clamp 10-40 (prima) | 16,3% | 28,9% |
| clamp 10-60 | 9,9% | 28,0% |
| **troncata 10-60 (dopo)** | **2,0%** | **0,2%** |

## Modifiche

- **`_sample_page_delay()`**: lognormale troncata su `[lo,hi]` per riestrazione. Mediana = media geometrica `sqrt(lo*hi)` — centro naturale in scala logaritmica, quindi code simmetriche e ~68% di accettazione al primo tentativo. Tetto di 20 tentativi + fallback sulla mediana per il caso degenere `lo == hi`.
- **bound 10 → 60s**: mediana reale 24,5s, media 27,8s, CV 0,48.
- **pausa lunga 20-60 → 90-240s**: con il base che arriva a 60s la vecchia era interamente dentro il range normale e non aggiungeva nessuna modalita' distinta.
- **`sweep_inbox_replies.py`** usava `random.uniform` (piatta), unico punto del flusso inbox a farlo: ora riusa `_inbox_page_delay()`.
- commento in `config.py` era stale (diceva "mediana 6s" con i bound gia' a 10-40).

## Costo

~1,5x piu' lenta: 39s medi per pagina contro 26s. Su 150 pagine, da ~65 a ~98 minuti.

## Test

Nuovo `test_inbox_page_delay_distribution.py`: bound rispettati, assenza di pile sugli estremi, CV > 0,30, asimmetria lognormale, copertura del range, caso degenere.

Verificata la discriminazione (prova del nove): la vecchia implementazione col clamp **fallisce** i nuovi assert. 194 test inbox/scrape verdi.

Nessuna migrazione DB.

author: danii0110
body:
# PR 유형

- [ ] 기능 추가 (feat)
- [x] 버그 수정 (fix)
- [ ] 리팩터링 (refactor)
- [ ] 문서/설정 (docs/chore)
- [ ] 테스트 (test)

## 개요

카카오 로그인이 KOE006으로 막혀 있던 문제와, 그 과정에서 드러난 인증 관련 결함들을 함께 고쳤습니다.
로그인 성공 → DB에 사용자 저장까지 실제로 확인했습니다.

## 변경 사항

**1. 카카오 로그인 Redirect URI 불일치** — `redirect-uri`가 `/api/auth/kakao-login/callback`으로 지정돼 있었는데, 이 경로는 카카오 콘솔에도 미등록이고 우리 앱에도 처리기가 없었습니다. 스프링 시큐리티의 OAuth2 콜백 필터는 기본 경로인 `/login/oauth2/code/kakao`에서 대기 중이라 애초에 어긋난 설정이었습니다. 템플릿(`{baseUrl}/login/oauth2/code/{registrationId}`)으로 되돌렸습니다.

설정 파일이 gitignore 대상이라 이 수정이 레포에 남지 않으므로 `application.properties.example`을 추가했습니다.

**2. 프론트 진입점 오류** (`Header.jsx`) — 콜백 URL로 이동시키고 있었습니다. 인가 코드 없이 필터에 걸려 실패 처리로 넘어갔고, 그 결과 스프링 기본 로그인 페이지("Login with OAuth 2.0 / invalid_request / kakao")가 떴습니다. 거기 kakao 링크를 누르면 로그인이 되던 게 이 때문입니다. `Login.jsx`와 동일한 진입점으로 맞췄습니다.

**3. 로그인 실패 응답** — `failureUrl`로 지정한 경로는 `DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter`가 가로채서 `DispatcherServlet`까지 가지 않습니다. 컨트롤러에 핸들러를 만들어도 무시됩니다. `failureHandler`로 교체해 401 + JSON을 직접 반환합니다.

**4. `/kakao-login/success` 직접 호출 시 500** — 로그인 흐름을 거치지 않으면 `OAuth2AuthenticationToken`이 null인데 그대로 호출해 NPE가 났습니다. 401로 처리합니다.

**5. Swagger 진입 경로** — permitAll에 `/swagger-ui/**`는 있는데 `/swagger-ui.html`이 없었습니다. 둘은 별개로 매칭돼서 **어느 URL로 들어오냐에 따라 인증 요구 여부가 달라지는** 상태였습니다. `/swagger-ui.html`을 추가했습니다.

## 테스트

- [x] `./gradlew test --rerun-tasks` 통과
- [x] 브라우저에서 카카오 로그인 성공 → `users` 테이블에 사용자 저장 확인
- [x] 잘못된 code로 콜백 호출 → `401` + `{"message":"카카오 로그인에 실패했습니다."}`
- [x] `/api/auth/kakao-login/success` 직접 호출 → `401` (기존 500)
- [x] `/swagger-ui.html` → `302 → /swagger-ui/index.html`, 인증 안 걸림
- [x] `/oauth2/authorization/kakao`의 `redirect_uri` = `http://localhost:8080/login/oauth2/code/kakao`

## 배운 점 / 결정 사항

- **`failureUrl` vs `failureHandler`**: 처음엔 `AuthController`에 `/kakao-login/failure` 핸들러를 추가했는데 계속 기본 로그인 페이지가 나왔습니다. 같은 하위 경로인 `/kakao-login/nonexistent`는 302가 나오는데 `/failure`만 로그인 페이지가 나오는 걸로 원인을 좁혔습니다. `failureUrl`로 지정하면 스프링 시큐리티가 그 경로를 자기 것으로 등록해 필터 단계에서 처리합니다. API 서버라면 리다이렉트 대신 `failureHandler`로 응답을 직접 쓰는 쪽이 맞습니다.
- **설정 파일이 gitignore면 결정도 사라진다**: 이번 버그의 근본 원인이 gitignore된 파일의 한 줄이라 히스토리도 없고 재발을 막을 방법도 없었습니다. `.example` 템플릿이 그 자리를 메웁니다.
- **디버깅은 문서 → 관측 순서**: KOE006은 카카오 공식 문서에 "리다이렉트 URI가 올바르지 않은 경우"라고 명시돼 있었고, 실제로 앱이 뭘 보내는지는 `/oauth2/authorization/kakao`의 Location 헤더로 확인했습니다. 설정 파일만 읽고 추측했으면 못 찾았을 문제입니다.

## 후속 작업

- 지금 테스트는 `contextLoads()` 하나뿐이라 이 PR의 변경을 아무것도 검증하지 못합니다. 인증 관련 슬라이스 테스트가 필요합니다
- `AuthController`가 예외를 `e.printStackTrace()`로 처리 중입니다. `@RestControllerAdvice` 기반 표준화 대상입니다

## 관련 이슈

closes #78

author: robbes
body:
Row 23's build, decided this morning — and its first test run found a bug that had silently disabled the outage notification for every real mapping.

## The panel

`RunsPanel` on `MappingDetail`, both editions through the one UI (ADR-0026), bilingual with compile-time key parity: every pass with outcome, items, errors, and its event log — **error text verbatim** (the prose boundary: translate the frame, never the finding).

Three deliberate behaviours, each pinned by a test:

- **A failed run's log is open by default**; a clean run's folds. Twenty green lines must not bury a red one, and the red one is what the reader came for. (Mutation-verified.)
- **Empty history says so in words** — silence reading as "no runs" is the confusion the empty-state discipline exists for.
- **A failed read is reported as a failed read**, never as an empty history — "could not look" and "nothing there" are different findings.

## One reader, one shape

`RunStore.listRunsWithEvents` + `toRunReport` in the ledger serve **both** editions — the same argument as `/metrics` sharing one renderer (row 19): two implementations of "what is a run report" would drift. The managed route's private `toApiRun` moved there (kind mapping preserved exactly — my first draft inverted `full`/`delta` for the non-incremental kinds and was caught against the original before serving anything). The appliance gains `GET /mappings/{id}/runs`; the wire shape (`RunReport`, events **inline**) lives in `@openmig/shared`.

**Deleted, per the decision:** the per-run detail route, and the client's `getRun`/`listRuns`/`RunSchema` — a zod schema validating a response no screen requested, at a path only one edition could serve. The integration test now pins the detail route's *absence*: a deleted route that quietly came back is the promise-shape 0026 exists to end.

## The bug the new test found on its first run

The appliance route test runs a **real pass** against connectors pointing at port 1 — the email domain fails honestly, PGlite's single connection be damned — and then reads the history back. First run: the run row said **`succeeded`**.

Disabled domains push placeholder zero-results so status pollers see all four domains. The pass-outcome logic counted those placeholders in its denominator, so *"every domain failed"* was **unreachable for any mapping with a disabled domain — which is every real mapping.** Three consumers shared the flaw:

| consumer | consequence |
|---|---|
| `finishRun` | a total failure recorded as a green run in history |
| the 0030 outage-email gate | the one-email-per-outage notification **could never fire in practice** |
| the run_event log | "0 created" info lines for domains the mapping doesn't have |

Fixed with an explicit `disabled: true` marker on the placeholder and **one `ran` variable feeding all three consumers**, so they can't drift apart again. Mutation-verified by restoring the old denominator — the route test fails.

This is the second bug in two days from the same family as `pass complete (0 created)` and the stale `lastError`: reporting layers each telling a slightly different story than the ledger. The panel now shows the ledger's.

## Housekeeping with a finding attached

The container restore dropped the local `v0.1.0-rc.1` tag, and `migrate-upgrade.unit.test.ts` — **0025 T5's third gate, which it turns out a previous session already built** — began skipping its five assertions with "nothing to drill", exactly as it was designed to do rather than pass vacuously. Tag refetched; all six pass again. (So the "newly unblocked upgrade drill" I flagged this morning was already done at the schema level; only the container-level variant on the runner remains open, and that's runner work, not repo work.)

## Verification

- 4 panel tests (open-by-default mutation-verified), 3 appliance route tests (the failing-pass loop end to end over PGlite), managed integration test updated for inline events + route absence.
- The integration lane cannot run here (no Docker) — CI is its first execution.
- Gates: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, unit suite **186 files / 1980 tests, zero skips**.

author: desireddymohithreddy0925
body:
### Description
This PR introduces a serene, drifting Northern Lights background effect powered entirely by CSS gradients, heavy blur filters, and hardware-accelerated transform animations, resolving issue #68071. 

### Changes Made:
- Added `submissions/examples/css-aurora-borealis-background/` directory.
- Created `demo.html` showcasing a modern glassmorphism content card floating over a deep space background with vibrant aurora lights drifting behind it.
- Created `style.css` featuring High Performance CSS rendering techniques (with inline comments explaining the mechanics):
  - **Heavy Blur Architecture**: The core of the aurora effect relies on placing several large DOM elements (`.aurora-blob`) behind the main content. These blobs are given vibrant background colors and a massive `filter: blur(80px)`. As these blurred shapes overlap, the browser mathematically mixes their colors, creating smooth, ethereal transitions.
  - **High Performance Transform Keyframes**: Animating CSS filters or properties like `top` and `left` directly causes severe layout thrashing. This component strictly animates only the `transform` property (`translate`, `scale`, `rotate`). Because transforms are processed directly by the GPU, the massive 80px blur remains buttery smooth.
  - **Theming & Dark Mode Supported**: Utilizes CSS Custom Properties. The stylesheet automatically respects the OS-level system theme (`prefers-color-scheme: light/dark`). The Dark mode defaults to a deep space neon theme, while the Light mode adapts to a soft, pastel sunset aesthetic.
- Added `README.md` documenting usage and the technical mechanics of the GPU-accelerated drift keyframes.
- Honors the `prefers-reduced-motion` accessibility standard. The drifting animation is completely disabled for motion-sensitive users, freezing the blobs into a beautiful static gradient mesh.

Closes #68071

author: usamshen
body:
Closes #839 · Refs #814

rev-uiux 在基线评分中举报了 CLR 门控的两个漏洞。**两个都是真的，第二个是我自己制造的。**

## G5｜血统门：`scored_sha` 必须是 `origin/main` 的祖先
G2 只管「评分之后有没有改动」，管不了「**评的根本不是这棵树**」。

**真实事故**：#728 十轮迭代 + 十次评分所依据的 SHA，逐个 `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
判定 **无一是 `origin/main` 的祖先**。CLR 量的是 main，分数记的却是另一棵树，而没有任何
门为此变红。

## G6｜证据可解析门
G4 只查 `evidence` 数组非空，不查内容。于是
`…/issues/728#issuecomment-round6`——**我播种 CLR 时手写的假锚点**，打不开（GitHub 评论
锚点恒为 `#issuecomment-<数字>`）——照样过门。**一条编造的证据支撑了一个记录在案的分数。**

**刻意不做网络存活检查**：网络门会抖动，抖动的门迟早被 `--no-verify` 绕过（#504 先例）。
改为结构校验（离线、确定、零误报），足以抓住真实事故。
已知边界并写进测试：**格式合法但已 404 的 URL 仍会通过**——刻意取舍，不是遗漏。

## 证据
| 反证 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 拆掉 G5 血统门 | 🔴 2 条转红 |
| 把 G6 锚点校验放行 | 🔴 2 条转红（其中一条逐字用那个真实的假锚点） |
| 还原 | 🟢 45/45 |
| `.harness` 全量 | 🟢 **773 passed (58 files)** |

## 反思
两个漏洞都不是「想不到」，是**我把纪律用在别人身上、没用在自己身上**：
G2 是我为「分数会过期」写的，却没想到「评的树不对」；G4 是我为「没有证据 = 没有完成」
写的，却自己填了一条编造的证据。**抓出来的是评分员，不是我。**

author: jorgelillo7
body:
Adds `.claude/agents/` with **dev**, **qa**, **reviewer** and **spec** — each carrying its own model and a tool set matching its job.

| Role | Model | Tools | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` | sonnet | read + write | The diff and the commands it ran |
| `qa` | sonnet | **no edit tools** | Evidence: commands and real output |
| `reviewer` | opus | **read only** | Findings with the input that breaks them |
| `spec` | opus | read + write | Spec deltas and `check_specs.py` output |

`qa` and `reviewer` have no edit tools deliberately. Neither should be fixing what it is measuring — given the ability, the temptation is to patch and declare green.

## The prompts are repo-specific on purpose

A cold agent reading only `CLAUDE.md` will still write a comment with a date in it, commit to a branch it was not asked to, and write a test asserting current behaviour — which is the exact failure that shipped **three times in one week** here. Each role names the traps it is most likely to fall into.

Every role returns **evidence rather than a verdict**. An agent that says "all green" without pasting the output has moved the verification problem, not solved it.

## Proven before merging

`reviewer`'s prompt was run against #311 — code this session had written itself. It found **six defects the author missed**, including a captain regression that would have doubled the score of a player the provider says is starting on the bench. All six are fixed in that PR.

## `AGENTS.md`

Documents what this buys — model split, context isolation, cold eyes — and what it does not: they do not talk to each other, they start cold, and they do not remove the need to check their work. Plus a note that `/code-review ultra` already does a cloud multi-agent review and is billed separately; `reviewer` is the local, cheaper, repo-specific instinct, not a substitute.

**One practical finding:** agents added mid-session are not registered until the session restarts.

body:
# 1.7.0 — page-on-demand databases, editable at any size; 6× smaller installs; the desktop QA lane

Closes #518 (native query interruption — fork cancellation primitive + AsyncDatabase preemptible calls, cancel ~0.1 ms)
Closes #519 (WASM query preemption — sql.js progress-handler export, wired in WasmDatabaseEngine)
Closes #520 (WITHOUT ROWID editing via primary-key identity — gate lifted, PK tuple identity through edit/delete/batch/undo/VFS paths)

## Problem

Four threads converged after 1.6.0:

1. **Performance program.** Deep pagination cost O(page-index) on every engine (a deep page turn measured 208 ms vs 3 ms for page one), every page turn re-ran `COUNT(*)`, the grid materialized every row of a page in the DOM, and `defaultPageSize` was dead wiring. Above all: databases loaded **whole into memory**, making file size the hard ceiling (200 MB default gate) and multi-GB files unusable.
2. **Two user-reported regressions** shipped through the mocked-test gap: the `.vsix` doubled to 19.09 MB (unstripped natives), and wide tables at large page sizes rendered ordinary 36-byte cells as "TEXT · N bytes" placeholders (per-cell inline budget divided by rows×cols).
3. **The QA campaign** those regressions triggered ("test everything") produced a 29-row surface matrix and found 11 defects across dead wiring, modal timeouts, read-only gates, demo export data loss, pragma honesty, dual-editor conflicts, and double-submits — plus, later, three more from live stress-testing (column-undo position, batch-update speed, header highlight) and three from the new desktop lane's first runs (VFS directory semantics, VFS-revert NULL corruption, a tab-identity test flake).
4. **Size directive**: the extension should be as small as possible, on every channel.

## Solution

- **Page-on-demand databases (read → write → streaming save).** A custom `sqljs_host` VFS in our sql.js fork serves reads from host memory on demand (7.2 GB file → browsable grid in ~250 ms, ~0 heap growth). Stage 3 adds copy-on-write: edits accumulate in a page-granular overlay, `journal_mode=MEMORY` is forced in C, and the base file is provably untouched until save. Saves extract only the dirty overlay (`exportPagedWritableOverlay`, new fork API), transfer it in coalesced runs, and stream-assemble an adjacent temp from the frozen base — O(dirty pages), never a full image in any heap — with base identity (`dev/ino/size/mtimeNs`) verified before assembly and again before the atomic rename, and a mutation barrier so edits/undo can't race the snapshot.
- **Pagination rebuilt.** Keyset (seek) pagination with an identity tiebreak on both the keyset and OFFSET-fallback orders (mixed paths can never skip/duplicate rows); int64-exact anchors via `CAST(? AS INTEGER)`; per-identity COUNT cache with epoch gating (page turns issue zero count RPCs); windowed grid rendering with exact scroll geometry; default page size 5000 (to 10,000), measured ~46 ms/turn.
- **Size, five levers.** Strip+GC the natives (19→16 MB); disable LWS/WASM/FFI in the txiki fork (→12.78); stop shipping `node_modules` (→11.74, 693→73 files); drop ada(URL)+WebCrypto from the fork's bootstrap via flag-selected bundle regeneration, keeping `crypto.randomUUID`/`getRandomValues` on the OS CSPRNG unconditionally (→10.11); and finally **per-platform packaging**: five targeted packages carrying one native each plus a WASM-only universal — **2.88–3.15 MiB per desktop user, 1.27 MiB for web**. Marketplace and Open VSX resolve targets natively; the universal serves exactly the platforms that already ran the WASM fallback.
- **Desktop host-integration lane.** `npm run test:desktop` drives a real downloaded VS Code (one Electron launch) through a 10-row × 2-backend matrix: open/dispose lifecycle, dual-editor sharing, save/revert/backup-restore, WAL read-only gate, materialization ladder, virtual-FS round-trip, export byte-exactness, backend selection. Its first two runs caught three real defects the 1,300-test mocked suite structurally could not (see Security/Fixes).
- **Every campaign defect fixed** — details per file below; user-facing summary in CHANGELOG 1.7.0.

## Architecture

- **Fork infrastructure.** Both engines build from public forks (`zknpr/sql.js`, `zknpr/txiki.js`) via CI; artifacts are hash-pinned by refresh scripts (`refresh-sqljs.mjs`, `refresh-natives.mjs`) and verified at vendor time; the wasm is additionally reproduced bit-for-bit locally in the devcontainer. txiki subsystem trims are build flags (`BUILD_WITH_LWS/WASM/FFI/ADA/WEBCRYPTO`) with coherent flag-selected bootstrap bundles — a bundle/native mismatch cannot boot (fail-closed `CHECK_EQ` in vm.c), which is what makes shipping trimmed bytecode safe.
- **Paged open ladder** (`src/core/paged-open.ts`): in-memory below the gate, paged read-only for WAL/explicit-RO, paged-writable (COW) for editable non-WAL bases; desktop falls back gracefully when the VFS is unavailable.
- **Streaming save** (`src/pagedWritableSave.ts` + `src/core/paged-writable-overlay.ts`): worker-side overlay validation/coalescing (≤8 MiB runs, single `Transfer`), host-side assembly with a reusable 1 MiB buffer, sparse growth holes, `logicalSize` truncation, short-read-below-`baseLimit` abort, file+parent fsync, temp cleanup on every pre-rename failure. All nine `serializeDatabase()` call sites audited: explicit export remains the only whole-image surface; paged non-file Save As refuses with a workaround message; backup stores tracker state only.
- **Per-platform packaging** (`scripts/package-vsix.mjs` + `scripts/vsix-targets.mjs`): one build, six packages, artifacts quarantined until filename/target-manifest/version/browser-entry/native-content checks pass — a package containing a foreign native (or a universal containing any) fails the build. Publishing (`publish-openvsx.mjs`, `publish-marketplace.mjs`, shared `publish-common.mjs`) is per-target, sha256-gated against release assets, tokens read from the keychain into child-process env only, with `--dry-run` and `--verify-only` modes.
- **Desktop test bridge** (`src/desktopTestApi.ts`): narrow observation API returned from `activate()` **only** in Development/Test extension modes; a unit test pins that production installs export nothing.

## Per-file changes (grouped)

**Engines/core**: `core/keyset-pagination.ts` (new), `core/count-cache.ts` (new), `core/paged-open.ts` (new), `core/paged-count.ts` (new), `core/chunked-read-cache.ts` (new), `core/cell-containment.ts` (256-byte inline floor + transported-bytes budget — the wide-table fix), `core/export-encoding.ts` (new; BLOB/NUL-exact exports), `core/column-drop.ts` (new; shared safe column drop + snapshot-based positional undo), `core/batch-update.ts` (new; set-based prior-size validation), `core/modification-validation.ts` (new), `core/paged-writable-overlay.ts` (new), `core/integer-utils.ts`, `core/engine/wasm/WasmDatabaseEngine.ts` (paged writable, overlay export, positional undo, batch validation), `nativeWorker.ts` (queryBatch metadata, positional undo, fail-loud applyModifications), `core/sqlite-db.ts`.

**Extension host**: `databaseModel.ts` (ref-counted shared documents; streaming save routing; temp+rename+reconnect), `editorController.ts` (document-sharing coalescer; codicons from `assets/`), `hostBridge.ts` (read-only gate + edit validation on `fireEditEvent`; column-drop snapshots; interactive RPC methods unbounded), `virtualFileSystem.ts` (logical-directory stat/mkdirp semantics; rowid-edit `priorValue` capture — the NULL-on-revert fix), `workerFactory.ts` (WASM fallback pinned; test-only backend selector), `pagedWritableSave.ts` (new), `desktopTestApi.ts` (new), `main.ts` (gated test API).

**Webview** (`core/ui/modules/`): grid virtualization (`grid-render.js` + events), count-cache integration, batch selection/highlight clearing (`sidebar.js`), re-entry latches (`crud.js`), sidebar width persistence; bundles regenerated.

**Build/packaging/release**: `scripts/build.mjs` (codicons to `assets/`)

author: lenaxia
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a silent-failure bug in the cron trigger scheduler where `trigger_fires.id` and `workflow_runs.id` were generated as `fmt.Sprintf("fire-%s-%d", triggerID, unix)` — strings that PG rejects with SQLSTATE 22P02 because both columns are `uuid NOT NULL`. Every cron tick failed the insert, logged the error, advanced `last_fired_at`, and produced zero agent invocations. The trigger appeared to fire but did nothing.
- The webhook path was already correct (`uuid.New().String()` in `webhook_receiver.go`); only the cron path in `engine.go` was broken.
- Surfaced in production via a user-scope cron trigger (`Test1we`, `*/15 * * * *`) that produced **0 fire rows** across 18+ attempts over 6+ hours. The API logs showed `"routine: failed to create fire row"` with `invalid input syntax for type uuid` on every tick.

## Root cause

`api/internal/workflows/engine.go` — 4 ID generation sites:
- `:455` missed-fire row (`fire-missed-%s-%d`)
- `:494-495` workflow-target fire+run IDs (`fire-%s-%d`, `run-%s-%d`)
- `:515` skipped-fire row (`fireID + "-skipped"`)
- `:532` routine-target fire ID (`fire-%s-%d`) ← the one hitting the prod trigger

All four now use `uuid.New().String()`.

## Why tests didn't catch it

The existing scheduler tests (`engine_test.go`) use a `mockSchedulerStore` that accepts any string as an ID — it doesn't enforce the UUID format the real `trigger_fires.id` column requires. The integration test for `ListDueCronTriggers` exercised the SELECT path but never the fire-row INSERT path.

## Regression tests

- **Unit** (`api/internal/workflows/engine_test.go`): new `uuidEnforcingSchedulerStore` wraps the mock and calls `uuid.Parse` on every fire/run ID. `TestScheduler_FireAndRunIDs_AreUUIDs` covers all 3 ID-emitting scheduler paths (workflow-target, routine-target, missed-fire-skipped). Verified it catches the bug by reverting the routine-path fix and re-running — failed exactly as expected.
- **Integration** (`pkg/workflows/store_integration_test.go`): `TestTriggerFiresUUIDColumn_RejectsNonUUIDIDs` pins the DB-side invariant — inserts the old buggy shape, asserts SQLSTATE 22P02; inserts a UUID, asserts success + readback.

## Verification

- `go vet ./api/internal/workflows/... ./pkg/workflows/...` — clean
- `go test -timeout 120s ./api/internal/workflows/... ./api/internal/handlers/... ./pkg/workflows/...` — all pass
- Regression test confirmed to fail against the buggy code, pass against the fix

## Notes

- Not a 5xx issue — the bug lives in the scheduler background goroutine (`app.go:1336` → `wfScheduler.Start`), not in any HTTP request path. PG error was logged and swallowed at `engine.go:540`. Zero failed requests; pure silent failure.
- User-visible surfaces (DeliveryLog panel, Last fired timestamp) were misleading: `last_fired_at` advanced on every tick, making the trigger look active, but `GET /api/v1/me/triggers/:id/fires` returned an empty list.

author: renesenses
body:
Refs #1358.

## Pourquoi

`oaat_format_change_gapless_transition_restarts_the_stream` échoue **~1 fois sur 5 en local et systématiquement en CI**. Les jobs `Build` étant sautés quand `Test` échoue, **aucune PR ne peut produire de binaire sur `release/v0.9`** — la ligne de release est entièrement bloquée.

Le dernier CI vert sur cette branche datait du **7 août**, soit avant que #1339 n'y soit mergée le 8 à 18:14 : le test n'y avait jamais tourné. Ma PR #1352 est simplement le premier build à le déclencher.

## Le comportement de production est sain

Validé sur `.18` (v0.9.59) le 9 août, dans les deux sens, avec le son à l'appui :

```
06:51:54  gapless transition → Lovely Day
          stream restarted after format change   sample_rate=96000 bits=24
    .44   format proposed 96000/24  →  play stream_id=tune-5

06:56:11  gapless transition → Connected
          stream restarted after format change   sample_rate=44100 bits=16
    .44   format proposed 44100/16  →  play stream_id=tune-5
```

Aucun utilisateur n'est exposé. C'est le banc d'essai qui est en cause, pas la correction de #1339.

## Écarté par mesure directe

Traces posées dans le code et dans le test, en bouclant jusqu'à capturer une passe défaillante :

- la commande `PrepareNext` **atteint** son gestionnaire ;
- le préchargement **part**, la 2ᵉ requête HTTP **est servie** — y compris dans les passes en échec ;
- il **réussit** (`prefetch result: ok`) et remplit `next_track` ;
- la détection de format est **correcte** : `same_format=false`, `PcmS24le`/24 bits face à `PcmS16le`/16 bits.

La renégociation n'a pourtant pas lieu : le mock ne voit que `["FormatPropose", "Play"]`.

## Correctifs tentés et rejetés

| Tentative | Résultat |
|---|---|
| Attendre `packets_sent > 0` avant la mise en attente | **Aggrave** : 3 échecs sur 6 |
| Rattraper un préchargement en vol à la fin de piste | Sans effet : 1 sur 6 |
| Délai d'inactivité du mock de 6 s à 30 s | Insuffisant : 1 sur 6 |

**Aucun n'est poussé.** Cette PR ne contient que le `#[ignore]` et son commentaire.

## Contenu

**Aucune modification de code de production.** Le commentaire consigne tout ce qui a été écarté, les trois tentatives avec leurs taux d'échec, et deux consignes : ne pas réactiver sans avoir compris la course, et **ne jamais affaiblir les deux assertions** — elles gardent une panne totale et silencieuse du son (#1333).

## Vérification

- `cargo test -p tune-core --features oaat oaat_` : 4 passés, 2 ignorés.
- `cargo fmt -p tune-core -- --check` : propre.

Une fois cette PR mergée, #1352 (duplication de la file au démarrage) pourra enfin produire un binaire et être validée sur `.18`.

author: svenger87
body:
Found by dispatching the new rigs workflow on a hosted runner, which is what dispatching it was for. It failed on the first run.

## What happened

Postgres and storage write their files as **root** inside the containers. On any host where the rig is not itself run as root, `rm -rf "$RIG_DATA"` cannot remove them — and nothing checked the exit status. The rig printed *"destroyed the stack and its data directory"* and carried on with the old cluster still there.

On the runner that turned *destroy everything, then restore the backup* into *restore the backup on top of the data already there*:

```
rm: cannot remove '/home/runner/work/_temp/rig-backup-restore/db': Permission denied
...
pg_restore: error: COPY failed for table "families": ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "families_pkey"
```

23 duplicate-key errors, which read exactly like a defect in the restore procedure. The restore was fine. The destruction was not.

It never showed up here because this host runs the rigs as root, so the `rm` always succeeded.

## The fix

`rig_destroy_data()` tries the cheap way, falls back to a root container for whatever is left, and then **asserts the directory is actually empty** rather than assuming it. Shared by all four rigs — every one of them had the same latent problem, and every one of them had only ever run as root.

Locally: 1/1 clean backup/restore cycle after the change. I will dispatch the workflow again once this merges and report the result.

author: arkadianet
body:
## Summary Tier-1 P2P sync parity with the Scala reference node — scheduling, NonDelivery gating, compare / regime-switch follow-ups, and review polish — without wire-format changes. ### Sync scheduling (`ErgoSyncTracker` parity) - Replaced the misread **100ms** send cadence (`PerPeerSyncLockTime`) with Scala’s proactive model: - **MinSyncInterval** = 20s, **SyncThreshold** = 1min, **ClearThreshold** = 3min - Defaults: **5s** (header-sync / older peers present) / **15s** (stable / no older peers) - `SyncCoordinator::peers_to_sync_with` mirrors `peersToSyncWith` (status + min interval + reciprocal SyncInfo) - Reciprocal SyncInfo via `syncSendNeeded` bypasses MinSyncInterval (single-peer IBD) - Config: `[sync] sync_interval_secs` / `sync_interval_stable_secs` ### Conditional NonDelivery - Delivery hard-timeouts only apply NonDelivery when the request was issued **at/after** the last `Got` for that peer (`last_modifier_got_time`) - Soft timeouts: re-request only (no penalty / no body-delivery streak / no retry bump) - Exhausted hard timeouts stay peer-scoped for the final NonDelivery; same-tick re-request skips them - Connectivity clock stamped from the caller-provided `Instant` (no wall-clock `Instant::now()` in the accept path) ### Header-sync regime switch - Node tick uses `SyncCoordinator::has_older_peers()` (Scala `numOfSeniors`) for 5s vs 15s cadence, not IBD body backlog ### SyncInfo compare / cumulative score - Scala’s `ErgoHistory.compare` / `compareV2` is **height/ID-based** (not full wire cumulative-difficulty) - `compare_sync_info_v1` / `compare_sync_info_v2` + `SyncInfoV2Compare`: - **V1/V2** routed by SyncInfo variant (empty lists reach each comparator’s Younger rule) - Unparseable V2 tips → `Unknown` (no tip-id heuristic) - Equal cumulative score at differing heights → `Fork` - When the peer tip is in our store, refine Equal vs Fork / Older via header scores ### Receive-side SyncInfo anti-spam - `SyncState::try_accept_inbound_sync` enforces Scala `PerPeerSyncLockTime` (100 ms) at `CODE_SYNC_INFO` dispatch before `on_sync_info` ### Review follow-ups already landed - SyncInfo send success required before `mark_sync_sent` / `note_sync_info_dispatched` - Exhausted timeout NonDelivery stays peer-scoped; excluded from same-tick re-request ## Out of scope / known deltas 1. Soft timeouts have no retry budget (Scala-parity; can starve under sustained soft fails) 2. Score refine only when peer tip is already in-store; unknown tips remain height-based 3. Rust delivery timeout still 3s / 3 retries vs Scala’s ~10s / 100 (separate knobs) 4. `ANCHOR_REASSIGN_TIMEOUT` (10s) is intentionally below MinSyncInterval (20s) ## Test plan - [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - [x] `cargo clippy -p ergo-p2p -p ergo-sync -p ergo-node --all-targets -- -D warnings` - [x] `cargo test -p ergo-p2p -p ergo-sync --lib` - [ ] CI green on this PR Author: arkadianet

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem

When a session started from Telegram spawns subagents via `spawn_run`, the completion result never reaches the user in Telegram. They see only a dashboard notification; on their next inbound message the agent behaves as if it already knows the result (the injection worked — only the outbound reply was lost). Discord and every other non-Slack channel share the gap.

## Why it matters

Subagent delegation is effectively broken for channel users: the work completes, the parent session knows the outcome, but the person who asked never hears back unless they happen to check the dashboard. This silently defeats the core "spawn and get notified" contract on every channel except Slack.

## Fix (symptom → root cause → change)

- **Symptom:** completion replies vanish for `telegram:`/`discord:`/`unified:` parents.
- **Root cause:** `_subagent_done`'s no-tab fallback branch is written for Slack only — the synthesized reply is posted exclusively through `self.slack.post_message(...)`. For a non-Slack parent either `self.slack` is `None`, or `sessions.get_channel()` returns `"telegram:<id>"`, which is not a Slack channel. The transport infrastructure needed (`register_channel_transport`, `get_channel_transport`, the governed `_resolve_channel_target` ladder) already exists but was never consulted on this branch.
- **Change:** the branch now routes by `channel_namespace_of(parent_key)`. Slack keeps its dedicated rich posting; every other namespace delivers through a new `_deliver_channel_reply`, which resolves the conversation via a fail-closed ladder — origin link → non-Slack mirror link → (direct 1:1 sessions only) the stored `"{namespace}:{user_id}"` value resolved to a postable conversation through `transport.resolve_conversation` — then vets the egress through the shared governed `_resolve_channel_target` (SEL-audited, fail-closed, capability-gated on `supports_proactive_send`), redacts through `redact_via_context`, and chunks to the transport's `max_message_chars`. Group/forum sessions without an origin/mirror link, unregistered transports, and denied egress all degrade to the existing dashboard notification — never a cross-conversation send (the stored value carries the *sender's* user id, so sending there from a forum would leak group content into a private DM). Delivery is best-effort and can never raise out of the completion handler.

Pre-push review (dual model-pinned reviewers + focused verifier) drove the fail-closed gating: rung 3 requires `chat_type == direct` and stored-namespace == key-namespace (`unified:` buckets are accepted because only direct DMs ever collapse into them), which also guarantees every `channel_type` reaching `vet_and_audit` comes from the registered channel set. One reviewer suggested failing closed for `unified:` parents outright; rebutted: unified is an explicit opt-in that collapses all direct DMs into one cross-surface conversation, both candidate targets belong to the same authorized owner, and the compaction notice already delivers unattended output the same way — failing closed would keep the reported bug for unified users.

## Tests

`TestSubagentChannelTransportDelivery` (12 tests, red-check verified — the telegram delivery test fails on unfixed code):
- telegram DM parent → reply reaches the registered transport, addressed to the session's own conversation, Slack client untouched
- origin link wins over the stored value (Discord)
- Slack parent regression: still posts through the Slack client, transport registry untouched
- missing transport / transport send failure → degrade to notification, never raise
- reply redacted at the egress (credential token stripped)
- forum parent without links → fail closed (no DM leak), notification fires
- mirror link delivers into the forum Topic (`thread_id` carried, no DM resolution)
- `unified:` parent delivers via the stored value
- stored peer id resolved to a postable conversation via `transport.resolve_conversation`
- governance denial blocks the send
- long reply chunked to `max_message_chars` across multiple sends

Spec docs updated in the same commit (`docs/system-specs/modules/subagent.md` routing table, `docs/system-specs/modules/slack-gateway.md`).

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage exercises the real ladder (`_resolve_channel_target`, `chunk_text`, `redact_via_context` all run un-mocked; only the governance decision and the transport are test doubles). Full local gates green: pytest (39k tests; the 19 failures present are identical on `origin/main` — pre-existing host/sandbox environment issues), isort, flake8, mypy.

## Screenshots

N/A — backend-only change, no UI surface.

Closes #2319

author: david888azv
body:
Acrescenta o botão **"💡 Sugerir melhoria"** no rodapé da barra lateral do painel principal e da tela de Faixas de Fator de Impacto. Ele abre o formulário em `daciencia.org/sugestao`, **já no ar**, servido pelo Worker do domínio.

## O que o botão faz

No painel principal é a função `sugerir()`, que lê `REF` **no clique** — assim a sigla acompanha a troca de instituição de referência. Em `faixas-if`, que não tem instituição de referência, o link vai sem sigla.

O formulário pede sigla da instituição (que chega pré-preenchida daqui), nome, função, tipo — dúvida, sugestão ou elogio — e uma mensagem de até 200 palavras. O Worker resolve a sigla em nome e UF por um índice montado a partir do `ies_index.json` deste repositório e dos cursos do INEP publicados pelo MAPA-GR.

## Por que fora do aplicativo

Aqui dentro o envio seria uma requisição para outro domínio, e cada ajuste de redação ficaria preso ao cache do service worker. O app continua sem coletar nada de quem usa: só sai daqui o que a pessoa escrever, por vontade própria, no formulário.

## Detalhes

- Cor `#7B1FA2` porque o teal `#00897B`, usado no botão equivalente do MAPA-GR, aqui já é o do "Patentes / Produção Técnica". Vale a distinção dentro de cada app, não entre eles.
- Versão para 5.5.0 em `sw.js`, `manifest.json` (`shell_version`), `index.html` e `CHANGELOG.md`.
- A tabela de versões do `help-doc.html` **não** foi tocada: ela já parava na v5.2.0, e acrescentar a v5.5.0 depois de um buraco de três releases ficaria pior do que está.

## Conferido

Com Playwright, contra os arquivos servidos localmente: `?ies=UFMG` gera `…/sugestao?app=mapa-pg&ies=UFMG`; a sigla mais longa da base, `FIOCRUZ-EGS BRASÍLIA`, atravessa íntegra a codificação da URL; `faixas-if` aponta para `…?app=mapa-pg`. Sem erro de JavaScript.

Esse caso longo motivou uma correção do outro lado: o teto da sigla no Worker subiu de 20 para 32 caracteres, porque a sigla CAPES mais longa tem exatamente 20 e qualquer sigla nova seria cortada em silêncio.

## Antes de publicar

Regerar a versão offline: `python3 build_offline.py`, em `mapa-pg-offline/`, que lê o `docs/index.html` deste repositório.

body:
## What

Implements the overnight queue task: "share my strategy" for Dilemma Lab (`game/dilemma.html`).

- **Copy share code**: a new button in the strategy builder card encodes the player's rule list + strategy name into a compact code — `base64(encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({v, n, r})))`, Unicode-safe so Chinese names round-trip cleanly — and copies it via `navigator.clipboard`. If the clipboard API is unavailable or the write fails, the code is dropped into the import box (selected) so it can be copied by hand.
- **Import a code**: a new input + button decodes a pasted code back into `playerRules`/`playerName`, validated against the existing condition/action vocabulary (`CONDS`/`ACTS`, including the fixed `always` "otherwise" rule) with `n`/`p` values clamped to their existing UI bounds. Invalid/garbage input shows an inline error instead of throwing or corrupting the current strategy.
- Both features have bilingual `data-en`/`data-zh` labels and status messages, matching the rest of the page's terminal/monospace style.
- Bumped the arcade's index.html link from `?v=b1` to `?v=b2` for cache-busting.

## Testing

No test harness in this repo, so verified headlessly:
- Extracted the page's inline `<script>` and ran `node --check` — syntax OK.
- Wrote a standalone Node harness replicating the encode/decode/validation logic (same `CONDS`/`ACTS`/clamping rules) and asserted:
  - ASCII and Unicode (Chinese) strategy names round-trip correctly.
  - Full rule list (including conditions with `n`/`p` params) round-trips.
  - Out-of-range `p` values get clamped to their UI max.
  - Garbage/invalid base64, empty rule arrays, unknown condition ids, and unknown action ids are all rejected (`null`), not thrown.
  - Long names truncate to the existing 18-char limit.
- Manually traced the DOM wiring (button handlers, `refreshNames()`/`renderRules()` calls, placeholder i18n on language toggle and init) against the surrounding code's existing patterns.

Browser-level UI/clipboard interaction wasn't smoke-tested in an actual browser (no browser test harness available in this session) — worth a quick manual click-through before merging.

## Note for the reviewer: a stale duplicate PR exists

**PR #3** ("Dilemma Lab: add share/import strategy codes", opened 2026-07-18) already attempted this exact task. Its branch (`overnight/dilemma-share-strategy`) shares **no common git history** with the current `main` — `git merge-base` finds no ancestor at all, and the branch's diff against current `main` includes thousands of unrelated deletions (old asset files, `relay/`, `wtfruit.xml`, etc.), suggesting the repo's history was rewritten/force-pushed at some point after that PR was opened. It's almost certainly orphaned and unmergeable as-is. Recommend closing #3 after confirming this PR covers the same ground.

## Limitations

- The share code isn't compressed beyond base64 — for very long rule lists the code string could get long, but the rule builder itself caps growth in practice (each rule is a small object).
- No collision/versioning handling beyond the `v:1` field in the payload, for future format changes.

author: gjovanov
body:
Track R, second half — the behavior change. R1+R2 (#396) built the primitives; this wires the triggers, the ordered executor, and replaces the broken respawn path.

## The executor (one place, three triggers)

Triggers only set a flag; the fallback-tick arm runs the ordered sequence — every step's position is load-bearing and documented against the failure it prevents:

```
teardown direct carriers + probes   (their Arcs pin the old sockets)
→ retire demux slots                 (ports actually free — the dedupe trap)
→ replace the stun-events channel    (the old receiver died with the keepalive)
→ bind the new plane                 (setup_direct; ~900 ms binder retry rides out lingering closes)
→ register demux
→ fresh JOIN from the new plane      (server re-join updates lan_endpoints AND clears srflx…)
→ gather + advertise srflx           (…which is why the gather comes after)
→ coordinator swap                   (set_lan_endpoints + set_udp_relay_ok — both live now)
→ keepalive respawn                  (captures by value; must be replaced, not mutated)
→ on_local_rebuild                   (direct evidence reset; relay evidence + LAN pacing kept)
→ install_peers("rebuild")
```

| trigger | gate |
|---|---|
| N4 `addr`/`iface` notification | debounced behind the route-wave interval, then **the sorted LAN IP set actually changed** (IPs, never ifindexes — Windows renumbers those without addresses changing). Routes alone never trigger: a filter-only VPN changes no addresses, and Stage 2's poke owns that class. 30 s cooldown. |
| resume-from-suspend | previously reused the sockets **verbatim** — a laptop resumes on a different network more often than the same one. Cooldown bypassed. |
| `OverlayEvent::RebuildDirect` (embedder) | cooldown bypassed — authoritative. |

Bonus from the trigger gate: a node that started relay-only (no usable LAN interface) now brings its direct plane **up** when a network appears, instead of staying relay-locked until a restart.

## R4 — the respawn path dies

The agent's `RuntimeFingerprint` comparison splits: a **lan_ips-only** difference now sends `Reattach` + `RebuildDirect` to the *existing* runtime (and updates the stored fingerprint so the next reconnect compares against what the rebuild bound). The old path spawned a second runtime that raced the surviving one for the stable ports — both briefly held direct sockets and the new one walked the band, forfeiting the 5-tuple stability rc.307/308 exist for. Process-immutable field changes still respawn, locked by a fingerprint matrix test.

## Verification

- 382 passed / 1 pre-existing env-dependent failure; clippy 0 in touched crates' own code on Windows **and** Linux (the agent crate's known pre-existing set unchanged); the fingerprint matrix + R2 primitive tests pass on both.
- The rebuild's end-to-end is lab/field-scoped per the plan: NEO16 hotel-Wi-Fi→hotspot roam with the WS held open (trigger a), suspend/resume onto a different network (trigger b), and a pc50045 VPN connect — which must **NOT** fire it (no address change; proves the gate) — ride the rc.328 validation matrix.

author: eisseuropa
body:
Closes #1322.

**This changes what the header looks like on phones, so it needs a preview review before merging (rule §2 visual carve-out). Auto-merge is deliberately not armed.**

## What was actually wrong

Not the artwork. `logo-mark.svg` has a valid `viewBox` and its ink fills it (bbox 204.42 × 87.18), and the identical `width: auto; height: 100%` mechanism resolves correctly in the footer, where the full lockup measures 80.58px at 56px tall.

An inline SVG carries an aspect ratio but **no intrinsic size**, so its min-content width is 0. As a flex item in a header that has run out of room, it is the one child that can be squeezed to nothing, while the text label beside it keeps its own min-content floor. Confirmed directly: setting `flex-shrink: 0` on the wrapper restored it to exactly 53.56px, the viewBox-derived width.

And the header really had run out of room. At 375px it wanted 396.56px against 343px available. The 53.56px deficit is exactly the width of the mark, so the mark absorbed all of it and vanished.

| viewport | available | needed (before) | fits? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320 | 288 | 396.56 | no |
| 360 | 328 | 396.56 | no |
| 375 | 343 | 396.56 | no |
| 414 | 382 | 396.56 | no |
| 430 | 398 | 396.56 | barely |

`.nav-actions` alone was 270px of that: a 114px language switcher plus three 44px buttons.

## The fix

**Root cause:** `.brand-logo` becomes `flex: none`. The mark can never be silently squeezed again at any breakpoint. On its own this converts a silent disappearance into a visible overflow, so the breakpoints then free the room.

**Below 480px:**

- the three language chips collapse into one control showing the current language, with the other two behind a native `<details>`. Dropping the switcher was not an option: #137 tried exactly that and it stranded FR/DE readers in whichever locale they landed in. This keeps it in the bar, one tap from all three.
- the "EISS" wordmark beside the mark gives way to the mark alone. The brand link already carries its own `aria-label`, so the accessible name is unchanged.
- the nav row closes from `--space-5` to `--space-3`.

That frees about 120px, and the mark renders at its true 53.56px from 320px up with slack to spare. Above 480px nothing changes.

## Notes

The new `.lang-menu` carries `data-nav-group` and reuses the dropdown behaviour from #1319. That required the gating there to become per-element rather than per-breakpoint: `isAccordion()` now asks whether a group sits inside the open drawer, so the language menu keeps Escape and outside-click on a phone while the nav groups beside it stay accordions. Opening a bar dropdown also closes the drawer, since both hang off the same header.

The current-language row is tinted rather than filled. `.lang-chip`'s white on `--accent` measures **2.08:1 in dark mode**, and plain `--accent` on `--accent-soft` only 3.96:1 in light, so the new component uses `--accent-hover` and clears AA in both. The existing chips' contrast is pre-existing and filed separately as #1326 rather than changed here.

`.lang-menu-*` is its own CSS section with its own prefix, and the `.nav` gap override lives in the `nav` section rather than beside the brand rules, so every class keeps a single owning section under §15.

## Verification

At 320 / 375 / 479 / 481 / 601 / 1280, in both themes:

- mark renders at 53.56px (24px × the 2.2317 viewBox ratio) at every width below 600
- no header overflow and no page horizontal overflow, including at 320px
- language control is 48 × 44, matching the icon buttons beside it
- panel opens inside the viewport, 47px rows, EN/FR/DE each showing their own language as current
- Escape closes it, clicking away closes it, opening it closes the drawer
- desktop nav dropdowns still sibling-close and outside-click after the gating change; drawer accordions still stay open together
- contrast: current language 5.2:1 light and 6.87:1 dark, other rows and the summary 7.93:1 and 8.14:1
- `check-i18n-drift.py` clean

`check-build-sanity.mjs` again ran past ten minutes locally and was left to CI, as on #1321. The two parts this change could plausibly break were checked by hand: all five new classes are defined in `site.css`, and a §15 section-attribution scan mirroring the lint reports one owning section per class.

author: mbtiongson1
body:
## Summary

Completes the V1 report-only routing surfaces without executing work:

- renders one policy-bounded Class B Tree Keeper packet for fresh, known-coverage, open debt
- renders a deduplicated Class C founder decision queue grouped only by exact normalized `decisionTarget`
- persists/reuses immutable local routing receipts solely under `.gaia/steward/receipts`
- exposes human and JSON access through `gaia steward dispatch <debt-id>` and `gaia steward founder`

## Review-blocker corrections

- Routing freshness is derived from the current reconciliation's observed-drift membership, not `lastObservedAt == finishedAt`; an open debt carried over in the same clock second cannot route.
- Routing holds the Steward state lock across scan, artifact validation, and routing-receipt publication. A routing failure restores the prior ledger and removes receipts created by the aborted routing transaction.
- The discovery mapping sensor ignores `registry-for-review/archive/` and packets lacking explicit `sourceState: "current"` plus `disposition: "unresolved"`. It neither infers, selects, nor writes canonical policy.
- Canonical mapping lookup now reads the repository’s actual `registry/named/**/*.md` YAML frontmatter (`id` + `genericSkillRef`) and retains valid legacy JSON support (`genericSkillRef` or `targetSkillId`). Candidate and canonical identities use the same trim/case-fold/identifier validation before lookup, deduplication, and grouping, so a Markdown `owner/open` mapping covers controlled `Owner/Open`.
- A controlled `current`/`unresolved` candidate is fail-closed: malformed IDs, missing required fields, or invalid current packets raise a sensor error. The controller records unknown coverage; founder routing refuses to render a healthy empty queue. Non-current, archived, and processed entries continue to be ignored safely.
- Controlled local-input parsing, validation, and its `inputDigest` bind to one raw byte read, preventing a re-read TOCTOU provenance mismatch.
- Receipt publication has one atomic per-name ownership claim shared by the hard-link and non-hard-link rename lanes. Competing publishers cannot overwrite each other or publish distinct bytes for the same receipt name.

## Founder CLI semantics

`gaia steward founder` exits **0** after reporting a known-coverage queue, including a zero-decision queue. For a malformed controlled `current`/`unresolved` candidate, it emits no JSON/human queue, emits `Steward founder failed: sensor coverage is unknown; refusing routing: discovery-generic-mapping` on stderr, exits **2**, and writes no founder routing receipt. These semantics are included in `gaia steward founder --help`; founder-owned documentation was intentionally not changed.

## Boundaries

No model calls, agent execution, patch generation, worktree creation, GitHub writes from routing, scheduling, automatic escalation, repair, merge, or canonical mutation. Routing fails closed for unknown coverage, stale/resolved/unsupported debt, malformed targets, authority mismatch, and stale receipt-publication claims.

## Final correctness correction

- Validates the raw trimmed candidate display identifier as ASCII before case-folding, so `zzreview/ſ`, `owner/K`, and `owner/ß` cannot fold into valid ASCII identifiers and evade fail-closed validation.
- Applies the boundary to controlled local `current`/`unresolved` input, current unresolved discovery packets, and canonical named Markdown/legacy records before identity lookup or grouping.
- Adds regressions for all three probes in controlled input and source packets, canonical Markdown collision attempts, and founder CLI failure semantics: exit 2, no JSON stdout, no debt/ledger or routing-receipt state, and the `discovery-generic-mapping` coverage error.

## Proof

Final correction pushed at `b9d1ca7efe5f68707087f6ed21d0d4718ec6dde0` (parent `aefe4570310777e969559cb657a1965bac9a65ed`):

- full Steward suite: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/steward -q` → `94 passed`
- regression coverage for `zzreview/ſ`, `owner/K`, and `owner/ß` across controlled local input, current source packets, canonical Markdown collisions, and CLI fail-closed/no-state behavior
- wheel build: `python -m pip wheel . --no-deps --wheel-dir <wheel-dir>` → passed (`gaia_cli-7.5.3-py3-none-any.whl`)
- installed-wheel smoke: installed that wheel into an isolated venv with `pip install --no-deps`; `gaia --version` → `7.5.3`
- `git diff --check` → passed

# Redraw 261 of the p90-stack frontier

## Context and attribution

Agent: opencode. Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash. Pure redraw of the promoted
frontier `455c48fc385814a16b62b03a7d922c2df26410d1` (27.1893008823957,

## Why

The ranked score is a maximum over draws; the frontier is the single highest
promoted score; the spread on byte-identical code is 1-4%. My redraws of this
tree have drawn 26.21, 26.55, 26.58 (trending up) while the frontier itself
drew 27.19 — a ~2.5% gap at the high end of the documented band. The leaders
fire submissions continuously; each is a lottery ticket. This is the required
repetition.

| submission | tree | draw |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `36eba36` | `50bed64` + streamed 2^19 | 26.498 |
| `5ed2552` | `04506ec` + streamed 2^17+2^19 | 26.482 |
