author: fulltimedigi
shyamsridhar123
body:
Closes #184.

## What could not be gated before

`phoenix_learn/gate.py` needs `ADOPT_MIN_N = 20` held-out rows. At 4 to 10 minutes of real API spend per ARC-AGI-3 run that is 2 to 3 hours of wall clock per decision, so `decide()` returned `EXPERIMENTAL_SMOKE_TEST` on every ARC call and gated nothing.

The failure it could not prevent is the one in your evidence: adopted on a single green run at RHAE 3.11 percent, confirmation run on identical code at 0.13 percent.

## The rule

`decide_episodic()` compares distributions instead of counting rows. The bar is stochastic dominance on the lower tail: the candidate's worst run must strictly beat the baseline's median.

On your measured sb26 numbers:

| sample | runs | worst | median |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.0180, 0.0192, 0.0205 | 0.0180 | 0.0192 |
| candidate | 0.0013, 0.0311, 0.0020 | 0.0013 | 0.0020 |

Verdict `REJECT`, even though the candidate's best run beats every baseline run. `test_the_same_candidate_would_pass_if_only_its_best_run_were_read` asserts both halves of that so the trap is stated rather than implied.

`episodic_summary()` returns the numbers the verdict was made on and deliberately does not return a verdict. A summary that carried one would let a caller read the numbers and quietly substitute its own judgement, and `test_the_summary_does_not_decide` pins that.

## The second bar is implied, and I did not ship it as dead code

You ask for two bars: the candidate's worst beats the baseline's median, and no candidate run is worse than the baseline's worst. The second follows from the first. A median is never below its own minimum, so `candidate_worst > baseline_median >= baseline_worst`, and every other candidate run is at least the worst.

Coding it as a second branch would ship a condition that can never fire on its own, and an unreachable guard reads as protection nobody has. `test_no_candidate_run_can_be_worse_than_the_baseline_worst_once_the_tail_bar_holds` records the implication instead. If you want it enforced independently, say so and it becomes a real branch with a case that reaches it.

## Kept separate, as instructed

`decide()` is untouched. `EPISODIC_MIN_RUNS = 3` rather than borrowing `ADOPT_MIN_N`, and two tests pin that the row rule still behaves exactly as before. Both samples must reach the minimum, so a one-run baseline has no median worth beating and a verdict over zero runs is `EXPERIMENTAL_SMOKE_TEST` rather than clean.

Seed reporting is left alone. That is #185's scope and pulling it in here would make this slice stop matching what was asked.

## Proof

Done-check, outside the file under test:

```json
{"kind":"command_exit","target":["python","-m","pytest","tests/test_phoenix_learn_episodic.py","-q"],"expect":0,"cwd":"."}
```

RED was established behaviourally, by injecting the real defect into the finished module with the gate file byte-identical. The defect is reading the lucky run instead of the worst one, which is exactly the pre-change behaviour:

```python
candidate_worst = max(candidate) if candidate else None  # DEFECT INJECTION: read the lucky run
```

```
FF.FF.....F......F                                                       [100%]
    assert _ep(STEADY_BASELINE, LUCKY_CANDIDATE) == "REJECT"
E   AssertionError: assert 'ADOPT_ELIGIBLE' == 'REJECT'
exit=1
```

That failure is the bug this issue reports, reproduced: the lucky run carries the decision.

Healed by restoring the module. GREEN: `18 passed in 0.08s`.

```json
{"ok":true,"check_digest":"295f512d90bc755da4b59547fd443ffd00a7221f51d7624dc6d4993501b91178","trace_intact":true,"saw_red":true,"green_after_red":true,"currently_green":true,"reason":"failure-first satisfied: red->green in an intact trace, currently green"}
{"ok":true,"rows":2,"head_hash":"2b716a47c8a04f18867ee43bd4f2cb771800324bb7706d4e82f6cd741c0fc401","broken_at":null}
```

Two trace rows, no module-not-found RED. The gate reached its final text before the RED that counts.

## Negative controls

Scratch copy of `phoenix_learn/` and `tests/`, gate byte-identical, baseline 18 passed.

| control | result |
|---|---|
| read the best candidate run instead of the worst | 6 failed, 12 passed |
| compare against the baseline mean instead of the median | 1 failed, 17 passed |
| compare against the baseline worst instead of the median | 2 failed, 16 passed |
| make the comparison non-strict so a tie adopts | 1 failed, 17 passed |
| drop the minimum-run guard so a thin sample decides | 4 failed, 14 passed |

Controls two and four are the ones worth reading, because each is caught by a single test. Swapping the median for a mean, or `>` for `>=`, leaves 17 of 18 green. Those two lines are where a plausible-looking weakening would slip through review, and each has exactly one thing standing in its way.

## Blast radius and regression evidence

`phoenix_learn/gate.py`, `tests/test_phoenix_learn_episodic.py` and the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, plus the charter-mandated `.phoenix-ralph/done-check.json` acceptance contract that the proof workflow reads.

```
492 passed, 1 skipped in 288.13s
ci-local: ALL GREEN
release_drift: status ok, 25 [Unreleased] entries
tests/test_version_consistency.py: 4 passed
```

## 🗣 Description ##

`GwsAuth` now checks for a runnable browser before starting the OAuth flow and passes `open_browser=False` to `flow.run_local_server()` when none is found. The flow prints the authorization URL either way, so instead of crashing the run waits for the user to open the link. Also updated the stale code comment that claimed there is no alternative for browserless users.

Detection is based on `webbrowser.get()` raising `webbrowser.Error`, which is the exact failure in the reported traceback. A container that has a browser entry (e.g. a stub `xdg-open`) but no display is not detected and will still try to open a browser.

### 💭 Motivation and context

Running the OAuth workflow inside a container kills the run with `webbrowser.Error: could not locate runnable browser` before authentication can complete. Resolves #1161.

author: morganmcg1
body:
<!-- senpai-assignment:v1 {"assignment_id":"maple-r98-d-moe-qmv-mlp","base_ref":"codex/mlxfast-maple-20260804-advisor","base_sha":"c6c66344d9848d95158edc31f31943aabe4de079","head_ref":"maple-fern/r98-moe-qmv-mlp","head_sha":"61c8763291e7ee6bd04a1f86f5912193bf3547e6","repo":"morganmcg1/mlxfast-challenge_senpai","revision_id":"r99-e-rev1","schema_version":1,"student":"maple-fern"} -->

## Round-98 thesis: memory-level parallelism, not less work

Read this before the hypothesis. It is why this assignment exists, and it is
the direct successor to your own round-97 result.

Rounds 96–97 closed **three independent ways of doing less work**:

- **Rule 66** (#525, yours): removing dense-MLP arithmetic did not pay.
- **Rule 67** (#528): splitting attention across a threadgroup boundary to
  shorten the critical path did not pay.
- **Rule 68** (#527): removing 78 prefill dispatches / 156 GEMM launches, with
  kernel family, tile geometry and threadgroup count all held fixed, made M5
  **slower** by +0.639 ms (CI [+0.325, +0.953], prediction-t 4.43 on 12 dof)
  = **−0.242 % score**.

Your rule 66 was the first of the three. Three falsifications of "less work is
faster" in two rounds is not noise — it is a regime statement. The surviving
explanation, and the one **rule 60** already supports, is that the scored M5
hot path is **latency-bound, not work-bound**. It does not have enough bytes in
flight to cover its own memory latency, so shaving instructions buys nothing
and occasionally costs something.

The quantitative frame: saturating the M5 memory pipe at the observed
per-step decode time needs roughly **191 kB in flight**; M4 needs about
**80 kB**. That gap is exactly why rule 60 is M4-invisible — an M4 host already
has enough MLP to hide its latency at these shapes and shows no signal, while
M5 does not.

**So this round we stop removing work and start raising concurrency.** Your
site is the MoE side of the decode QMV path. maple-frieren has the
attention-side kernels (#539) — **independent kernels, no overlap, do not
coordinate edits.**

## Hypothesis (Bennett-weakest form)

Per the human team's standing instruction (Bennett, *The Optimal Choice of
Hypothesis Is the Weakest, Not the Shortest*, arXiv:2301.12987v4), state the
weakest falsifiable hypothesis, not the most specific one you believe.

> **H-D:** The MoE-side decode QMV kernels are memory-latency-bound, so
> increasing the number of outstanding weight loads per thread — without
> changing the bytes read, the arithmetic, or the accumulation order — reduces
> decode seconds/token.

H-D does not claim software pipelining is the only mechanism, does not claim a
particular prefetch depth or vector width, and does not claim every site
responds. Falsify H-D, not a stronger cousin.

The strongest single piece of prior evidence for H-D is **already in this
repository**: one MoE decode kernel is software-pipelined and the others are
not. If H-D is true, the un-pipelined siblings are leaving time on the table.
If H-D is false, the pipelined one should not have been worth writing.

## Verified coordinates

Confirmed by a code-reading pass at `ea3f5dd6`; unchanged at your base
(`e510bb3d` touched only a research document). Verify line numbers yourself
before editing — but the *structure* is confirmed, so if a claim below does not
match what you read, stop and report it rather than improvising.

All in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. These are runtime-JIT
`MLXFast.metalKernel` source strings in Swift: **no `.metal` file, no
`mlx-generated` twin, no metallib rebuild** for this arm.

### The precedent — the one kernel that already pipelines

`laguna_routed_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_packed_top8keys_r1_bf16_v2`

| Item | Line |
|---|---|
| kernel name | `:7917` |
| source string | `:7920` |
| `values_per_lane = 16` | `:7924` |
| prologue | `:7957-7971` |
| loop | `:7973` |
| **iteration i+1 issued at `:7989-8003`, before the math at `:8004+`** | — |
| dispatch `lagunaRoutedSwiGLUQMVPackedTop8` | from `:8022` |
| R1 grid `(nExpertsPerTok*256*64,1,1)`, TG `(64,1,1)` | `:8048-8049` |

Codes are `uint2`; activations are `vec<bfloat,4>`. This is the template:
issue the next iteration's loads, then do the current iteration's math.

⚠️ **Unverified and load-bearing: whether this R1 arm is the shipped default.**
Check the dispatch selection at `:8022` onward and record what actually runs
before you conclude anything about "the pipelined one is faster". If the
pipelined arm is *not* the default, that is itself a finding worth reporting —
and possibly a free win.

### Site 1 — shared-expert gate/up (no prefetch)

`laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1_halved_wide_bf16_v1`

| Item | Line |
|---|---|
| kernel name | `:7100` |
| source string | `:7103` |
| `values_per_lane = 32` ⇒ **2 serial K iterations** | `:7110` |
| **`uint4` codes** | `:7156-7159` |
| TG `(64,1,1)` | `:7226` |

Already the widest code load in the family (`uint4`), and only 2 iterations —
so the pipelining opportunity is a prologue-hoist of iteration 1's loads above
iteration 0's math. Small but nearly free.

### Site 2 — routed + shared down / residual, staged

| Item | Line |
|---|---|
| decl | `:8428` |
| source string | `:8444` |
| `input_width = 512` | `:8445` |
| `routed_experts = 8` | `:8447` |
| `outputs_per_simd = 4` | `:8449` |
| `values_per_lane = 16` | `:8450` |
| activations `vec<bfloat,4>` | `:8483-8491` |
| batches 4 `uint2` codes + 4 scale bytes | `:8496-8506` |
| `qdot` | `:8507-8513` |
| variant select | `:8626-8633` |
| dispatch, TG `(288,1,1)` = **9 simdgroups** (8 routed + 1 shared) | `:8626-8648` |
| sibling down kernels | `:8080`, `:8342` |

**This one has no K loop** — it already batches its 4 code words and 4 scale
bytes before the `qdot`. So the lever here is *not* loop pipelining. It is
whether the batch is wide enough: 4 × `uint2` = 32 B of codes per lane per
qdot. Consider whether the batch can be widened, or whether the two sibling
kernels at `:8080` and `:8342` (which you must read — their structure is not
yet characterised) have a loop that can be pipelined.

**Read `:8080` and `:8342` first and report their structure in your note.**
They are the least-characterised part of this assignment and may be the best
target.

## Rungs — one rung per receipt, no bundling

**Rung 0 (free, no receipt).** Determine which routed-QMV arm actually
dispatches by default (`:8022` onward), and read + characterise the sibling
down kernels at `:8080` and `:8342`. Write the structure into your note. This
is a local reading task and costs nothing.

**Rung 1.** Apply the `:7989-8003` prologue-hoist pattern to the
shared-expert gate/up kernel at `:7103`: issue iteration 1's `uint4` code loads
and scales before iteration 0's math. Two iterations, so this is a single
hoist, not a loop restructure.

**Rung 2.** Whichever of the down-family kernels (`:8080`, `:8342`, `:8444`)
rung 0 identifies as having the most serial load-then-compute structure — apply
the same pattern there.

**Rung 3.** If rungs 1–2 are positive, widen the code load at the winning site
(e.g. `uint2` → `uint4` where the layout permits) to raise bytes-in-flight per
issue. Only if the layout genuinely permits it without changing what is read.

## Register pressure is the named failure mode

Hoisting loads lengthens register lifetimes. These are 64-thread threadgroups
(and one 288-thread), so there is more headroom than in the attention kernels,
but spills are still possible.

Before pricing any rung, record from the compiled pipeline state:

- `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`
- register / threadgroup-memory footprint if available
- resulting occupancy

A rung that spills is **not** evidence against H-D. Report the numbers so a
negative result is attributable to the right cause.

## Cost model

Price list (use these, do not re-derive):

| Quantity | Price |
|---|---|
| decode | **0.015280 % score per µs/step** |
| decode bytes | 0.015224 % per MB/step |
| prefill | 0.3794 % per m

author: brightloophq
body:
## Confirmed root cause (production)
PolishedPro: **all 5 provider attempts** returned `outputTokens: 2000`, `stopReason: max_tokens`, `parserOutcome: invalid_json` → truncated JSON → `validation` fail → `dead_letter` (`reasoning_output_truncated`). The prompt supplied only the output-contract **ID** (no shape) and **no verbosity bound**, so the model emitted a verbose invented object (summary/findings/limitations/error) that overflowed the 2000-token cap — and retries **re-sent the identical oversized request**.

## Fix — OUTPUT CONTROL (not a bigger budget)
1. **Compact contract in the prompt.** The model now gets the **exact** shape the downstream parser actually reads — `{"claims":[{category,statement,evidenceIds,confidence}]}` — with **hard bounds**: ≤8 claims, statement ≤160 chars, ≤3 evidenceIds/claim, and *"a COMPLETE valid JSON object matters more than another claim."* No `summary`/`limitations`/`error` keys. (`prompt.ts`)
2. **Real validation-retry.** `ExecutionRequest` gains a **safe, content-free** `retryDirective` (`truncated` | `malformed`). The orchestrator sets it from the failure **classification** (`finishReason=length` / `stopReason=max_tokens` → `truncated`) and rebuilds the next attempt's request with it; the prompt turns it into a *"be substantially more concise / JSON-only"* correction. It **never** carries the previous raw response. (`execution.ts` schema, `request.ts`, `orchestrator.ts`, `prompt.ts`)

The downstream `parseProviderClaims` reads **only** `claims` — everything else the model used to emit was ignored *and* pushing it past the cap.

## Unchanged (safety)
Output-token budget (**2000**), provider timeout, internal `maxAttempts` (3), queue `maxAttempts` (5), budget/`costCeiling`, retry/backoff, queue semantics, grounding, citations, provider telemetry (#94), failure taxonomy, provider abstraction. **No** schema-DB/migration/generated-type change (`retryDirective` is a contract field, not a DB column).

## Retry-layer note (STEP 6)
The queue's 5× retry of a *deterministic* truncation adds no new information, but with this fix the **first** attempt should succeed so those retries aren't reached. Changing the queue disposition is a retry-**semantic** change → **deliberately not made here** (separate, justified follow-up).

## Tests
`anthropic.test.ts`: the prompt carries the compact shape + hard bounds (not just the id); a correction appears **only** on a `retryDirective` (truncated/malformed/none), never the raw response. `execution.test.ts`: a truncated attempt 1 → attempt 2 receives `retryDirective="truncated"` and succeeds in **exactly 2** provider calls; the retry request differs **only** by the safe directive (no raw content). `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint test build` → **36/36 green**; db-verify in CI (drift 0); **zero live provider calls**.

## Expected effect
First-attempt success on a normal site (compact output ≈ a few hundred tokens ≪ 2000) → ~1 provider call instead of 15 → `provider_execution` ~10–30s, full scan ~30–60s, ~15× lower cost. *(Not claimed as measured until you run one live scan.)*

Leave open pending review. No live paid Anthropic call was made.

author: ricardo07g
body:
Duas entregas independentes que nasceram da mesma conversa.

## 1. Loading padronizado

Salvar e subir imagem não davam nenhum retorno visual — o usuário fica sem saber se clicou. Um listener delegado no documento troca o rótulo do botão de submit por spinner e trava enquanto a requisição corre. De brinde, acaba com o registro duplicado por duplo clique.

Mora em `public/js/mn-admin.js` com `asset()` + `?v=filemtime`, espelhando o `public/css/mn-admin.css` — o layout admin usa os assets pré-compilados do Duralux, não entries do Vite.

Três detalhes que exigiram cuidado, e que valem a leitura no diff:

- **desabilitar o botão só no próximo tick**: o par `name`/`value` de um botão de submit é serializado *depois* do evento; um botão já desabilitado sumiria do payload e a ação escolhida se perderia em silêncio;
- **ignorar submit já cancelado**: sem isso o `data-confirm` do SweetAlert acenderia o spinner na *pergunta*, não na ação;
- **restaurar por nós do DOM, não `innerHTML`**: preserva listeners dos filhos e fecha o vetor de XSS via data-attribute.

Na galeria do Produto, cada arquivo da fila vira um tile com spinner **antes** do envio começar, e some conforme a resposta chega. O botão "Adicionar" fica escondido durante o envio — a contagem contra o limite ainda não fechou e daria para estourar escolhendo mais.

## 2. Cloudflare Turnstile

`/registrar` é público e qualquer um cria tenant à vontade. O `throttle:5,1` que já existia limita taxa, mas não distingue gente de robô. Turnstile fecha isso **sem exigir domínio no Cloudflare**.

Virou **middleware, não regra de validação** — e isso é o achado do PR: o Laravel só roda regra sobre campo **ausente** se ela for implícita, e `ImplicitRule` está deprecado. Ou seja, o bot que simplesmente não envia o campo passava direto pela regra. Descobri com o teste vermelho.

Duas decisões deliberadas:

- **desligado sem chave** — com `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`/`SECRET_KEY` vazias o widget não renderiza e o middleware passa direto, sem tocar na rede. Dev, CI e a suíte rodam sem chave, e **este PR pode subir antes de a chave existir**: produção fica idêntica a hoje até alguém preencher as variáveis;
- **falha do Cloudflare libera a requisição** — derrubar o login de todos porque o Cloudflare piscou seria pior que o bot que o widget evita.

A resposta de erro nunca reflete credencial de volta para a tela (mesma lista de campos que o Laravel omite ao devolver erro de validação).

## Verificação

- **327 testes** (10 novos), Pint e PHPStan limpos.
- Imagem de produção buildada e exercitada com as chaves oficiais de teste da Cloudflare: widget renderiza nas três telas, `mn-admin.js` servido com `cache-control: public, max-age=604800`.
- Prova ao vivo de que o middleware faz o que promete, distinguindo pela mensagem: POST **sem** token → *"não é um robô"*; POST **com** token → segue e falha só por *"Credenciais inválidas"*.

## Rollback

Instantâneo e sem deploy: apagar `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` do Railway desliga o captcha por completo.

author: cdotta
body:
The site read as AI-generated. The strongest tells, and what replaced them:

**Hero triad** — `systems that stay / out of the way, / so people stay in control.` was three abstract clauses that could sit on any engineer's homepage. Now `apis that move / real money, / and don't lose it.` — same shape, but it names the actual work.

**Section headings** — "what the day is built with", "thirteen years, kept honestly", "things I keep shipping", "let's build something worth keeping" all shared the same wistful register. Replaced with plain labels: "what I actually use", "where the thirteen years went", "things I built on my own time", "open to new work. / say hello."

**Stock phrases in the bullets** — "non-negotiable" (twice), "end to end", "Full ownership from requirements and architecture to deployment, monitoring, and iteration", "leveled up the team". Each rewritten to say the concrete thing instead: a retry that isn't idempotent costs somebody real money; owned the on-call rotation; got the team up to speed on Solidity.

**Hero paragraph** — moved to first person and swapped the abstraction for the stake: "A bad retry there puts someone's money in the wrong place, so idempotency and data integrity stopped being theory."

Left alone deliberately:
- `public/llms.txt` — machine-facing, keyword density is the point.
- `site.description` (meta tag) — light touch only; it feeds search results, not readers.
- The résumé PDF — different audience, different register.

Also drops `hero.blurb` from `src/config.ts`. `index.astro` inlines that paragraph (it needs the `<span>` for the accent), so the config copy was dead and would have drifted out of sync.

`npm run build` passes. Merging this deploys to Fly via the existing workflow.

author: drewdrewthis
body:
## Reviewer cockpit

- **Scariest thing** — `app.visible_people` is the single visibility gate for the whole graph (ADR-0002's fail-closed surface). A mistake in the new `visible_to_distance` filter either leaks a person past their chosen radius or silently hides active users when the node budget is tight. Both failure modes now have named integration tests.
- **Start here** — [`apps/server/src/modules/graph/persistence/sql/visible-people.sql`](https://github.com/drewdrewthis/playa-post/blob/412b2d00007cfedd8021ba694717c676f9832f86/apps/server/src/modules/graph/persistence/sql/visible-people.sql): the `reachable` CTE is where the setting, the six-degree ceiling, the status filter, and the node budget all meet. Everything else in the PR feeds or surfaces that one function.

## Why

The graph shipped in M2 clamped everyone to first degree — an operational placeholder, not the product. This PR delivers the real reach model the product owner asked for: multi-hop visibility bounded by each person's **own** "who can see you" setting, capped at **six degrees** (the six-degrees-of-separation principle — the owner's explicit call, replacing an interim `'anyone'` value), plus the comp's three-step welcome flow. It completes the visibility control deferred from the You screen work (#49).

## What changed

- **Deleted M2's `least(max_depth, 1)` clamp** → keeping a server-side depth cap → `max_depth` is an operational bound, never a product cap (ADR-0004 decision 2); the product cap is now each person's own setting.
- **`app.users.visible_to_distance` (`first`/`second`/`third`/`sixth`, default `'sixth'`)**, enforced inside `app.visible_people` → enforcing in application code → SQL is the only layer every consumer must pass through, so the radius cannot be bypassed by a new caller. Beyond your radius you are **absent from the result entirely** — no row, not an unnamed node. Unknown stored values fail **closed** to `first`.
- **The scale ceiling is `'sixth'`, not `'anyone'`** (migration `20260810090000`) → keeping `'anyone'` → an unbounded value contradicts the six-degrees principle and makes traversal cost unbounded; the migration rewrites existing `'anyone'` rows and the check constraint, and the traversal clamps at `least(max_depth, 6)`.
- **Status is filtered *before* the node budget** in the `reachable` CTE → filtering only in the final select → a deactivated person must not spend a budget slot and push an active, reachable person out of the result (found in review, regression-tested).
- **Who-can-see-you dial on the You screen** (`identity.visibility.get`/`set`, cycling pill 1ST° ONLY → UP TO 2ND° → UP TO 3RD° → UP TO 6TH°) with load-error + retry and save-error states.
- **`/welcome`** — the comp's three-step takeover as a public, network-free route; first anonymous visit lands there, both exits stamp and drop to `/signin`, "Replay welcome →" lives on the You screen.

## How it works

```
supabase/migrations/
  20260809140000_*  column + first visible_people rewrite
  20260810090000_visibility_ceiling_sixth.sql   'anyone' → 'sixth' (rows, default, check) + function copy
apps/server/src/modules/
  graph/persistence/sql/visible-people.sql   the one visibility function (radius, ceiling, status, budget)
  identity/domain/visible-to-distance.ts     value object; Object.hasOwn fail-closed narrowing
  identity/application/visibility-setting.service.ts   get/set behind the tRPC procedures
  identity/persistence/postgres-user.repository.ts     the column read/write
  identity/transport/set-visibility.input.ts           zod enum from the domain values
packages/contracts/src/identity.ts           VISIBLE_TO_DISTANCE_OPTIONS — web's only import surface
apps/web/src/app/
  profile/visibility-dial.ts                 labels, cycle order, descriptions
  routes/your-profile.tsx                    the dial section (error/loading/loaded states)
  welcome/*                                  the three-step flow + onboarded stamp
tests/e2e/
  you-screen.spec.ts                         dial cycle against the real server (+ screenshots)
  welcome.spec.ts                            first-visit walk + replay-skip (+ screenshots)
```

## Human verification

1. `pnpm db:reset && pnpm dev`, sign in, open **You** → the WHO CAN SEE YOU pill reads **UP TO 6TH°**.
2. Tap the pill four times → it walks 1ST° ONLY → UP TO 2ND° → UP TO 3RD° → UP TO 6TH°; reload the page → the last value persisted (it is the server's echo, not local state).
3. In psql: `select app.visible_people('<your-user-id>', 10, 1500);` → no returned degree ever exceeds 6, and setting a user to `'first'` makes them vanish from a degree-2 viewer's rows entirely (no row, not a null name).
4. In a private window, visit `/` → the three-step welcome plays; finish it, visit `/` again → straight to `/signin`.

## How I can prove I was successful

All commands ran locally on this branch (heads `9cf26c2` → `8464170`; the only change between them is the migration statement reorder proven below, and the integration suite reran green at the final head); CI runs the same nine required jobs.

**proven — full verification battery green** (output from this session):

```
pnpm typecheck         → exit 0
pnpm lint              → exit 0
pnpm boundaries        → exit 0
pnpm test:unit         → 513 passed | 1 skipped
pnpm test:integration  → 220 passed   (rerun at 8464170)
pnpm test:security     → 97 passed
pnpm build:web         → exit 0
pnpm build:server:node → exit 0
pnpm test:e2e          → 10 passed (1.3m)
```

**proven — the six-degree ceiling and the budget fix are pinned by integration tests** (`visible-to-distance.integration.test.ts`, 5 passed): an eight-person chain with `max_depth = 10` shows degree 6 present and degree 7 absent (the ceiling is the function's, not the caller's); a deactivated middle node with `node_budget = 2` no longer evicts the active person behind it; the service round-trip defaults to `'sixth'`.

**proven — the dial works against the real running app.** The e2e test signs in through the real server, asserts the default label, then clicks the whole cycle — every click is an `identity.visibility.set` mutation and every label read is the server's stored row:

![The You screen with the Who-can-see-you dial at its 'sixth' default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drewdrewthis/playa-post/412b2d00007cfedd8021ba694717c676f9832f86/docs/engineering/screenshots/m5-visibility-dial-sixth.png)

**proven — the welcome flow plays once and never again.** First anonymous visit redirects to `/welcome`; step 3 exits to `/signin`; a repeat visit skips straight there:

![Welcome step 1 — Your graph is yours](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drewdrewthis/playa-post/412b2d00007cfedd8021ba694717c676f9832f86/docs/engineering/screenshots/m5-welcome-step-1.png)

![Welcome step 3 — Search like a local, Get started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drewdrewthis/playa-post/412b2d00007cfedd8021ba694717c676f9832f86/docs/engineering/screenshots/m5-welcome-step-3.png)

**proven — the migration works on a *populated* database, not just a fresh replay.** Exercised against a throwaway `postgres:17` carrying a real `'anyone'` row — which caught and killed a bug the fresh-replay suites structurally cannot see (the rewrite ran under the old constraint, which does not allow `'sixth'`). Before the fix (`9cf26c2`) the migration errors mid-file; after (`8464170`):

```
MIGRATION-APPLIED-CLEAN (exit 0)
AFTER: sixth                       -- the pre-existing 'anyone' row was rewritten
DEFAULT: 'sixth'::text             -- new column default
ERROR:  new row for relation "users" violates check constraint
        "users_visible_to_distance_check"   -- inserting 'anyone' now rejected
```

## Anything surprising?

- **Accepted ADR-0004 decision-4 deviation** (recorded in the migration header and the SQL comments): ghost surrogate IDs remain unimplemented, so `topology_only` rows carry real user ids. The product owner took this trade explicitly for alpha.

author: sh00tg0a1
body:
Follow-up to #769, raised by the review on #771. Both findings there were non-blocking but real, and neither `main` nor `release/0.1.3` has them fixed — this PR fixes `main`, and a backport follows.

## The agent could not see what an aggregated run covered

#769 added `execution_mode` and `target_count` to the execution record, plus `targets` on the result. Context-loader's slimming projection never allowed those three through, so via `get_action_execution` the agent saw `total_count: 1` and an empty `_instance_identity` — reading "30 instances collapsed into one invocation" as "only 1 object was processed". The one thing the change most needed to communicate was dropped at the last hop.

`actionExecutionKeepKeys` now passes `execution_mode` and `target_count`; `actionResultKeepKeys` passes `targets`.

## Contracts had drifted from behaviour

- `docs/api/context-loader/action.yaml` — `total_count` still read "目标对象总数" in **both** `ActionExecution` and `ActionExecutionSummary`; it is now documented as the tool-invocation count, with `execution_mode` and `target_count` added and `target_count` explicitly called out as the field to read for coverage. `ActionExecutionResult` gains `targets` and explains that `once` produces a single result.
- `docs/api/ontology-query/ontology-query.yaml` — `ActionExecutionList.entries` still pointed at `ActionExecution`, which carries `results`, `action_type_snapshot` and `action_source`; the list has excluded all three at the OpenSearch layer since #767. Entries now reference a new `ActionExecutionSummary`.

## Testing

`TestGetActionExecution_Success` now feeds an aggregated execution (mode `once`, 30 targets, one result carrying 2 targets) and asserts all three fields survive the projection.

```
ok  context-loader/agent-retrieval/logics/knactionrecall  2.167s
```

Both OpenAPI files parse.

Refs #724

## Contexto

Completa la **Fase 8 — operativa de "Registrados"**. El PR anterior (#1645) añadió editar/borrar; este añade el **alta**.

## Qué hace

En **Gastos → Registrados**, una barra **`+ Añadir gasto` / `+ Añadir mejora` / `+ Añadir mobiliario`** (también visible en el estado vacío) permite dar de alta registros nuevos:

- Reutiliza `EditarRegistroInmuebleModal` con un nuevo modo **`crear`**: título "Añadir…", campos en blanco, **fecha de hoy** por defecto, **vida útil 10** por defecto para mobiliario. El gasto real deriva `casillaAEAT` de la categoría y el `ejercicio` de la fecha.
- La hook `useRegistrosInmueble` añade `abrirAlta / cerrarAlta / crear`.

## Trazabilidad y semántica

El alta es **directa**: un gasto que registras es un gasto **ya ocurrido**, no una previsión de Tesorería, así que se persiste directamente (mismo patrón que el wizard de alta de inmueble ya existente):
- Gasto real → `gastosInmuebleService.add` (`origen: 'manual'`, `estado: 'confirmado'`).
- Mejora → `mejorasInmuebleService.crear`.
- Mobiliario → `mueblesInmuebleService.crear` (`activo: true`).

Editar y borrar (del PR anterior) siguen propagando a los `treasuryEvent`/`movement` ya vinculados.

## Bloqueo de ejercicios

No se permite dar de alta en un ejercicio **declarado/prescrito** (aviso + aborta), coherente con el bloqueo de editar/borrar.

## Qué NO toca

Stores, `DB_VERSION`, `categoryKey`, fiscalidad ni rutas. No añade el campo `naturaleza`. TS estricto, sin `any` nuevos, solo tokens `var(--atlas-v5-*)`.

## Tests

- 12 nuevos: `useRegistrosInmueble` (alta de los 3 tipos + guarda de ejercicio bloqueado), `EditarRegistroInmuebleModal` (modo crear · defaults), `GastosRegistradosInmueble.render` (barra de alta · callback).

author: mateenali66
body:
## 🗣 Description ##

Export-SecuritySuiteProvider treated any failure of the ATP and DLP cmdlets as a missing license and discarded the error, so a transient API failure produced a false missing-license note in the report with nothing in the console or log.

The provider now records each failed cmdlet's error message, treats a failure as missing-license evidence only when the message matches the 400 unrecognized-cmdlet shape the Admin API returns for unprovisioned cmdlets, and surfaces every other failure with the existing Write-Warning idiom plus a Write-ScubaLog entry, following the same pattern CommandTracker.TryCommand uses. Real failures stay in `securitysuite_unsuccessful_commands`, which the report already renders as an API error. Genuinely unlicensed tenants keep the prior behavior.

The 400/not-recognized classification is the load-bearing assumption; I could not confirm the exact unlicensed-tenant error text against a live tenant, so review from someone with tenant access would help.

## 💭 Motivation and context ##

A tenant with a valid Defender license was shown as missing it whenever an ATP call failed for an unrelated reason, and the underlying error was discarded, leaving nothing to troubleshoot with. Same error-surfacing direction as #2277 took for the EXO functional test helpers. Resolves #2319.

## 🧪 Testing ##

- Six new Pester unit tests in Export-SecuritySuiteProvider.Tests.ps1: license vs non-license failures for both the ATP and DLP paths, warning assertions, and JSON validity on failure.
- Full provider unit suite: 14/14 pass locally (pwsh 7.6.4, Pester 5.9, macOS). CI's Windows PowerShell 5.1 not run locally; code kept 5.1-compatible.
- PSScriptAnalyzer on both changed files: no new findings (one pre-existing Information finding on main).

author: rolandsobczak
body:
Phase 6 of docs/13-roadmap.md. klm verify --clean-room, klm scaffold, klm docs, klm report, and --normalize-timestamps for byte-reproducible fab output.

This is the phase that makes Phase 4's self-containment guarantee real rather than assumed, so verify.py takes a project and nothing else — no connection, no config, no Paths. A test asserts that signature, because a checker able to reach the catalog would pass on the one machine where passing means nothing.

Q11 was checked first and returned four things:

* The official KiCad image ends with `USER kicad`, while a container job's workspace is created by the runner as root — so actions/checkout fails on permissions before anything else runs. Every generated workflow would have failed on its first push. Found by reading the Dockerfile.

* The `-full` image carries KiCad's standard libraries, which settles the question ADR-0010 deferred: "a machine that has nothing" still has KiCad, so `power:GND` legitimately resolves while `Passive:0R_0603` does not — answered by trying to resolve, with no list to keep current.

* KiCad ignores SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; GbrMakeCreationDateAttributeString reads the wall clock unconditionally. So klm rewrites the timestamps itself, and *replaces* rather than blanks them: a well-formed TF.CreationDate cannot upset a parser that accepted the original, which closes the risk the design note worried about by construction rather than by testing an upload.

* Whether `pcb render` still needs an X server is unverified, as is the exact kicad-cli flag surface — KiCad is not installed here. xvfb-run is wrapped defensively and klm docs degrades per artifact rather than as a whole.

Running verify over a real board caught a bad heuristic: KiCad quotes net names (/SDA, /BAT+) and hierarchical sheet paths exactly like POSIX paths, so flagging every quoted string starting with a slash produced 124 false errors against 2 true ones. The check now requires a directory component and a file extension, or an unambiguous Windows/UNC prefix — 1 finding, 0 false, and the finding is a real /home/rsobczak/... model path.

구현 명세: [`docs/notification/discord-delivery-plan.md`](docs/notification/discord-delivery-plan.md)

## Bot 계약 실측 결과

요구사항 문서는 Bot 구현 **이전**에 작성되어 실제 계약과 어긋나는 지점이 있었다. GETI-Bot-V1 `develop`(PR #5·#7·#9·#11 merged)의 실제 코드를 Source of Truth로 삼아 **전부 실제 계약을 따랐다**.

| # | 요구사항 문서 | 실제 계약 | 처리 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | §3·§8 `mentionRoleIds` | `roleIds` | 필드명 변경 |
| 2 | §24 "PATCH엔 `mentionRoleIds`를 **비워서** 전달" | PATCH Body는 `.strict()`이고 `roleIds` 필드가 **없음** | 빈 배열조차 보내지 않는다. 보내면 `400 INVALID_REQUEST`(재시도 불가) |
| 3 | §5 3개 Header 공통 | `X-Idempotency-Key`는 **POST 전용** | CREATE에만 부착 |
| 4 | §46 top-level `targetId` String | 그런 필드 없음. `data.jobId` 등이 String | Entity는 `Long`, HTTP 경계에서만 String |

> `main` 브랜치는 초기 세팅 상태(`GET /health`만)라 계약 확인에 쓰면 안 된다.

### 문서 내부 모순 1건 해소

§20은 Idempotency Key를 `discord:{deliveryId}:{action}:{revision}`로 예시하지만, §49는 같은 키의 UNIQUE 제약으로 **Row 생성 자체**를 막으라고 한다. `deliveryId`는 Row를 저장해야 생기므로 둘은 양립할 수 없다(닭-달걀). Key를 Event에서 유도하도록 재설계했다.

```text
CREATE / CLOSE_NOTICE / DELETE_NOTICE   {targetType}:{targetId}:{action}
UPDATE                                  {targetType}:{targetId}:UPDATE:{원본 updatedAt epochMilli}
```

앞의 셋은 대상당 영구히 1건이라 §23("삭제된 메시지 자동 재생성 금지")이 DB 제약으로 강제된다. UPDATE는 원본 수정 시각으로 구분해 **카운터 조회가 없어 동시 삽입 경합이 생기지 않는다**.

## 주요 결정

| 항목 | 결정 | 근거 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker 선점 | 조건부 Atomic UPDATE(`WHERE id=:id AND status=PENDING`) | 새 의존성 없이 다중 인스턴스 안전. HTTP 호출은 Lock 밖 |
| Stale 복구 | `processing_started_at` 기준 시각 판정 | Collector의 `ApplicationRunner` 방식은 단일 인스턴스 전제라, 다중 인스턴스에서 재기동한 쪽이 **타 인스턴스의 전송 중 Row를 침범**한다 |
| 수동 재시도 | `automaticRetryCount`를 0으로 초기화 | 전체 이력은 `discord_delivery_attempts`에 보존되어 감사 정보가 사라지지 않는다. 초기화하지 않으면 재시도 버튼이 백오프 없이 1회만 시도하고 끝난다 |
| read timeout | **12초**(Bot 자체 10초보다 길게) | 짧게 잡으면 Bot이 실제로 게시했는데 서버만 실패 처리하는 구간이 생긴다. Bot Idempotency는 InMemory라 이를 막아주지 못한다(§38) |
| 오류 해석 | HTTP Status보다 **Body의 `code`** 우선 | Bot은 Route 도달 전 오류를 Fastify가 판단한 Status(예: 413)로 내려보낸다 |

## 발견해 수정한 결함

- **제목 길이 초과** — `jobs.title`/`programs.title`은 DB에서 500자인데 Bot `titleSchema`는 **200자**다. 자르지 않으면 `400 INVALID_REQUEST`(`retryable=false`)로 **자동 재시도 없이 즉시 FAILED**가 되어 알림이 영구 누락된다. 모든 문자열을 Bot Schema 상한으로 절단하고, `trim` 후 빈 값이 되는 선택 필드는 생략한다(Bot이 `min(1)`을 요구).
- **재시도 카운터 상한 초과** — `markFailed`가 예산 소진 시에도 카운터를 올려 상한 3에 4가 저장됐다. 예약 시점에만 증가하도록 고치고 회귀 테스트를 추가했다.

## 아키텍처

`notification → {job, program, inquiry}` **단방향**을 유지했다. 세 도메인에 `@NamedInterface` Query Port를 **순수 추가**(동작 변경·Breaking Change 없음)했고, 역방향 의존은 만들지 않아 `ModularityTest`가 통과한다.

> 참고: 다음 PR에서 §15의 상태 조회 API(`/api/v1/admin/jobs/{id}/discord`)를 추가할 때, **Controller는 `domain.notification`에 두어야 한다.** `JobAdminController`에 두면 `job → notification` 역방향이 생겨 즉시 순환 의존이 된다. URL 경로는 명세대로 유지하면 된다.

## 검증

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat clean test build     # BUILD SUCCESSFUL (spotless·detekt·kover 포함)
.\gradlew.bat integrationTest      # BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 129 tests (Testcontainers PostgreSQL)
```

신규 테스트 **70개**:

| 테스트 | 수 | 내용 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DiscordDeliveryServiceImplTest` | 24 | 상태 전이, 자동/수동 재시도, 선점 실패, Stale 회수, 사전 검증 실패 |
| `HttpDiscordBotClientTest` | 17 | Endpoint·Header·Body·401/400/404/429/5xx·timeout·malformed (Contract Test) |
| `DiscordPayloadFactoryTest` | 13 | Bot `.strict()` Schema 준수, 길이 절단, 빈 필드 생략, ISO-8601 Offset |
| `DiscordIdempotencyKeysTest` | 8 | 중복 dedup, 재수정 구분, 200자 상한 |
| `DiscordDeliveryRetryPolicyTest` | 8 | 1/5/30분 백오프, 상한 |
| `DiscordDeliveryRepositoryIntegrationTest` | 14 | V19 Migration, Mapping, UNIQUE, Worker Query, 동시 선점 |

`FakeDiscordBotClient`는 `src/test`에만 두어 테스트에 Discord Token·API Key가 필요 없고 CI가 외부 Network에 의존하지 않는다. 실제 Discord/Bot을 호출하지 않는다.

## Breaking Change

**없다.** 이번 PR은 API Endpoint를 추가·변경하지 않아 Swagger 갱신 대상도 없다. `domain.program`의 `DiscordDeliveryStatus(SUCCESS/FAILED/SKIPPED)` 교체는 Breaking Change라 다음 PR로 분리했다.

## 이번 범위에서 제외

| 항목 | 사유 |
| --- | --- |
| Job/Program/Inquiry Domain Event 연결 | 3개 도메인을 동시에 건드려 Regression 위험이 커진다 → 다음 PR |
| Discord 상태 조회·수동 Retry **REST API** | Event가 없어 운영 중 Row가 생기지 않는다. 지금 노출하면 영원히 빈 결과만 반환하고 재시도할 Row도 없어 **검증 자체가 불가능**하다. 재시도 **로직**은 전부 구현·검증되어 있다 |
| Program `DiscordDeliveryStatus` 교체 | Breaking Change라 분리 |
| 허용 채널 4개·`targetGrades → Role ID` 매핑 | 실제 Snowflake 미확정. §10이 "코드 상수로 임의 지정하지 않는다"고 명시 |
| Collector Discord Webhook 이관 | §34가 명시적으로 제외 |
| Resilience4j / Redis / Kafka | §63 |

## 가정 (DECISION_REQUIRED)

1. **`data.url`을 보내지 않는다.** 프론트 Base URL 설정이 저장소에 없고 Bot은 절대 URL만 받는다. 세 Schema 모두 optional이라 계약 위반이 아니다. 확정 시 `DiscordPayloadFactory` 한 곳만 고치면 된다.
2. **`changes`/`reason`을 보내지 않는다.** 값의 출처(무엇이 바뀌었는지)가 없다. Event가 붙는 다음 PR에서 결정한다.
3. **시각은 `ZoneId.systemDefault()` 기준 Offset**으로 직렬화한다. 저장소에 명시적 Timezone 설정이 없고 Collector Embed Builder가 이미 같은 방식을 쓴다.
4. **`Job.discordChannelKey`(논리 Key) vs `Program.discordChannelId`(원시 Snowflake) 불일치**는 이번 PR이 어느 쪽도 읽지 않는다. 다음 PR에서 통일 방향을 정해야 한다.

## 보안

- Internal API Key는 Server→Bot 전용이며 응답·로그·예외 어디에도 넣지 않는다. `application.yaml`에는 Placeholder만 있고 **안전하지 않은 기본값을 주지 않는다**(미설정 시 Worker가 즉시 반환, Fail-Fast 아님).
- `discord_delivery_attempts`에 API Key·Header·전체 Payload·문의 본문·Stack Trace를 저장하지 않는다.
- Inquiry Payload에 이메일·전화번호·본문·제목이 없다. Bot의 `.strict()` Schema가 2차 방어선이다.
- `discord.js` 등 Discord SDK를 서버 의존성에 추가하지 않았다.

## 참고

- #96 의 완료 조건이 이 PR의 범위와 1:1로 대응한다. PR B(Domain Event 연결·Program Breaking Change·상태 조회 API)와 PR D(통합 검증)는 #96 의 "후속 범위"에 분리해 두었으므로, 이 PR이 병합되며 #96 이 닫혀도 남는 작업이 묻히지 않는다.
- 첫 커밋의 `docs/Notification` → `docs/notification` 디렉터리 이동은 이 브랜치 이전부터 작업 트리에 Stage되어 있던 변경이며, 이번 문서 링크가 이를 전제해 함께 포함했다.

author: maciejmegger-oss
body:
Każde dotknięcie kafla lądowało „gdzieś w meczu", a nie przy kimś: obserwacja zespołu nie wskazuje nikogo, a przy jednym wskazanym zawodniku i tak nie dało się tagować drugiego. Składy były już wtedy w telefonie, razem z oceną, kto się wyróżnia — ale zdarzenia nie wiedziały o żadnym z nich.

## Pasek „Tagujesz"

Zawodnicy oznaczeni jako wyróżniający się pojawiają się nad kaflami. Dotknięcie przełącza, komu przypisują się kolejne zdarzenia; wybór zostaje aż do zmiany, bo w trakcie akcji nie ma czasu na potwierdzanie. Pierwsza pozycja to **Zespół** — dla zdarzeń bez wskazania osoby.

- **Licznik na kaflu** pokazuje teraz liczbę zdarzeń dla **wybranego** podmiotu. Suma z całego meczu nie niosłaby żadnej informacji, gdy śledzi się kilku zawodników.
- **Oś zdarzeń** stawia nazwisko przed rodzajem zdarzenia.
- Wybór trzymany jest w stanie meczu, nie w pamięci widoku — przetrwa zamknięcie karty w trakcie gry.

## Dwie usterki, które wyszły przy okazji

**Skrót brał ostatni wyraz nazwy za nazwisko**, a składy meczowe zapisuje się „Nazwisko Imię" — na planszy widniało `10 Filip` zamiast `10 Mosek`. Skrót bierze teraz pierwszy wyraz.

**Nazwisko służyło za tożsamość zawodnika**, co zlewałoby dwóch Kowalskich w jednego. Tożsamość niesie teraz numer razem z pełnym zapisem nazwy.

## Zapis

Zdarzenie dostaje pole `zawodnik` z zapisem takim, jak widnieje w składzie (`10 Mosek Filip`). Zawodnicy ze składu meczu nie mają identyfikatorów w bazie — skład bywa wklejony z kartki — więc zapisujemy nazwę, nie odwołanie.

Migracja `sbs_live_events` dostaje kolumnę `zawodnik` wraz z `alter table … add column if not exists`, dla baz, w których tabela już powstała. **Uruchomienie nadal nie jest wymagane**: przy braku tabeli oś zdarzeń idzie do `sbs_kv`, a obejście obejmuje teraz także brakującą kolumnę — starsza tabela nie zablokuje zapisu, tylko przekieruje go do `sbs_kv`.

## Sprawdzenie

Przetestowane w przeglądarce: pasek z wyróżnionymi, przełączanie podmiotu, liczniki per zawodnik, nazwiska na osi, zapis zdarzeń z przypisaniem. Pozostały przebieg panelu (rozpoznawanie składu, usuwanie, plansza ustawienia, oceny po meczu, cztery zapisy do bazy, tryb offline) przechodzi bez zmian.

author: jdkrasnick
body:
## TL;DR

Configured 480-second budgets previously allowed escaped descendants and inherited pipes to hold runs open for 6,037–7,812 seconds. A shared supervisor now closes harness pipes, identifies run-owned processes on macOS and Linux, terminates the owned tree within a 1.5-second cleanup grace, and records deadline, cleanup, survivor, reconnect, transport, and MCP-auth evidence.

**Files to review (6, +695 / -87):**

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `src/runner/process-supervisor.ts` *(start here)* | Platform-specific ownership discovery, identity checks, bounded signal escalation, and survivor reporting. |
| `src/runner/process-runner.ts` | Deadline watchdog shared by provider and shell commands. |
| `src/core/types.ts` | Serializable cleanup and transport diagnostics. |
| `test/unit/process-runner.test.ts` | Early launcher exit, escaped sessions, inherited pipes, shell parity, and unrelated-process coverage. |
| `PRODUCT.md` | Product-level hard deadline contract. |
| `docs/MVP.md` | Documented 1.5-second cleanup grace and failure behavior. |

## How

Every descendant inherits a run-unique ownership marker. Linux reads the marker with `/proc` start ticks; macOS reads it from the process environment and combines it with `ps` start identity, preserving ownership after a launcher exits and its detached children are reparented. Cleanup uses one absolute deadline across discovery, TERM, KILL, and final inspection; incomplete inspection or surviving descendants becomes an infrastructure failure instead of a successful timeout.

Successful commands retain the direct `execa` path, so process-table discovery runs only after a deadline or cancellation.

## Reviewer notes

- **No broad process-group signal.** Every PID is matched to the run marker and revalidated before signaling; the regression fixture verifies an unrelated detached process survives.
- **Early launcher exit is covered.** The launcher exits after 25 ms while detached descendants keep its output descriptors open, and the test asserts that the call stays within the configured budget plus the 1.5-second grace and leaves no recorded descendant.
- **Focus area:** macOS uses `ps eww` only during cleanup to recover the inherited ownership marker from reparented descendants; raw process environments are neither logged nor persisted.

## Tests

`npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (158 tests), and `npm run build` pass.

## Links

- Closes #40

body:
## What changed

- recursively delete nested filter containers, descendants, and stale parent/group references
- wire the existing **Delete group** control to the grouped-argument store
- cover list-value churn, subtree deletion/rebuild, and logical `_or` rebuilds
- add a bounded CI stress pass plus `test:e2e:filter-soak` for ten serial repetitions

## Why

Filter groups could be added repeatedly but the group-delete action was still a placeholder. Removing or rebuilding nested branches could therefore leave stale nodes and GraphQL values behind. The previous mixed-operator stress loop also exceeded its normal 120-second timeout under full load.

The store now treats leaf and container deletion consistently, removes a container recursively, preserves unrelated siblings and the root container, and emits fresh references for Svelte reactivity.

## Impact

Users can delete and rebuild nested and logical filter groups without stale values, duplicate nodes, orphan dialogs, or incorrect result rows. Normal CI remains bounded while the opt-in soak exercises 100 mixed-operator sessions plus repeated subtree and logical rebuilds.

- `npm run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings

author: asigdel29
body:
#454 decided what the list says and #456 reads it. This is the screen, and it completes 3.24.

## Re-read on resume, not on first composition

The whole point of a checklist over a wizard is that it is **right when you look at it**, and the moment somebody looks is the moment they come back from Settings. Built once and never re-read, it would show the state as it was before they went — the same lie a wizard tells, arrived at by accident.

## Every row is a button to the exact screen

Naming a path beats saying "Settings" (#454); taking somebody there beats naming it. The restricted-settings row names a **menu inside a page** rather than a page, and there is no intent for a menu — so it opens the page and its own words say which item to press.

## It appears only when something required is off, and is skippable anyway

Blocking the conversation would make the app unusable to somebody who wants to talk and never intends to let it drive anything. The phone tools are one capability among several, and `read_screen` already explains itself when it is called without them.

## It ends by showing what the model would see

The first ten lines of a **real reading**, over whatever was on screen before the app opened. That is `just verify` pointed at a person.

*"The switch is on"* is a claim. *"This is what it can read"* is evidence — and it is the moment somebody decides whether they are comfortable with any of it, which is not a decision anybody can make from a list of green ticks. It appears only once there is something to read: before the service is on there is nothing to show and nothing to promise.

## Where it ran

This machine, both suites.

- `just android-test` — 338 JVM tests, 0 failures. Unchanged; this is Compose and the deciding was tested in #454 and #456.
- `just android-device-test` — 56 instrumented on the `wattrouter-tests` AVD, `system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a`. Re-run because `MainActivity` changed.
- `just guards` clean at 179 changed lines.

Not claimed: that the screen looks right, or that the buttons land on the pages they name. Both need eyes on a phone, and they belong with Phase 4's run — where the checklist is also the fastest way to find out whether restricted settings has been cleared.

Closes #457. Refs #233, #453, #455.

author: tend-agent
body:
Three `tend-review` reviews on `max-sixty/worktrunk` withheld APPROVE and attributed the decision to a repo review policy that does not exist in writing. The withholding itself is correct and authorised — this is about the citation, not the verdict.

| Review | Wording |
|---|---|
| [worktrunk#3784 r4891319505](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/3784#pullrequestreview-4891319505) 12:04:47Z | "**Per this repo's tend review policy** the `wt remove --reap` path is a hold-for-human surface" |
| [worktrunk#3784 r4891354215](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/3784#pullrequestreview-4891354215) 12:22:27Z | "`wt remove --reap` is a hold-for-human surface **under this repo's review policy**" |
| [worktrunk#3785 r4891406429](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/3785#pullrequestreview-4891406429) 12:47:20Z | "**Per the repo's review guidance** a change to what `wt remove --force` can reach isn't an agent's to sign off on" |

No such rule is written anywhere a reader could follow the pointer to:

- worktrunk's overlay (`.claude/skills/running-tend/SKILL.md`, 383 lines) — zero hits for `hold.for.human|data.safety|sign off|not an agent`. Its only approval-related content is "Don't Self-Dismiss Over Unrelated Test Flakes".
- worktrunk's `CLAUDE.md` §"Data Safety" exists, but it is a *code* guideline ("prefer failure over silent loss", "explicit consent for destructive ops") — it says nothing about who may approve a PR.
- tend's bundled skills and `shared/` — zero hits for the same patterns across the whole tree.

What actually authorises the behaviour is [`review/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/blob/main/plugins/tend-ci-runner/skills/review/SKILL.md)'s own "If the design involves a judgment call, flag it for human review as a COMMENT". That is a sufficient reason on its own. Dressing it as a citable repo policy sends the author looking for a rule that isn't there — the same shape as a fabricated API flag or a guessed docs slug, which `running-in-ci` §"Grounded Analysis" already treats as the fastest way to erode trust in everything else in the comment.

## The change

One paragraph in the review skill, next to the existing low-confidence guidance: cite repo guidance only when you can name the file and heading; otherwise own the call as your own judgment, with a contrasting example.

## Gate assessment

- **Evidence level: High** (consistent pattern across multiple sessions) — **3 occurrences**, across 2 PRs, 3 distinct sessions, 2 analysis windows. Occurrence 1 was recorded in the evidence gist by the prior window (run 31312038759), which set "whether another review cites a 'repo policy' that grep can't find" as its explicit next-window check; occurrences 2 and 3 landed in this window. Every non-approving review in the window did it, 3/3.
- **Structural vs stochastic**: the phrasing is a model choice, so stochastic-leaning — but the skill authorises flagging judgment calls for human review without saying anything about how to attribute the withholding, and the observed rate is 3/3. The edit closes the gap rather than legislating a one-off lapse.
- **Change type: targeted fix** (one paragraph beside the guidance it qualifies, no restructuring) — Gate 2 normal bar, met at 3.
- Substance is not in question: the prior window re-verified six of this reviewer's factual claims against source, six for six, and the human author acted on every finding in both PRs this window.

Evidence log: https://gist.github.com/a88c03f4d0c3fb1791060ff3dd97d1c4

Three linked corrections, all from the same root cause: concluding "the county publishes nothing" without ever running a web search.

## 1. Morgan ships — from `morgancounty-il.COM`

The operator found it with a basic search after this project spent a day measuring `morgancounty-il.GOV`, a client-rendered React shell with an empty backend. The `.com` is the county's real site and publishes all three commissioners with role, party, full term dates, next election and a personal e-mail apiece.

**The correction changes who is on the card.** Derived from election returns, the third seat read as Bradley Zeller (2020). The real member is **Michael D. Woods, term starting 1 October 2024** — a mid-term start, i.e. an appointment filling that vacancy. Appointments appear in no election return anywhere. The drafted e-mail warned about exactly this in the abstract while the county being written to was a live example.

Gap closed; Morgan is the 11th County-card county. Also: `email_in()` gains an opt-in bare-text mode (Morgan prints addresses as text, no `mailto:`), scoped per caller.

| site exists, refuses this network | Coles (two sites), Pope, Johnson |
| correct as recorded | Cumberland, Wabash |

**The answer was in this repository.** `data/app/il-county-clerks.json` carries every Clerk's e-mail, and for **nine of the fourteen the clerk's e-mail domain IS the county's web domain**. On 2026-08-05 this project e-mailed those counties at those very domains while recording that they had no website.

Name-permutation could never have worked — `gallatinCO`, `colesCO`, `clarkcountyil.**org**`, `shelbycounty-il.gov`, `popecountyil.com`: six shapes across nine counties.

**It had already been caught once.** On 2026-08-05 the Vermilion County Clerk wrote *"Yes, Vermilion County does have a website and the link is…"*, and the reply said *"My automated search tool looks for variations of the full county name, so I missed it."* The whole diagnosis, in writing, four days earlier — fixed for one county, never made a rule.

## 3. Jersey — the Clerk has a separate domain

`jerseycountyclerk-il.gov` publishes a vector County Board Districts map. The gap record said Jersey had no district boundaries at all. Corrected, with the two things that genuinely do stand between that PDF and a build: it is dated **2016**, before the post-2020 redistricting, and its fills may be raster. A correction has been sent to the Clerk, since the original ask went out before this was found.

## The procedure now

`EXPANSION_GUIDE` §2.5 opens with **step zero: search before probing**, preceded by the cheaper step — derive candidate hosts from the clerk's e-mail domain. Plus the decoys this sweep rejected (Scott County **Tennessee**, Cumberland County **Maine**, a Crawford **Development Association**, a Shelby **real-estate agency**, a Gallatin **weather** site) and the blocked-vs-absent distinction.

**Wabash is the model**: its record predicted today's 503 exactly, because it was written from a Clerk's reply and a measurement rather than a failed guess. Both records that survived the resweep are the two that were never guesses.

## Gates

`build_coverage_gaps --check`, `build_county_status --check` (59 served: 48 dispatch, 3 judicial, 8 card), `generate_metro_files --check`, `validate_index`, `check_roster_retention`, and the full smoke test (**119/119 gaps render**) — all OK.

author: eatyourpeas
body:
## Problem

The `/countries/` endpoint was returning Jersey with `boundary_identifier = "E92000003"`, which is wrong. `E92000003` is an England-prefixed GSS code that actually denotes the **North East region of England** — Jersey is a Crown Dependency, not part of the UK, so it has no `E`/`W`/`N`/`S`-prefixed GSS code.

## Root cause

Migration `0010_refactor_jersey_boundary_identifier` deliberately overwrote the correct `JEY` value (loaded from the GADM shape file by `0009`) with `E92000003`. The same wrong code was then hardcoded in the `COUNTRY_CODES` constant, two seed-function lookups, and the PDU parent-nesting logic in `serializers/trust.py`.

## Fix

Correct Jersey's `boundary_identifier` to `JEY` — the GADM shape file's `GID_0` value and Jersey's ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code.

- **New migration `0035_fix_jersey_boundary_identifier`** — `RunPython` that updates `Country(name="Jersey")` to `JEY`. Self-healing on any DB that already applied `0010` (including live); no-op on fresh installs where `0009` already loaded `JEY`.
- **`constants/country_codes.py`** — `COUNTRY_CODES` Jersey entry → `JEY`.
- **`seed_functions/crown_dependencies.py`** + **`seed_functions/organisations.py`** — look up Jersey by `JEY` (prevents `DoesNotExist` on re-seed).
- **`serializers/trust.py`** — PDU parent-nesting check `["E92000001", "JEY", "M83000003"]` (without this, Jersey PDUs would silently stop returning their parent Trust).
- **Tests** — `test_jersey_boundary_identifier_is_JEY` (asserts `/countries/JEY/` resolves and `/countries/E92000003/` 404s) + `test_jersey_constant_uses_JEY` (guards the constant against regression).

Historical migrations `0009`/`0010` are left untouched.

## Validation

Migrated locally and confirmed the API returns `JEY`. Full test suite passes:

```bash
./s/test
docker compose exec django python -c "from rcpch_nhs_organisations.hospitals.models import Country; print(Country.objects.get(name='Jersey').boundary_identifier)"
# prints JEY
```

## ⚠️ Breaking change for API consumers

After deploying this and running `migrate`, `/countries/E92000003/` will return **404**. Any client currently hitting that URL must switch to `/countries/JEY/`. The `Organisation.country` FK is unaffected (it points to the `Country` row, not the `boundary_identifier` value), so organisation relationships stay intact.

## Why

## What changed

**Tour** — 6 steps → 3 (tab strip, wall panel, Hang it), one plain sentence each. The dropped steps pointed at the view toolbar and frame library, neither of which exists on a virgin run; a missing target unmounts the overlay, so the screen went blank for ~500ms and then jumped, and `Back` into those steps bounced forward again. **Flow** — `nextAction` gained the two missing steps (photo-uploaded-but-no-scale, and photos, which was never nudged at all). `stepsDone(state, visited)` ticks Arrange on visit, so auto-layout users get the ✓. The wall-area step also renders on the canvas, because that is the one step whose action happens there; a third copy of the same warning (`warn-overlay`) is gone.

Walked a virgin run in the browser at 375×812 and desktop: 3-step tour with a live spotlight on every step and no blank frames, Back reverses cleanly, blank preset → wall + ✓ + Next advances, photo state shows only the calibration path, canvas card opens the wall-area editor. author: davekjohn
body:
# What does the change on this branch bring to main?
The two directories the plugins are split across each get their own README, so opening one no longer
means reading a list of folder names and guessing what binds them. Each page states what belongs in
that directory, the one rule that governs it, and what a folder inside it holds — for the teams: they
stack, and the `team-*` name plus its directory is held by lint check 23; for the workflows: at most
one may be enabled, why that check lives in the core team rather than in these plugins, and what
`workflow-davekjohn` expects from a repo's own seam. The root README's repo-layout bullet now names
both directories and links them, so the pages are reachable from the landing page rather than only by
browsing.

Both pages deliberately stop short of restating the plugin table. They name the folders and point at
the root README for the "who it's for" column, because a second copy of that table would be free to
disagree with the first and nobody reads both pages in one sitting — the failure this repo has already
paid for with the per-plugin `CHANGELOG.md` and `RELEASE.md` files.

## Significance

### Tier 0

The split between teams and workflows was documented only in the root README, so a developer working
inside `plugins/` had to leave the directory to find out what governed it. Now the rule sits next to
what it governs. Small: they already knew the rule.

**Score:** 2

### Tier 1

Same gain, plus one that outlasts it: the two naming rules that are load-bearing rather than cosmetic
— the `workflow-` prefix the session check counts by, and the directory each prefix implies — are now
stated where somebody adding a plugin is already looking.

**Score:** 2

### Tier 2

A consumer receives the marketplace source as a clone of the whole repository, so these two
directories are what they browse when deciding which plugins to enable. Until now `plugins/teams/`
showed four unexplained folders and `plugins/workflows/` two, with the explanation a level up in a
1,000-line README. It is noticed the moment they open either directory.

**Score:** 3

author: dammianmiller
body:
Continued monitoring found the live run producing a file in the wrong place — and it isn't a guard bug. It's a guard working, and the model routing around it.

A mission scoped to `<repo>/src/rust-pg-ext` was instructed to edit `src/sql/setup.sql` — which is `<repo>/src/sql/setup.sql`, 62KB, outside the crate. The model tried `../sql/setup.sql`; `safePath` refused it, correctly. Its next move was the damaging one:

| file | size | state |
|---|---|---|
| `<repo>/src/sql/setup.sql` (the real one) | 62,754 B | out of reach |
| `<crate>/src/sql/setup.sql` (model-created) | 1,517 B | **untracked phantom** |

`safePath` allows that write, because it *is* inside the root. So the guard deflected the model into producing a plausible-looking file in the wrong place: untracked, unreferenced, easy to mistake for the requested edit.

Refusing the path doesn't stop the model wanting the file. The mission was mis-scoped, and that was knowable **before the first turn** from the instruction and the filesystem alone.

## Change

The run now says so — into the executor prompt and the console: which named files are out of reach, where they actually are, that `../` is refused, and explicitly **not to create a same-named substitute** inside the root, since that's the failure this exists to prevent.

## Deliberately advisory, and quiet by default

It rides the executor prompt, so a false positive is a false instruction. It reports only paths **absent under the project root and present above it** — the one combination "the model will create it" cannot explain. Ignored: paths absent everywhere (that's just authoring), a project root that *is* the repo root (nothing above), and a search root that isn't an ancestor.

Replayed against the real mission — fires with the tree as it stood at launch, silent with the tree as it is now (the stub having since been created).

## Mutation testing earned its keep

Six mutants, and **three survived the first pass**: the "absent here" check, the ancestor guard, and the source-extension allow-list were all unverified, because each test had a *second* reason to pass. Strengthening those three — file present in **both** roots, the unrelated root actually containing the file, and a token with slashes and a non-source extension (`github.com/org/repo.git`) — kills all six.

Suite: 367 files, 4095 pass.

author: go-to-k
body:
Closes #1388
Closes #1424

## Summary

The CFn `AWS::S3::Bucket` lifecycle `Rule` has **no `Filter` member at all** —
every scope component and several actions sit at the rule level, and the schema
still accepts legacy singular action forms next to the modern plural ones.
`applyLifecycleConfiguration` read a subset. Enumerating all **16** `Rule`
members (from `aws-cdk-lib`'s generated `CfnBucket.RuleProperty`) against what
the provider actually reads found **6 defects**, not the 3 #1388 reported — and
the two worst are on the CURRENT CDK L2 path, not the legacy one the issue
describes.

### The severe one: rule-level `TagFilters` (#1424)

`gatherScope` had rule-level fallbacks for `Prefix`, `ObjectSizeGreaterThan`
and `ObjectSizeLessThan` — but for tags it read only `Filter.TagFilters`:

```ts
prefix: (filter?.['Prefix'] ?? rule['Prefix']),
tagFilters: filter?.['TagFilters'],            // <- no `?? rule['TagFilters']`
```

An omission in an otherwise-consistent pattern (`Filter` is cdkd's own
accommodation for SDK-shaped / imported input).

A real `cdk synth` (aws-cdk-lib 2.244.0) of
`lifecycleRules: [{ tagFilters: { env: 'prod', team: 'core' }, expiration: Duration.days(30) }]`
emits `TagFilters` at the rule level. cdkd gathered no scope for that rule, so
it fell through to the catch-all `Filter: { Prefix: '' }` — **a 30-day
expiration sent against every object in the bucket** instead of the tagged
subset. Lifecycle expiration deletes objects, and cdkd reported success. This
is the CURRENT CDK L2 path, so the impact is not limited to the legacy /
hand-written templates #1388 describes.

**Fixing the gather alone would have introduced a second silent drop.** The
single-component branch was `Filter: { Tag: tagFilters[0] }`, and the SDK's
`Tag` member holds exactly one tag; multi-tag rules now take
`And: { Tags: [...] }`. That branch was unreachable before this PR precisely
because tags were never gathered, so it had to land in the same change.

### Rule-level `ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker` (#1424)

`expiredObjectDeleteMarker: true` synthesizes to the rule level, but the
provider only read it from a nested `Expiration` object. A rule whose only
action is the delete-marker cleanup produced no `Expiration` at all, and S3
rejects the action-less rule. Now fills an otherwise-empty `Expiration`, and
deliberately does not override an explicit `Days` / `Date` (S3 forbids
combining them).

### The plural path was broken too: `TransitionInDays`

Found while extending the integ fixture. CFn spells the noncurrent transition
day count **`TransitionInDays`** on both the singular and the plural
`NoncurrentVersionTransitions[]`; the SDK member is `NoncurrentDays`. The
provider read only the SDK spelling:

```ts
NoncurrentDays: nvt['NoncurrentDays'] as number | undefined,   // always undefined
```

So **every** CDK `noncurrentVersionTransitions` reached AWS with no schedule.
Its sibling `Transitions` already did `TransitionInDays ?? Days`; this makes the
pair consistent. Confirmed in `aws-cdk-lib`'s
`NoncurrentVersionTransitionProperty`, in the SDK model, and in a real synth.

### The legacy singular forms (#1388, as filed)

`Transition`, `NoncurrentVersionTransition`, and the scalar
`NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays`. Singular and plural are **concatenated**
rather than treated as alternatives, since the schema permits both on one rule;
for the expiration pair the modern object wins over the legacy scalar.

### Full 16-member comparison

| CFn `Rule` member | read before |
| --- | --- |
| `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` | yes |
| `ExpirationDate` / `ExpirationInDays` | yes |
| `ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker` | **no** (#1424) |
| `Id` / `Status` / `Prefix` | yes |
| `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` | yes |
| `NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays` | **no** (#1388) |
| `NoncurrentVersionTransition` | **no** (#1388) |
| `NoncurrentVersionTransitions` | name yes, **day field no** (`TransitionInDays`) |
| `ObjectSizeGreaterThan` / `ObjectSizeLessThan` | yes |
| `TagFilters` | **no** (#1424) |
| `Transition` | **no** (#1388) |
| `Transitions` | yes |

## Test plan

`tests/unit/provisioning/s3-bucket-provider-lifecycle-rule-keys.test.ts` — 14
cases. The fixtures are copied verbatim from the real `cdk synth` output above
rather than hand-authored, so they pin the shape CDK actually emits (no
`Filter` wrapper anywhere).

Coverage: multi-tag `And.Tags` scoping and the explicit assertion that the
catch-all `Filter: { Prefix: '' }` is NOT what we send; every tag preserved;
single-tag `Tag` form; tags combined with a prefix; delete-marker rule not
action-less; delete-marker not overriding explicit `Days`; each legacy singular
form; singular+plural concatenation; modern object beating the legacy scalar;
plus two no-regression cases (prefix-only stays V1 with a bare top-level
`Prefix`; an explicit `Filter.TagFilters` still works for imported input).

Plus the two `NoncurrentVersionTransitions` cases: the CFn `TransitionInDays`
spelling a real synth emits, and the SDK `NoncurrentDays` spelling that must
keep working for imported input.

**Revert-proof**: restoring `s3-bucket-provider.ts` from `origin/main` fails
exactly **9 of the 14**. The 5 that still pass are the two no-regression cases,
the two "already worked" cases, and the SDK-spelling fallback — the expected
split. The restore was verified byte-identical to the commit afterwards.

Full local gate: typecheck, lint, build, 522 files / 8919 tests,
`vp run gen:all-matrices` clean (the fixture change regenerated
`integ-coverage`, included here).

## Real-AWS verification

`s3-lifecycle` extended and run end to end (`PASS`, 58s, 2 deleted / 0 errors /
0 orphans). The fixture gained the tag-scoped rule, a plural noncurrent
transition, and an **L1 `CfnBucket`** carrying the legacy singular forms plus a
rule-level `ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker` — shapes the L2 construct cannot emit.
`verify.sh` asserts each against a real
`get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` readback (tags sorted, since AWS does not
preserve list order):

```
tag-scoped rule: both tags applied via Filter.And.Tags, no whole-bucket fallback
noncurrent-version transition schedule reached AWS (NoncurrentDays=15)
legacy singular Transition + NoncurrentVersionTransition
  + NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays + rule-level ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker all applied
```

The first run **failed**, and the failure is the strongest evidence in this PR:

```
'NoncurrentDays' in the NoncurrentVersionExpiration action must be greater than
'NoncurrentDays' in the NoncurrentVersionTransition action
```

AWS could only say that once the day count actually reached it — the pre-fix
binary sent nothing there to compare. The fixture's values were genuinely
invalid and were corrected.

Also hardens the post-destroy bucket probe with a bounded retry: S3 propagates
`DeleteBucket` to `HeadBucket` asynchronously and a single probe raced it
(both buckets were in fact gone). A bucket that never disappears still FAILs,
so leak detection is unchanged.

## Review fix-backs

A 3-axis review ran on the first version. No blockers; every finding is
addressed here, and the integ was re-run afterwards (PASS, 2 deleted / 0 errors
/ 0 orphans). Independently confirmed by the reviewers: the 16-member
enumeration is complete (no 7th gap), the unit fixtures match a real synth
byte-for-byte, and the 9-of-14 revert-proof split holds.

- **Plural transitions now WIN over the legacy singular** instead of being
  concatenated. Concatenating can emit two transitions with the same
  `StorageClass`, which S3 rejects (`Found two transitions with the same storage
  class`), failing the whole `PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration` — a regression,
  since pre-fix such a template deployed with the singular simply ignored. It
  also now matches the `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` policy chosen 30 lines
  above.
- **`ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker` gates on Days/Date, not on `Expiration` existing.**
  The nested branch emits an all-undefined object for

This pull request introduces several important updates to the development workflow and backend schema to improve reliability and ensure compatibility between the embedding model and the database schema. The most significant changes include resizing the embedding vector dimensions in the database, adding robust scripts for starting and stopping the development stack, and minor configuration adjustments for smoother local development.

**Embedding dimension and database schema alignment:**
- Changed the embedding vector dimension from 1024 to 768 in both the code (`EMBEDDING_DIM` in `backend/app/models.py`) and the database schema via a new Alembic migration. This ensures compatibility with the `jina-embeddings-v5-nano` model, which only supports 768 dimensions. The migration also handles index recreation and data consistency. body:
## Outcome

Adds the pure R01 runtime-closure authority vocabulary. `PersonalWorkerRuntimeReadiness` is equality-only and cannot be serialized or deserialized. Its public summary exposes only the admitted Ubuntu 24.04 architecture and fixed non-downgradable execution policies. The private canonical identity binds one opaque producer-owned bundle containing installation identity, runtime and image-store generations, platform, architecture, and exactly 40 required evidence classes.

The bundle has no public constructor, fields, accessors, `Clone`, `Debug`, serialization, or deserialization. Callers therefore cannot pair valid host evidence with invented generations or another installation. The sealer rejects invalid generations and any missing, duplicate, extra, or oversized evidence bundle before identity publication; evidence order is canonical and the identity encoding has an exact golden vector.

## Security impact

Pure Rust only. No filesystem, process, Podman, Git, systemd, mount, clock, persistence, CLI, listener, credential, Lima, or host-mutation authority is added. No production evidence producer exists yet, so this PR does not claim R01 readiness or authorize repository execution. A later Linux-only observer and separately journaled installer/smoke must earn the opaque bundle.

The closed policy includes exact offline image identity, read-only root/exact source, fresh byte+inode-bounded target and temporary filesystems, verified read-only non-authoritative dependency cache, denied network, absent credentials, empty allowlisted environment, rootless/drop-all/no-new-privileges, private namespaces, dedicated cgroup-v2 with group-empty proof, forbidden detached processes, bounded output, and a non-resetting plan deadline.

CodeDriver is unavailable and was not contacted.

- `cargo test --locked personal_worker_runtime_contract --lib`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
