author: rbutera
body:
Closes part of #109 (the per-line controls half; the roll-up + staging reshape stays gated on the holistic design pass, see flags below).

## What this does

The collation draft canvas already collated dispositions and derived a verdict, but the only per-line control was a plain `<select>` type dropdown. This makes the per-line verdict a **real, iconographic control** and makes the roll-up **visible while you work**.

### Per-line verdict controls (the #109 title: approve / request changes / comment / question on any line)
- Each collated item now carries the four verdict buttons as real icon controls, not a dropdown: **approve = check**, **request-change = warning triangle**, **comment = bubble**, **question = help-circle** (the #133 icon set), on the #133 glass palette.
- The current verdict reads as **pressed** (`is-active` + `aria-pressed`), coloured by type (approve green / request-change amber / comment+question private-blue), so a line's verdict is legible at a glance.
- Setting a line's verdict calls `retypeItem` on the draft, exactly as the old select did. So it is a **real round-trip into the draft**, not a cosmetic toggle: the collated draft, the outbound payload, the derived verdict, and the sign all reflect the choice.

### Live verdict roll-up readout
- A readout on the canvas shows the verdict the current per-line choices derive, from the **same `deriveReviewEvent` the sign wire posts** ("what you see is what leaves", R33). Any `request-change` line escalates the whole review to **REQUEST CHANGES** (#109: ">= 1 request-changes block => the WHOLE PR review becomes request changes"), so the per-line -> final-review connection is visible before the sign, per mode (own-branch phrasing vs other-pr phrasing).

### How it feeds collate -> draft -> verdict
`DispositionBar(active, onDisposition)` -> `retypeItem(draft, id, type)` -> `onChange`/`setDraft` (the host state) -> `collationItems`/`reviewComments(draft)` -> `deriveReviewEvent` (the verdict the paper shows and the sign wire posts) and `publishTarget`/`publishTargetPayload` (the outbound bytes). Unchanged pipeline; the controls just author into it honestly.

## Design nuances flagged for Rai (implemented sensible default, did NOT unilaterally reshape)

These three are the parts #109 explicitly reserves for the holistic design pass + a Contracts ruling. I built the visible, low-blast-radius half and left the reshapes for your call rather than changing the publish engine / staging semantics unilaterally:

1. **approve should NOT publish (it is a personal "viewed" marker).** Today `deriveReviewEvent` still returns `APPROVE` when a review is approve-only, and it is a pin-tested twin of core's `deriveReviewEvent` (`packages/ui/src/canvas/publish.ts` + `packages/core/src/publish-review.ts`). Correcting it (approve never rolls up; approve items excluded from the published review) reshapes #22's roll-up, R36-R40, and core's engine (real-egress territory), so I left it and the readout honestly shows current behaviour. **This is the roll-up correction #109 wants your ruling on.**
2. **staged-vs-talk-to-orchestrator split for comment/question.** #109 says comment/question mostly go to the current local orchestrator, not staged. Today everything stages. Not represented yet; left as-is.
3. **anchored per-block threads (#36 "talk to any block").** The canvas has the honest orchestrator-on-tap seam note; the real anchored thread per disposition is still a follow-up.

## Checks
- `npx nx run rennet-ui:typecheck --skip-nx-cache`: green.
- `npx nx run rennet-ui:test`: 277 passed (added: verdict-button retypes the item; current button reads pressed; setting one line to request-change flips the whole review's derived verdict to REQUEST_CHANGES and the readout shows it).
- Screenshot of the controls + roll-up in action rendered from the real component: `~/navi/workspace/media/rennet-review-controls/per-line-controls.png`.

## Heads-up: pre-existing `rennet-ui:lint` red on origin/main (NOT from this PR)
Verified by stashing this branch and linting pristine origin/main. Two pre-existing failures, neither in this diff:
- `app.tsx:755` -> the #133 `no-restricted-syntax` hex-lint rule reads `#123` inside the placeholder string `"owner/repo#123 ..."` as a 3-digit hex colour (false positive). Also `app.tsx` fails `assist/source/organizeImports`.
- `decisions.tsx` -> a biome `format` diff.

I did not touch those files to keep this PR scoped; worth a quick follow-up (change the placeholder example number, run `biome format --write`).

author: awdawmip
body:
## A3 L1 owner generation — sparse relation lattice

This is a fresh A3 mother-theorem generation created because canonical governance marks `core/a3-relation-state-v2` as fully absorbed/provenance and explicitly instructs new A3 work to start from then-current main.

The result was discovered while auditing E001 contact/momentum specializations, but **no E001/contact physics is imported here**.

## Canonical object

For positive integer capacities `m_i` and integer state totals `p_i`, canonical A3 pair relations are

`Z_ij = m_j*p_i - m_i*p_j`.

For any oriented spanning tree `T`, keep exactly the `N-1` tree-edge relations and the grand total

`P = sum_i p_i`.

The integer coordinate map

`p -> (P, (Z_e)_{e in T})`

has exact image-lattice index

`I_T = (sum_i m_i) * product_i m_i^(deg_T(i)-1)`.

## Proof structure

Write `p=Mq`, `M=diag(m_i)`, and let `B` be an oriented tree incidence matrix. Each edge relation is `m_u*m_v*(q_u-q_v)` up to orientation sign. Therefore, after multiplying the coordinate matrix by `M`, factor `m_u*m_v` from each relation row; the remaining matrix is `[m^T; B^T]`.

Every maximal cofactor of a tree incidence matrix is `±1` with the common orientation sign, so expansion along `m^T` has absolute determinant `sum_i m_i`. Dividing by `det M=product_i m_i` yields the index formula.

The regression suite independently computes exact integer determinants by Bareiss elimination on every labelled tree through five vertices for several capacity families.

## Canonical relation quantum / translation period factorization

Let

`g=gcd_i(m_i)`,
`a_i=m_i/g`,
`tau=sum_i a_i=(sum_i m_i)/g`.

Every tree relation is divisible by canonical A3 relation quantum `g`. After normalizing to primitive relations `z_e=Z_e/g`, the exact index becomes

`I_T^prim = tau * product_i a_i^(deg_T(i)-1)`.

Thus the canonical A3 translation period `tau` is the unavoidable global integer-lattice factor after all local relation quanta are removed; tree topology contributes only the primitive-capacity degree factor.

## Basis-choice theorem

For `N>=2`, every tree has `deg_i>=1` and `sum_i(deg_i-1)=N-2`. Therefore over all spanning trees on the complete vertex set:

`I_min = (sum_i m_i)*(min_i m_i)^(N-2)`,

`I_max = (sum_i m_i)*(max_i m_i)^(N-2)`,

attained by stars centered at minimum- and maximum-capacity vertices respectively. Primitive indices satisfy the identical statement with `tau` and `a_i`.

This gives an exact integer-lattice meaning to a precision-friendly sparse relation basis: all trees have the same rational rank, but topology changes the congruence density of legal integer coordinates.

## Unit-primitive star corollary

If some primitive capacity `a_c=1` and a star is centered at `c`, orient every edge `c->i`. Then

`z_ci = a_i*p_c - p_i`,

so

`p_c = (P + sum_i z_ci)/tau`.

Hence arbitrary integer sparse coordinates are legal exactly when the numerator is divisible by `tau`; all totals then reconstruct by integer formulas. In this optimal case the entire legality burden collapses to one global congruence modulo the canonical translation period.

## Boundaries / ownership

- this is A3 integer relation-state/lattice mathematics, not E001 material/contact semantics;
- no novelty claim is made relative to standard incidence, Smith-normal-form, or matrix-tree lattice theory;
- prior-art audit is required before any novelty language;
- the current code is an exact executable theorem companion/regression, not a substitute for a future Lean proof;
- relation orientation changes signs only and does not affect the lattice index.

## Validation targets

- exact determinant equality on every labelled tree through `N=5` for multiple capacity families;
- exact removal of `g^(N-1)` under primitive relation normalization;
- min/max star bounds equal brute-force tree enumeration;
- unit-primitive star reconstruction and one mod-`tau` legality condition;
- orientation invariance and single-vertex identity boundary.

author: lequangbui
body:
Three defects that are visibly wrong in production today, all caused by unlayered component stylesheets overriding each other purely by bundle emit order. No page layouts are converted — that is the next phase.

## What was actually broken

**Every product card was wearing the detail page's price panel.** `ProductDetail.css` is emitted last, so its `.product-price` beat `ProductList.css` and `Bookmarks.css`. Three `.product-price` rules shipped in the live bundle and the wrong one won:

```
.product-price{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:2px}      <- ProductList (authored)
.product-price{color:var(--success);font-weight:700}            <- Bookmarks
.product-price{padding:24px;background:var(--bg-tertiary);      <- ProductDetail  WINS
              border-radius:16px;border:1px solid var(--border)}
```

Cards on `/`, `/browse` and `/bookmarks` rendered a 24px-padded bordered panel nobody designed. `ProductDetail.jsx` uses none of those classes — the rules were dead in their own page and existed only to corrupt others. Same story for `.no-image` (a 320px min-height on cards) and `.product-info`.

**`/alerts` had no pagination CSS at all.** It rendered `<Pagination>` and was styled entirely by leakage from Home and Bookmarks, neither of which it imports. Meanwhile Bookmarks' `border: none` was stripping Home's oxblood border from pagination on *every* page.

**`.btn` was 38.8px and `.retry-btn` 36.4px**, both under the 44px floor, both reused across most of the app.

## What changed

- `Pagination` is now self-contained — the class had to leave the markup in the same commit that deleted both CSS blocks, since unlayered CSS beats utilities and there is no working intermediate state.
- The four dead `ProductDetail.css` rules are gone; `.product-panel*`, `.product-sku` and `.error-message` are untouched and `/products/:id` is unchanged.
- `.btn`/`.retry-btn` raised to 44px; `--success`/`--success-dark` bridged into `@theme`.

## The guards are the point

A new `collision.guard.test.js` keys each class to its **exact permitted owner set**, so adding a class to a third file — or re-adding it to one it was removed from — fails the build even though the name is allowlisted. The first version keyed by name alone and a review proved the exact deleted rule could be restored verbatim with CI still green.

`tokens.guard` also could not see hoisted class strings (`const BUTTON = [...]`), which is now the reference pattern for self-contained primitives; it scans whole file text.

Every guard was proven by mutation rather than assumed: verbatim re-add, descendant selector, pseudo-class, a brand-new two-file collision, a shrunk owner set, and a hex hidden in a hoisted constant — all now red, clean tree green.

## Verification

77 tests, up from 64 at the start of the responsive work. The backend does not run locally, so visual proof came from rendering the real `ProductList.jsx` markup against genuine before/after production bundles — the padded price panel disappearing is directly visible.

Six collisions remain, deliberately allowlisted and enforced. They are scoped in `price-stalker-guide/design-docs/2026-08-08-responsive-phase-2-carry-forward.md` along with `/alerts`' error box, which is still leakage-styled from `UserProfile.css` — the same bug class, one page over.

author: nimrodavni78
body:
## Summary

Three semconv enum attributes had an `unknown` fallback that is not a member of the enum they
belong to. OBI's registry deliberately leaves `unknown` undeclared, so any signal carrying it
fails live-check with `undefined_enum_variant`.

None of the three fallbacks is reachable. Rather than declare a value OBI cannot legitimately
send, this removes the fallbacks so the code matches the contract the schema already states.

## What changes

**`db.system.name` and `messaging.system` now omit the attribute.** The metrics recorder routes
only database span types to `db.client.operation.duration`, and only Kafka/MQTT/NATS/AMQP to the
messaging metrics, so a span the getter cannot classify never reaches them. The two HTTP-client
sub-cases satisfy the getter's guards by construction: the Elasticsearch path sets `SubType` and
the `Elasticsearch` payload together, and the SQL++ path always resolves `DBSystem` to either
`couchbase` or `other_sql`. Both getters now return an invalid `KeyValue` — the same omit idiom
already used a few lines up for `error.type`, `gen_ai.operation.name` and `gen_ai.provider.name`,
dropped by the expirer and mapped to an empty label by the Prometheus getter.

**`telemetry.sdk.language` gets a real default instead.** Here `"unknown"` is load-bearing, just
not for telemetry: `InstrumentableUnknown` is the zero value of `ProcessAttrs.detectedType`, and
the selection-criteria matcher compares `languages:` against `String()`, so a process on an
ignored system path correctly matches nothing. Telemetry reads a different field —
`svc.Attrs.SDKLanguage`, only ever assigned from `FindProcLanguage`, which returns `generic`
rather than `unknown` when it recognizes no runtime. Its single construction site in the typer
just left the field at its zero value. It now initializes to `InstrumentableGeneric`, so the
export path cannot observe the un-classified state. `String()` is untouched, and discovery
behaves exactly as before.

`generic` stays exported. It is a classification — "this process carries no SDK" — not the absence
of one, and it is the extra resource attribute `traces_target_info` needs for the service to
appear in the services list.

**Schema.** The `db` and `telemetry` override groups described `unknown` as a bug marker left
undeclared so weaver keeps flagging it. That sentence no longer holds and is dropped. No members
change.

## Not covered

Two other enum attributes emit `unknown` on paths that *are* reachable, and each needs a contract
decision rather than a deletion:

- `jvm.memory.type` — `InferJVMMemoryType` falls back to `"unknown"` for pool names outside its
  substring lists (OpenJ9's `nursery-allocate`, `class storage`, `JIT code cache`; legacy
  `Perm Gen`), while semconv declares only `heap` and `non_heap`.
- `network.type` — any EtherType other than IPv4/IPv6/ARP stringifies to `"unknown"`, and the
  registry declares exactly those three.

Both want either a better classifier, an omitted attribute, or a declared member.

## Validation

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] If this enhances / fixes / changes a core feature, I have updated the [features documentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/blob/main/devdocs/features.md) and [support matrix](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/blob/main/SUPPORT_MATRIX.md) as needed.

author: amaadmartin
body:
Please ensure you have read the contribution guide before creating a pull request.

### Link to Issue or Description of Change

1. Link to an existing issue (if applicable):

2. Or, if no issue exists, describe the change:

**Problem**: The two long-running-operation loops in `AgentEngineSandboxCodeExecutor` sleep 1000 ms **before** their first status poll. `createInternal` returns a pending operation, so the loop is always taken and the executor cannot see a finished operation for a full second. An executor built with neither `agentEngineResourceName` nor `sandboxResourceName` runs both loops, so the first `executeCode` pays a minimum of 2000 ms of dead time.

**Solution**: Sleep between polls instead of before them. Each loop now delays only when `attempts > 0`, so the first poll fires immediately and the poll that observes `done` returns with no timer pending. The interval moves into a module-level `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` constant.

The bound is unchanged: `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (180) still counts status polls, and both timeout error strings are byte-identical. As a direct consequence each loop now performs 180 polls separated by 179 sleeps instead of 180, so the worst-case wall clock before a timeout is one interval shorter per loop. That is the intended meaning of "sleep between polls".

I considered extracting one shared poll helper for the two loops and did not. The two responses come from different SDK methods with different declared types, so a generic helper needs a type parameter and a `done`-bearing constraint; getting that wrong is how `any` or `as never` enters the diff. The in-place edit changes no types at all.

The same defect exists in `core/src/sessions/vertex_ai_session_service.ts` and `dev/src/cli/deploy/cli_deploy_agent_engine.ts`. Those are a separate change and this PR does not touch them.

Collision check: I listed all 400 open PRs on the fork and scanned every one for a diff touching `agent_engine_sandbox_code_executor.ts`. Five touch either file (#497, #514, #565, #678, #806) and none changes a poll loop; their hunks are disjoint from mine. #777 fixes the _trailing_ sleep in the two sibling files and states the code-executor loops are out of its scope. So this branches from `main`.

### Testing Plan

Please describe the tests that you ran to verify your changes. This is required for all PRs that are not small documentation or typo fixes.

Unit Tests:
[x] I have added or updated unit tests for my change.
[x] All unit tests pass locally.

Three new tests in `core/test/code_executors/agent_engine_sandbox_code_executor_test.ts`, 26 tests before and 29 after. No existing test was edited, skipped, weakened or deleted; the only changed line is the `vitest` import, which now also imports `afterEach` for a shared `vi.useRealTimers()` hook.

- Test 1 makes both create calls return a pending operation and leaves both operation getters at their `done: true` defaults. It drains microtasks with `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)` and asserts `vi.getTimerCount() === 0`, then that `executeCode` resolves after one poll per loop.
- Tests 2 and 3 hold one loop's operation at `done: false` and step the fake clock. Each asserts the first poll lands at 0 ms, no second poll at `POLL_INTERVAL_MS - 1`, a second poll at `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, and exactly 180 polls before the unchanged timeout error.

Commands run on the pushed commit:

```
npx vitest run --project unit:core core/test/code_executors/agent_engine_sandbox_code_executor_test.ts   # 29 passed
npm run build          # exit 0
npm run lint           # exit 0
npm run format:check   # exit 0
```

`npm run ts:check` reports `Found 287 errors in 42 files` both on this branch and with the two files restored from `main`. Neither changed file appears in that list, so this change adds no type error.

Coverage of the changed file is 99.64% statements and 98.57% branches. Both sides of both new `attempts > 0` guards are exercised, so the new lines and new branches are at 100%. The one uncovered line is 84, the `default:` throw of the unsupported-language switch, which is untouched by this change and uncovered on `main` as well.

Mutation testing. Each mutation was applied, the suite was re-run, and the source was restored:

author: philippe-tressard
body:
`export-hors-site.sh` s'arrêtait sur « sudo: a password is required ». Le volume de
sauvegarde appartient à root, et `ptressard` ne dispose de `sudo` sans mot de passe
que sur **rpi1**. Le rôle alternant chaque nuit, la copie ne fonctionnait qu'une nuit
sur deux. Les deux nœuds ne sont pas configurés à l'identique — même classe que les
crontabs divergents du 06/08. Le contrôle d'âge l'aurait signalé le 13/08 ; c'est
l'utilisateur qui l'a vu avant.

### Pourquoi un script dédié plutôt qu'une règle sur `cat`
`NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/cat` donnerait la lecture de **n'importe quel fichier en root**.
`export-source.sh` n'expose que trois verbes (`liste`, `sha`, `flux`), détermine le
volume lui-même, et n'accepte qu'un **nom** d'archive validé en liste blanche ancrée
— jamais un chemin. Neuf cas de rejet verrouillés par `--selftest` (chemin absolu,
remontée de répertoire, substitution de commande…).

### Pourquoi /usr/local/sbin et non /opt/5hostachy
`/opt/5hostachy` appartient à `ptressard` et `auto-deploy` y réécrit tout. Une règle
`NOPASSWD` visant un fichier que l'appelant peut réécrire n'est pas une permission
restreinte : c'est un accès root complet.

### Diagnostic plutôt que blocage
`sudo -n` partout — sur un canal SSH non interactif, `sudo` nu attend un mot de passe
qui ne viendra jamais. Et le script établit d'abord qu'il a **pu regarder** avant de
conclure d'une liste vide (socle 04 §1). Trois causes distinguées et nommées : script
absent, sudo indisponible, listage impossible.

💡 What: Switched to `rename_into` inside the `Query::Rename` execution block.
🎯 Why: `Query` execution naturally owns its intermediate `relation` results. Using the `rename` method created a redundant clone of the relation and its tuples, whereas `rename_into` consumes the owned relation and modifies tuples in-place.
📊 Impact: Eliminates a redundant collection allocation and tuple cloning step per query rename execution, saving time and memory on the heap.
🔬 Measurement: Run `cargo bench --bench database` and observe the allocation and time performance of query execution.

author: miguel-heygen
body:
## What

Dragging a group no longer makes one member snap back to its starting position for a frame, and the whole group is saved in one request instead of one per member.

## Why

Each member of a group was written separately, and every write patched the live GSAP tween in place and then seeked the player. A seek re-renders the whole timeline, not the tween that changed, so members still queued behind that write got repainted from their un-patched tweens — back to their pre-drag position, where they sat until their own write landed. Only members whose tween renders at the playhead showed it, which is why a group of three flashed one element and left the others still.

Separately, a three-element drag cost 3 writes and 9 parse reads, each write re-reading and re-serializing the whole composition.

## How

The group commit defers the seek for every member but the last, so queued members keep the transform the gesture left on them and the group repaints once from the fully patched timeline. Mutations are queued and sent as one batch write; anything that re-reads the file flushes the queue first, so a member resolving a shared or stale tween never reads a composition missing writes it is about to build on. The parse endpoint shares an in-flight request per file.

## Test plan

- Measured in a real browser before and after: 9 reads and 3 writes became 2 reads and 1 write for a three-element drag
- The jump reproduced in 3 of 3 runs before the fix and 0 of 3 after; reverting the one-line change brings it back

---

author: cpmadrid
body:
Closes #241

## Summary

`cron-relay-drift-check` sat red 2026-07-27 → 2026-08-03 with no signal after the
first hour. The Sentry rule behind it fires on `First seen` OR `Regression`, so a
weekly cron alerts once and then goes quiet — **day 6 of an outage renders
identically to day 1**. The Slack half of this work is merged in `platform`
(#602, #603); this is the **ambient** half: while the cockpit is open, a red
monitor is simply visible, with how long it has been broken.

A new quarter-width **Sentry Crons** panel on the Tauri cockpit, reading
`GET /api/0/organizations/{org}/monitors/` through the existing `SentryClient` and
the operator-entered `org:read` token — no new credential, no new dependency.

**The age rule is the whole panel.** It is measured from
`activeIncident.startingTimestamp`, **never** from `lastCheckIn`: a job that runs
on schedule and keeps failing checks in constantly, so measuring from the last
attempt reproduces the exact bug this exists to remove. On the monitor that
motivated it the two read **7d 22h** and **0d 22h**. So `CronAge` is an enum
rather than a `u64` — the check-in figure is a *separate variant*, reachable only
when there is no incident, and it renders as the weaker claim it is (`≈`, amber,
and a detail line naming the fallback). `lastCheckIn: null` with no incident is
words, not a duration; an unreadable timestamp is the em dash and does **not**
borrow the other field.

**Three wire traps**, each with a test, all traceable to fixtures built from the
Sentry **MCP server's** normalised output rather than the raw REST payload:

| the mistake | the truth |
|---|---|
| `projectSlug` | nested at `project.slug` — the flat field does not exist (the Slack half rendered `undefined/prd`) |
| `hasMoreEnvironments` | does not exist, and there is no environment-truncation signal of any kind — so no guard here pretends otherwise |
| `activeIncident` present ⇒ failing | it is a key on **every** environment and is `null` on the healthy ones |

**Blind reads are red, never empty-and-green.** No monitors at all, or a monitor
carrying no environments, paints a warning — with the rows that *were* read still
on screen under it — and the trailing label says `couldn't read` rather than
`all ok`. Configuration follows `panel::Configured`, with `Present` recorded when
the credential is read and **before** the request, so the first frame is a loading
line rather than a setup instruction on a machine whose token is fine.

There is deliberately **no** "suspiciously few monitors" guard: the wire carries
no expected count, so a threshold shipped in the binary would be a number nobody
set, warning a fresh org about a list that is simply short.

## Changes

**`crates/usage/src/sentry.rs`** — `SentryClient::cron_monitors()` (org-wide, no
project filter) and `cron_monitor_status()`, the wire structs, and the pure
`summarize_monitors()` fold beside the existing `summarize()`:

- `CronAge` — `Incident` / `SinceLastCheckIn` / `NeverCheckedIn` / `Unreadable`,
  so provenance is structural rather than documented.
- `CronSuppression` — `status == "disabled"` or `isMuted == true` (**strict**
  `true`; missing, `false`, `1` and `"true"` all stay red) at **either** monitor
  or environment level. Suppressed entries are counted and shown with their
  reason, never dropped. `isMuted` decodes as a `Value` so an odd payload cannot
  fail the whole read.
- `CronMonitorsSummary` — `NoMonitors` carries no counts to mistake for health;
  `Measured` cannot exist without a monitor. `blind_read()` names the two
  untrustworthy readings.
- Rows sort oldest-first, with never-checked-in and unreadable-age leading, ties
  broken on the row id so the order is stable across polls.
- Monitor-level pagination is walked via the `Link` header (only a
  `results="true"` next relation means there is more — Sentry emits `next` on the
  last page too), and a list past ten pages is a **failure**, because a partial
  list of monitors reads as "the ones that are missing are fine".

**`app/src-tauri/src/crons.rs`** (new) — the view side: `CronsState` with the
`Configured` ladder, the `Xd Yh` age format (matching the Slack digest verbatim,
`0d` included), the row/detail/title strings, the message ladder
(loading → setup → failure → blind read → measured all-clear), and five dumpable
fixtures whose **wire** objects run through the real classifier so the dumped ages
are the code's output, not strings typed into a fixture.

**`app/src-tauri/src/main.rs`** — `crons` command, `crons_loop` + `poll_crons` on
`usage::PROVIDER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS` (one constant, shared with the other Sentry
read) with a 60s first-read retry, `crons`/`crons_wake` on `App`,
`generate_handler!` registration, `--dump-crons` (`--empty` / `--error` /
`--blind` / `--unconfigured`). Saving or clearing the Sentry token — and editing
the org slug — now wakes **both** loops: one credential, two panels.

**`crates/viewmodel/src/cockpit.rs`** — `PanelKind::SentryCrons`
(id `sentryCrons`, title `Sentry Crons`, `min_width` 240.0), `ALL` and
`DEFAULT_ORDER` to 9, and **Azure Cost from `ThreeQuarters` to `Half`**. That
trade is measured, not estimated: Azure Cost's body splits at
`2 × 400 + 16 = 816pt`, which a Half clears down to a 1648pt cockpit where a
ThreeQuarters cleared it from 1094 — both boundaries are pinned by a new test so a
future span change has to look at them. The last two rows are now the same shape
(Half + Quarter + Quarter), which also puts their gridlines on top of each other.

**`app/ui/`** — `cronsPanel` section, `cronmonitors.js` (its own IIFE),
`.cron-*` styles, and the `PANEL_SECTIONS` entry. Rust decides every string and
colour; the JS cannot tell an incident-derived age from a check-in-derived one and
does not try.

**Docs** — `app/README.md` gains a `crons` command section (payload shape, the age
rule, the three traps, the blind-read ladder, the cadence) and a smoke-checklist
line; `CLAUDE.md` gains the panel, the module map entries, the credential note and
the Azure Cost trade.

## Testing

`./dev test` and `./dev lint` both pass locally.

- **`cargo test --locked --workspace`** — all green. New coverage:
  - **The age regression test uses a fixture whose `lastCheckIn` and
    `activeIncident.startingTimestamp` are a week apart**, so it cannot pass under
    the wrong formula — and it asserts the two figures are *not* equal, because the
    sibling implementation's original test used equal values and proved nothing.
  - `wiremock`: a live-shaped **healthy** payload end to end, the request shape
    (path, bearer header, **no** project filter), a blank slug making no request at
    all, a 403 auth failure carrying the token prompt, a malformed payload, a
    two-page list walked to the end, an endless list failing rather than answering
    partially, and the token never reaching the URL.
  - Folding: the failing environment, the check-in fallback, `lastCheckIn: null`,
    an unreadable incident start, a future timestamp, suppression at both levels
    across four truthiness variants, the monitor reason outranking the
    environment's, an absent `status` not passing for healthy, the sort order and
    its tie-break, both blind reads, and the wire-shape test that asserts the
    fixture's key list *is* the live API's and that `projectSlug` /
    `hasMoreEnvironments` are absent — plus a test that a payload carrying them
    anyway changes nothing, since the honest assertion is indifference.
  - `crons.rs`: the four-state message ladder including the first frame (`Unknown`
    must never paint the `Absent` instruction), the footer being the last
    **success** and not the last attempt, an unreadable keychain degrading rather
    than unconfiguring, a cleared token dropping its retained rows, and every
    fixture carrying the whole payload shape.
- **`tests/frontend` Playwright (140 tests)** — new `crons.spec.js` (12) covers the
  populated, healthy-empty, blind and error fixtures: `7d 22h` and *not

author: barbs2989
body:
Audit of the Climbs tab — the one surface backed by the live catalog rather
than seed data, so it has failure shapes the Crew/Logbook/Profile audits
structurally could not reach. Walked the area tree to leaf depth, a route
list, an enriched alpine route across all six sub-tabs, and a bare
bouldering route.

Three fixes:

- The GETTING THERE row labelled "Trailhead" rendered
  `road.driveNote || road.name`. driveNote is a note about the drive, so the
  label misdescribed it AND the fallback meant the actual road name never
  showed. 1,023 of the 1,050 routes carrying road data have both fields, so
  the road name reached a screen on ~23 routes. Cockscomb Ridge read
  "Trailhead: Adds about 9 miles and 2,000 ft round trip beyond the washout"
  while "Glacier Creek Road (FR 39) to Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead" sat
  unrendered — and that name is what makes the road-status line below it
  make sense. Now two rows: "Road / access point" and "Drive notes".

- Every state page printed its own name twice — "Washington / State /
  Washington" — because the grey subtitle renders `area.region`, and a
  state's region is itself. All 48 states, i.e. the first screen you land on
  after picking one. The subtitle now drops a region equal to the name, and
  builds from parts so it disappears entirely rather than leaving an empty
  row. (Region and peak pages are unaffected: they still show the parent
  state, elevation and prominence.)

- The route-row rank phrase was hardcoded "#N on the cliff" for every area
  type. Only 2 routes in the catalog carry sort_order and both are on peaks,
  so it was wrong on every route that rendered it — Mount Baker read "#2 on
  the cliff". Now "in this area", which is true of a crag, a peak or a
  boulder.

What the walk did NOT find is worth recording: no undefined/NaN/[object
Object] in any rendered copy, nothing painting past the viewport, no
horizontal document scroll on any screen, route counts reconciling exactly
at every level of the tree (8,375 = the sum of its 10 children), correct

author: krutagyakaneria
body:
## Summary

This PR decouples live GPS WebSocket broadcasting from MongoDB telemetry persistence.

Previously, the location update path could perform MongoDB persistence as part of handling a live GPS update. This coupled customer-facing tracking latency to database performance.

The repository also contains an existing buffered/batched GPS persistence mechanism, resulting in multiple telemetry persistence paths.

This change establishes a single bounded telemetry pipeline while allowing live location broadcasts to remain responsive independently of MongoDB persistence.

## Problem

The previous flow could effectively behave as:

GPS Update
    ↓
MongoDB Write
    ↓
Live WebSocket Broadcast

When MongoDB was slow or temporarily unavailable, this could delay the live tracking path.

The repository also contained separate GPS persistence mechanisms, increasing the risk of duplicate writes and inconsistent behavior.

## Changes Made

### Decoupled Live Broadcasting

Live WebSocket broadcasting is now independent of MongoDB persistence.

The updated flow is:

GPS Update
    |
    +-----------------------> Live WebSocket Broadcast
    |
    +-----------------------> Telemetry Buffer
                                      |
                                      v
                                Batch MongoDB Write

The WebSocket broadcast no longer waits for MongoDB persistence to complete.

### Buffered GPS Persistence

GPS telemetry is persisted through a bounded buffering mechanism.

The buffer:

- Has a maximum capacity.
- Flushes based on batch size and/or interval.
- Prevents unbounded memory growth.
- Reuses the existing tracking infrastructure where appropriate.

### Batched MongoDB Writes

Multiple GPS updates are persisted using batched MongoDB operations instead of issuing an independent database write for every location update.

This reduces database write amplification and improves scalability for high-frequency driver telemetry.

### Persistence Failure Handling

MongoDB failures are handled independently from the live broadcast path.

The persistence layer provides controlled retry and recovery behavior while preventing:

- Infinite retries.
- Unbounded memory growth.
- Unlimited concurrent database operations.

### Buffer Overflow Protection

The telemetry buffer has explicit capacity and overflow behavior.

This prevents high-frequency location updates from causing unbounded memory consumption during database degradation.

### Graceful Shutdown

Pending telemetry is flushed during application shutdown using the existing process lifecycle.

Shutdown is bounded so the application cannot remain stuck indefinitely because MongoDB is unavailable.

### GPS Retention / TTL

The existing GPS retention and index configuration is reviewed and the required TTL behavior is enforced where necessary so historical telemetry does not grow without bound.

### Observability

Added or updated telemetry visibility for:

- GPS events received.
- GPS events broadcast.
- GPS events buffered.
- Batch flushes.
- Batch size.
- Persistence latency.
- Persistence failures.
- Retry attempts.
- Buffer size.
- Buffer overflow.
- Dropped telemetry where applicable.

GPS payloads are not unnecessarily included in logs.

## Testing

Added or updated tests covering:

- Normal GPS ingestion.
- Live broadcasting.
- Slow MongoDB persistence.
- MongoDB failures.
- Batched telemetry writes.
- Buffer capacity limits.
- Buffer overflow behavior.
- Persistence retries.
- Partial batch failures.
- Duplicate telemetry handling.
- TTL/index behavior.
- Graceful shutdown.
- Final telemetry flush.
- Concurrent flush protection.
- High-frequency GPS telemetry.

## Performance Validation

The implementation verifies that:

- Live WebSocket broadcasts are not blocked by slow MongoDB writes.
- Multiple GPS records can be persisted through bounded batch operations.
- Memory usage remains bounded under sustained telemetry load.
- Database write amplification is reduced.

Actual benchmark results are based on the tests and measurements executed for this PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Live GPS broadcasting does not wait for MongoDB persistence.
- [x] GPS persistence uses a bounded buffer.
- [x] GPS records are persisted using batch writes.
- [x] Buffer overflow behavior is explicitly handled.
- [x] MongoDB failures do not block live broadcasts.
- [x] Persistence retry behavior is bounded.
- [x] Concurrent flushes are controlled.
- [x] Pending telemetry is handled during graceful shutdown.
- [x] GPS retention/TTL behavior is verified.
- [x] Existing WebSocket and GPS behavior remains compatible.
- [x] Regression tests are included.

## Type of Change

- [x] Performance Improvement
- [x] Reliability Improvement
- [x] Scalability Improvement
- [x] GPS Telemetry Improvement
- [x] Test Coverage
- [ ] Breaking Change

## Breaking Changes

None expected.

Existing GPS payloads, WebSocket events, authentication, validation, and tracking behavior remain compatible.

## Related Issue

Closes #8450 

##GSSoC
#ECSoC26

This PR is submitted as part of GirlScript Summer of Code (GSSoC) 2026.

## Expected Outcome

A slow or temporarily unavailable MongoDB instance can no longer directly block the customer-facing live GPS broadcast path.

GPS telemetry is persisted through a single bounded and batched pipeline, reducing database overhead while maintaining controlled memory usage and reliable persistence.

author: zantvoort
body:
Kotlin has no package-private and explicit API mode was off, so classpath consumers of the Kotlin modules — the norm, JPMS or not — saw their whole impl surface. storm-kotlin was the worst affected: the `Flow` operators colliding by name and signature with their kotlinx.coroutines namesakes, the generically named top-level predicate factories polluting completion, and every `*Impl` class.

- Every declaration under storm-kotlin's `st.orm.template.impl` and `st.orm.repository.impl` is `internal`, as are storm-kotlinx-serialization's converter provider and the Kotlin starter's auto-configured repository post processor (its `@Bean` method now declares the public `RepositoryBeanFactoryPostProcessor` base). storm-ktor already kept its machinery `internal`.
- All five Kotlin modules — storm-kotlin, storm-kotlin-spring, storm-kotlin-spring-boot-starter, storm-ktor and storm-kotlinx-serialization — compile their main sources with `-Xexplicit-api=strict`, so a declaration without an explicit visibility fails the build; the public API carries explicit `public` modifiers accordingly. The flag sits on the compile execution, keeping test sources exempt.
- The coroutine-aware SQL log recording that the Ktor plugin consumes is the one deliberate cross-module share. Kotlin's `internal` stops at the artifact boundary, so it moves to `st.orm.template.recordSqlLog` behind the new `@InternalStormApi` opt-in (`@RequiresOptIn`, level ERROR): Storm's own modules opt in, application code gets a compile error naming the contract.

Verified with the full reactor (all module test suites green) and a standalone consumer project compiled against the built jar: importing `flattenConcat` or `QueryBuilderImpl` fails with "it is internal in file", and calling `recordSqlLog` without the opt-in fails with the marker's message.

Also names `scroll` alongside `resultGroupedBy` in the existing `widen()`/`narrow()` changelog entry.

Fixes #396

author: gm2211
body:
## What

The verdict banner answered "can I go" and nothing else. Weather, current and sunset each lived one tab away, so the Plan tab's headline answer cost three tab visits to make sense of.

Adds a context row alongside the existing reason chips:

- **Weather** — temperature range across the window, conditions at the departure hour, and a shower/thunder phrase only when there is real precipitation forecast.
- **Current** — phase and speed at departure, plus the next slack.
- **Sunset** — time, and how it falls relative to the planned return.

Each chip is dropped entirely when its own source is missing, rather than rendered as "n/a" — an absent chip is quiet, an "n/a" chip reads as a data failure the verdict itself never claimed. Reasons still render first and the context chips are dimmer, so "why this verdict" stays ahead of "what it's like out there".

## Notes

- The direction recommendation is now computed before the verdict renders, so the banner and the Direction card can never disagree about the phase at departure.

author: pichu2707
body:
Primera rodaja de #92. No mide vatios todavía: abre el camino.

## Por qué

Para dar **Wh por token** hay que excluir la **carga del modelo**, y el
endpoint OpenAI-compatible de ollama —el único que el proxy sabía hablar—
publica solo contadores de tokens. Tira el reparto interno del tiempo.

La API nativa sí lo reporta. Medido a través del proxy, modelo **frío**:

| | |
|---|---:|
| `load_us` | **1.451 ms — el 57% de la petición** |
| `prompt_eval_us` | 23 ms |
| `eval_us` | 1.070 ms |
| `total_ms` | 2.548 ms |

Sin separar eso, una petición fría inflaría los Wh/token unas **2,5 veces**.
`ttft_ms` mezcla carga y prompt y no los distingue; estas tres cifras sí.

Y aparte: el tráfico **nativo** de ollama no se medía en absoluto. El proxy
solo veía el camino OpenAI-compatible.

## Lo que NO arregla

**No corrige ningún error en `tokens_per_sec`.** Lo escribo porque yo mismo
afirmé lo contrario al abrir esta rama, y la afirmación era falsa.

En streaming el proxy calcula `salida / (total − ttft)`, y el `ttft` **ya
absorbe la carga**: el primer chunk no sale hasta que el modelo está cargado.
Sobre esa misma petición, `ttft_ms` fue **1.477 ms** contra **1.474** de
`load_us + prompt_eval_us`, y la velocidad publicada **126,1 tok/s frente a
126,2 reales**. Fuera de streaming el campo es `None`, no un número malo.

El "42% de error" que cité salía de una división que hice a mano sobre el
reloj de pared, sin cruzarla con lo que el proxy publica. Hay un test
(`el_tramo_de_generacion_del_proxy_ya_coincide_con_el_motor`) que fija la
equivalencia para que la afirmación no vuelva a colarse.

## El cambio de fondo: el escáner deja de saber de dialectos

Ollama nativo hace streaming **por defecto** —al revés que OpenAI— y manda
**NDJSON**: un objeto JSON por línea, **sin prefijo `data:`**. `scan_sse_line`
exigía ese prefijo a todo el mundo. Contra este dialecto habría ignorado cada
línea y publicado **cero tokens en silencio**, indistinguible de una respuesta
sin tokens.

Ahora el formato de línea lo decide el proveedor: `Provider::payload_de_linea`,
**sin default**. Heredar "SSE" dejaría a un proveedor nuevo publicando ceros
sin que nada fallara; que no compile obliga a decidir, igual que
`extract_tool_use` y `captura_invocaciones`. La regla SSE vive en un solo sitio
(`payload_sse`) para que los cuatro dialectos de nube no la copien y diverjan
— pero cada uno sigue teniendo que declarar que la usa.

Dos decisiones más, con test cada una:

- `decompose` reutiliza `split_history_and_last_turn` en vez de reimplantar el
  criterio: qué es historial no puede depender del proveedor. En
  `/api/generate` no hay conversación, así que el historial es **cero medido**,
  no un hueco.
- El default de `stream` es **true**. Darlo por `false` haría que el escáner
  leyera un NDJSON entero como un solo JSON y no encontrara el usage de nadie.

## Cambios

| Fichero | Cambio |
|---|---|
| `src/provider/ollama.rs` | **Nuevo.** Dialecto nativo: NDJSON, usage de la línea `done`, `stream` por defecto true |
| `src/provider/mod.rs` | `payload_de_linea` sin default + helper `payload_sse` compartido; 3 campos en `Usage` |
| `src/telemetry/metered.rs` | El escáner delega el formato de línea al proveedor |
| `src/telemetry/logger.rs`, `recent.rs` | `FIELDS` 16 → 19; `CONTRACT_VERSION` sigue en **1** (aditivo) |
| `src/config.rs` | `target_ollama_url` + `OXIDEGATE_OLLAMA_API_BASE` (por defecto `127.0.0.1:11434`) |
| `docs/telemetry-per-request.md` | §4.18 nueva, con lo que separa y lo que no |
| `README.md` | Fila de la variable de entorno |

## Cómo se probó

- **562 tests** en verde · `clippy -D warnings` limpio · `fmt --check` 0
- Extremo a extremo a través del proxy contra ollama real (`qwen2.5:7b`), con
  `OXIDEGATE_STORAGE_DIR` aislado y el modelo **frío** — las cifras de arriba
  salen de ahí, no de un fixture
- Guardas de forma: el conjunto exacto de claves publicadas está fijado en test

Rodaja **A** de #92 — no lo cierra: quedan la energía por petición (B) y las
señales de VRAM/throttling (C).

author: pher217
body:
## Goal

You reported the UI was "not well formatted on all pages — tables and KPIs, borders and so on." That turned out to be a single real CSS bug affecting the whole app, not a per-page styling problem. This fixes it, applies the warm retheme, and adds the README demo you asked for.

## The bug

`apps/ol-ui/src/index.css` declared a bare reset **after** `@import "tailwindcss"`:

```css
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0 }
```

Tailwind v4 emits every utility inside `@layer utilities`, and in the CSS cascade an **unlayered rule beats any layered rule regardless of specificity**. So that one declaration silently overrode every `p-*`, `m-*` and `space-y-*` in the application. Colours, borders and radii were unaffected, which is exactly why it read as a layout problem rather than a CSS one.

Tailwind's own preflight already applies that identical reset inside `@layer base`, where utilities can override it — so the hand-written copy was redundant *and* harmful. Removed, with a comment so nobody re-adds it.

Visible symptoms, all gone: `€507,000.00` rendering as `€507,000.`, section labels sitting on card borders, list rows spilling past their containers, cards touching with no gutters.

## Changes

- **`index.css`** — removed the unlayered reset; swapped the palette tokens to warm cream/amber (`#faf7f2` ground, `#d97706` primary, warm borders, warm-anchored chart series). Token values only — no structural change.
- **`badge.tsx`** — added ERP document-status pill variants (`draft`/`confirmed`/`delivered`/`invoiced`/`paid`/`unpaid`/`partlyPaid`/`overdue`/`cancelled`/`lowStock`/`inStock`) for the document views to consume.
- **`KpiCard.tsx`** — tabular figures, truncation with a `title=` fallback, size stepping up only at `2xl`, and a semantic right-edge accent bar. The grid now drops to 3 columns before 5 so a card is never too narrow to hold a formatted currency value.
- **`docs/demo/coolerp-walkthrough.gif`** + a Demo section above the fold in the README.

## Approach

The retheme is deliberately **token-level only**, per the earlier advisory: adopt the warm palette and the pill vocabulary, but not another product's visual identity wholesale. The right rail stays as-is in this PR; reframing it around the MCP capability contract is separate work.

I did *not* touch page or layout components — once the cascade bug was fixed, every page laid out correctly on its own, which is the evidence that it was one root cause rather than many.

## Test Summary

| Layer | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Lint | `npm run lint` | clean |
| Unit | `npm run test` | 17 passed |
| Build | `npm run build` | succeeds |
| Browser | live `ol-api` + Postgres | **0 console errors**; Overview, Journal Entries, Accounts, Inventory, Processes all verified visually |

The demo GIF is a real run, not a mockup. It posts a balanced `Dr 1000 / Cr 4000` entry through the web form, and the Overview afterwards shows cash `507,000.00 → 509,500.00` and revenue `10,000.00 → 12,500.00` because the ledger actually changed.

## Files Changed

- `apps/ol-ui/src/index.css` — the fix + palette tokens
- `apps/ol-ui/src/components/ui/badge.tsx` — status pill variants
- `apps/ol-ui/src/components/KpiCard.tsx` — overflow fix + accent bar
- `apps/ol-ui/src/pages/Overview.tsx` — KPI grid breakpoints
- `README.md`, `docs/demo/coolerp-walkthrough.gif` — the demo

## Note, not part of this PR

While debugging I found a `next-server` dev process from another project squatting on IPv6 `*:3000`. The browser resolves `localhost` to `::1` and hit that instead of `ol-api` on `127.0.0.1:3000`, producing CORS errors that looked like an API bug. Our CORS config is fine. I left that process alone.

author: miguel-heygen
body:
## What

A resized element keeps its new size across a seek instead of snapping back to its stylesheet size.

## Why

Size does not compose the way the position offset does: both channels write width and height, so the later write wins. Standing aside meant nothing held the size while a soft reload reverted the old timeline, since GSAP hands back each tween's recorded starting width. The element sat at its stylesheet size until the new timeline rendered, and the next gesture then started from a box disagreeing with the committed size.

## How

The size reapply no longer skips GSAP-sized elements. Only elements on which Studio has committed a size carry the reapply variables. Those variables intentionally remain authoritative across seeks; when the same element also has authored width or height GSAP tweens, the Studio-committed size wins until a later Studio resize changes it.

## Test plan

- Resize an element, scrub the timeline, and verify the committed size holds
- Verify an untouched element keeps its authored width and height behavior
- Verify a Studio-resized element with width or height GSAP tweens keeps the documented Studio-committed precedence

author: mesuef1974
body:
> ⚠️ **مسوّدة — يعتمد على #27.** الملفّان `verify_runtime_db_role.py` و`provision_rls_role.py` مشتركان بين الـPRين؛ يُعاد التأسيس على main بعد دمج #27.

## لماذا لم تكفِ إزالة `'*'`

النسخة الأولى من هذا الـPR حذفت التجاوز وأبقت المُسند `school_id = app_rls_school()` يقرأ `app.current_school_id`. قِسْتُ ذلك على مخطّط التطوير بدور `shschool_app` نفسه:

| السياق المضبوط | الصفوف المرئية |
|---|---|
| فارغ | 0 |
| UUID خاطئ | 0 |
| **UUID المدرسة الهدف** | **12 — كل الصفوف** |

الطرف الذي تحكمه السياسة كان هو من يُعرّف هويته فيها. أي أن RLS لم يكن حدّ ثقة مستقلاً، بل حارساً ضدّ أخطاء منطق التطبيق فقط.

## التصميم الجديد

الهوية تأتي من **اعتماد الاتصال**، وهو ما لا يستطيع الـSQL المحقون تغييره:

```sql
app_rls_school() -> SELECT school_id
                    FROM app_rls_role_school
                    WHERE db_role = session_user
```

`session_user` لا `current_user`: الثاني يتبع `SET ROLE`، بينما الأول يسجّل الدور الذي صادَق ولا يُغيّره إلا `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` وهي superuser-only. المُسند نصّه لم يتغيّر — تغيّر فقط ما تقرأه الدالة.

## ثلاثة أشياء كشفها البناء

**تكرار لانهائي.** جدول الربط يحمل عمود `school_id`، فالتقطته حلقة المطابقة وأنشأت عليه سياسة تستدعي `app_rls_school()` التي تقرأه. أول استعلام أعاد `stack depth limit exceeded`. استُثني كبنية تمهيدية ويُحمى بالمنح لا بـRLS.

**نفس الثغرة في موضع جديد.** `provision_rls_role` يمنح `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES` — أي أن الدور كان سيستطيع **إعادة كتابة هويته**. السحب يجب أن يأتي **بعد** المنح الشاملة وإلا أعادها الإطلاق التالي.

**نافذة إقلاع.** لو زُرع الربط في `provision_rls_role` وحده، لرأى الخادم القائم صفر صفوف بين `migrate` و`provision`. الترحيل يزرع الربط بنفسه حين تكون هناك مدرسة واحدة.

## بوابة القبول — قياس فعلي بمدرستين

بدور `shschool_app`، مدرسة A شرعية ومدرسة B ضحية، داخل معاملة مُلغاة:

| # | البوابة | المطلوب | المُقاس |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | صفوف مدرسته | تعمل | **12** ✅ |
| 2 | `SET ...='*'` | بلا أثر | **12 — لم تتغيّر** ✅ |
| 3 | `SET ...=UUID_B` | بلا أثر | **12 — لم تتغيّر** ✅ |
| 4 | رؤية صفوف B | صفر | **0** ✅ |
| 5 | `INSERT school_id=B` | مرفوض | `violates row-level security policy` ✅ |
| 9 | تعديل جدول الربط | مرفوض | `permission denied for table app_rls_role_school` ✅ |

البند 8 (`SET ROLE` إلى دور مميّز) يغطّيه #27 عبر `pg_has_role`. البند 10 (`UNPROTECTED_SCHOOL_SCOPED_TABLES=0`) يحتاج جرداً على الإنتاج.

**حدّ القياس:** الاختبار استخدم `SET ROLE` فبقي `session_user` هو المالك، فزُرع الربط للاثنين. هذا يُثبت أن السياسة تتجاهل المتغيّر تماماً، لكن الطوبولوجيا الإنتاجية (`session_user = shschool_app` عبر اتصال حقيقي) تحتاج تحقّقاً بعد النشر.

## الفاحص والتوفير

`verify_runtime_db_role` يفشل مغلقاً عند غياب الربط (وإلا عمل العامل أعمى على NULL) وعند كون جدول الربط قابلاً للكتابة. و`provision_rls_role` يحلّ المدرسة من `APP_DB_ROLE_SCHOOL_ID`، أو يستنتجها حين تكون هناك مدرسة واحدة فقط، ويرفض التخمين فيما عدا ذلك.

## التراجع

`reverse_sql = migrations.RunSQL.noop`. التراجع عن إصلاح أمني يجب ألّا يُعيد سلطة المستأجر إلى العميل.

## متعدّد المدارس لاحقاً

الكود لا يتغيّر: يُولَّد دور تشغيل لكل مستأجر (`shschool_app_school_A` …) ويُضاف سطر في جدول الربط. السياسات كما هي.

author: pac-cee
body:
Part of the same report as api#130: *"I can do things and still stay, yet it's a new day."* That PR fixed the server's idea of a day. This one fixes the phone's.

## The bug

`dailyRides` and `dailyDeclines` were **only ever incremented**. The only places setting them to `0` are profile-**creation** sites, which run on a fresh login and never again:

- `context/AuthContext.tsx:125-126` (`buildLocalDriverProfile`, only when `prev === null`)
- `hooks/driver-onboarding/onboardingSubmission.ts:32-33`
- `data/remote/repositories/RemoteDriverRepository.ts:247-248`

There was no reset logic anywhere in the app, and no field recording which day the counters belonged to — a stale day was not even detectable.

## What that broke

- `driverStatisticsViewModel.ts:138` raises the **"reduced priority" warning at 10 declines**. A driver who had *ever* declined 10 rides carried it permanently.
- `AuthContext.tsx:545` uses `dailyRides + dailyDeclines` as the acceptance-rate denominator. It only grew, so a bad first week could never be recovered from.

## The fix

`DriverProfile.dailyCountersDate` records the local calendar date the counters belong to. `withDailyCountersForToday` zeroes them when that date is not today, and runs:

- **on hydration**, so a driver opening the app on a new day sees today's numbers, not yesterday's carried forward
- **before each increment**, so a ride or decline just after midnight starts the new day rather than extending the old one

The day is the **device's local calendar day** — the one the driver reads off their own phone — which now matches the backend, where a day is the local calendar day in the platform timezone rather than a UTC one that rolls at 02:00 in Kigali.

### Migration

A profile stored before this field existed has no stamp, and its counters cover an unknown span, so they are **cleared rather than trusted** — carrying them forward would keep the stale total alive for one more day. Counters already at zero are simply stamped. Lifetime totals (`completedRides`, `earningsTotal`) are never touched.

## Verification

- 8 new tests in `domain/__tests__/driverDailyCounters.test.ts`, including the 00:30-vs-23:59 boundary and idempotence within a day
- `AuthContext.test.tsx` fixtures now stamp today (those tests are about counting *within* a day); a new test covers a ride completed on a new day starting at 1
- `tsc --noEmit` clean

## Still open

`acceptance_rate` on the backend has `DEFAULT 100.00` and **zero writes**, and it wins over the local value at `driverStatisticsViewModel.ts:110` — so the stats screen shows a hardcoded 100% beside a decline-driven warning. Fixing that needs a scoring-window decision and is deliberately not in this PR.

author: adriensauvageot34
arturhoo
body:
Top of the stack, on [#25](https://github.com/arturhoo/ghostty/pull/25)
(`tmux-window-close-notify`).

Two ways the session could end that it should not have, and the diagnostic that
would have told us which.

## A stray line killed the session

The parser's idle state treated any byte that was not `%` as unrecoverable:
`broken()`, then `.exit`, every native window in the session gone. That is a
very large consequence for a line we merely failed to understand. A stray line
is now discarded with a warning and the parser carries on.

**The provocation I wrote this for does not exist**, and I should say so
plainly. The theory was that tmux accepts any valid UTF-8 as a name and does not
escape it, so `rename-window $'a\nb'` would put a bare `b` on its own line. It
does not: `window_set_name` runs names through
`utf8_stravis(VIS_OCTAL|VIS_CSTYLE)`, and tmux 3.5a puts
`%window-renamed @0 a\nb` on the wire with a literal backslash and `n`, one
line. Same for `rename-session` and pane titles.

So this is defence against input we did not anticipate, not a fix for a
reproducible bug — and the live test injects the malformed bytes into the chain
directly rather than pretending tmux produced them. The first version asked tmux
and **passed with the recovery removed**; an adversarial review of the harness
caught that. The unit test caught the mutation; the live test did not, because
it was testing a provocation that never happened.

## `%exit` was an unknown notification

Exit worked, but only by accident of layering: tmux writes `%exit` and then the
string terminator, and it was the terminator ending the DCS that the viewer
noticed. The `%exit` line itself fell into the unknown-notification
fall-through, so its reason — the only explanation tmux ever gives — was
discarded.

That reason is worth having. `%exit too far behind` and a clean detach are the
same event from the viewer's side and very different events for whoever is
debugging. The notification carries it now and the viewer logs it.

## Testing

Unit: `%exit` with and without a reason; a `%window-renamed @1 a\nb` sequence
that leaves the parser alive and parsing the next notification.

Live: feed `stray line with no percent\n` straight into the chain mid-session,
then assert the session is not merely un-exited but still working — a write
still reaches the pane afterwards, which it would not if the parser were left
broken.

Verified load-bearing by mutation: restoring the fatal idle behaviour now fails
both the unit test and the live one. The earlier live test failed only the unit
one.

The flood test's flakiness and the `pump` bug behind it are fixed in #24, where
that test lives, so each PR is green on its own.

## AI disclosure

Written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5) under human review.

author: kislaykishore
body:
### Description
This PR optimizes `gcs.Folder.UpdateTime` by refactoring it from a 24-byte `time.Time` struct to an 8-byte `int64` (unix nanoseconds), and enhances `GCSFolder()` to perform direct mathematical conversion from protobuf `controlpb.Folder` timestamp fields (`seconds * 1e9 + nanos`) without allocating intermediate `time.Time` objects.

#### Struct Sizing & Go Heap Class Reduction
- `gcs.Folder` shrinks from 40 B to 24 B, dropping across the Go heap allocator class boundary from 48 B to 24 B.
- Saves **24 bytes (-50.0%) of real heap memory per folder**, yielding **24.0 MB saved per 1M folders** (and **240.0 MB per 10M folders**).
- Slice allocations (e.g. folder listings) save **40.0% allocated bytes**.

author: gtauzin
body:
## Description

Adds a `step_transformer` slot on forecasters, applied to the wide `{base}_step_1..H` frame derived from `X_future` and `X_forecast` before it joins the design matrix, plus the transformer family that fills it.

A 48-hour forecast over four variables becomes 192 columns to express what a model usually wants as twelve numbers, and nothing could act on that block. The existing `forecast_transformer` slot cannot substitute: it is anchored at `vintage_time` while the quantity a modeller wants ("minimum temperature over the next 48 hours, as of now") is anchored at the observation time, and as-of vintage selection makes the two diverge. `X_future` has no transformer seam at all.

**Stacked on `feat/additive-forecaster`.** Base that branch, not `main`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `BaseStepTransformer` | new `kind="step"`, stateless; the step frame shares the actual frame's single `"time"` index, so the tag is the only thing preventing a step transformer from silently no-opping in `actual_transformer` |
| `StepAggregator` | min / max / mean / std / sum over a closed vocabulary, with a null policy and an opt-in coverage companion |
| `StepColumnReducer` | lifts any sklearn transformer onto the step axis, one estimator per variable, keeping per-variable provenance |
| `StepFrameReducer` | one estimator over the whole step frame, capturing cross-variable structure |

The transform is a **parameter of `_derive_step_columns`** rather than applied at its call sites. There are six of them, four transform-only and one inside a `try/finally` state swap; a missed site yields a design matrix disagreeing with what the estimator was fitted on.

Composition rather than flags: `FeatureUnion` keeps raw steps alongside summaries, `ColumnTransformer` routes variables to different reductions, and a `FunctionTransformer` inside `StepColumnReducer` covers anything outside the closed vocabulary.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update

Additive throughout. The slot defaults to `None`, and with it unset the alignment-filter change and the rank-warning suppression are both no-ops, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Motivation and Context

The library already measures this problem and warns about it, in `_warn_rank_deficient_step_columns`, but the only remedy that warning could offer was "generate it with an `actual_transformer` instead", which serves deterministic clock features and does nothing for a genuine external forecast. This gives that warning a second, applicable answer.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project
- [x] I have run `just fix` to format my code
- [ ] I have run `just lint` to verify linting and type annotations
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes
- [x] All new and existing tests passed
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, and `rumdl` are clean. `ty` and `interrogate` are **not** clean, and neither failure is from this change; see below.

## Additional Notes

### Verification

```
pytest        5779 passed, 18 skipped, 2 xfailed, 0 failed   (~124 new tests)
ruff          check + format clean
rumdl         no issues in 100 files
doctests      5 passed
mkdocs build  --strict, 0 warnings
```

### Pushed with pre-push hooks skipped, deliberately

Two pre-push gates fail on this branch, and both fail identically on the pristine tip of `feat/additive-forecaster`. Verified by checking that branch out into a temporary worktree and running each tool there.

- **`ty`**: 7 diagnostics, all in `_observe_predict_bulk_origins`, `_observe_predict_batched_origins`, and `capture`, added by this branch's perf work. This change touches none of them.
- **`interrogate`**: 3 undocumented nested functions, `_chains_are_batch_invariant.declared`, `_chains_are_batch_invariant.every`, and `_observe_predict_batched_origins.assemble`. The pristine tip scores 95.3% on those two files; with this change the same 21-file set scores 98.7%, so this PR raises the ratio rather than lowering it.

Both want fixing on the base branch. Flagged here rather than fixed, to avoid editing in-flight work inside an unrelated feature PR.

### One unrelated fix is included

`pyproject.toml` gains `MD057` to the existing `.claude/skills/**` rumdl per-file-ignore. Those files document markdown syntax with a literal `[text](url)` example, which the linter reads as a broken relative link, and it blocks **every** commit for anyone with those files present. It matches the `MD007` exemption already there for the same glob.

### Behaviour worth a reviewer's attention

**Global panel columns are localised.** Under `panel_strategy="global"` each group gets its own fitted step transformer, and a shared unprefixed column comes back per group (`holiday` becomes `A__holiday_step_mean`, `B__holiday_step_mean`). Invisible for arithmetic aggregation; for a fitted reduction each group's estimator yields different values for the same shared input. This matches how `forecast_transformer` already behaves, and consistency was chosen over exempting globals in one slot but not the other. Documented in the how-to.

**The rank-deficiency warning is suppressed by any step transformer**, not only one that removes the redundancy. Suppression asks whether the block's original names still reach the estimator, and every step transformer renames its output. Discriminating would need output columns attributed back to their source variable, which `StepFrameReducer` deliberately makes impossible. Forecasters without a `step_transformer` are unaffected.

**Partial coverage in the wrappers is diagnosed by trying, not by tags.** scikit-learn takes a `Pipeline`'s input tag from its **last** step, so `Pipeline([SimpleImputer(), PCA()])` reports `allow_nan=False` while handling NaN correctly. A tag gate rejected the very composition the error message recommends as the fix, so the wrappers attempt the fit and add the diagnosis only when it actually fails.

### Docs

New how-to (`reduce-step-features.md`), the `transformer-kinds.md` explanation extended from two kinds to three, a companion marimo notebook, and regenerated API reference pages.

author: dustin-riley
body:
Editing more than one sport in a sitting did not reliably survive a save. Two separate causes, both in how `redhawks_gameday_sports` meets core's objects-setting editor.

## Rows had no labels

The schema declared no `identifier`, so [`generateSchemaTitle`](https://github.com/discourse/discourse/blob/main/frontend/discourse/admin/components/schema-setting/editor.gjs) fell through to its generic branch:

```js
return title || `${schema.name} ${index + 1}`;
```

Every row in the navigation tree read "sport 1", "sport 2", "sport 3". Nothing tied a row to its sport, so past one row there was no way to tell which sport you were editing or to confirm a value had landed where you meant it to. Core has a test for this fallback — *"generic identifier is used when identifier is not specified in the schema"*. Naming `sport` as the identifier puts each row's own sport name on it.

## One untouched row discarded the whole batch

`mode` was `required: true` with `default: "off"`. Core's enum field does:

```js
@tracked value = this.args.value || (this.args.spec.required && this.args.spec.default);
```

It sets its **own local** value to the default and renders it, but never calls `onChange`. A row whose Mode dropdown was never opened therefore shows "off" while storing no `mode` key at all. Server-side, `SchemaSettingsObjectValidator#validate_property` fails the required check — and because the whole list is one setting value, that rejects **every** row, not just the offending one. Add three sports, leave one Mode alone, lose all three.

Dropping `required` lets such a row save. The planner already treats a blank mode as off; that is now covered by a spec, since it went from incidental to load-bearing.

## Trade-off

With `required` gone, the editor no longer renders the `"off"` default either — `spec.required && spec.default` short-circuits to `false` — so a new row's Mode dropdown starts **empty** rather than pre-filled with "off". Empty behaves as off. Core offers "shows off" or "stores off", not both, and storing it is the half that matters.

## Testing

`~/.gem/ruby/2.6.0/bin/rspec spec/lib` — 109 examples, 0 failures.

Not yet verified against the live site; that needs a container rebuild. `category` is still `required: true`, so a row saved without one will still block the batch the same way — left alone for now since it was not part of the reported symptom, but it is the same failure shape if it bites.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01B3u54tfiMqSVanCQBdZJvn

author: jefersonfborba
body:
## Problem

`StartClient()` (called on every reconnect: disconnect retries, session
checks, `ConnectInstance` API calls) creates the whatsmeow session store
container via:

```go
container, err = sqlstore.New(context.Background(), "postgres", w.config.PostgresAuthDB, dbLog)
```

`sqlstore.New()` calls `sql.Open()` internally, opening a **brand-new,
unbounded** Postgres connection pool on every call — and the resulting
`container` is never closed anywhere in `StartClient()`. Each reconnect
leaks one idle connection that is never released.

On a shared Postgres instance, this accumulates over days until
`max_connections` is exhausted, and **every other service/database sharing
that Postgres** starts failing with:

```
FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections (SQLSTATE 53300)
```

We hit this in production 4 times over ~10 days (self-hosted, shared
Postgres): 2026-07-31, 2026-08-04, 2026-08-06 (escalated to exhausting even
the superuser-reserved slots, requiring a full `docker restart` of the
shared Postgres — affecting unrelated projects on the same server), and
2026-08-08 (~43 idle `evogo_auth_user` connections, oldest ~1d19h,
106/100 connections at capture time).

## Root cause

`whatsmeowService` already opens `authDB` **once**, at startup, with a
correctly bounded pool (`initPostgresAuthDB` in `cmd/evolution-go/main.go`):

```go
db.SetMaxOpenConns(25)
db.SetMaxIdleConns(5)
db.SetConnMaxLifetime(5 * time.Minute)
db.SetConnMaxIdleTime(1 * time.Minute)
```

...and injects it into `whatsmeowService.authDB` via `NewWhatsmeowService`.
But `StartClient()` never uses it for the whatsmeow session store — it
opens a fresh, unbounded pool from the DSN string every time instead.

## Fix

Use `sqlstore.NewWithDB(w.authDB, "postgres", dbLog)` — which wraps an
*existing* `*sql.DB` instead of opening a new one — reusing the
already-pooled, already-limited connection. Since `NewWithDB` skips the
auto-upgrade that `New()` performs, `container.Upgrade(ctx)` is called
explicitly right after.

The sqlite fallback path (`PostgresAuthDB == ""`) is untouched — it isn't
the source of this leak (local file, not a shared server).

## Validation

I wasn't able to run `go build ./...` for this PR — my local Docker
daemon has a corrupted/read-only containerd filesystem unrelated to this
repo, and I don't have a local Go toolchain. The change is a 2-line
semantic substitution (confirmed against `go.mau.fi/whatsmeow`'s
`store/sqlstore/container.go` — `NewWithDB(db *sql.DB, dialect string, log waLog.Logger) *Container`
signature matches exactly what's used here), but please run a build/lint
pass before merging — I couldn't verify it locally this time.

## Related

Full incident history (4 occurrences, mitigation steps, `pg_stat_activity`
snapshots) documented downstream in a consumer project's backlog:
https://github.com/jefersonfborba/tabloides/blob/master/docs/backlog.md
(search "BL-028").

## Summary by Sourcery

Reuse the existing pooled Postgres connection for the Whatsmeow session store to prevent connection pool leaks on client reconnects.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix a Postgres connection leak caused by opening a new, unbounded connection pool on every StartClient reconnect without closing it.

Enhancements:
- Standardize session store initialization to use a shared Postgres DB handle when configured, while keeping the sqlite fallback behavior unchanged.

author: prdb-net
body:
Closes #5.

ADR 0009 keeps the API key, the download directories, the library and its layout in the database rather than the container environment. This adds the path that collects them, and the settings screen it becomes afterwards — one configuration, not a wizard with a second page behind it.

## What it does

- **The API key is checked before it is stored**, through `Prdb.Sdk` against `GET /user-identity`. A key that is wrong is told apart from a prdb that is down: only the first is the user's to fix, and storing the second would be the tool claiming something it does not know.
- **Directories are checked the way the tool will use them** — listed, and for the library written to — so a path nothing is mounted at, a source it may not read and a library it may not write to each produce a message that names what is wrong and what to do about it.
- **Each download directory says whether videos will be renamed or copied.** ADR 0002 makes that the difference between a millisecond and an hour, and it depends on something the UI cannot show, so it is said while the user can still mount the two from one volume. Mounts are compared rather than devices: Linux refuses a rename across two mounts even of the same filesystem.
- **The inspections are made fresh on every read**, never stored, so a volume that failed to come back after a restart shows up as a sentence next to the directory instead of a scan that quietly does nothing.
- Until onboarding is finished the tool scans nothing and says so; the stored key never returns to the browser and never reaches a log.

## Shape

`Core` gains the configuration domain and the two ports it declares (`IDirectoryInspector`, `IPrdbApiKeyCheck`), `Infrastructure` implements them next to the service that stores what is collected, and `Host` exposes `/api/configuration` behind the password with the contract regenerated. The browser side is the guided path, revealing a step once the one before it is answered, and the same screen edits the settings once it is done.

## Checked

`dotnet build`, `dotnet test` (57 tests, 20 of them new), `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, and the contract regenerated. The host tests drive the real application over HTTP; only the socket under the SDK is replaced, so the client, its redirect rule and the mapping from a status code to a sentence all run. The path was also walked in a browser against the real prdb, which is where the wrong-key message above comes from.

author: prafed
body:
Three defects in the Pulse Finances data layer, plus the frontend change needed to see the fix. Each bug produces a plausible-looking but wrong dashboard rather than a visible failure, which is why they're easy to miss.

Found while populating the Finances tab with real GBP data on a fresh install.

## 1. Non-USD amounts parse as zero

`parseCurrencyCell` strips `$` and commas but not `£` or `€`:

```ts
const cleaned = cell.replace(/\*\*/g, "").replace(/[~$,]/g, "").trim()
```

`"£1,234"` survives as `"£1234"`, fails `cleaned.match(/^[\d.]+/)`, and returns `0`. Every row on a non-USD dashboard silently becomes zero — the tab renders normally and shows a total of 0.

Also now accepts the Unicode minus (U+2212), which typographic pipelines emit, so negative rows parse rather than being dropped by the `amount > 0` filter in `parseCurrencyTable`.

USD behaviour is unchanged; regression cases below.

## 2. Obligation `scope` is hardcoded in two places

`obligations.yaml` can declare `scope: business`, but the value is overwritten with `"personal"` both in the YAML normalizer and again in the resolver. Fixing only the first has no visible effect, which makes this awkward to debug. Every business-paid obligation renders as personal.

## 3. Sample vendors silently delete real expenses

`knownLabels` is built from all vendors and obligations, then substring-matched against `EXPENSES.md` rows to avoid double-counting:

```ts
if (lower.includes(known) || known.includes(lower)) return false
```

Every row of the shipped `install/USER/FINANCES/vendors.yaml` is a zero-value `unconfigured` sample (`"Sample Employer Inc."`, `"Sample Landlord"`, …). A user who fills in `EXPENSES.md` but leaves the sample file alone — it looks inert — has those sample names suppress their genuine expense rows.

On my install this removed roughly 40% of real expenses from the outbound total with no warning: the tab showed £32k against a true £55k.

A zero-value entry has nothing to double-count, so suppression is pure data loss. Only entries that actually contribute spend can now suppress a row.

## 4. Frontend: currency symbol from `state.json`

`fmtHero`/`fmtExact` hardcode `$`. They now read `state.currency` (already present in the API payload) and fall back to `$` when absent, so existing installs are unaffected. Without this the parser fix is invisible: a GBP install shows `$0` everywhere, then `$98K`.

## Verification

Parser, including USD regression:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `£1,234` | 1234 |
