author: justinjoy
body:
Closes #1019. Two commits: a whitespace-only `uncrustify` reformat of `frontier.c` (which failed the hard gate on base and which the fix edits), then the fix.

Incremental evaluation decides which strata to re-run by asking, per rule, which relations its body reads — by walking the rule's plan operators. **Two rewrites leave nothing for that walk to find:**

| rewrite | what it does to the operands |
|---|---|
| `rewrite_multiway_delta` | moves them into `wl_plan_op_k_fusion_t.k_ops[]` behind `opaque_data` — hidden, present |
| `rewrite_lftj_chains` | copies only `rel_names[]`/`key_cols[]` and **`free_op()`s the originals** — gone |

`col_compute_affected_strata` then returns 0 and the caller concludes nothing changed.

## Severity, in order

**Retraction is the worst case**, because `session.c` *intersects*: `affected_mask &= col_compute_affected_strata(..., last_removed)` from `UINT64_MAX`, so one blinded 0 zeroes the whole mask. Removing `Edge(2,3)` leaves `Path(1,3)` and `Path(2,3)` in the snapshot — **retracted tuples retained**, worse than tuples merely missing.

**Insertion derives nothing.** `--watch` + `Edge 3 4` emits no deltas; the single-IDB-atom form emits three. Multi-stratum plans starve transitively.

## The issue was filed as a K-fusion defect. It isn't.

`rewrite_lftj_chains` blinds a plain **non-recursive** star join `R(x) :- A(x,y), B(x,z), C(x,w).` whenever the host doesn't call `wirelog_optimize` — which `wirelog-advanced.h` documents as supported — and via `wirelog_optimize` too, since `enable_semijoin` is public. That stratum is neither recursive nor fused, so **every fusion-shaped test misses it**.

Nor is "two IDB atoms in one rule" the trigger: `count_delta_positions` sums across *all* rules of a head, so two ordinary single-atom recursive rules fuse identically. That's the shape real programs have.

## Why the stratum, not the relation

`wl_plan_relation_t` is rebuilt or copied in three places that would each need to carry a new field — `col_plan_split_at_exchange` assigns members individually, and two designated initialisers in `eval.c` zero what they don't mention. **#975's relation-level `recursive_agg` is already silently dropped by two of them.**

`wl_plan_stratum_t` is never struct-copied in production. The three frontier unit tests build strata on the stack — 18 arrays — and every one `memset`s first, so `rule_refs == NULL` and they keep taking the scan path unchanged. Proved by rebuilding them with `-ftrivial-auto-var-init=pattern`, which would turn an unzeroed `rule_refs` into a fault.

## Under-marking is impossible

Recorded before the rewrites ⇒ superset of the post-rewrite scan, identical for non-fusing plans. Instrumented over the full suite, **470 frontier queries: 0 under-marks, 37 recoveries — all on `K_FUSION` or `LFTJ`, none on any other operator shape.** A second reviewer's independent harness over 210 plans × 7 optimizer configurations (130,032 rule pairs) agreed: 0 under-marks.

Perf is *better* — the refset short-circuits before touching the op array (mask microbench at 28 strata: 485–489 ns vs 566–568 ns).

## Safety

Fault injection at all three allocation sites, 120 plan builds under ASAN+UBSAN+LSAN: 105 built, 15 failed cleanly, no leak, no double free. `rule_refs` is written before the plan is published and never mutated; TSan clean at W=4 and W=8.

## Written down rather than asserted away

- `has_empty_forced_delta` is deliberately not hoisted (needs live per-iteration state). A fused shape blinds **four** of its call sites — both the sequential and TDD paths have a whole-stratum early exit and a per-rule pre-scan. An earlier revision of that comment said two. Correctness is unaffected; the loss is early-exit only.
- Two `frontier.c` comments claimed indices ≥ 64 are "re-evaluated unconditionally by the caller's fallback". **There is no such fallback** — `session.c` gates on `1ULL << si` with no clamp, which is UB. Both corrected; filed as #1033.

## Tests

`tests/test_affected_strata_rewrites.c`, **13 cases, 12 failing against the parent commit.** Every case builds a *real* plan via `wl_plan_from_program` — a hand-built plan takes the fallback and would be vacuous — and asserts its own premise first (that the specific blinding operator is present), so a change to when rewrites fire turns the file red rather than green. The LFTJ case additionally asserts the optimized build does *not* use LFTJ, so it can't quietly become a duplicate if SIP absorbs the shape.

Covers both rewrites, cross-rule fusion, precision (an independent stratum stays clear), transitive propagation, the rule-level mask, retraction (exact deltas + post-retraction snapshot), `--watch` end to end, and incremental-equals-full-evaluation at W ∈ {1,2,4,8}.

The unfused control is killed by no mutation and **says so in the file** — it earns its place by asserting the inverted premise, not by detecting faults.

## Validation

Suite **271 ok / 1 fail / 11 skipped** in release and ASAN+UBSAN+LSAN; the failure is the pre-existing `sbom_snapshot` pin drift. uncrustify clean on all five changed files. gcc + clang `-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wshadow -Wpedantic` — no new diagnostics.

## Follow-ups filed, not fixed

#1030 (snapshot route stays stale — which is why the rule-level half has no end-to-end observable today and is pinned by a unit assertion), #1031 (mixed insert+remove step evaluates zero strata), #1032 (~20 TDD predicates blind to LFTJ), #1033 (≥64 index UB).

author: vak-sah
body:
Four independent wording fixes to the operating contract and the onboarding script. No new files, no new rules beyond the four below, no behaviour change anywhere in the code.

## `START_HERE.md` Step 6 — the merge deadlock

The fallback for branch-enforcing environments said onboarding "is not complete until that PR is merged" without naming who does the merging. Read literally that is a handoff: the agent opens the PR and stops, leaving the user holding a blocker `AGENTS.md` §3 already authorises the agent to clear. Where the environment opens PRs as drafts, the user cannot merge it either without knowing to mark it ready first.

Now: merge it yourself once CI is green, marking it ready first if it was opened as a draft. The report line is reserved for an actual refusal, which is the only case that is genuinely the user's.

## `AGENTS.md` §4 — coined names explain themselves

§4 required docstrings to cover what a thing does, its inputs/outputs, and what is safe to change. Nothing required the *vocabulary* the agent invents along the way to explain itself — the metric names, field names and modes that are obvious while the design conversation is fresh and opaque to the same user later. §8's premise is that the user is an amateur in the domain, so this is exactly the part they cannot reconstruct.

New bullet: beside the definition, say what the term measures and what a good value looks like; if it reaches a printed report or a stored record, that one line goes into the record too, so an output opened months later explains itself without the code. Explicitly not a glossary file — the bullet above it already forbids a second home for the truth.

## `AGENTS.md` §7 — one runtime assumption removed

§7 asserted Colab-and-Drive-only ("Assume that, not a local machine", "One Drive root") while every rule inside it is location-independent: only code in git, one root set in the config cell, secrets never in the repo, tests run without the root. A project that also runs locally therefore had to amend the operating contract before writing a line of code.

Colab stays the shipped default and `DRIVE_ROOT` keeps its name. The section now states the principle once and lets the config cell decide where the root sits.

## `AGENTS.md` §2.5 — one branch per step

Nothing said not to reuse a branch, so the natural move is to push the next step to the branch already in hand. After a squash merge that branch holds commits the default branch does not, the push is rejected, and the only way through is a force-push — which §3 gates behind asking and some environments refuse outright. A fresh branch per step removes the class rather than documenting the recovery.

## Checks

`pytest -q` — 14 passed. No new tests: all four changes are wording, and a test for any of them would assert on prose rather than a fact.

author: ceharris
body:
Implements the priority interrupt controller (PIC) device on top of the foundational primitives from #319/#322: `Pic` is an `IoDevice` exposing a single 8-bit Interrupt Enable Register (IER), paired with a `VectorResolver` implementation that ranks `IrqSource(0..6)` into their own vector slots at `0xFFE0`-`0xFFED` and folds `IrqSource(7..63)` onto a shared lowest-priority vector at `0xFFEE`, matching real PIC "wired-OR" conventions; the RESET and NMI vectors pass through unchanged. The IER uses the same set/clear-mask write encoding already used by the VIA's IER (bit 7 selects enable vs. disable, bits 0-6 select which slots are affected), and always reads bit 7 as 1 since IRQ7-63 can't be individually masked.

While designing this, we found a gap in the foundational work: the IER can only ever be a vector *routing* table, not real masking, because the CPU decides whether to recognize an IRQ (`InterruptController::irq_active()` plus the I flag) before any `VectorResolver` gets a say — a disabled low-priority source could still assert the physical IRQ line and force the CPU into service with no dedicated vector to route it to. This PR resolves that by adding `VectorResolver::irq_mask()` (default `u64::MAX`, so existing resolvers are unaffected) and has `Cpu::step` AND it against the raw active-sources bitmask before recognizing an IRQ or waking from WAI. This keeps `InterruptController` policy-free — the masking policy lives entirely in the PIC's own `VectorResolver` impl — while making a disabled IER slot behave like a real "enable" bit rather than just a vector-selection hint.

Also adds `PicModule`, a config-driven `DeviceModule` registered under the type string `pic/finch`, so a system config can install a PIC with `pic/finch@address`. `BusConfig::device` and `BusConfig::vector_resolver` each take ownership of their own boxed trait object, and those objects end up on different fields of the built `Cpu` (the bus's device list vs. the CPU's resolver slot) — so the module can't just hand the same `Pic` to both. `Pic::ier` moves behind an `Arc<AtomicU8>` and gains `Pic::vector_resolver()`, which hands out a `PicVectorResolver` sharing that state; the module registers the `Pic` as the bus device and installs its `PicVectorResolver` as the CPU's vector resolver, so both stay in sync as the IER is written at runtime.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (no warnings)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` (1159 lib/bin tests + integration suites, including the Klaus Dormann 65C02 conformance suite, all pass)
- [x] Unit tests for `Pic`'s IER read/write/reset semantics, `resolve()`/`irq_mask()` priority-routing behavior, and `PicVectorResolver` tracking live IER writes
- [x] `PicModule` tests covering bus registration and an end-to-end CPU IRQ-service test through the config-instantiated device + resolver pair

Closes #324

author: jlgarcia75
body:
## Problem

After marking a statement `.md` ready, the pipeline logged:

```
PyYAML is required to read the statement-type registry (pip install pyyaml).
```

**Root cause:** `finance_statements.zsh` defaulted `PYTHON_BIN=python3`. The pipeline runs from a **LaunchAgent** with a minimal PATH, so bare `python3` resolves to the **system Python**, which lacks the pipeline deps. This stayed invisible until routing began using the statement-type registry (`resolve_statement_type.py`), which imports PyYAML. Only the project venv (`~/.venv`, where `MARKITDOWN_BIN` already points) has PyYAML / openpyxl / jsonschema.

## Fix

- Default `PYTHON_BIN` to `${MARKITDOWN_BIN:h}/python3` — the interpreter in the **same venv markitdown already uses** — falling back to PATH `python3`. Still overridable via `.env`.
- **Preflight** the interpreter: abort early with an actionable message if it can't `import yaml`, instead of failing mid-run inside a routing/extract step.
- Document `PYTHON_BIN` in `config/local.example.env`.

(The user's local `.env` — gitignored — was also set to the venv interpreter for an immediate fix; this makes the default correct so it can't recur on other machines or a reset `.env`.)

## Verification

- With `PYTHON_BIN` unset, the derive-default resolves to `~/.venv/bin/python3` and the preflight `import yaml` passes.
- The exact step that failed (`resolve_statement_type.py ... --format sh`) now succeeds under the configured interpreter.
- `zsh -n scripts/finance_statements.zsh`, `py_compile scripts/*.py`, and `tests/smoke_test.py` all pass.

author: kasunben
body:
## Summary

Continues the keychain-storage investigation (task 17.4 → RFC 0082 → RFC 0072's addendum) by shipping the addendum's platform-side half: seeding a native, secretless, PKCE-required OAuth client per official shell (`sovereign-desktop`, `sovereign-mobile`) at auth-server startup, idempotently, per instance. This is the foundation RFC 0082 §5's durable-session sequel — and transitively `sovereign-desktop` epic task 17.4 (still parked) — need.

**Does not by itself unblock 17.4 or §5.** Only the seeding infrastructure ships here; the shell-side PKCE flow (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`/Custom Tabs) and OS keychain storage that actually consume it remain unbuilt and unscheduled — a separate, larger cross-repo undertaking.

### A real correction, found live not assumed

The addendum's own proposed mechanism (call `adminCreateOAuthClient` directly — it's `SERVER_ONLY`) doesn't actually work: verified against a real migrated `:memory:` DB that its handler still requires a genuine user session internally (`assertClientPrivileges` throws `UNAUTHORIZED` without one), and there is no session at server boot. Seeds via a direct `INSERT` into `oauthClient` instead — the same pattern `instrumentation.ts`'s RFC 0021 owner-migration already uses for `better-auth`-owned tables. The row shape (JSON-encoded array columns, boolean-as-0/1 on SQLite, `ON DELETE CASCADE userId` left `NULL`) was reverse-engineered from a client actually created through the legitimate admin path with a real session, then confirmed to resolve correctly through `getClient()` — the same internal resolver the real authorize flow uses — not just typechecked against the package's `.d.mts`.

### Also fixed along the way

`provisionAuthSqldNamespace()` (`apps/auth/src/db.ts`) was missing the `:memory:` carve-out its sibling `getAuthDb()` already had, so any plain (no encryption key) `:memory:` caller crashed with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND sqld` outside Docker's network. Found while trying to verify the seeding logic against a real migrated test DB — no existing test exercised this path (`db.pg.test.ts` only hits the early-returning Postgres branch). Regression test added.

### What's new

- `apps/auth/src/builtin-oauth-clients.ts` — `seedBuiltinOAuthClient(s)()`, called from `instrumentation.ts` after migrations.
- `apps/auth/app/api/oauth-clients/route.ts` — public, unauthenticated, re-seeds on read.
- `runtime/src/instance-oauth-clients.ts` + `GET /api/instance`'s new `oauthClients` field — omitted (not erroring) when the auth server is unreachable, resolving the addendum's own upgrade-window open question.
- RFC 0072's addendum corrected (mechanism, both resolved open questions — `sovereign-mobile`'s redirect scheme confirmed identical to desktop's, `sovereign://oauth/callback`); the client revocation/recreation gap (`cachedTrustedClients` deliberately unused) is now confirmed real, not hypothetical — left open since no real consumer exists yet.
- Epic task 1.24, ROADMAP slot `0.70.0`, task 17.4's note updated to reflect the current accurate blocker state.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm format:check && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm design:tokens:check && pnpm test` — all pass (1984 tests, ran via pre-push hook)
- [x] Seeding verified idempotent against a real migrated `:memory:` DB (not mocked)
- [x] Seeded client verified to resolve through better-auth's own `getClient()`/`getOAuthClientPublic`, with a genuine session
- [x] `GET /api/instance` verified to include/omit `oauthClients` correctly on auth-server success/failure/non-2xx

author: dababiyoda
body:
Stacked on `agent/daleobanks-phase0-operating-substrate` (PR #67).

**606 passing. CI green** via the documented `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

```bash
python -m daleobanks validate    # names every decision you have not made
python -m daleobanks preflight   # what is authorized, what is blocked
python -m daleobanks seed        # the canon, and the full blueprint
python -m daleobanks run         # one full cycle, shadow only
python -m daleobanks report      # computed from the store, not typed
python -m daleobanks opus        # what any of this has done outside itself
```

It runs with no config at all: the declaration falls back to the canon, so `run` seeds four territory nodes, three pillars and five primitives, then correctly refuses to chase a goal because no budget ceiling has been declared.

---

## The blueprint, and the gate that is not on it

The map is complete: **56 components across action → asset → system → business → network → infrastructure**, each naming the external consequence that would prove it earned its place. Completeness is the point — a component that is not on the map gets rediscovered from scratch every time someone reaches for it, and future work needs a target to build against.

Mapping is therefore never rationed, and recording something as already built is never refused. A ledger that refuses facts is worse than no ledger. What is rationed is **advancement**.

Each component grows through:

```
BLUEPRINT → SKETCHED → BUILT → EXERCISED → PROVEN → HARDENED
                                            └──── outside evidence only ────┘
```

- **Levels cannot be skipped.** The skipped step is precisely the work nobody did.
- **PROVEN cannot be declared**, at registration or by advancing into it. It is reached only by recording a consequence outside this system — and a repo path is not a consequence, a simulation is not a consequence, and one component may not cite another as evidence that it worked. That last one is the real guard: a system can be perfectly coherent and entirely imaginary.
- **HARDENED costs three external proofs plus a named failure mode survived.** Once is luck; adversity without repetition is an anecdote.
- **Deadlines force a verdict.** Past due with no external proof: MODIFY, HARVEST, KILL. `INTEGRATE` is deliberately absent.
- **Nothing dies unharvested.** Kill refuses without a recorded lesson, or the tuition gets paid twice.

What the ledger says about this branch right now:

```
verdict: ARCHITECTURE_ONLY        blueprint: 56        proven: 0

BLUEPRINT 29 · SKETCHED 6 · BUILT 21 · EXERCISED 0 · PROVEN 0 · HARDENED 0

in_construction: 27 / 12   →   may_construct: false

cheapest_real_world_test:
  one daily edition → one reader who did not ask for it, who comes back
```

Twenty-seven components are half-built and not one of them has touched the world. The ledger will not permit a twenty-eighth until one does. That is the correct answer, and it indicts this build.

## The rest of the branch

**The optimizer was paying for anger.** `fame` is engagement, `penalty` is platform slaps, nothing measured comprehension — so outrage that never trips a block raised the J-score and got sampled harder. §55 names that loop; §75 listed the guard; it did not exist. I then built it and left it disconnected for four commits. It is wired now at the point a reward becomes the Beta prior, and `ExperimentsService` computes per-arm engagement/capability/trust deltas by split-half comparison so it can actually fire. An arm with no quality evidence gets **no delta rather than a zero** — absence of signal is not neutral signal.

**One owner for the WMI evidence rule.** Written twice, the copies disagreed, and the looser one governed recorded state. 322 tests passed because nothing exercised the divergence.

**One ladder, not six systems.** §59's progression is the spine. Rungs need verified voluntary actions; revenue needs reconciliation plus delivery plus acceptance; withdrawal cascades once.

**23/23 adversarial controls**, each with a negative control. The health guard's own permit case caught an inversion pre-commit: raw-text scanning flagged "this is not a diagnosis" as a diagnosis.

**Failure posture executable** — loosening only through recorded recovery against conditions declared while the incident was open.

**A composition root.** Wiring the parts together immediately surfaced two integration defects that per-service tests were green on: `AccountLane` takes `legal_principal`, not `owner`, and `shadow_publish` is a coroutine. Neither was reachable without composing them. Three refusals hold that layer honest: it will not run on a partial declaration, it will not raise authority (surfaces seed `SHADOW`/`SHADOW_ONLY`, asserted directly), and it will not report what it did not do.

## What this still is not

Participants 0 · owned relationships 0 · reconciled revenue 0 · advancement actions 0 · gates cleared 0 · accounts ACTIVE 0 · components proven 0.

The machine runs. Nobody has walked through the door. The outrage guard fires only on arms carrying helpfulness ratings; content guards are keyword heuristics with unmeasured error rates; guards bind the service path, not the store.

## Governance

`DB-DEC-003/004/005` — five roles, two passes, do-nothing alternatives, dissent preserved as binding on reporting. All validate. `DB-DEC-002` freed for the Phase 1 branch. Four §85 docs. PR #66 ownership resolved as composition. PR #65 carried verbatim.

**Phase 1 overlap:** both branches stack on PR #67 and rewrite `README.md` and `governance/operating_work_packet.json`. Take Phase 1's as base, re-add the four `docs/DALEOBANKS_*.md` links. `agent/daleobanks-phase1-editorial-control-loop` is still not on origin, so those commits remain unreachable and the merge cannot be done from here.

---

**Next action.** Take one BUILT component to EXERCISED, then to PROVEN. The ledger names the cheapest and refuses everything else until it clears.

author: geoffdavis
body:
Phase 2 of pi-talos-home-ops#66, which put a nix daemon behind sshd on each RPi5 cluster node. The client half couldn't land until the pods generated their host keys, since `publicHostKey` is pinned per builder.

## Native armv7l, verified on these nodes

Not inherited from torrey's measurement — checked here: **`CONFIG_COMPAT=y`**, and an `arm32v7` image executes with **ELF class byte 1** and **32-bit virtual addresses** (`00ac0000-00b8b000`).

armv7l is the fleet's real bottleneck (windowpi) and the one thing no x86 or Apple Silicon machine here can do without emulation. This takes it from **one** native builder to **four**.

## Deliberately conservative where torrey isn't

| | torrey | talos nodes | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxJobs` | 2 | **1** | These also run the Kubernetes control plane, and **etcd shares their NVMe**. Its failure mode under load is fsync latency — surfacing as leader elections, not as anything labelled "disk". One job per node keeps build I/O clear of it. |
| `speedFactor` | 3 | **2** | Above nas-sdg's emulated 1, below torrey. Real ARM cores, but nodes with a day job — so nix prefers torrey and spills here. |

If etcd ever gets unhappy, **`maxJobs` is the lever** — not the DaemonSet.

## Access shape

Port **30022**, not 22: Talos runs no sshd of its own, so this is the DaemonSet's listener on the node's host network. `sshUser = root` is root **inside the container** — Talos has no such login — and every key is pinned to `nix-daemon --stdio` by a forced command, so it grants building and nothing else. Same client key nas-sdg and torrey already accept.

Host keys were collected from the running pods and persist on each node's ex-Longhorn partition; regenerating them means updating these literals.

Verified: `nix flake check` passes, lint clean, all three answer sshd on `172.29.51.{11,12,13}:30022` from birdrock.

author: durchnull
body:
```
   .              *                  .                         *
                            *
        *        .-.                             .                    .
              .-'   `-._                *
   .      .--'  ()  ()  `--.                          *
         (   ===  <##>  ===   )      .                        .
          `--.  ()  ()  .--'
      *       `-._   _.-'         .              *
                  `-'                                    .
        .                    *              .                     *
```

## WHAT CHANGED

**Not a version — v31 is still on the cabinet.** `main` stopped taking pushes.
A version reaches it by branch and pull request from now on, merge commit only,
and there is nobody who can go around it — no bypass actors on the ruleset, not
for the pilot who owns the place and not for the machines.

Two readings, as usual. `.githooks/pre-push` refuses every push to `main` while
the pilot is still at the keyboard, with the commands to fix it in the refusal;
the remote's **main is the scoreboard** ruleset refuses the same ones four
seconds later in github's own words. GR7 already said the history is not
editable. It now also says the front door is not a door.

Merge commit only is not fussiness: squashing would collapse three versions
into one and rebasing would hand every commit a new sha, and the book counts
versions off commits.

## WHAT IT DOES TO THE OTHERS

The **Ground Crew** lost its shortcut. Github will not accept the Actions app as
a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, which turned out to be the better
design — `book.yml` now branches, files, opens its own pull request and merges
it, so the paperwork goes through the same window as everybody else. Expect a
small merged pull request after every landing. Nobody has to read them; the book
passes over its own filing in silence, and merge commits stay invisible to the
chronicle, the ledger and the flight meter, all of which read `--no-merges`.

Whoever pilots here next meets the rule as a refusal with instructions in it,
rather than as a rejected push and a puzzled minute.

And this box changed. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` now ends the way a turn
at the keyboard ends — a ship drawn fresh every time, then what the next pilot
finds out by playing, then who else it happens to — with the same discipline
that a block this branch gave nothing to say gets deleted rather than filled
with "None". This pull request is written on it, and has one block fewer than
the template offers, which is the template working.

## THE TAPE

- [ ] I flew this build, and the tape is on `docs/RANKINGS.md`
- [x] or: this does not move the game, so there is nothing to fly

## YOUR MOVE

1. Read `GOLDEN_RULES.md` GR7 — that is the whole rule, and it is four
   paragraphs.
2. Merge it with **Create a merge commit**, which is the only button left.
3. Watch the ground crew file its own pull request a minute later. That is the
   workflow proving itself, and if it goes red the book is one commit stale and
   nothing else is hurt.

- persist objective fragrance/product ownership facts only: brand, name, product line, concentration, fragrance family, scent type, key notes, bottle size, amount remaining, purchase metadata, availability, and safe image metadata

- introduce a generic private-image processing contract while keeping Wardrobe's existing image contract intact; the same hardened Sharp implementation validates signatures/pixel bounds/animation, strips metadata, resizes, and converts to WebP

author: evetev-dev
body:
## Qué hace este PR

Añade la **interfaz gráfica** de Eve Studio: chat a la izquierda, previsualización en vivo a la derecha, con pestaña de código, copiar y descargar.

Estática y sin dependencias ni paso de compilación. Vercel sirve `public/` y la misma app expone `/api/chat` — el patrón que **ya usa `apps/website`** (estáticos + función en `api/`) y que está funcionando en producción, en lugar de montar un segundo proyecto solo para la UI.

### Decisiones de comportamiento

- **El token se pide una vez** y se guarda en `localStorage`. Sin él la API responde 401, así que la interfaz lo reclama antes de dejar generar.
- **Candado de reentrada:** cuatro intentos durante un envío producen **una sola llamada**. No es cosmético: cada llamada gasta créditos de Moonshot.
- **Errores accionables:** se traducen por código (401, 502, 504, falta de configuración en el servidor) en vez de mostrar el error crudo, y llevan **ícono además de color** (regla C5).
- **En el chat va un resumen**, no el volcado del HTML, que lo haría ilegible. El historial sí guarda el mensaje crudo, que es el contexto real del agente.
- El HTML generado se inyecta con `srcdoc` en un iframe con **`sandbox`**: se renderiza aislado y no puede tocar la página que lo contiene.

### Marca

Tokens desde el CDN con respaldo local en `:root`, Baloo 2 para titulares e Inter para interfaz, botones pill, foco visible y `prefers-reduced-motion`. **Un único botón coral en toda la vista** (regla C2), verificado en ejecución.

## 🐛 Un bug detectado al probar, y corregido

En el camino de error había un `historial.pop()`. Como los `push` ocurren **después** de la respuesta correcta, en ese punto no se había añadido nada de ese turno: el `pop()` borraba la respuesta del intercambio **anterior** y corrompía el contexto que se manda al agente.

Verificado midiendo el historial que viaja en cada petición:

| Turno | Resultado | Historial enviado |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | éxito | 0 |
| 2 | éxito | 2 |
| 3 | **fallo** | 4 |
| 4 | éxito | **4** ← no se corrompió |

## Cómo se verificó

Como llamar al agente de verdad gasta créditos y requiere las llaves, monté un **simulador local que imita los códigos y cuerpos de la función Python** y probé contra él el flujo completo:

- Guardar token → generar → burbujas de chat → el código llega al iframe → botones de copiar y descargar se activan.
- **Los cuatro caminos de error**, cada uno con su mensaje específico: agente caído (502), timeout (504), servidor sin `AGENTE_API_TOKEN` (503) y token inválido (401).
- Bloqueo de reenvío con respuesta lenta: 4 clics → 1 llamada, y el botón recupera su rótulo al terminar.
- Pestañas Vista previa / Código con `aria-selected` correcto, y el `sandbox` del iframe presente.
- Móvil (375 px): una columna, sin desbordamiento horizontal.

## Checklist (Definition of Done)

**Funcionalidad**
- [x] Flujo feliz y cuatro casos de error probados contra el simulador.
- [ ] **Probado contra Moonshot real** — no ejecutado: requiere las llaves, que solo están en tu entorno.

**Código**
- [x] `lint`, `typecheck` y `test` en verde — no-ops en `@evetev/eve-studio`.
- [x] Sin dependencias nuevas: HTML, CSS y JS planos.

**Seguridad**
- [x] El código generado se renderiza en iframe con `sandbox`.
- [x] El token no se escribe en el repo; vive en el navegador de cada persona.
- [x] Sin secretos añadidos.

**Accesibilidad**
- [x] Errores con ícono + texto, nunca solo color.
- [x] Pestañas con `role="tab"` y `aria-selected`; foco visible; `prefers-reduced-motion` respetado.
- [ ] Lighthouse/axe — **no ejecutado**.

## Riesgo conocido y pendiente

**El enrutado estático + función Python en el mismo proyecto** solo se confirma al desplegar. Está resuelto con `outputDirectory: "public"`, que es la misma forma que funciona hoy en `apps/website`. Al abrir la preview: la raíz debe mostrar la interfaz y `/api/health` devolver `{"ok": true}`.

**Falta proteger el acceso a la página.** El token cuida el endpoint, pero la URL es pública para quien la conozca. Para una herramienta interna lo razonable es activar **Deployment Protection** en el proyecto de Vercel y dejar el token como segunda capa. Anotado en el README.

author: connorxtan
body:
## Why

The Vercel Blob free tier caps "advanced operations" (list/put/delete) at 2,000/month. The gallery burned through them and Vercel paused the store for 30 days — every clip URL 403'd, even with the read-write token, taking the whole killcam gallery down.

## What

Storage now lives in Supabase project **ltn-killcam** (org LTN, ref `ghwdeywxlpqosusimxor`, us-east-1 — same coast as Vercel's functions):

- MP4s go in the public `killcams` Storage bucket (10 MB/file cap, mp4-only), served through Supabase's Cloudflare-fronted CDN with a 1-year immutable cache header (filenames are unique).
- Clip metadata and like/save/visit marks move from filename-parsing + marker blobs into Postgres (`clips`, `social_marks`, `visits`). Tables are RLS-enabled with no policies, so only the service key held by the functions can touch them.
- `lib/supabase-store.js` is the new storage layer; all four endpoints keep their exact request/response shapes, so **the shipped iOS app and the gallery page need no changes**.
- No more per-operation quota; free tier is 1 GB storage / 5 GB egress a month.

Vercel prod env already has `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` set and this code is already deployed from the working tree — merging makes git-based deploys match production so the next push to main doesn't revert to the dead Blob code.

## Verification

Production smoke-tested end to end: a real H.264 MP4 (AVFoundation-encoded, same codec family as the killcam pipeline) uploaded through the app's exact API contract, listed with correct metadata, served byte-identical with `video/mp4` + `accept-ranges: bytes` + working 206 partial responses (what iPhone Safari requires to play video), liked/unliked with correct counts, then deleted with cascade. Local e2e suite: 10/10.

author: dareinelt
body:
## Why

Attaching large photos to a chat message could push the base64-encoded payload past the model's context window (as seen with a "Kontextlimit erreicht" error on a multi-MB image). There was also no way to control the OpenAI Vision `detail` level (`low`/`high`), which trades off image fidelity against token cost.

## What changed

- **Client-side downscaling**: before an attached image is base64-encoded, it's now drawn onto a `<canvas>`, resized so its longest side is at most 1536px, and re-encoded as JPEG (quality 0.82). Animated GIFs are left untouched since canvas would flatten them to a single frame.
- **Detail level dropdown**: a new select (Auto / Niedrig / Hoch) appears next to the image attach button whenever images are pending. Choosing "Niedrig" or "Hoch" adds `"detail": "low"` / `"high"` to the corresponding `image_url` content part; "Auto" omits the field, preserving prior behavior.

Both changes are purely client-side (`index.php`) and don't touch the backend request handling in `api/chat.php`.

## Review notes

- Downscaling is skipped for images already under the size threshold, and for GIFs.
- Default dropdown value is "Auto" so existing conversations/requests are unaffected unless a user explicitly picks a detail level.

author: bhpcv252
body:
## What

Brings `main` up to date with two portability fixes finished on `dev` after PR #15 was merged, so `main`'s own `release.yml` run failed with the same Linux/macOS errors the original bug report showed.

## Why

PR #15 merged `dev` at a commit before these two fixes landed, so `main`'s automatic Release-workflow run (triggered by that merge) failed identically to the original report: Linux failed because `ubuntu-22.04` doesn't have `<format>` without a third-party PPA, and macOS failed because Apple's libc++ (through Xcode 15.4, what `macos-14` runners ship) doesn't implement `std::from_chars` for floating-point types.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: switched the Linux runner from `ubuntu-22.04` to `ubuntu-latest`, matching what `ci.yml` already relies on for a modern-enough default GCC.
- `src/Core/Config.cpp`: `parseDouble` now uses `std::from_chars` only where the standard library actually implements it for floating-point, falling back to a locale-neutralized `strtod` otherwise. Verified this fallback round-trips every value `std::format` can produce (denormals, ±infinity, NaN, extremes) under both the `C` locale and a comma-decimal locale, and rejects empty/garbage/leading-whitespace input identically to `std::from_chars`.
- `src/Core/README.md`: updated the one line describing `parseDouble`'s implementation to match.

## Tests

1188/1188 tests passing, both `YSQ_BUILD_GRAPHICS` states, with `-DYSQ_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON`. The fallback parser was additionally validated with a standalone round-trip test against 15 representative double values (including denormals, ±infinity, NaN) under two different locales before being adopted, since this is exactly the kind of platform-specific behavior that's easy to get subtly wrong.

author: teddychan
body:
The wording nit from the #57 review, which #58 didn't pick up. Prose only, on one hand-written page.

## The problem

> the Mac App Store build ... **links no third-party framework**

That is precise only if *framework* is read narrowly as an embedded `.framework` bundle — which is what was meant, since `Sparkle.framework` is the only one. Read plainly it says the sandboxed build carries no third-party code at all, and it does: **it still links DragonKit**, whose MIT notice sits a few rows further down this same page. A licences page is the one place that ambiguity is worth spending three words to remove.

## The change

Three lines, in the two places the claim is made:

- `links no third-party framework` → **`embeds no third-party framework`**
- the Sparkle section adds: **"It still links DragonKit, whose notice is below."**
- intro: `links no updater` → **`ships no updater`** — an updater is not something an app *links*

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| all 7 `<pre class="notice">` bodies vs `origin/main` | **byte-identical** — no licence text touched |
| `python3 -m pytest i18n/tests -q` | **18 passed** |
| `scripts/cache-bust.sh` | run last, as the publish invariant requires |

The page is hand-written, not generated by `build_i18n.py`, so no rebuild is involved — confirmed separately that a full rebuild + cache-bust reproduces `main` exactly.

## Related, not changed here

`clipmenu-2`'s `app/Sources/ClipMenu/AboutConfig.swift` carries the same phrasing in a code comment ("the sandboxed build links no third-party framework and must not claim one"). Same imprecision, but it is a comment in another repo and not user-visible, so I left it alone rather than widen this.

author: plykov
body:
## Summary

The identical application code passed 3-platform CI plus 10 local repetitions (#10, verified independently and by Codex), then failed the same `"Final commission must spawn and phase an Accuser boss"` assertion on a later CI run (macOS, triggered by the docs-only #11) with zero code changes in between. That proves the earlier fix — reset `EncounterDirector._tick` and let the engine's next scheduled frame pick it up — was never fully deterministic, just lower-probability than before.

Fix: call `EncounterDirector._process(0.0)` directly and synchronously at frame 5, at the exact point the test needs the boss to exist, instead of nudging engine-scheduled timing and hoping a frame lands right before frame 220. Combined with the existing `_physics_process(0.0)` fix for the phase update (#10), both halves of this assertion — boss spawns, boss reaches the required phase — are now driven by explicit synchronous calls the test controls, with no remaining dependency on how many real engine frames occur in a given window.

`PHASE2_SCOPE.md` updated to document this as a pattern worth remembering: a fix that passes CI and even 10 repeated local runs is not the same as a fix that removes a race — it can just make the race rarer. For anything timing-shaped in this codebase, prefer removing the race entirely (call the thing directly, synchronously) over reducing its probability.

Test-only change — no production code touched.

## Test plan

- [ ] `godot --headless --path . res://tests/campaign_smoke.tscn`, repeated at least 20-30 times in a loop (10 wasn't enough to catch the previous regression) — confirm the boss reliably spawns and reaches phase ≥ 2 every time
- [ ] `scripts/verify.ps1` / `scripts/verify.sh` on all three platforms

author: guarzo
body:
## Problem

`saleColumnsAliased` was maintained by hand next to `saleColumns` and had drifted by six columns:

    original_list_price_cents, price_reductions, days_listed,
    sold_at_asking_price, was_cracked, order_id

Both LEFT JOIN queries in `analytics_store.go` select the aliased list, so every sale loaded through `GetPurchasesWithSales` came back with those six fields zeroed — and a zeroed `int`/`bool` is indistinguishable from a genuine zero, so the loss was silent.

## Fix

- `saleColumns` becomes the single source of truth; `saleColumnsAliased` is derived from it by `aliasColumns`.
- Both scan paths (`scanSale` for the direct SELECT, `scanPurchaseWithSale` for the JOIN) now share one `saleNulls` / `saleScanDests` pair. Adding a column to the list without a destination is now a length mismatch, not a silent misalignment.
- `scanPurchaseWithSale` no longer re-declares ~23 `sql.Null*` locals inline.

Unifying on nullable destinations is strictly more permissive than the previous direct-struct scan, so the non-JOIN path cannot regress on rows it used to read.

## Tests

`internal/adapters/storage/postgres/sale_columns_test.go`:

- `TestSaleColumnsMatchScanDests` — arity of list vs. destinations.
- `TestSaleColumnsAliasedIsDerived` — every aliased entry is `s.` + the canonical entry.
- `TestSaleLoadsIdenticallyThroughBothPaths` — DB-backed; seeds a sale with **every** column populated to a non-zero value and requires the direct and JOIN reads to be `require.Equal`.

## Verification

- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` — clean
- `make test-postgres` — `ok ... 10.237s`; verbose run confirms the three new tests execute rather than skip
- Mutation check: adding a column to `saleColumns` without a destination fails `TestSaleColumnsMatchScanDests` (`should have 30 item(s), but has 29`)
- `make check` — passes (file-size warnings pre-existing, none in touched files)

### Update [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **3.6.0** to **9.1.1**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.1.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `14220 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14220>`_: Fixed a logic bug in :class:`pytest.RaisesGroup` which would might cause it to display incorrect "It matches `FooError()` which was paired with `BarError`" messages.


- `14591 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14591>`_: Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 which caused overriding a parametrized fixture with an indirect `pytest.mark.parametrize` to fail with "duplicate parametrization of '<fixture name>'".


- `14606 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14606>`_: Fixed ``list-item`` typing errors from mypy in :ref:`pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref>` ``argvalues`` parameter.


- `14608 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14608>`_: Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 where ``conftest.py`` files located in ``<invocation dir>/test*`` were no longer loaded as initial conftests when invoked without arguments.
  This could cause certain hooks (like :hook:`pytest_addoption`) in these files to not fire.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.1.0
   ```
   =========================

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes
---------------------------------------------------

- `14533 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14533>`_: When using :option:`--doctest-modules`, autouse fixtures with ``module``, ``package`` or ``session`` scope that are defined inline in Python test modules (not plugins or conftests) will now possibly execute twice.

  If this is undesirable, move the fixture definition to a ``conftest.py`` file if possible.

  Technical explanation for those interested:
  When using `--doctest-modules`, pytest possibly collects Python modules twice, once as :class:`pytest.Module` and once as a ``DoctestModule`` (depending on the configuration).
  Due to improvements in pytest's fixture implementation, if e.g. the ``DoctestModule`` collects a fixture, it is now visible to it only, and not to the ``Module``.
  This means that both need to register the fixtures independently.



Deprecations (removal in next major release)
--------------------------------------------

- `10819 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10819>`_: Added a deprecation warning for class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods (without ``classmethod``). Such fixtures set attributes on a different instance than the test methods use, leading to unexpected behavior. Use ``classmethod`` decorator instead -- by :user:`yastcher`.

  See :issue:`10819` and :issue:`14011`.


- `12882 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12882>`_: Calling :meth:`request.getfixturevalue() <pytest.FixtureRequest.getfixturevalue>` during teardown to request a fixture that was not already requested is now deprecated and will become an error in pytest 10.

  See :ref:`dynamic-fixture-request-during-teardown` for details.


- `13409 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13409>`_: Using non-:class:`~collections.abc.Collection` iterables (such as generators, iterators, or custom iterable objects) for the ``argvalues`` parameter in :ref:`pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref>` and :meth:`metafunc.parametrize <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize>` is now deprecated.

  These iterables get exhausted after the first iteration,
  leading to tests getting unexpectedly skipped in cases such as running :func:`pytest.main()` multiple times,
  using class-level parametrize decorators,
  or collecting tests multiple times.

  See :ref:`parametrize-iterators` for details and suggestions.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute is now deprecated.
  Use :meth:`config.getini() <pytest.Config.getini>` to access configuration values instead.

  See :ref:`config-inicfg` for more details.


- `14004 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14004>`_: Passing ``baseid`` to :class:`~pytest.FixtureDef` or ``nodeid`` strings to fixture registration APIs is now deprecated. These are internal pytest APIs that are used by some plugins.

  Use the ``node`` parameter instead for fixture scoping. This enables more robust node-based
  matching instead of string prefix matching.
  If you've used ``nodeid=None``, pass ``node=session`` instead.

  This will be removed in pytest 10.


- `14335 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14335>`_: The method of configuring hooks using markers, deprecated since pytest 7.2, is now scheduled to be removed in pytest 10.
  See :ref:`hook-markers` for more details.


- `14434 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14434>`_: The :option:`--pastebin` option is now deprecated.
  The same functionality is now available in an external plugin, :pypi:`pytest-pastebin`.
  See :ref:`pastebin-deprecated` for more details.


- `14513 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14513>`_: The private ``FixtureDef.has_location`` attribute is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10.
  See :ref:`fixturedef-has-location-deprecated` for details.


- `1764 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1764>`_: :func:`pytest.console_main` is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10.
  It was never intended for programmatic use; use :func:`pytest.main` instead.



New features
------------

- `12376 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12376>`_: Added :func:`pytest.register_fixture()` to register fixtures using an imperative interface.

  This is an advanced function intended for use by plugins.

  Normally, fixtures should be registered declaratively using the :func:`pytest.fixture <pytest.fixture>` decorator.
  Pytest looks for these fixture definitions during the collection phase and registers them automatically.
  For some plugin usecases the declarative interface can be cumbersome or unviable, in which case this imperative interface can be used.


- `14023 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14023>`_: Added `--report-chars` long CLI option.

author: afkcodes
body:
First green iOS build. **Do not merge — for architect review.**

Green run: https://github.com/afkcodes/rn-media/actions/runs/31322488036

## Root cause

The first-ever iOS build (run 31320994997) died at the app link step. `xcpretty`
printed the headline but dropped the body, so the symbol list was invisible.
With the raw log captured, the undefined symbols were the entire mpv client API:

```
Undefined symbols for architecture x86_64:
  "_mpv_create",   referenced from: rnmedia::MpvClient::MpvClient(...)  in libRnMediaPlayer.a(MpvClient.o)
  "_mpv_wait_event", ... "_mpv_command_async", "_mpv_initialize", "_mpv_observe_property",
  "_mpv_set_property", "_mpv_get_property", "_mpv_free", "_mpv_error_string",
  "_mpv_set_option_string", "_mpv_request_log_messages", "_mpv_terminate_destroy",
  "_mpv_unobserve_property", "_mpv_wakeup", "_mpv_set_property_string"
```

The generated `Pods-RnMediaPlayerExample.debug.xcconfig` carried **no**
`-framework "Mpv"` and **no** `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/RnMediaPlayer`
search path, and no `XCFrameworkIntermediates/RnMediaPlayer` directory was ever
created — CocoaPods believed `RnMediaPlayer` vendored nothing at all.

Cause: `exclude_files` is not source-only. `Sandbox::FileAccessor#paths_for_attribute`
passes `spec_consumer.exclude_files` as the exclude pattern for *every* file
attribute, `vendored_frameworks` included, and `ios/Frameworks/**/*` matches the
`.xcframework` bundle directories themselves (`**/` matches zero directories).
The guard written to keep the prebuilt binaries out of the *compile* step
removed them from the *link* step.

Note what this was **not**: the `React_RCTAppDelegate` / `CoreAudioTypes` /
`SwiftUICore` linker complaints are unrelated noise. `React_RCTAppDelegate` is
declared as a `framework module` inside RN 0.86's prebuilt `React.xcframework`
modulemap, so `import React_RCTAppDelegate` emits an autolink for a framework
that does not exist as a separate binary; the symbols come from `React.framework`.
All three are still present in the green build.

## Changes

- `packages/player/RnMediaPlayer.podspec` — narrow `exclude_files` for
  `ios/Frameworks` to `*.{swift,m,mm}`. Nothing under `ios/Frameworks` is matched
  by `source_files` anyway, so the guard keeps its intent and loses its side
  effect. Rationale documented inline.
- `.github/workflows/ios-build.yml`
  - tee raw `xcodebuild` output; an `if: failure()` step mines it (errors,
    undefined-symbol block, `Ld` invocation, generated xcconfigs, unpacked
    xcframework slices); logs + xcconfigs uploaded as an artifact.
  - assert right after `pod install` that `-framework "Mpv"` and the
    `RnMediaPlayer` xcframework search path reached the app target — this class
    of regression now fails in seconds with a named error.
  - drop `USE_CCACHE=1` and the `CC`/`CPLUSPLUS`/`LD`/`LDPLUSPLUS` overrides
    (ccache is not installed on the runner; CocoaPods warned about exactly that,
    and RN's own iOS CI does not pass them).
  - `-destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'` instead of a named simulator
    that matched several destinations.

## Verified in the green run

- `BUILD SUCCEEDED`, both simulator arches (arm64 + x86_64).
- All ten vendored frameworks linked and embedded into `RnMediaPlayerExample.app/Frameworks`.
- All Swift compiled for the first time — `HybridRnMediaAudioSession.swift`,
  `HybridRnMediaMediaSession.swift`, `ArtworkCache.swift`, `RemoteCommandBinding.swift`,
  `PositionProjection.swift`, `AppDelegate.swift`. No audio-session/media-session
  errors ever surfaced; they compile clean.
- 37 warnings total, **zero** from our own sources (the only three attributable
  to this repo are `-Wdocumentation-deprecated-sync` inside the vendored upstream
  `cpp/third_party/mpv/include/mpv/client.h`).

body:
## What

Routes every projection store entry point (Refresh, List, Get, TaskHistory, CommitHistory, Resolve, Advance, Invalidate) through a `withActiveDatabase` seam that recognizes SQLite's two "the cache file was pulled out from under this handle" verdicts — `SQLITE_READONLY_DBMOVED` (1032) and `SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE_NOENT` (5898) — reopens the replacement (rebuilding only if unusable), and redoes the operation, bounded at three attempts before returning a sanctioned contention refusal that `TestBuiltBinariesMutateOneRepositoryConcurrently` now recognizes as a legitimate lost race.

Workbook task: WB-01KZKGJW0YTPQEQDE68Y2DGJST — "A concurrent create can hit SQLITE_READONLY_DBMOVED instead of a contention answer".

## Why

Two processes share one projection at `<git-common-dir>/workbook/cache.sqlite`; a rebuild replaces it via temp-file + rename. A handle from before the rename fails its next write with 1032 (or transiently 5898, because SQLite locks live on inodes while the rollback-journal path is shared), and the CLI surfaced "run `workbook rebuild`" as an operational error — sometimes **after the Git ref was durably written**, inviting a duplicate-creating retry. This failed the v0.4.3 release gate twice consecutively (runs 31319572941 attempts 1–2) and measured 3 failures in 20 Linux runs. AGENTS.md's concurrency rules call for absorbing exactly this kind of race.

## Verification

- Two deterministic regression tests (barrier-interleaved Refresh redo; poisoned-stat Advance redo) — both red before the seam, green after; rename-count assertions prove the redo reopens the replacement rather than rebuilding over it (mutation-verified).
- A panic test pins the defer-released read lock, since `workbook serve` recovers handler panics and a leaked read lock would wedge the store permanently.
- 50 consecutive runs of `TestBuiltBinariesMutateOneRepositoryConcurrently` in a golang:1.26-bookworm container (pre-fix rate: 3 failures / 20 runs), plus `go test -short ./...` and full `internal/cli` + `internal/projection` locally.

## Adversarial review

Reviewed by an independent adversarial pass; all four findings verified and addressed: (1) major — the seam initially dropped `defer`-based unlocking, leaking `rebuildMu` on a panicking body (fixed with deferred unlocks + regression test); (2) the redo tests didn't pin reopen-over-rebuild (fixed with rename counters, mutation-verified); (3) the 5898 stat-gate missed the live handle being the journal-race victim — accepted with a stronger resolution than suggested: the gate was removed since ENOENT-on-unlink is contention by construction (a disk fault reports `SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE` instead); (4) stale "three wordings" doc and off-by-one line reference in the multiprocess test (fixed).

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Environment variables (`MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`, `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) were being accessed using the `env()` function directly within controllers and services (e.g., `PaymentController`, `GeminiService`).
🎯 Impact: When configuration caching is enabled in a Laravel production environment (via `php artisan config:cache`), the `env()` function returns `null` for variables not loaded inside the config files. This misconfiguration can lead to silent authentication failures and security boundaries evaluating against empty credentials (e.g. signature verification evaluating against `null`).
🔧 Fix: Mapped the required variables in `config/services.php` and updated `PaymentController` and `GeminiService` to pull those values using the `config()` helper method instead of `env()`.
✅ Verification: Ran `php artisan test` successfully. Manual code check via `grep` confirms these files no longer use `env()` directly for these secrets. Appended `.jules/sentinel.md` with these learnings.

author: arasz
body:
Fixes every issue found in the 1.5.0 manual tool sweep (`docs/reviews/2026-08-09-manual-tool-sweep-1-5-0.md`, #227).

## The headline defect was worse than the sweep found

The sweep reported that `memory_share_extract(mode=promote)` returns `unknown-hash` after already promoting earlier candidates — a misleading error. Reading the code showed the real damage: `PromoteAsync` **dequeues each candidate before sharing it** (deliberately, to claim it against a concurrent discard), on separate connections with no transaction and no try/catch. So the candidate that throws is already deleted and was never shared — **permanently lost**, not retried.

Root cause, verified against the live bank: nothing invalidated `promotion_queue` when the `entries` rows it points at were deleted or re-chunked. 19 orphaned rows had accumulated in ~a day, all from watched ADRs that were edited and re-ingested. **ai-raccoon's rank-1 candidate was one of them**, so every background pass destroyed the top candidate and promoted nothing. The gap was asserted as intended behaviour in a green test.

## Work packages

| WP | What | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| WP1 | `AFTER DELETE ON entries` trigger drops matching queue rows; `ai-raccoon extract prune [--apply]` clears rows orphaned before it existed; ADR-0022 | `PromotionQueueInvalidationTests` + storage/extraction suite |
| WP2 | Per-candidate isolation in `PromoteAsync`; `PromoteOutcome.Failures` / `ShareExtractResult.{SkippedDuplicates,Failures}` so a caller can tell what actually happened | `PromotionQueueServicePromoteRaceTests` + hosted-service + MCP |
| WP3 | `ToolRefusals.PrefixFor` walks the base chain; `ArgumentException` family maps to `invalid-argument`. Fixes `"An error occurred invoking 'X'."` for all 22 tools, both binding failures and in-body guard clauses | `ToolRefusalsTests` |
| WP5 | `foreign-subject` no longer fires on ids inside brackets; the silent `+0.10` gets its own `many-foreign-projects` tag; the `mid-sentence` channel boundary is pinned by tests | scoring suite |

**No scoring weight, prior or clamp changed.** The calibration fixture that could validate one is deliberately uncommitted, so a weight change would ship unmeasured. Detector correctness only.

## Design decisions

- **Trigger, not per-call-site invalidation** — five deleters today and every future one would be a hand-maintained list that drifts (`derive-or-delete-the-list`). Additive DDL, so no schema-version bump and existing banks get it on next open.
- **Per-candidate isolation, not batch atomicity** — atomicity would span two store abstractions with no precedent, and would let one poison candidate roll back a good batch forever.
- **A claimed-but-stale row is dropped, never re-queued** — propose re-adds it if the entry still exists, and re-queuing would reopen the race the claim exists to close.
- **No new metric instrument** — the Warning log and the tool response carry the signal.

## Verification

Every package wrote its failing test first and *watched it fail*, including the deliberate near-misses: WP1 built the trigger without its `NOT EXISTS` guard and watched a live sibling's candidate get wiped; WP2 used a bare `catch (Exception)` and watched cancellation get swallowed; WP5 temporarily wired the mid-sentence penalty into each branch and watched the boundary tests flip.

Merged result: `dotnet build` clean, **294 tests pass** across all four packages' gates combined.

author: jmgirard
body:
A refused encode used to leave a zero-byte file sitting where a result should
be, and said nothing about it. FFmpeg creates its output before it knows the
command will work, and truncates an existing one to zero on its way to failing.

`ffm_run()` now deletes that file on a non-zero exit and names it in the abort
it already raised. Every Layer 1 and Layer 2 execution path inherits this,
`ffm_batch()` included, because each reaches that one site.

One exception: `overwrite = FALSE` against a path that already existed. FFmpeg
was told not to replace that file, so neither does tidymedia — narrowed to
pre-existence, so a non-overwriting run that *created* its output still gets it
cleaned up. If the removal itself fails, the abort says the file is still there
rather than claiming a cleanup that did not happen.

Not covered, and recorded as such: Layer 0's `ffmpeg()`, which runs a verbatim
command string it cannot parse for an output path.

- No new export and no new argument: `git diff master..HEAD -- NAMESPACE man/`
  is empty.
- `devtools::check()` Status: OK — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
- Rationale recorded as D045.

author: primetheus
body:
## Summary

Root-cause fix for the "My Notes text disappears on tap" defect, plus two window-management defects confirmed by an adversarial Codex review. The headline defect was diagnosed by running the Android app empirically (emulator build from the parity checkout) side-by-side with iOS: tapping a My Notes row's collapsed verse quote *expands* into the styled passage on Android but blanked the row on iOS, because iOS hardcoded `osisFragment: null` in every Bible bookmark payload while the shared `BookmarkText` component renders exactly that fragment in its expanded state.

## Scope

- `Sources/BibleUI/Sources/BibleUI/Bible/BibleReaderAnnotationPayloadFactory.swift` — per-bookmark OSIS fragment serialization
- `Sources/BibleCore/Sources/BibleCore/Services/WindowManager.swift` — links-window clone category reset; closed-row visibility
- `Sources/BibleUI/Tests/BibleUITests/BookmarkReaderBridgeTests.swift` — fragment contract test

No shared-frontend changes; `BookmarkText.vue` is byte-identical to Android's and simply starts receiving the data it always expected.

## Contract references

- Android baselines: `BookmarkControl.addText` renders each serialized bookmark's verse range from the bookmark's own module (default-Bible fallback) via `readOsisFragment` with null-on-`OsisError`; `bookmarksForVerseRange(withText = true)` applies it to chapter, My Notes, and StudyPad documents alike. Window parity: Android's `showLink` overwrites a chained links window's cloned page synchronously, and `WindowRepository.visibleWindows` renders only `VISIBLE` windows.
- Commits follow the locked commit-message standard.

## Change details

1. **`bibleBookmarkJSON` now emits the real fragment**: stored source ordinals resolve in the bookmark's own versification, map into the resolved module's domain (bookmark module first, active-module fallback), and render through the existing `BibleReaderInstalledScriptureFragmentBuilder` with Android's null-on-failure semantics. Applies to chapter, My Notes, and StudyPad payloads — the same universality as Android.
2. **Chained links windows can no longer boot into My Notes**: `createManagedWindow` resets a cloned `mynote` page category to `bible` for links windows. Android clones the same state but overwrites it synchronously before it can be observed; iOS's asynchronous pane boot could restore the clone first (Codex-confirmed, explains phantom My Notes panes deepening the links chain).
3. **Synced `closed` windows stay hidden**: `refreshWindows` excludes `closed` rows from `visibleWindows` like Android's VISIBLE-only rendering. Local close deletes rows; `closed` arrives only via synced/imported Android workspaces.

## Validation evidence

- `BibleUITests` (BookmarkReaderBridgeTests 54, ReaderBridgeParityTests 21, ReaderNavigationTests 86): 161 tests, 0 failures; `BibleCoreTests` (WorkspaceSyncRestoreTests, WorkspaceWindowStoreTests, WindowCloneFidelityTests): 76 tests, 0 failures (iPhone 17 simulator).
- Empirical Android baseline: and-bible standardGithub debug build (v5.1.1112) on a Pixel 7 API-34 emulator, exercising the exact My Notes tap flow.
- `git diff --check`, docblock and commit-message guardrails pass for both commits.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Fragment rendering adds per-bookmark SWORD reads to bookmark-bearing document emissions — the same cost Android pays on every `addText`; ranges are verse-scale.
- SQLite-backed bookmark modules fall back to the active module's fragment (Android falls back to the default Bible); a dedicated SQLite fragment path can follow if divergent-module fidelity matters there.

## Issue closure

Closes: none — follow-up fixes from empirical parity testing and the Codex window-management review; no open issue maps to them (verified against the GitHub issue list).

author: steipete
body:
No issue: this is a bounded maintainer-requested bug fix.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a Cloud Worker session could remain on an inert `/new` page throughout worker provisioning, with no durable progress and failures that could disappear with the route. It also fixes the user-reported live error where selecting GPT-5.6 High could be rejected as unsupported after ChatGPT catalog discovery admitted Platform-only alias rows with incorrect reasoning metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

There were two owner-boundary failures:

1. The OpenAI plugin admitted Platform-only bare `gpt-5.6` and `chat-latest` rows into the ChatGPT catalog. A bare row without reasoning metadata published `reasoning: false`, so generic validation correctly rejected High. Catalog admission now filters those Platform-only IDs while preserving the authoritative metadata of valid ChatGPT models.
2. `NewSessionPage` synchronously owned durable session creation, worker dispatch/provision/sync/start, first send, and navigation. The application-lifetime Cloud startup coordinator now owns continuation after durable session creation. The page navigates immediately, Gateway-owned durable placement transitions flow through coalesced `sessions.changed` events, canonical requested/provisioning/syncing/starting/sending progress renders in the created session, and the initial message is sent only after active ownership. Runtime ownership is isolated per canonical session key, and framed v2 recovery records persist per session so reconnect and stale-client takeover cannot cancel or delete another session's work. Legacy migration rolls back safely if the replacement record cannot be committed.

The rebase resolution also preserves the latest `main` route-owned draft behavior, including destination-owned input, terminal startup, and worktree creation. This changes no config, protocol, generated baseline, or performance budget.

## User Impact

Cloud Worker startup now has an immediate visible destination and clear progress instead of appearing frozen. The accepted prompt survives route changes exactly once, send waits for active worker ownership, and terminal startup failures remain visible in the created session. Valid GPT-5.6 ChatGPT models retain their supported High reasoning capability.

## Evidence

### Synthetic after screenshot

![Synthetic Control UI Cloud session with High effort selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/192e4c72-b9b3-4289-b7d8-0f10ba930790)

The user-provided before screenshot was reproduced live but is omitted from this public PR because signed-in session/sidebar data could not be safely captured. The attached after screenshot is synthetic and contains only fixture identities.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup-failure.e2e.test.ts` — 9 browser E2E tests passed.
- Blocked-chunk browser proof commits the created chat route and shows pending startup before the runtime loads; dispatch and send remain gated.
- Two-session same-scope proof advances both Cloud sessions independently with no delete, abort, or environment destroy, while preserving the newer durable recovery record.
- Reconnect proof covers stale-client takeover, framed v2 per-session migration, exact-key cleanup, and rollback that preserves the legacy record when replacement persistence fails.
- The focused public OpenAI provider test passes against the shared upstream route contract used to classify catalog aliases.
- Earlier focused Gateway, Control UI, and OpenAI coverage passed 369 tests; private-observer coverage passed 60 tests; lazy-coordinator coverage passed 10 tests.
- Source-blind behavior validation passed immediate routing, visible placement phases, send-after-active ownership, stable idempotency, exactly one prompt, route survival, and visible failure.

### Static and build proof

author: whiteoakowl
body:
## Summary

A full pass through auth, session, dependency, file-upload, and output-escaping surfaces, verified with real requests/uploads rather than assumed.

**Confirmed already solid (no change):** parameterized SQL throughout, bcrypt password comparison, open-redirect protection on the login `next` param, correctly-scoped `requireAdmin`/`requireFullAdmin` gates, and image/document upload filtering (already requires mimetype+extension agreement and deliberately excludes SVG).

## Fixed

- **Session cookie had no `secure` flag.** Used `secure: 'auto'` (marks Secure only when the connection genuinely is HTTPS) instead of hardcoding `true`, which would've broken login on this app's typical deployment (plain `http://` on a LAN). Added an opt-in `TRUST_PROXY` env var for reverse-proxy deployments, documented in README/.env.example.
- **No brute-force protection on `/admin/login`.** Added a small, dependency-free in-memory limiter — 5 failed attempts per IP per 15-minute window, resets on success.
- **CSRF investigated, not bolted on.** `sameSite: 'lax'` (already set) blocks cookies on cross-site state-changing requests in every modern browser. Confirmed comprehensively that zero GET routes anywhere in the app mutate the database — the one gap that setting doesn't cover. A full token system would mean touching 40+ forms for marginal benefit over an already-solid setup.
- **`xlsx@0.18.5` has an unpatched prototype-pollution advisory** in the exact code path this app's import features use. Added centralized sanitization in the one shared `readRowsFromFile` function every import route funnels through. Verified against a deliberately hostile payload through a real import-merge-confirm flow.
- **6 duplicated multer instances had no `fileFilter`** — any file type was accepted for spreadsheet imports. Centralized a new filter and wired it into all 6. Verified a legitimate `.csv` still imports, a `.exe` gets rejected.
- **Hardened one fragile manual escape** (`admin-members-import-confirm.ejs`) that was correct today only by accident of which quote character its attribute happened to use. Swapped to standard EJS auto-escaping.
- **Added `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` globally.**

## XSS sweep

Checked every `<%- %>` (unescaped EJS output) in the codebase (57 files). All but 5 were `<%- include(...) %>` (always safe). Of the 5: 3 already route through a purpose-built `jsonScriptSafe()` helper, 1 renders badge markup from a renderer that already escapes every dynamic value, and the 5th is the fix above.

## Testing

Every fix verified live — real HTTP requests, real file uploads (including a deliberately hostile CSV payload with embedded `<script>`, quotes, and ampersands, confirmed to round-trip through the full merge flow without executing and land correctly in the database as inert data), rate-limiter unit tests, and a full syntax+lint+boot regression after every change.

author: timofeylednev
body:
`hss.dll` was registration without implementation: every entry point returned success and no PCM was ever produced, so JumpyBall had no way to notice it had no audio. Four names the game imports had no handler at all — the `const wchar_t*` overloads of `load` (only the `void*, bool` ones were registered; overloads mangle differently) and both volume getters (only the setters were there).

HSS hands over a filename and expects the library to decode it, so this adds the decoder:

* `.wav` reuses coredll's `decode_pcm_wave` rather than growing a second set of rounding bugs.
* `.tkm` is a renamed Protracker module, so `decode_clip` tries both decoders against the content — the extension is not load-bearing on a device and it isn't here either. The renderer is `pocket_kernel:: tracker`, parser plus mixer with no guest-memory awareness so it is testable on its own.
* A DC blocker on the mix bus. JumpyBall's samples carry means of +65 to +99 out of ±128, which an Amiga's AC-coupled output discarded and a modern DAC will not; it had pinned music1's mean at +6515.
* Voice groups, so `stopMusics` silences music without cutting effects that are still playing — JumpyBall calls it on every level change.
* Decodes cached by path behind an `Arc`: the game re-loads `mainmenu.tkm` into a fresh object three times before the first level, and each load was re-rendering 148.5 s of stereo.

Also carries the four coredll fixes that boot Toy Golf to its main menu, and documents the audio subsystem as docs/AGENTS.md §11.

Verified: zero unimplemented calls (was 7), all 16 HSS entry points dispatching across 48 calls including `playSound`, and a 22050 Hz stereo capture that is 100% non-zero at peak 20228. No audio device on this machine, so the evidence is the trace and the PCM, not listening.
