## Summary

Makes the v111 listening bulk backfill self-diagnosing so future provider stops identify their exact safe cause without another forensic code change.

- records provider deferral kind and exact safe reason (`retry`, provider error, provider halt, or repeated-item circuit breaker)
- records retry eligibility time when a provider deferral is caused by an explicit dated retry
- records aggregate provider outcome reason counts without track IDs, titles, artists, tokens, URLs, or secrets
- distinguishes UsageTracker denial causes such as `daily_cap`, `per_run_cap`, `policy_denied`, or unavailable usage hooks
- persists usage-block diagnostics before stopping, while still making zero provider calls after denial
- carries diagnostics across internal 100-step chunks
- persists the aggregate diagnostic snapshot inside the existing maintenance checkpoint for post-run inspection
- includes diagnostics in every bulk progress line and the final aggregate summary
- preserves current item/provider/global safety policy, provider pacing, quota accounting, provider ownership, immutable source observations, and focused fail-fast behavior
- preserves legacy UsageTracker compatibility when old state lacks explicit cap fields
- adds synthetic regression coverage for Spotify provider failure, MusicBrainz retry, retry eligibility, repeated malformed-item circuit breaking, explicit Spotify quota halt, usage-cap diagnosis, durable usage-block checkpointing, safe checkpoint persistence, diagnostic carry across chunks, and aggregate-only log output

## Production evidence behind the change

The post-PR-#102 separately authorized production invocation attempted 473 provider calls and durably persisted 472 results. MusicBrainz was deferred and later Spotify was also deferred. Read-only derived-state inspection identified MusicBrainz as `retry:http_503`, but the final Spotify provider-level cause could not be recovered because provider-scoped failures correctly leave the track untouched and the bulk summary only retained the provider name.

This PR closes that observability gap generically rather than adding another provider-specific exception. It does not alter which outcomes are item-, provider-, or global-scoped.

## Review corrections found and resolved

The implementation/review loop caught and corrected the following before merge readiness:

- missing legacy compatibility when UsageTracker state lacks explicit cap fields
- the persisted maintenance context initially did not expose the usage gate's safe block reason to the bulk wrapper
- usage denial was diagnosed in memory but initially was not durably checkpointed before stopping
- retry diagnostics initially retained the retry reason but not the exact `nextEligibleCheckAt` needed to decide when a provider can safely be retried
- a stale regression assertion still expected usage denial to perform no persistence at all; it now proves the intended diagnostic-checkpoint-only write while provider and derived writes remain blocked
- continuity documentation initially stopped before the fifth production bulk invocation; `LIVEVAULT_STATE.md`, `LIVEVAULT_DECISIONS.md`, and the Build D runbook now record the 473/472 result, the confirmed MusicBrainz `http_503`, the unrecoverable historical Spotify reason, and the durable self-diagnostic policy

A final review of the exact-head diff found no further blocking issues. The branch is directly ahead of current `main` and has no unresolved review threads.

## Continuity

Updated:
- `docs/LIVEVAULT_STATE.md`
- `docs/LIVEVAULT_DECISIONS.md`
- `docs/DATA_AUTOMATION_LISTENING_BUILD_D.md`

`docs/LIVEVAULT_BUILD_STATE.json` remains deterministic with `appVersion` and `serviceWorkerCacheVersion` both at v111, so no generated build-state content change is required.

## Validation

Exact-head PR QA run `31333017038` / #945 passes at `c6d7e95c2244b074f36fdee2e9c671b4fdd13851`:

- unit tests and safety checks
- JavaScript syntax
- version/cache synchronization

- Cloudflare Builds configuration validation
- synthetic fixture validation

- QA safety checks and whitespace validation
- desktop Chromium QA
- mobile Chromium QA

Cloudflare synthetic preview also deployed successfully for the exact head. Automated QA used synthetic fixtures/fake backend only; it did not call live providers or production R2.

## Production boundary

No production provider calls, production R2 writes, production workflows, deployment, or backfill invocation are part of this PR. Production resumption remains separately authorized after review and merge.

La excepción transversal de `h0-sesion-authoptions` **venció el 2026-08-08**. Su propio texto lo prescribe: «un permiso que nadie retira es un permiso permanente». Su PR ya mergeó.

Pero retirarla no se podía. Cuatro pruebas de `ownership-gate.test.mjs` leían `h0.excepcionTransversal` sin preguntar si existía, así que borrar la clave —lo único que el candado te pide hacer— rompía la suite. Y esa suite es el gate `tests` de **todo** el repositorio.

No es teórico. La prueba «la que está escrita hoy sigue vigente» se puso roja sola a las 00:00Z del 2026-08-09, y ese día las **siete** corridas de PLATAFORMA de la cohorte de medición de La Fragua murieron con `gates_failed:tests` — en seis carriles distintos, tocando archivos distintos, ninguno relacionado con la excepción.

Ahora **no haber ninguna es el estado sano**:

- `nadie más que H0 puede declarar una` admite cero; sigue prohibiendo dos, o una en otro carril.
- `sin excepción, H0 alcanza exactamente sus propias rutas` — el nuevo lado del candado: comprueba que la escotilla quedó **cerrada**, no sólo que estuviera bien abierta.
- Las cuatro que describen una excepción concedida viven bajo `describe.skipIf`.
- `un carril de construcción NO puede concederse una` **sale** del bloque condicional: usa un carril sintético y tiene que correr siempre.

author: zkrebbekx
body:
Closes #578.

`restoreGlobals` captured `otel.GetTracerProvider()` — the global **delegating wrapper**, not what sits behind it — so setting it back was a no-op. The runtime says so in the line right before the failure:

```
"Setting tracer provider to its current value. No delegate will be configured"
```

Once `TestInitWithEndpoint` installed an SDK provider as the delegate it was permanent for the process, and on the second iteration the test asserting a non-recording span saw a recording one.

It now installs an explicit no-op, which restores the observable behaviour a fresh process starts with — what the helper was always trying to do.

CI runs `-count=1`, so this never failed there. It blocked the `-count=2` run a release review wants, which is how it surfaced.

**With #574 drained as well, `go test ./... -count=2` now passes across the whole repo** — it did not before. That is the first end-to-end evidence the CI flakiness class is actually settled rather than retried around.

Mutation-checked: restoring the wrapper capture makes it fail again.

body:
## Summary

Two real bugs reported and fixed:

- **Meal templates were unreachable unless you'd already saved one.** Now always renders with a "+ New template" button, an empty state, and a create-from-scratch mini-form, moved up right after the meal composer.
- **There was no actual Insights destination.** Replaced the invisible conditional Home snippet with a real `renderInsights()` view wired into the bottom nav as a 4th tab — stat tiles (sessions, kcal burned, food logged, weight trend, sleep avg, recovery) plus the full insight list with a proper empty state.

**Tab bar**: expanded 3→4 columns, sliding indicator extended, switched to icon-above-label so longer professional names (Training/Nutrition/Wellness/Insights) fit cleanly. Internal `activeTab` keys unchanged.

**Food tab restructuring**: composer → draft review → templates → "Today's trackers" (supplements/weight/water) → today's log.

**Color system**: fixed two real collisions — `weight-card` reused "success green", `supplement-card` reused "review-due purple". Both moved to blue, joining `water-card` as the "today's vitals" family.

**Estimated calories burned per workout** — MET-based estimate (session type × latest logged weight × duration), clearly labeled as an estimate on the completion screen, in History (summary tile + per-row), and in Insights.

**Wellness checklist now names real products**, sourced from the user's own hygiene routine PDF (linked in `REP_HEALTH_GUIDE.sources.drive`) instead of generic instructions — Bobai Oil Defense SPF50, Pardonotx, Rivoli/Mood Vanilla Shower Gel, Nivea, Listerine, Keratin AD, and the full Kerella/Nizapex hair-treatment schedule. This also **fixed a real discrepancy**: the app's hair schedule had Saturday as a wash+mask day and no Sunday treatment, but the actual doctor-guided routine has Saturday as a non-wash rest day (mask moved to Wednesday) and Sunday carries a Kerella dose. Added a new "After work" section and weekly/monthly reference lists (shown in the Full Care Plan overlay). Preserved the exact array positions the non-negotiables tracking hardcodes, verified explicitly.

**Daily sleep log** in Recovery — no HealthKit access from a PWA, so this is manual entry: bedtime + wake time read off the Apple Watch and typed in, with automatic hours calculation (midnight-crossing handled), a 7-day average, and history with delete. The weekly check-in's sleep field now prefills from this live average. Found and fixed a real bug while wiring it up: `updateCheckin()` was eagerly persisting whatever the form showed on every render, silently locking in the first-ever value and shadowing the fallback logic — fixed the priority order so the live daily average always wins once real data exists. New Insights tile + an automatic insight when the average drops below the configured minimum.

**Activity logging for unstructured sports** (padel, football, basketball, swimming, cycling, tennis, or a custom "other" name) — a lightweight, non-guided flow distinct from the structured Training sessions: pick a sport, enter duration and RPE, optional notes, save. MET-based calorie estimate reuses the same weight/duration model as workouts. Entries appear in History with the right label/RPE/kcal (previously would have crashed, since activity records don't have an exercise/session lookup) and sync to Notion through the existing Workout Type select property (previously silently mislabeled as "Recovery").

Bumped the service worker cache (v25 → v29 across these commits) and ran `scripts/sync-static.mjs` throughout.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` on all JS/data files after every change
- [x] `dist/client` vs `outputs` sync diff clean after every change
- [x] Playwright smoke tests across all of the above: tab labels/Insights tile rendering, template empty-state and manual creation, weight/supplement card colors, a forced 45-minute session producing the correct calorie estimate, non-negotiables tracking the right checkbox after the full hygiene data rewrite, Full Care Plan showing the corrected hair schedule and new sections, product names visible in the checklist, the sleep log's math/persistence/delete/Insights-tile/check-in-prefill, and logging a padel session + a custom "other" activity end-to-end (History row, RPE/kcal display, Insights) — zero console errors throughout

body:
Collapses the research programme into the tool the owner actually asked for: a single CLI that reports how full a Claude Code session's context window is.

## What lands

- **`vitals.py`** — one stdlib-only file. `--self`, fleet `-l`, prefix lookup, `-H`/`-i`/`-j`, and an edge-triggered `--monitor` built for Claude Code's Monitor.
- **User-owned policy.** Bands, thresholds, exit codes and the *instruction text* all come from a JSON file. The tool measures; the policy decides.
- **`tests/FMEA.md`** — 45 failure modes, 25 of them silent, each naming the test that catches it.
- **97 tests**, a drift guard, and a mutation harness (9/9 caught).
- **CI** — 6 jobs across Linux/macOS/Windows on Python 3.9 and 3.13.

## Repo shape

Root shows `vitals.py` and `README.md`. The 17 research documents move to a gitignored `.meta/` — still on disk, out of the repo view. Earlier commits retain them; that is deliberate.

## Two properties worth protecting

`vitals.py` must keep working as **one file with no project around it** — that is what makes it copyable and cheap enough to run from a per-turn hook. Enforced by an AST-walking test and a CI job that runs it in a directory with no `pyproject.toml`.

Exit codes are a contract: `0` healthy, `1` attention, `2` act now, `64` usage error, `69` could-not-determine. `69` is deliberately not `0` — unmeasurable is not healthy.

## Not included

The `UserPromptSubmit` hook is documented with its trade-offs and **not installed**. `~/.claude/settings.json` is untouched.

author: yjack0000
body:
Reworks the voice keyboard UI (feedback from dogfooding: it looked flat and dead) and bumps the iOS build to 6 so the release can carry the fix.

## The problems

- Hard-coded 216pt height inside SwiftUI, fighting the edge-pinned host constraints.
- A static "Listening…" line — no sign the session on the other side of the App Group was actually alive.
- `.buttonStyle(.plain)` keys with zero press feedback; flat equal-width caps.
- Colors followed the **system** appearance, so a dark-themed host app got a light keyboard in light mode.

## The fix

- **Live pulse**: a three-bar indicator that keeps breathing while listening; the mic control turns into a red **Stop**. Deliberately not a level meter — the audio lives in the container app, and streaming real levels across the App Group per-frame would cost far more than the reassurance is worth. It says "still running", nothing it can't know.
- **Press feedback**: a custom `ButtonStyle` darkens keys and the mic under the finger.
- **Right appearance**: follows the host field's `keyboardAppearance` (re-read on `textDidChange`), not the system — a dark app gets a dark keyboard even in light mode. New `KBTheme` centralizes the palette since the extension can't reach the app's `Theme`.
- **Layout**: a settled 258pt height constraint (`.defaultHigh`, so landscape can still compress) replaces the internal 216; the transcript preview sits in its own rounded well at a fixed height so it never jumps.
- Minimal key row (globe / space / return / delete) unchanged in function — still types without Full Access (4.4.1).
- zh-Hant added for the two reworded strings.

## Verification

- `xcodebuild` app + keyboard extension → **BUILD SUCCEEDED** (iPhone 17 Pro sim).
- 1:1 layout preview of all four states (listening / idle / light pressed / no-Full-Access) reviewed.
- Not yet run on device — the live feel should be confirmed once on TestFlight.

Bumps `CFBundleVersion` to 6 for the 1.1 release build.

author: gordo-v1su4
body:
## What

- **Tabbed browser rail.** The clip bank was a full-width strip above the rack; the FX library a column beside it. Both are "things you drag onto a slot", so they share one 160px rail with `FX | CLIPS` tabs — using the `sideRailTab` store that was already declared and never wired. `ClipTray.svelte` is deleted, replaced by `SideRail.svelte` + `rack/ClipBrowser.svelte`. **PGM rail is untouched and always visible.**
- **BANK FOR SECTION** block at the top of the FX tab, with `⤓ RECALL BANK TO RACK` — ported from the `test_media/refining-beat-surfer-ui_v2` prototype. AUTO-BANK was rearranging the rack with nothing on screen saying what it was rearranging into.
- **MIN ALL · ARRANGE** collapses the rack *and* opens the dock in one gesture, and latches lit while active. The dock now takes the freed height instead of leaving a black void under it.
- **Dock rebuilt as a step matrix** — one row per rack slot × 16 columns. One grid declaration owns every column edge, so the ruler, the trigger lane and all ten slot rows cannot drift apart. Replaces the single row of fat cells plus the separate PAINT selector.
- **Onsets plumbed through.** Essentia has been returning `onsets` all along and `AudioEngine.applyRhythmAnalysis` discarded them. They now feed a trigger lane that folds the track's hits onto the bar. Seconds→beats uses the hosted beat grid, not constant BPM, so a drifting track doesn't smear its back half into the wrong sixteenth.
- **AUDIO/MIDI is a real route**, not just a display toggle — `AppLoop` previously let a MIDI layer win by merely existing, which made loading one irreversible.
- Renamed to **BEATSMAXXER PRO** (top bar, tab title, access gate).

## Verification

- `bun run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `bun run test` — 317 passed, 2 skipped
- `bun run build` — clean
- Driven in the browser at 1720×980: column alignment between the trigger lane and both the first and last matrix rows verified identical; zero gap between the dock and the bottom of the rack column; no horizontal or vertical page overflow; `RECALL BANK TO RACK` confirmed to swap all ten slots.

## Known gap

The matrix is still one bar on a loop sitting under a song-length section strip, so a 16-bar VERSE draws the same sixteen columns sixteen times — there is no position in it that maps to a position in the song. The linear song timeline that fixes this (cuts at absolute bar positions, sections seeded from Essentia's `structural_segments`, MIDI ticks at true song positions) is the next change, tracked separately.

author: gpolcode
body:
## Why

`copyNote()` discarded the boolean `Clipboard.copy()` returns and set the success flag unconditionally:

```ts
this.clipboard.copy(buildNorthernSkyNote(...));
this.copied.set(true);
```

`copy()` from `@angular/cdk/clipboard` returns `false` when the write fails - clipboard locked down by browser policy or an extension, or the synchronous copy rejected. The panel showed the green "Copied to clipboard." confirmation regardless, so a raid lead pasted into the game and found an empty or stale buffer with no idea the copy had failed.

## What changed

`copyNote()` reads the returned boolean and drives both states from it, so the confirmation and the failure message are mutually exclusive. `openPanel()` resets both, matching how it already reset the confirmation.

Failure copy: **"Clipboard write failed. Retry the copy."** - it names what happened and what to do, per the writing rules. It renders with `text-[var(--critical)]`, the failure tone token already used for error text elsewhere in the app.

No manual-copy fallback (a selectable textarea) was added - the UI has no such affordance today and that would be new functionality rather than a fix.

## Verification

`npm test` (1078 tests, 2 new), `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` all pass. The new specs fake `Clipboard` to return each outcome and assert through `mountVm` that a successful copy shows only the confirmation and a failed copy shows only the failure message.

## Review notes

One of a series of independent bug-fix PRs from a review of the newer features. Two sibling PRs touch this same component for unrelated defects (the silent load-error and the empty-panel/persistence bug), so expect small conflicts depending on merge order; this diff is confined to the clipboard result handling.

author: 577-industries
body:
Lint has been red on main since ~2026-07-06 on an unchanged tree. Two independent toolchain-drift causes:

**1. mypy could not parse numpy's stubs.** `[tool.mypy] python_version = "3.11"` makes mypy analyse *as* 3.11, so it rejects numpy's PEP 695 `type` statements:
```
numpy/__init__.pyi:737: error: Type statement is only supported in Python 3.12 and greater  [syntax]
```
This is **not** a stale mypy pin — reproduced on mypy **2.3.0** (current), and the dependency is already an open `mypy>=1.10` bound, so bumping the floor changes nothing. Targeting 3.12 is the fix.

Runtime support for 3.11 is **unchanged**: `requires-python = ">=3.11"` stays and the test matrix still runs 3.11. The trade-off is that mypy no longer catches 3.12-only stdlib usage that would break on 3.11 — the 3.11 test job covers that at runtime.

**2. `ruff format` drift** from newer ruff versions arriving via dependabot.

Fixes the lint half of #15.

### Verification
Ran the full lint job locally against this branch:
```
ruff check .          -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check . -> all files already formatted
mypy                  -> Success: no issues found
```

- Смена работы: три оффера на столе, у каждого множитель и набор эффектов — чем больше множитель, тем больше минусов. Эффект про то, кто в компании приносит деньги (разработчики/продажники/контент/управленцы). Обновить стол можно трижды.
- Балансовая находка ботами: мини-игра платила фиксированные 60 тыс независимо от эпохи — в 2008-м это два найма даром. Пол убран, награда пропорциональна эпохе.

author: bdart
body:
Makes the appointment organizer window a first-class add-in surface and hardens the appointment↔email partition throughout.

## What's in here

**Surface**
- Manifest activation rule (`ItemIs Appointment/Edit`) + `AppointmentOrganizerCommandSurface` button in both override generations of the local XML manifest; `meetingDetailsOrganizer` context in the unified manifest.

**Facet pipeline**
- Appointment context/rewrite ride two **config-defined** facets (`outlook_review_appointment`, `outlook_rewrite_appointment_selection`) delivered as a configuration package (companion PR: EratoLab/erato-subscription-content#6). Sends *and* the context chips are gated on `GET /me/facets`, so the UI never claims context a send wouldn't carry.
- Appointment fields are re-read from the live item at send time — editing an appointment form fires no `ItemChanged`, so bind-time state goes stale; reads are bounded with per-field fallback so a wedged host degrades instead of losing the send. Start/end go out as local-offset ISO plus a `timezone` arg.
- Sticky scheduling never claims appointment-compose turns: the schedule facet's confirm path opens a *new* appointment, which is never right while editing one, and each proposal would refresh the stickiness window. Calendar reads stay reachable via the review facet's tool allowlist.
- `getComposeBodyType()` failures on a compose→read race no longer reject the send.

**Identity & isolation**
- Appointment identity is a page-load-scoped mint shared by the provider and anchor paths — never `seriesId`, which Office.js sets to the parent series id on every occurrence (two occurrences would share a chat and pass the insert gate). Minted identities don't count as navigation evidence.
- Appointment attachments never surface as email context (provider skips reading them; email-source provider nulls its source once via an `emailItem` alias).
- `isMessageRead` widened to `SupportedOutlookItem`, deleting eight compound guards; `itemKind` is now required in the facet resolver; dedup markers renamed to `…DraftFingerprint` to match their broadened semantics.

author: jeffcrouse
body:
First slice of **ADR-0032 Phase A** (audio device model — decision #1 + device-half of #6). This is the **refactor + persistence + fallback foundation**; the enumeration/selection UI and control/MCP land in slices 2–3, so there's **no new user-visible surface** yet.

## What changed
- **NEW `app/src/audio/audio_device_manager.{h,cpp}`** — `AudioDeviceManager` owns the miniaudio `ma_context` + `ma_device` behind a **PIMPL**, keeping `miniaudio.h` out of the header (main, control handlers, diagnostics, and the headless test all include it). The `ma_device` is an `Impl` member, so its address is **stable** → `App::audio_device` (the opaque handle the offline bounce pauses/resumes) is set once and **`audio_bounce_app.cpp` is untouched**. `enumerate()`/`open()`/`start()`/`stop()`/`close()`/`status()`; pure inline `resolve_device_index()`.
- **`app.h`** — fwd-decl + `audio::AudioDeviceManager* audio_devices` (keeps the `void*` handle).
- **`app_settings.{h,cpp}`** — persist `audio_device_name` / `sample_rate` / `period_frames` / `fallback_to_default` (machine-level, `settings.json`), per-field guarded load/save.
- **`main.cpp`** — the ~60-line device-init block collapses onto the manager: open the persisted device (or default), **pin the session to the opened rate** (native by default → preserves today's `sampleRate=0` behavior, no new resampling), `VLOG_WARN` on fallback + on an unhonored *requested* rate. The `reduce_motion` save now writes the **full** `AppSettings` — a positional literal would have zeroed the new device fields (the persistence bug-guard).
- **Tests** — NEW `test_audio_device_resolve` (pure name resolution, `HEADLESS_SMOKE`); extended `test_app_settings` (device-field round-trip + malformed→defaults, the clobber guard).

## Design notes
- **Sample-rate policy:** open at the device's native rate at launch (unchanged behavior); the "pin" is the *readback*. A runtime device switch (slice 3) will request the pinned session rate so the session never rebuilds. `DevicePrefs.sample_rate` defaults to 0 (native).
- **Device identity = the device name string** (miniaudio's `ma_device_id` is a non-serializable backend union). Re-resolved at open; falls back to default if gone. Known v1 limitation: duplicate names collide.
- **Zero-device / headless safe:** context-init failure + empty enumeration → the app runs headless exactly as before this class existed.

## Verification
- **Live:** launches, opens the default device at native **44100 Hz**, `get_health` shows session active, severity ok, no crash, no fallback.
- Full app build clean; **81 HEADLESS_SMOKE + 12 AUDIO_ENGINE + 5 THREAD** tests pass.

author: brunoarchviz
body:
## Objetivo

Ingerir a proveniência das evidências primárias da tipologia Suprema correr 2 folhas **sem copiar os arquivos brutos para o Git** e **sem antecipar regras dimensionais**.

## Principais entregas

- abstração de acervo externo por **raiz lógica + path relativo** (`forma_referencia="acervo_externo"`);
- SHA-256 e tamanho de cada artefato;
- **validação estrutural independente da presença física do acervo** — roda em qualquer clone;
- **verificação física explícita** do acervo — raiz ausente reprova, nunca "pula";
- segurança de path **por descritores de arquivo** (`dir_fd` + `O_NOFOLLOW` em todos os componentes);
- proteção contra traversal e symlinks;
- separação entre **natureza da evidência** e **participação em fingerprint** de independência (campo `abrangencia`);
- `registro_de_campo` como **evidência primária documental**;
- `benchmark_externo` com **autoridade limitada** (Wvetro);
- `referencia_sistema_anterior` com **autoridade limitada** (VidroSys);
- papéis **DIRETA / CORROBORATIVA / DERIVADA / CONFLITANTE**;
- suporte a **múltiplas fontes por afirmação**;
- validação de **grafo de derivação sem ciclos**;
- **namespace global** de IDs para afirmações e conflitos;
- **manifesto de proveniência** da Suprema 2F (A01–A16).

## Acervo registrado por metadados

| medida | valor |
|---|---|
| artefatos | **112** |
| bytes | **22.401.782** |
| hashes únicos | **112** |
| fotos | 78 |
| registro de campo | 1 |
| artefatos Wvetro | 30 |
| artefatos VidroSys | 3 |

> **ARQUIVOS BRUTOS NÃO SÃO VERSIONADOS.**
> O acervo vive fora do repositório. O que entra no Git é metadado: rótulo do
> acervo, caminho relativo, sha256 e tamanho. Nenhum caminho absoluto de máquina
> é commitado — a localização física é informada em tempo de verificação, por
> parâmetro ou pela variável `ESQUADRIACORE_ACERVO_<RAIZ_LOGICA>`.

## Limites preservados

**Não** foram implementados:

- `L-32`; `H-5`; `H-55`; `(L-132)/2`;
- fórmulas de vidro; fórmulas de baguete;
- tolerâncias; arredondamento/truncamento;
- offsets de planos; acessórios; renderer;
- integração Wvetro; integração VidroSys;
- persistência de `ReceitaTipologia`; motor de cálculo.

**Continuam pendentes de arbitragem:**

- `TMS001` ≠ `SU-001` — literal preservado, nenhum alias criado;
- `934` × `994` (vidro da folha 2) permanece registrado como **conflito**, sem escolha automática;
- "trilho interno" ≠ `PLANO_INTERNO` até arbitragem;
- **A07 e A08 continuam `PENDENTE`**, com teste que falha se forem fechadas sem decisão.

## Gates

| gate | estado |
|---|---|
| visualização preliminar | **ABERTO** |
| cálculo | **BLOQUEADO** |
| produção | **BLOQUEADO** |

A diferença histórica de contagem de bloqueios com/sem raiz externa
(16/20 com raiz, 17/21 sem raiz) é **PREEXISTENTE** e foi comprovada idêntica no
baseline `7294c756…` e na E.4F, extraindo o baseline com `git archive` e rodando
o mesmo script nos dois.

## Testes

Rodada 3:

- `tests/test_proveniencia.py`: **104 passed**
- `tests/test_receita_suprema.py`: **443 passed** (inalterado)
- collect: **1044**
- suíte completa: **1044 passed**
- EXIT=**0**
- `git diff --check`: limpo

Performance da suíte completa (~8 min) foi auditada e classificada como
**PREEXISTENTE**, dominada principalmente pelo teste OCR/Tesseract da Sprint D
(`test_regressao_alcoa_suprema`, ~240 s — metade do total). Os quatro arquivos
que dominam o tempo não são tocados por esta sprint.

## Revisão independente

Foram realizadas **duas revisões independentes pelo Codex**.

**Primeira revisão** encontrou três achados P2:

1. ciclos indiretos em `derivada_de`;
2. IDs duplicados de conflitos;
3. TOCTOU na verificação física.

Todos corrigidos no segundo commit, `d33dd11408d8796e2aacc05ebb63f24a67a67069`:

- **P2-1** — validação do grafo completo por DFS iterativa, ordem-independente, genérica (nenhum `A01`…`A16` em código), com o ciclo nomeado no erro;
- **P2-2** — unicidade de conflitos e política de **namespace global** declarada e testada;
- **P2-3** — descida por descritor (`dir_fd` + `O_NOFOLLOW` em todos os níveis), tipo e tamanho por `fstat`, hash lido do próprio descritor; nenhuma leitura por caminho no fluxo. `O_NONBLOCK` impede bloqueio em FIFO.

**Segunda revisão — VEREDITO: APROVAR**

- os três achados anteriores **FECHADOS**;
- nenhum novo defeito material (P0/P1/P2/P3);
- nenhum motivo técnico identificado para impedir a PR.

## Nota sobre política de symlink

O acervo externo passou a recusar symlink em **qualquer** componente do caminho,
inclusive apontando para dentro da própria raiz. É mais estrito do que a regra
dos arquivos **do repositório**, que segue inalterada (E.4D/E.4E não mudam de
comportamento). Motivo: aceitar symlink interno exigiria decidir **por caminho**
se o destino está na raiz, e é essa decisão por caminho que abre a janela de
troca entre a checagem e a leitura. O acervo real tem **zero symlinks**.

## Commits

Dois commits, preservados separados para tornar a auditoria explícita:

| commit | o quê |
|---|---|
| `06f1ebb` | `feat(composicao): proveniência das evidências primárias externas` |
| `d33dd11` | `fix(composicao): endurece a validação de proveniência externa` |

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Summary

`cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib` was red on `main` (blocking every open PR
via the per-PR `--lib --bins` gate), with all three
`gc::tests::runtime_roots::generator_attach_prototype` tests failing:

- `attach_prototype_survives_an_alloc_point_copying_minor_inside_the_call`
- `attach_closure_prototype_survives_an_alloc_point_copying_minor_inside_the_call`
- `the_shipped_default_defers_the_trigger_out_of_the_callees_window`

## Root cause

Bisected in an isolated worktree by checking out each of today's three
merges (`c9079531d` → `ca8c0d617` (#7721) → `cbb682d31` (#7723) →
`c156f8a41` (#7724)) and running just this test file:

- `c9079531d` (pre-#7721): all 3 pass
- `ca8c0d617` (#7721, moving-loop poll default flip): all 3 pass
- `cbb682d31` (#7723, no-move window for lazy intrinsic towers +
  `per_test_global!` conversion): **all 3 fail — first bad commit**
- `c156f8a41` (#7724, root-dominance phi fixes): uninvolved, already broken

**#7723 did not break `js_generator_attach_prototype` /
`js_generator_attach_closure_prototype`.** It correctly converted the six
generator-intrinsic-tower `AtomicI64` statics
(`GENERATOR_FUNCTION_INTRINSIC_PTR` and siblings) from plain process-globals
to `per_test_global!`, so every test starts from a guaranteed first-touch
"tower not yet built" state instead of whichever test happened to run first
in the process silently pre-warming it for everyone else. That is exactly
what `gc::tests::lazy_intrinsic_towers` needs to gate #7251, and it is the
right fix for a real cross-test hazard.

What it exposed was a latent bug in this test file's own setup helper:

```rust
fn warm_generator_intrinsics() {
    let _ = crate::object::js_generator_attach_prototype(
        f64::from_bits(crate::value::TAG_UNDEFINED),
        0,
    );
}
```

`js_generator_attach_prototype` returns at its very first line for any
non-pointer `obj` (`!jv.is_pointer()`), so this call never reached
`generator_prototype_ptr` / `ensure_generator_intrinsics()` — it always was a
no-op. Pre-#7723 that didn't matter: the tower statics were process-global,
and by the time this test ran, some earlier test in the same binary had
almost always already built the tower, so the *real* call under test found it
cached regardless of what `warm_generator_intrinsics()` did.

Once the towers became per-thread (per-test), that accidental priming went
away. With nothing pre-built, the real call now pays the
dozens-of-allocations tower build itself, inside `build_generator_tower`'s
`GcSuppressScope` (#7251's own no-move window for that build — also correct).
Traced with instrumented `gc_check_trigger` / `GcSuppressScope` logging: on
the last-good commit the real call's first allocation reaches
`gc_check_trigger` unsuppressed and services the test's injected trigger
directly (1 relevant call); on #7723 the ~1800-call tower build runs entirely
inside one suppression window first, swallowing every trigger check that
happens during it, and by the time the window closes the following
allocations no longer need a new arena block, so the trigger is never
serviced — "subject not live" in the two alloc-point tests, and the
deferral witness's `GC_SAFEPOINT_PENDING` never gets set in the third.

## Judgement call

This is neither "the PR broke behaviour" nor "the test's premise is now
wrong" — #7723's production and test-isolation changes are both correct and
their invariants are unaffected. It's a pre-existing bug in this test file's
own helper, masked by accident until the isolation fix removed the accident.
Fixed the helper to call the real builder
(`crate::object::ensure_generator_intrinsics()`, the same one
`lazy_intrinsic_towers.rs` uses) instead of a call shape that never reached
it. The liveness/deferral assertions in the three tests are untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib generator_attach_prototype --
  --test-threads=1` — 3/3 pass, repeated 3x for flake-checking
- [x] `cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib lazy_intrinsic_towers --
  --test-threads=1` — 2/2 pass (adjacent #7723 gate, unaffected)
- [x] `cargo test -p perry-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1`
  — 1961 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (one unrelated timing-sensitive test,
  `promise::keyed_table::tests::settling_many_keys_is_not_quadratic`, flaked
  once under host load 40–70 and passed clean on every isolated re-run;
  confirmed unrelated to this change)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

author: vitorpamplona
body:
## Summary

When the relay alias fold identifies duplicate relays and stops dialling them, their historical sync bands remain in the state file and get charted on `/stats.json`, making a working fold appear as if it never happened. This change removes folded relay bands from the persisted state while keeping them in memory to allow resumption if the fold verdict expires.

## Changes

- **SyncBands.dropFolded()**: New method that removes bands for folded relays from the file on each pass. The implementation:
  - Replaces (not accumulates) the folded set each cycle, so verdicts that expire allow bands to resume rather than suppress them indefinitely
  - Filters folded relays on write rather than deleting them, since `SyncCoverage` has no removal API
  - Removes unclaimed pre-stream bands for folded relays (the only place they're dropped rather than re-written)
  - Returns count of newly folded relays for logging

- **SyncBands export()**: Filters out folded relays per stream when writing the file, preventing empty filter objects from being written

- **DynamicSync**: Calls `dropFolded()` after applying the alias fold, logging only when the set of folded relays changes

- **Documentation**: Added detailed explanation in AGENTS.md covering why bands must be dropped, why they're not merged onto the canonical relay, why the set is replaced each pass, and why the decision is per-stream

## Implementation Details

The folded set is stored in a `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<String>>` per stream and replaced atomically on each pass. This allows the flusher thread to see either the previous cycle's answer or the next one's, never a partial state. Bands stay in memory so a url whose verdict expires can resume from where it left off rather than re-walking from zero.

author: zgover
body:
Sixth promotion. Together the first two make Zach's request buildable end to end: a gradient default on the Marketing CTA, with per-instance overrides that reach the *headline* — so a white band gets black text instead of white-on-white.

**AGL-1331 — a gradient control in the Styles panel.** There was none: typing a gradient into Background Color was silently accepted, stored, emitted as an invalid `background-color`, and dropped by the CSS parser, leaving the band transparent with no error. New Background Fill field (solid / linear / radial) with a stop list and angle, stops selectable from the same token grid as every other colour field. Two judgment calls worth noting: it **rejects** invalid values rather than auto-routing them, because these fields commit per keystroke and a `gradient(`-shaped router would fire on `linear-gradient(2`; and token stops persist as `var(--mui-palette-…, #hex)`, because the canvas runs inside the console's `CssVarsProvider` and a bare token would paint the console's brand into the site's gradient.

**AGL-1332 — instance style overrides beyond the root.** Overrides were root-only, so an instance could change its background but not the leaves' hard-set `color: common.white` — setting a white background produced a white-on-white headline, re-creating AGL-1318 one page at a time. Overrides now key on the *definition's* node id (not the derived graft id, which is regenerated per placement), and detach was extended to bake per-leaf overrides too — a root-only bake would have repainted every overridden headline through the escape hatch.

**AGL-1333 — `plugins-commerce` was red on main since Aug 8.** Not an assertion failure: the suite died at module scope. The commerce server barrel reaches `next/cache` along one edge, and loading it evaluates `class NextRequest extends Request` — jsdom has no Fetch API, so `Request` is undefined. Fixed with `@jest-environment node` inside the license docblock (jest parses only a file's first comment). Also carries the docs-help registry regeneration that went stale in AGL-1312.

Gate — this one ran the corrected version, after a build-only gate let the stale registry through earlier tonight: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `TEST_EXIT=0` across console/tenant/aglyn/plugins-mui/plugins-commerce, `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` at 141/141 configs. No rules changes.

author: 577-industries
body:
Lint has been red on main since ~2026-07-06 on an unchanged tree. Two independent toolchain-drift causes:

**1. mypy could not parse numpy's stubs.** `[tool.mypy] python_version = "3.11"` makes mypy analyse *as* 3.11, so it rejects numpy's PEP 695 `type` statements:
```
numpy/__init__.pyi:737: error: Type statement is only supported in Python 3.12 and greater  [syntax]
```
This is **not** a stale mypy pin — reproduced on mypy **2.3.0** (current), and the dependency is already an open `mypy>=1.10` bound, so bumping the floor changes nothing. Targeting 3.12 is the fix.

Runtime support for 3.11 is **unchanged**: `requires-python = ">=3.11"` stays and the test matrix still runs 3.11. The trade-off is that mypy no longer catches 3.12-only stdlib usage that would break on 3.11 — the 3.11 test job covers that at runtime.

**2. `ruff format` drift** from newer ruff versions arriving via dependabot.

Fixes the lint half of #14.

Ran the full lint job locally against this branch:

ruff check .          -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check . -> all files already formatted
mypy                  -> Success: no issues found

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce authenticated accounts with admin approval, history tracking, and Pop!_OS-friendly CUDA setup while updating the sign interpreter to a 20-frame, wrist-relative landmark model with improved training and GPU diagnostics.

New Features:
- Add user and admin account system with registration, login, approval workflow, and per-user interpretation history pages.
- Provide an admin dashboard for approving users and viewing recent admin activity.
- Support loading both new native Keras models and legacy .h5 models, automatically using each model's expected sequence length.
- Add CUDA configuration utilities and a GPU diagnostics script to make TensorFlow CUDA libraries discoverable and verify NVIDIA GPU availability on Pop!_OS.

Enhancements:
- Update the interpreter pipeline to use wrist-relative, independently normalized left/right hand landmarks and a longer 20-frame sequence for predictions.
- Improve MediaPipe handedness handling to reliably identify left and right hands while retaining a positional fallback for older APIs.
- Refine the training script to use cosine learning-rate decay, optional early stopping by default, and more robust logging and NaN termination.
- Simplify environment helper scripts to work with any activated venv or Conda environment and modernize README guidance for Pop!_OS GPU setup.

author: 577-industries
body:
Lint has been red on main since ~2026-07-06 on an unchanged tree. Two independent toolchain-drift causes:

**1. mypy could not parse numpy's stubs.** `[tool.mypy] python_version = "3.11"` makes mypy analyse *as* 3.11, so it rejects numpy's PEP 695 `type` statements:
```
numpy/__init__.pyi:737: error: Type statement is only supported in Python 3.12 and greater  [syntax]
```
This is **not** a stale mypy pin — reproduced on mypy **2.3.0** (current), and the dependency is already an open `mypy>=1.10` bound, so bumping the floor changes nothing. Targeting 3.12 is the fix.

Runtime support for 3.11 is **unchanged**: `requires-python = ">=3.11"` stays and the test matrix still runs 3.11. The trade-off is that mypy no longer catches 3.12-only stdlib usage that would break on 3.11 — the 3.11 test job covers that at runtime.

**2. `ruff format` drift** from newer ruff versions arriving via dependabot.

Fixes the lint half of #15.

### Verification
Ran the full lint job locally against this branch:
```
ruff check .          -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check . -> all files already formatted
mypy                  -> Success: no issues found
```

author: viewfromthebox
body:
## Description

Implements `Services\AvailabilityService` per plan §5.2 — the `SlotResolver` the public widget, the admin calendar, and the round-robin assigner all ask "what is free for service X on date Y".

Availability is authored as wall-clock time in a provider's own zone, so a candidate slot is named as a clock face on a date and only then turned into an instant. That ordering is the whole design: it is what keeps nine o'clock meaning nine o'clock on the two days a year the offset moves, and it is why a local time the clocks skipped is dropped rather than quietly rounded into one that exists.

**Closes:** #12

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (adds new functionality)

## Related Issue

**Issue:** #12

## Motivation and Context

Every other surface in the package is downstream of this question, and it has to be answered correctly across DST changeovers, blackouts, and busy time ingested from external calendars — and fast enough for a widget asking about the next 60 days.

## Changes Made

- `src/Services/AvailabilityService.php` — expands weekly schedules and single-date overrides against the provider's timezone; subtracts blackouts, active bookings, and two-way busy blocks; applies buffers; caches per `(service, provider, provider-local date)` behind bumpable stamps.
- `src/Providers/BookingsServiceProvider.php` — binds `SlotResolver` → `AvailabilityService`, and bumps the cache stamps on every write that can change an answer.
- `resolveByProvider()` alongside the contract's `resolve()`, for the callers that need to know *who* is free rather than *when*.
- Three feature test files and shared availability helpers in `tests/Pest.php`.

### Extension hooks (#53)

All four fire, each with a test proving a consumer callback runs and that its return value is honoured. Returns are strictly validated — a subscriber handing back the wrong type raises `UnexpectedValueException` rather than corrupting a cached day.

| Hook | Type | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `ap.bookings.availabilityQuery` | filter | on the bookings query, before it runs |
| `ap.bookings.slotDuration` | filter | resolving the effective slot length |
| `ap.bookings.slotBookable` | filter | per-slot validation |
| `ap.bookings.availableSlots` | filter | after calculation, before return |

### Three decisions worth review

**1. Where the filters sit relative to the cache.** The issue asks for filter output *inside* the cached value, but its own acceptance test requires a filter-free request to be unaffected by a previously registered slot-removing filter. Those cannot both hold. Resolved by splitting on what a subscriber is actually saying: `availabilityQuery` and `slotDuration` describe the service and are cached with the computation; `slotBookable` and `availableSlots` describe the asker and run after every cache read. Satisfies the stated rationale and both required tests.

*Consequence worth knowing:* an `availabilityQuery` subscriber that varies by user — `->where('customer_email', auth()->user()->email)` — **would** poison the shared entry. Documented on the class. It is the cost of letting that hook shape the query rather than the results.

**2. `max_bookings_per_slot` is deliberately not honoured.** The partial unique index on `bookings` admits one active booking per `(provider, start_time)`, so a second seat cannot be written — reporting a group slot as free would offer a booking the insert then refuses. Seating a group needs an attendee row, which does not exist yet; `isFree()` marks where capacity gets read when it does.

**3. `resolve()` with no provider returns distinct *unassigned* periods**, keeping the contract's non-overlap guarantee and matching the shape round-robin wants. `resolveByProvider()` is the same work with the assignment kept.

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Testing Environment:**
- Operating System: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0)
- Browser (if applicable): n/a — no UI in this ticket
- PHP Version: 8.4.3
- Project Version: 1.0.0 (branch `release/1.0`)

**Tests Performed:**
1. `composer test` — 376 passing, 1301 assertions, sqlite.
2. `composer lint` — clean (php-cs-fixer, pint, phpcs).
3. Manual smoke run through `tinker` in the dev app: verified the 29-slot day, the clock face holding at 09:00 across spring-forward while the UTC instant moves 15:00 → 14:00, buffer clearance around a booking, and a filter narrowing slots then being removed again.

The DST cases the ticket requires all pass and are asserted on concrete UTC instants, not just counts: spring-forward and fall-back (`America/Chicago`), southern-hemisphere reversal (`Australia/Sydney`), no-DST (`America/Phoenix`), and fractional offset (`Pacific/Chatham`, +12:45/+13:45).

### Defects found during review and fixed here

The manual run and the review pass turned up eight, each now covered by a test verified to fail without its fix:

- Buffers enforced only the candidate's own gap, not the one an existing booking asked for — so a slot was offered the instant an appointment ended.
- The buffer rule could have demanded the *sum* of both parties' claims; it takes the larger.
- Buffers were read off the service being booked rather than off each booking's own service.
- The booking fetch window was widened by the candidate's buffers, so a neighbouring appointment on the next day whose own buffer reached back into this one was never fetched.
- A malformed custom-hours override silently fell back to the weekly schedule.
- Reassigning a booking, blackout, or busy block left the *previous* owner's cache stale — only the new one was invalidated.
- A cached day bakes in service duration, buffers, provider timezone, and calendar sync mode, none of which invalidated anything.
- `default_provider_id` stood in whenever no *active* provider was attached, so deactivating the last provider started offering someone who does not offer the service.

## Accessibility Tests Run

- [ ] Keyboard navigation tested
- [ ] Screen reader tested
- [ ] Color contrast verified
- [ ] ARIA labels checked

**Details:** Not applicable — this ticket adds a domain service with no rendered output. Accessibility is exercised by the widget tickets that consume it (#42 onward).

## Tests Added

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] All tests passing

**Test details:** 67 new tests across three files — `AvailabilityServiceTest` (generation, overrides, blackouts, bookings and buffers, busy blocks, multi-provider, caching and invalidation, malformed rows, tenant isolation), `AvailabilityTimezoneTest` (the five DST cases), and `AvailabilityHooksTest` (all four hooks, their validation, and the shared-cache isolation the issue requires).

## Documentation

- [x] Inline code documentation added
- [ ] README updated
- [ ] Wiki updated
- [ ] API documentation updated

**Documentation details:** Full PHPDoc throughout, plus prose on the reasoning that is not evident from the code — why the clock face precedes the instant, why the filters split across the cache, why capacity is not read, and why stamps carry the previous owner of a moved row.

## Screenshots

n/a — no rendered output in this ticket.

## Pre-Submission Checklist

- [x] Followed contributing guidelines
- [x] Checked for other open PRs for same update
- [x] Code passes all tests
- [x] Code has been linted
- [ ] Accessibility tests completed
- [x] Code follows project style guide
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Comments added for complex code
- [x] No new warnings generated

## Known limitations

- **Cold-cache cost.** ~4 queries per provider per day when nothing is cached; zero when warm. Per-day granularity is what the ticket specifies. The window a public caller may ask for is bounded at the endpoint (#42), not here.
- **Pivot writes via `attach()` / `updateExistingPivot()`** raise no model event on any supported Laravel version, so a `custom_duration` set that way is covered by the 5-minute TTL rather than by a stamp. Noted in the code.

body:
## Summary

### Reporting engine, document templates, and CSV export

- `internal/reports`: parametric reporting engine — `report_definitions`/`saved_report_runs` tables, `QuerySpec` translated to safe, parameterized SQL via a hardcoded per-entity field allow-list (`entityRegistry`), never raw SQL or string-interpolated values. `GET/POST /report-definitions`, `GET /report-definitions/{id}`, `POST /report-definitions/{id}/run`.
- `internal/documents` (new): firm-scoped document templates rendered to HTML via stdlib `html/template` (`missingkey=zero`, so an unknown field renders empty rather than erroring). Lazily-seeded default invoice template. `GET /invoices/{id}/render?templateID=`.
- `internal/portability`: CSV export format (`?format=csv` / `Accept: text/csv`), multi-section CSV via stdlib `encoding/csv`.
- Frontend: `/reports/builder`, a "My Reports" tab on `/reports`, `/settings/document-templates`, and an invoice "Preview" button.

### Multi-tenant isolation hardening + performance + cross-module features

- **N+1 audit**: fixed two real N+1s in `internal/portability.ExportFirm` — `inventory.ListStockForFirm` and `invoicing.ListInvoicesWithLines` each batch via one extra `ANY($1)` query instead of looping `Get*` per entity. Added `internal/platform/db/dbtest.ExplainAnalyze` as an on-demand investigation helper.
- **Performance indexes**: `migrations/0022_performance_indexes.sql` — `workflow_instances(firm_id, workflow_definition_id)`, `invoices(source_workflow_instance)` (a real pre-existing gap), `edge_events(firm_id, agent_id, received_at)`, `stock_movements(firm_id, product_id, created_at)`.
- **Cross-module linking**: workflow instance ↔ invoice, delivery → invoice, and customer → workflow instances, each surfaced via new/extended detail pages (`/workflows/instance/[instanceId]`, `/customers/[customerId]`).
- **Bulk operations**: `POST /workflow-instances/bulk-transition` and `POST /invoices/bulk-status`, both atomic — a single-entity function's core logic was extracted to take an already-open `pgx.Tx` so a bulk call shares one transaction across every entity (any failure rolls back everything already done in that call).

## Query-spec → SQL safety design

`BuildQuery` (`internal/reports/queryspec.go`) is the only place a `QuerySpec` becomes SQL. Every table/column name in the generated query comes from `entityRegistry`, a closed, hardcoded map of entity → allowed fields — never from the request directly. An entity, field, or aggregation not in that map is rejected with `ErrInvalidQuerySpec` (HTTP 400). Every filter/date-range *value* is bound via Postgres's own `$N` parameters, never interpolated.

## Document template rendering approach

Templates are rendered with Go's stdlib `html/template` (no new dependency) against a nested `map[string]any` data context with `template.Option("missingkey=zero")` set, so a template referencing a field that doesn't exist on the entity renders as an empty string instead of failing the whole render.

## Bulk-transition atomicity design

`workflow.ExecuteTransition`'s entire body became `executeTransitionTx` (unexported, takes `tx pgx.Tx`); `ExecuteTransition` is now a thin pool-opening wrapper. `BulkExecuteTransition` checks every instance shares one definition (`ErrBulkTransitionMixedDefinitions`) before touching any of them, then calls `executeTransitionTx` per instance inside one shared `zdb.WithFirmContext` transaction — a failure on any instance rolls back every instance already transitioned in that same call, via that helper's own `defer tx.Rollback(ctx)`. `invoicing.UpdateInvoiceStatus`/`BulkUpdateInvoiceStatus` follow the identical shape.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` (Postgres-backed integration tests skip without a local DB, including a query-counting `pgx.QueryTracer` test proving the N+1 fix and two atomicity/rollback tests for the bulk endpoints)
- [x] `go run ./cmd/ciaudit` (RLS/Permission Drift Audit) passes
- [x] `python3 scripts/license_headers.py --check`, `check_gosec.py`, `check_gitleaks.sh` pass
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_doc_sync.py origin/main`, `check_api_contract.py`, `check_migration_safety.py` pass
- [x] `web`: `npm run build`, `lint`, `test`, `check:i18n`, `check:permission-tags`, `check:audit` all pass
- [ ] `govulncheck` — blocked in this sandbox by network policy (403 from vuln.go.dev), not a code issue

author: trick77
body:
Fixes the five findings from the review of #24.

## Two collectors met the `BaselineEmitter` definition and were not declared

#24 introduced `BaselineEmitter` for collectors whose first `Collect` is data rather than a warm-up, because `Prime` discards that first Result. It declared the interface on `Systemd` and `Mdraid` — and missed two collectors of exactly the same shape, so `Prime` still ate their output.

**`packages` (the worst of the two).** Its first `Collect` *is* the inventory, and the parse stamps `lastMtime`/`lastParse` — so every later scrape short-circuits on "unchanged and recent". The discarded inventory therefore does not come back on the next scrape; it comes back when dpkg's mtime moves or the 24h floor elapses. A freshly enrolled host reported **no packages at all for up to a day**, and an existing one kept whatever it had before the restart, because `UpsertHostPackages` returns early on an empty set.

**`smart`.** Priming ran a full `--scan` plus `--all` per drive, threw the rows away, and stamped `lastRun` — spinning up every sleeping drive for a reading nobody kept, *and* costing the first hour of SMART data on every agent restart. Precisely what the `due()` self-gate exists to prevent.

The declaration test now covers all four and states why each qualifies, since the property is a statement about what the first `Collect` *means* and cannot be inferred from the type.

## The systemd baseline is restricted to failed units

#24 removed the `prev != nil` guard so the first scrape emits a baseline. Unrestricted, that is one event per loaded `.service` — 200–400 on a normal host, most of them `inactive/dead` oneshots.

`systemd_unit_events` is deliberately a plain table with **no retention policy**, and its own comment sizes it on the premise that *"a unit changes state a handful of times a month"*. So the baseline wrote hundreds of unprunable rows per host on every agent restart, multiplied by a crash-looping agent or a fleet redeploy. Before #24 that growth path was unreachable, because `Prime` swallowed the baseline.

Restricting it to **failed** units is not a compromise — a failed unit is the only case the baseline was added for ("a unit already failed when the agent starts produces no event at all"), and it is rare by construction, so this is normally zero rows. Transitions are untouched, including a unit that appears after the first scrape. This is now the one place the collector deliberately differs from mdraid, and says so.

## Sensors: ENOENT is an answer, not a wedge

The backoff was cleared only on a *successful* read. `ENOENT` hits neither the timeout branch nor the success branch, so a chip that timed out once and was then unbound — or renumbered by a driver rebind, `hwmon3` → `hwmon4` — left its entry in the map forever. `Capabilities()` reported `sensors: degraded` for the life of the agent with nothing actually failing, and the metadata hash never flipped back. Any non-timeout outcome now clears it.

## `filesystem_samples.used` is documented where it is read

#24 changed `used` from `Blocks - Bavail` to `Blocks - Bfree` to match `df`. The column is rolled up by `filesystem_samples_5m` / `_1h` as `used_avg` / `used_max`, so the definition matters to every consumer at every resolution. The schema now states it next to the table:

```
total = Blocks          free = Bavail          used = Blocks - Bfree
```

`used + free != total` by construction — the gap is the root reserve, which holds no data and is not available either. A fullness percentage must be `used / (used + free)`, as `df` computes Use%, never `used / total`.

No migration: per this repo's rule all schema lives in `0001_init.sql` and there is no `0002`.

## Verification

```
coverage-gate: hub   ok — 87.8% of lines (floor 75.0%)
coverage-gate: agent ok — 85.8% of lines (floor 75.0%)
agent patch coverage — 100% (floor 75%)
hub patch coverage   — n/a (no Go changes; the hub diff is a SQL comment)
```

Full suite green. The two most serious fixes are mutation-checked against the bug they fix: reverting `Packages.EmitsBaseline` to `false` fails the new test with `0 packages, want 1`, and the packages/systemd tests drive the real `Prime → ScrapeOnce → Flush` path rather than calling `Collect` directly — which is what hid the original defect.

## Unrelated: a pre-existing deadlock on master

Running the suite against merged `master` before starting this branch, `TestIntegrationGroup2TablesCascadeOnHostDelete` failed with `deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)`. Same retention-job-versus-cascading-delete race #24 addressed, but this one is in `internal/hub/store`, where the test issues its own raw `DELETE FROM hosts` and so never reaches the `DeleteHost` retry.

Not touched here: the real fix is to stop TimescaleDB's policy jobs for the duration of each test, and `resetSchema` already does exactly that for the schema *reset* (via `timescaledb_pre_restore()`) — the gap is that the jobs resume for the test body. Doing it properly means either a new helper threaded through 56 `OpenTest` call sites or a change to how the fixtures migrate. Worth its own PR.

author: asigdel29
body:
Refs #468 ## What changed `owned` and `answered` were byte-identical at the bottom of `jni_git.rs` and `jni_memory.rs`. They move to `jni_answer.rs`, gated on `android` with either `git` or `memory` — the shape `ffi_answer.rs` already established for the C half, and for the reason its header gives: two envelopes that agree today, and a caller unwrapping two shapes the day one changes. Two of the three rules `jni.rs` states for this boundary come with it: decode the way the crate documents, and clear a pending exception before returning nothing. The third — that no panic may cross into the JVM — wraps eight bodies in a closure, which re-indents both files. Adding it here took the diff to 356 changed lines, so it follows as its own change. ## Notes for review **The decode is not a bug being fixed, and the issue was rewritten once I measured it.** `to_string_lossy` resolves through `JavaStr` → `JNIStr` → `CStr` and reads the bytes as standard UTF-8. A JVM is permitted to write modified UTF-8, where a supplementary character arrives as a surrogate pair — invalid standard UTF-8, replaced with U+FFFD. That is what the change is against. It does not happen. I wrote the test, stashed the Rust change, rebuilt the core and ran it against the **unchanged** code: it passed. ART's `GetStringUTFChars` does not use the permission the specification gives it. So what this change buys is that one runtime's behaviour stops being load-bearing — `from_java_cesu8` falls back to `from_utf8_lossy` when its input is not modified UTF-8, so the documented route is correct under both encodings and the current one is correct under one. The test stays, as a statement of which runtime was measured rather than as a regression guard for a regression that never happened. Its comment says so. Same for the other two. The reachable `get_string` failure is a null reference, which the crate refuses before asking the JVM, so it raises nothing and there is nothing to clear; the clear is for the arm where the JVM itself refuses, which no test can reach. And the inner `wattrouter_*` calls are already guarded, so there is no live panic path today either. All three are rules the file next door follows and these two did not. One thing deliberately left alone: `jni_memory.rs`'s `usize::try_from(keep.max(0)).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` was worth a look, because saturating to `usize::MAX` bounds nothing — which is the opposite of what the line is for. It cannot fire: `abiFilters` is `arm64-v8a` alone, so no 32-bit ABI ships and the conversion cannot fail. The comment now says that, so the next person to notice it stops there. `just guards` reports one advisory: the emoji in `BEYOND`. It is the subject of the test rather than its register, and it stays. ## Verification Ran on this machine — macOS 27, Apple silicon. - `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean. - `cargo test --all-targets` — 94 passed, 0 failed. - `scripts/lint/file-headers.sh` — 290 files. `scripts/lint/doc-tags.sh` — 135 files. Both clean. - `just android-test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL. - `just android-device-test` — **57 instrumented tests on the `wattrouter-tests` AVD (Android 15, arm64-v8a), 0 failures.** 22 in `:app`, 35 in `:core`. This is the suite that matters: it is the only one that loads the `.so`, and this change is entirely inside it. - `just guards` — 0 hard failures, 1 advisory. The deliberate-red run described above is the reason the claim in this pull request is weaker than the one in the issue was.

Greptile Summary

The PR consolidates duplicated JNI string conversion and response-ownership helpers into a feature-gated shared module. - Uses the JNI crate’s documented Java-string decoding path and clears pending exceptions after failed input reads. - Preserves response conversion and Rust allocation cleanup for the Git and memory bindings. - Adds an Android instrumentation test covering supplementary Unicode characters. - Documents the shipped ABI assumption behind memory-retention size conversion.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge with no actionable defects identified. The shared module’s feature gates cover every importer, Java-string decoding follows the established JNI boundary pattern, and all reachable response pointers retain their matching allocation and deallocation path.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | router/src/jni_answer.rs | Introduces shared JNI input decoding and response conversion helpers while preserving the existing ownership and deallocation contract. | | router/src/jni_git.rs | Replaces duplicated local JNI helpers with imports from the correctly gated shared module. | | router/src/jni_memory.rs | Adopts the shared JNI helpers for all existing input and response paths without changing their caller-visible result shapes. | | router/src/lib.rs | Gates the shared module on Android plus either consuming feature, consistently with its importers and `ffi_answer` dependency. | | android/core/src/androidTest/kotlin/com/getlora/wattrouter/MemoryTest.kt | Adds device coverage showing supplementary Unicode characters survive memory storage and retrieval across JNI. |
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["Share one decode between the two JNI bin..."](https://github.com/asigdel29/anu-agentic-stack/commit/9038fa532db82274cb15dff96aace04e3f12da0c) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=51623873)

author: herjarsa
body:
## Problem

The vision bridge was not routing image requests to a vision-capable model, for individual models AND combos. Verified empirically against the live runtime (v3.8.49 npm):

- `auto/best-vision` resolved to `deepseek-v4-flash-free` (text-only model) — the virtual combo used the flat `smart` variant with NO vision candidate filter.
- Combo `REASONING` + image -> 400 with 3/3 targets attempted (minimax/MiniMax-M3 -> `403 (2013)` for remote image URLs; opencode-zen/kilo targets rejected images outright).
- The describe self-loop failed (`(unavailable)`) — the guardrail's `sk_omniroute` fallback key and the runtime's hooked global fetch (ProxyFetch) broke loopback calls.
- `hasUsableCredentialsForModel("auto/best-vision") === false` (no provider row named `auto`) blocked the reroute entirely.

## Fixes

1. **builtinCatalog**: `auto/best-vision` -> vision CATEGORY (candidate filter by capability), `auto/pro-vision` -> vision + pro tier. New pure `resolveBuiltinAutoSpec()` (tested).
2. **suffixComposition + visionBridgeRouter**: vision candidate pool excludes models whose catalog OVERSTATES vision support (opencode-go/opencode-zen/tokenrouter are forced through the bridge by `isVisionBridgeForcedModel`).
3. **visionBridge.ts**: `auto/*` reroute target is a virtual combo — a missing `auto` provider credential row must never block the reroute (`bestUsable === false && !auto/*`).
4. **visionBridgeHelpers.ts**:
   - `resolveSelfLoopApiKey()`: real DB key (memoized `getOrCreateApiKey`) instead of the `sk_omniroute` sentinel when `REQUIRE_API_KEY` is on.
   - `isClaudeWireFormatModel` + `ensureBase64ImagesForClaudeWire`: claude-wire backends (MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi) reject remote image URLs (MiniMax 403 2013) — resolve URLs to base64 before rerouting.
   - Describe self-loop uses undici fetch (bypasses the runtime's hooked global fetch / dead local proxy), sends `Accept: application/json` + `stream: false`, disables compression for the image payload.
   - Remote image downloads send a User-Agent (Wikimedia etc. reject headerless bots with 400).

## Verification

- Unit: 65/66 guardrails tests green (1 pre-existing Windows EPERM in vision-bridge-callmodel cleanup), autoCombo Vitest green except #8601 free-alias fitness which depends on local `models_dev_tier` state (CI DB is clean).
- Live runtime after rebuilding the bundle: `auto/best-vision` + image -> 200 (MiniMax-M3 describes: "The image is a solid pink/coral-colored square"), combo `REASONING` + image -> 200 (nemotron-nano-omni describes), describe self-loop -> 200 ("solid, uniform field of dark red color").

author: yisding
body:
## What changed

- adds the event-scoped dashboard overview endpoint backed by one aggregated SQL statement
- consumes canonical read-model views for submission, accepted-speaker, task, confirmation, and missing-asset counts
- adds 30-second polling with focus refresh and deep-linkable Today / Speaker Tracking tabs
- adds the dashboard widgets, designed empty states, widget-level degradation, and typed local fixtures
- preserves credential-free local rendering without pretending fixture data is deployed evidence
- uses event slugs for public form links and event IDs for admin links
- adds PGlite and rendered-component coverage for status zero-filling, empty events, task-count equality, and link correctness

## Why

M38 requires a near-real-time organizer dashboard whose numbers cannot drift from Abstracts or the portal task panel. The implementation consumes the same database views and fan-out law instead of re-deriving widget counts.

## Impact

Organizers get one dashboard endpoint and a polling UI for live submission and speaker-onboarding status. Empty events, credential-free local development, and isolated widget failures remain usable.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — 20 files, 137 tests passed
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint`
- `bash scripts/check-invariants.sh`
- `pnpm build`
- local dashboard route — HTTP 200, 25,956-byte rendered response

## Remaining acceptance evidence

The deployed count-drop demonstration, warm-query timing against `sb-dev`, and cross-surface preview comparison remain blocked until the R1 foundation PRs and seed/task runtime are merged and deployed. Keep this PR in draft until those external AC can be recorded.

body:
Both found in a LIVE regen (B0GVVY5TS9 18:54) that shipped
"THE CEO Futbol World Futbol Cup Soccer Tee Shirt | the Black Short Sleeve".

A — TRADEMARK OSCILLATION (not one bad regex — two nets fighting):
  scrubTrademarks inserts "futbol" (world cup -> world futbol cup)
  -> collapseRepeatedWords deletes the repeat, RESURRECTING a bare
     "World Cup" -> the route's scrub-on-serve re-doubles it.
  Both halves fixed: substitutions are now idempotent to a FIXED POINT
  (insertion-shape rules absorb their own inserted token; replacement-shape
  collapse only an immediately-repeated whole substitution, so
  "Board Game Super Bowl" survives), and collapseRepeatedWords REFUSES a
  dedupe that would introduce a mark the input did not carry. Rules are
  classified from TRADEMARK_RULES itself — adding a rule needs no second
  edit. The already-shipped gibberish SELF-HEALS on re-scrub (73 -> 66).

B — COLOR WORD IN A SHARED TITLE (SELLER_PROFILE section 5 — on paper only
  until now): stripVariantColorWords at the ONE bandTitle seam, after the
  money tail (keyword keeps first refusal) and before the audience net;
  both exits (broadcast + per-child). Verified per_child_titles is built
  per DESIGN GROUP / per CAPACITY, never per colour, so netting both
  surfaces is safe. Design carve-out protects "Black Cat" via the union of
  family + per-design names. Band-guarded and fail-open.
  No new predicate: the existing COLOR_WORDS list is split/exported and the
  three byte-identical "KEEP IN SYNC" copies collapse to one.

C — the stray lowercase "the" traced to its MANUFACTURER: the Title-Case
  polish lowercased a MINOR_WORD that opens a pipe-right clause. Fixed at
  the caser (a minor word after | , ; : keeps its capital), not with a new

author: arnaudmaillet
body:
**PR 2 of 3.** Base is #100, not `develop` — it touches the same `onFeedPopped` closure. Followed by #102.

Found while investigating a reported autoplay failure on the Following tab. Neither of these is that report (see #102 for what that turned out to be), but both are real and both silently kill playback.

## A playback handoff nothing closed

`openFeed` opens a handoff before it knows which path it is taking. The plain push a **text row** falls back to has no transition, so neither `onSourceReturned` nor `onPresentationCancelled` ever runs. `handoffID` stayed set for the life of the page, permanently exempting that post from both starting **and** stopping — and `discardPlaybackHandoff` on the way back does not clear it, it only retires the parked player.

Reproduced with `-grid-playback-log`: `handoff=post-new-02` still on the pool three samples after the grid was back on screen.

Closed in `onFeedPopped`, which is completed pops only — a cancelled swipe leaves the post up, where the grid underneath should stay stopped. The handoff is still *opened* on this path deliberately: it is what stops the grid's players while the post covers them, since `viewWillDisappear` declines to (a push must not stop a flight's video).

After the fix: `handoff=-` one sample after the pop, with `slots=4`.

## A pager that disagreed with its own scroll view

`setActivePage` moves `activeIndex`, then returns early when there is no width yet — leaving `reportedIndex` behind. `viewDidLoad` restores the persisted format through exactly that path.

Restore **Following**, then swipe back to **Discover**, and Discover never autoplays: the settle matched the stale `reportedIndex`, was dismissed as "no change", and skipped both `syncAutoplay` and `onPageSettled`. The page the viewer was looking at stayed marked inactive, and the view model's format stayed wrong — which also gates pagination.

It healed only on a tab tap or a round trip, and restoring the **default** format cannot reproduce it at all (the guard above returns first). That is why it survived.

Both new pager tests fail without the fix.

Feed **402 tests / 50 suites**.

author: olstaylor
body:
Unblocks `test:mvp`, which is currently failing on `main` and therefore on every open PR.

## The failure

```
CONTENT PROVENANCE CHECK FAILED
  - 3 route(s) have edited copy with a stale published date:
    /  (published 2026-08-09)
    /compare-concert-ticket-prices  (published 2026-07-13)
    /artists  (published 2026-08-09)
  - 1 route(s) have a lastmod that disagrees with the recorded fingerprint:
    /compare-concert-ticket-prices  (metadata 2026-07-13, expected 2026-08-09)
```

Copy edits to these three routes landed without running `npm run content:provenance`, so their recorded fingerprints went stale and `/compare-concert-ticket-prices` ended up with a `lastmod` that disagrees with its own content hash.

## Why it wasn't caught at the time

`prelaunch-validation.yml` triggers only on `pull_request`. `main` is never validated on its own after a merge, so a copy edit that skips the sync stays invisible until the next PR opens — and then fails at step four of the `test:mvp` chain, before anything that PR actually changed is exercised. That's how it surfaced on #684, whose diff is confined to the city/venue templates and cannot move these routes.

Possibly worth a follow-up to add a `push: branches: [main]` trigger so `main` fails on its own rather than through the next contributor's PR. Not doing that here — separate concern.

## What this changes

`npm run content:provenance` and nothing else. **No page copy is edited.**

- `functions/_route-metadata.js` — one line: `/compare-concert-ticket-prices` `lastmod` `2026-07-13` → `2026-08-09`
- `data/content-provenance.json` — re-records the content hash for all three routes; `content_updated_at` moves only for `/compare-concert-ticket-prices`

`/` and `/artists` were already dated `2026-08-09`, so their visible published dates do not move — only their stored hashes catch up to the copy already on the page.

The advanced date is the script's intended behaviour: the fingerprint proves the copy changed, and the recorded date is what was stale.

## Validation

Full `npm run test:mvp` passes on this branch.

---

Follows from the blocker described in #684. Once this merges, I'll merge `main` into that branch so its CI re-runs against a clean base.

Add implicit cast operators to allow ResultStatus to be converted directly to Success or Failure.

This simplifies result creation and improves readability by avoiding explicit conversion or repetitive mapping logic when the status code already determines whether the result represents a successful or failed operation.

Requirements:

- Add implicit conversion from ResultStatus to Success.
- Add implicit conversion from ResultStatus to Failure.
- Validate that the provided status code belongs to the appropriate status-code category.
- Throw an appropriate exception when a success status code is used to create a Failure, or a failure status code is used to create a Success.

Related #7

## Bối cảnh

PR 2/4 trong kế hoạch làm chuẩn PWA cho candidate. Nền tảng PWA (manifest, service worker, tap target) đã xử lý ở [PR #231](https://github.com/binhphanbp/upnext-frontend/pull/231) — PR này thêm thanh điều hướng chính dạng bottom tab bar cho mobile, thứ candidate app cài đặt dạng PWA cần có để cảm giác giống app thật, không phải trang web thu nhỏ.

## Vì sao cần

Trước đây trên mobile, mọi điều hướng của candidate đều phải qua nút "Mở menu" ở header — không có lối tắt 1-chạm tới các khu vực dùng nhiều nhất (Hồ sơ, Ứng tuyển, Đã lưu, Tin nhắn, CV). Đây là pattern chuẩn của app di động (iOS Tab Bar / Material Bottom Navigation) mà 1 trang PWA cần có để không bị cảm giác là "web thu nhỏ".

## Đã làm

- `CandidateTabBar` mới: 5 tab (Hồ sơ, Ứng tuyển, Đã lưu, Tin nhắn, CV), tap target 75×56px (vượt chuẩn tối thiểu 44px), trạng thái active theo route hiện tại, dấu đỏ báo tin nhắn mới trên tab "Tin nhắn" — dùng lại đúng state `hasNewRecruiterMessages`/`markRecruiterChatViewed` mà menu "Tài khoản" trên header đã có sẵn, không tạo state riêng.
- Hiện ở `<=820px` — **khớp đúng breakpoint mà header tự chuyển sang chế độ compact** (`marketing-home.css`, không phải mặc định `768px` của Tailwind). Lệch breakpoint sẽ tạo ra 1 khoảng ~50px nơi có tab bar nhưng header vẫn hiện đầy đủ nav desktop (hoặc ngược lại) — 1 layout lai không đẹp.
- Không hiện ở `/candidate/cv-builder` — trang này đã tách nhánh riêng từ trước (full-bleed editor, có action bar riêng), giữ nguyên logic đó.

## Vấn đề phát hiện thêm trong lúc làm

Nút nổi AI Copilot (`AiCopilotDrawer`) đứng cố định ở `bottom-5`, đúng vị trí thanh tab bar mới sẽ che lên. Đã thêm prop `raised` (opt-in) để nút này tự nâng lên tránh tab bar — chỉ áp dụng cho candidate; trang `/jobs` public dùng cùng component này nhưng không có tab bar nên không bị ảnh hưởng.
