author: domoki01
body:
Adds a standalone educational arbitrage scanner and executor for Solana DEXs, integrated via the Jupiter aggregator. The bot detects round-trip price discrepancies (USDC → token → USDC) across Orca, Raydium, Meteora and other pools, and optionally executes trades when profit exceeds a configurable threshold.

## Key changes

- **New bot directory** `bots/solana-arb/` with complete TypeScript implementation:
  - `src/index.ts` — main event loop scanning tokens and logging opportunities
  - `src/jupiter.ts` — Jupiter API client with quote and swap transaction building
  - `src/scanner.ts` — round-trip quoting and basis-point profit calculation
  - `src/executor.ts` — transaction signing and on-chain execution (live mode only)
  - `src/http.ts` — rate-limit throttling with exponential backoff for 429/5xx
  - `src/config.ts` — environment variable parsing and validation
  - `src/logger.ts` — timestamped logging with debug/info/warn/error/opportunity levels

- **Configuration** via `.env.example`:
  - RPC endpoint, Jupiter API key, request interval, trade size, profit threshold, slippage tolerance
  - Dry-run mode (default) logs only; live mode requires a private key and executes trades
  - Configurable token list (defaults to SOL, JUP, JTO)

- **Documentation** in Arabic (`README.md`):
  - Explains the bot's purpose, setup, and observed market conditions
  - Real data from mainnet showing why arbitrage is harder than viral stories suggest
  - Risk warnings: non-atomic execution, fees, phantom liquidity, API limits
  - Architecture overview and configuration reference

- **Build configuration**:
  - `package.json` with Node 20+ requirement, tsx runner, TypeScript strict mode
  - `tsconfig.json` with ES2022 target and strict type checking
  - `.gitignore` to exclude `.env` and `node_modules`

- **ESLint integration**: Updated root `eslint.config.mjs` to exclude `bots/**` from Next.js rules, since this is a standalone Node project with its own typecheck step.

## Implementation notes

- **Non-atomic execution**: The two swap legs are sequential, not bundled. Leg 2 is re-quoted after leg 1 confirms, so the edge can close at a loss within slippage tolerance. True atomic arbitrage requires a custom program or Jito bundles, which is beyond this educational scope.
- **Rate limiting**: Jupiter's free tier limits to ~1 req/s. The `Throttle` class serializes requests and backs off on 429; the `fetchWithRetry` function implements exponential backoff up to 30s.
- **Dry-run first**: The default `DRY_RUN=true` logs all round trips (including losses) so users can observe market conditions before risking real funds.
- **Observed reality**: Real mainnet runs show the best edge was +7 bps on a 10 USDC trade (~0.007 USD), far below the 30 bps threshold needed to cover fees. This is expected: Jupiter aggregates prices across DEXs, so remaining discrepancies are captured by professional traders with dedicated infrastructure before a public API bot sees them.

body:
## Summary
- `getPersistentMemoryStatus()` returned `memorySaveHistory.length` - an in-process array that only tracks memories saved since the current server process started, resetting to 0 on every restart.
- This feeds the Memory card on the Spacemonkey Brain dashboard (`MemoryCard.jsx`'s "Saved Memories" number) via `GET /api/spacemonkey/state`, so it showed a misleadingly low count any time the server had recently restarted, even with dozens of real memories already stored.
- Found while continuing the "real data vs. stub" audit that produced `GET /api/spacemonkey/brainwave` in an earlier PR - this one is a live route, just backed by the wrong data source.

## Fix
Query `prisma.memory.count()` (the real, persistent count) when a prisma client is available, falling back to the in-process count only when it's not - matches the existing null-check pattern already used elsewhere in this file for `saveMemory`/`findMemory`.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified against a copy of the real database (production untouched): `prisma.memory.count()` and the fixed `getSpacemonkeyCoreStatus().memory.saved` both return 31, matching exactly.
- [x] Confirmed via a real running server + curl that `GET /api/spacemonkey/state` and `GET /api/spacemonkey/brainwave` both return 200 with the corrected value.
- [x] `node --check` on all three changed files.

### What
The data controller's guard flags (`_columnsUpdating`, `_skipProcessingPagingChange`) now reset even when the guarded operation throws. Previously a throw in `updateSortingGrouping` skipped `_columnsUpdating = false` and wedged the controller, permanently suppressing later sorting/grouping `columnsChanged` events.

### How
Both guarded blocks are wrapped in `try/finally` so the flags reset even if the operation throws.

author: mylifeindigital
body:
Closes CR-012 — reshaped and implemented.

## The request was hiding a real defect

CR-012 sat as an index row from 2026-05-06 titled "Decide parser roadmap for Markdown processing", with no detail file. Gate 2 found the roadmap question already answered in code — `marked` for AST and HTML, `gray-matter` for frontmatter — and its one concrete deferral orphaned, since the browser-safe shim CR-011 pointed here existed for the admin preview that **CR-029 deleted this morning**.

Underneath it: `web/src/utils/markdown.ts` exported `extractFrontmatter` and `parseMarkdownContent` with **zero callers**, and they were *not equivalent to the live parser*. No type coercion, so `draft: true` parsed as the string `"true"` while `DraftFilterProcessor` tests `metadata.draft === true`. Anyone reaching for them in good faith would have published a draft.

Same failure mode as CR-028, different route in.

## What was removed

| | |
|---|---|
| `markdown.ts` | `extractFrontmatter`, `parseMarkdownContent`, `PostMetadata`, the `marked` import — 122 lines → 55, now types-only |
| `post-cache.ts` | six uncalled exports (11 → 5, all now called) plus the orphaned `itemsBySectionCache` |
| `web/package.json` | `@types/marked`, which publishes itself deprecated because `marked` ships its own types |

The three `Post` accessors were pre-section vocabulary — they'd have returned the wrong *shape* of answer to anyone using them by name, which is why they went with the parser rather than being left as harmless clutter.

## Decisions recorded

- **Both piles**, not just the parser. `web/src/utils/` is internal, not a published library, so an uncalled export is dead weight.
- **A `decisions/` wiki page**, not an extension of the concepts page. The concepts page says how Markdown *should* be treated and names no library; which library implements it, and what would change that, is a different kind of claim with a different shelf life. `docs/wiki/decisions/markdown-parser.md` records both, with three reconsideration triggers.
- **Browser-safe frontmatter deferred with a named trigger** — the Electron app needing a preview surface. Deciding it now would design for nobody. Filed in `docs/wiki/questions.md` so it resurfaces.
- **`markdown.ts` keeps its name.** 40+ imports of churn for clarity a file comment provides.

`post-cache.ts` also gained a header saying "cache" means an in-memory lookup index, not an HTTP or CDN cache — that name had already caused the confusion once.

## Verification

All 13 public routes rendered and compared against the pre-change baseline: **identical**. 41 tests pass, all three type-check programs clean, Worker bundles.

One deletion had a caller outside the repo — the scratchpad snapshot harness imported `getItemsBySection`. Updated to read `section.items`. Worth noting because it's the only evidence any of the six accessors were ever used, and it was tooling, not the application.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Closes rf2-8a6s.

`rf2-hic-001` created `implementation/hicasso/` while fenced out of `.github/`, so the package landed matching **no classifier case at all**. `TESTING.md` §Changed-surface classifier names that exact shape: a new artefact directory needs a classifier rule *and* a workflow gate whose `if:` reads it, and either side missing is a silent hole. This PR is both halves.

**What the hole actually was, stated precisely.** In CI, `detect_changed_surfaces` has no fallback: on a hicasso-only diff every output was `false` and every job simply skipped — green, having run nothing. The local spine behaves differently and it is worth knowing why, because it disguised the problem: an unclassified path trips `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`'s `conservative fallback (unknown surface)`, which arms *every* tier. Verified, not assumed — a probe whose only diff is an unclassified path reports `reason: conservative fallback (unknown surface)` / `PLAN docs=false jvm=true node=true`. So locally hicasso-only diffs **over**-ran while CI ran nothing at all.

## The classifier rule, and the sibling it is modelled on

`implementation/hicasso/*)` in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` arms **`cljs_node_test`, and only that**.

Modelled on the `implementation/freehand/*)` case immediately above it — same artefact-root POSIX glob (`*` spans `/`, so the tree is covered at any depth), placed adjacent to it, closing the identical hole `rf2-drpa3.58` closed for Freehand when its standalone workflow was folded into `test.yml`. It is deliberately **narrower** than that sibling's four outputs, because the artefact is not the same shape:

| Output | Freehand | Hicasso | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cljs_node_test` | armed | **armed** | `hicasso/src` + `hicasso/test` are on the global `:source-paths` and `re-frame.hicasso.smoke-cljs-test` matches the `:node-test` build's `cljs-test$` regexp. This is the one output whose job runs anything covering the artefact — and it schedules all three of its checks: the smoke, the freeze gate below, and the bench-lane compile already there. |
| `implementation_jvm` | armed | withheld | The runtime requires React, so every suite the artefact owns is CLJS. Its `:test` alias is a `--probe` classpath check and it is correctly absent from `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`'s roster — `check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` fails **both** ways, so a roster entry with no required job is its own red (the trap `rf2-2rtt6.143` hit). Arm this the same commit a JVM-runnable suite and the roster row land together. |
| `cljs_browser` | armed | withheld | Hicasso *is* on the `:browser-test` classpath, but that build selects `-dom-cljs-test$` and the package owns no such namespace. Arming it would schedule a Playwright job that runs not one line of the changed surface. |
| `cljs_prod` | armed | withheld | No `-elision-prod-test$` namespace. |

Also withheld: `bundle_isolation` / `ui_gates` / `ui_smoke` — no example resolves the artefact and it mounts no testbed those smokes drive. `TESTING.md` warns that a coarse rule clutters the matrix with skipping entries; a gate that executes none of the changed surface is worse than no gate, because it reads as coverage. Each withheld output carries its named release condition in the classifier comment and again in the tests, so a later widening is a deliberate edit rather than a drift.

## How the freeze gate is scheduled, and when it runs

`implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py` checks two properties that both stop being true silently: **FROZEN** — every donor file under `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**` still hashes to its digest in `frozen-sources.edn`, and every package file the copy produced is still present; and **SEALED** — nothing under `implementation/hicasso/` `:require`s a benchmark-tree namespace. It ran **only by hand**: the same shape the bench-lane compile was in before `rf2-2rtt6.73`, and the same failure mode.

It now has a scheduled home, wired exactly like its sibling `test:hicasso-compile`:

- **`implementation/package.json`** — `test:hicasso-freeze`, self-test then live check. That is the existing `test:ui-isolation` shape (`--self-test && … && live`), not a new one.
- **`.github/workflows/test.yml`** — a step of the **`cljs` job**, gated on `cljs_node_test`. Hosted there for the reason that job's own comment gives for hosting the bench-lane compile: it is where the hicasso gates live, and the freeze gate's **two** input surfaces — `implementation/hicasso/**` (this PR's new case) and the freehand bench tree it was copied from (already armed) — arm `cljs_node_test` and nothing else in common. Placed **before** the ~10-minute compile: it is a sub-second static read and a divergence should red fast.
- **`actions/setup-python`** added to that job, same pinned SHA and same `3.12` as the two other python-running jobs in this workflow. The gate is pure stdlib; no `requirements.txt` install.
- **`scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`** — the same lane in the spine's node tier, with its signature registered in `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` so the drift ratchet holds the local and CI sides in step.

**When it runs**: every PR touching `implementation/hicasso/**` or the freehand bench tree (both arm `cljs_node_test`), plus every PR touching core, adapters, feature artefacts or build config — everything that already lights the `cljs` job. Not nightly-only; it is on the PR critical path and reachable through `All required checks passed`.

Why not the always-on `verify-skill-mcp-drift` invariant job, the otherwise natural home for a cheap Python checker: `scripts/check_ci_reproduce_commands.py` requires every checker step there to be a single-line `python scripts/<name>.py` whose `scripts/<name>.py` exists on disk and whose step id equals the script stem. This gate lives at `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py`, and a `scripts/` shim existing only to satisfy a naming rule would be indirection for its own sake.

## Proof that a change under `implementation/hicasso/` now classifies to the lane

A rule that matches nothing looks like coverage and is worse than none, so this is shown in both directions on the same path, against current `main`.

**Counterfactual.** `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` as it stands on `origin/main` (`9848fa10f7`) versus on this branch, both invoked on `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/runtime.cljs`:

```
=== BEFORE (origin/main 9848fa10f7) ===
  outputs_true=0          # the entire surface classified to nothing
=== AFTER (this branch) ===
cljs_node_test=true
```

**The bead's own acceptance command.** `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` gathers its change set through `--repo-root`, so it was pointed at a scratch repo whose only diff against its own `origin/main` is one new hicasso file, while the spine and classifier came from this branch:

```
$ bash scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan --repo-root <hicasso-only repo>
  JVM tier:            skip
  node/CLJS suite:     run
  reason:              classified
PLAN docs=false jvm=false node=true
```

`reason: classified` is the load-bearing word — it is what separates a real arm from the `conservative fallback (unknown surface)` an unclassified path produces. A first attempt at this probe was **vacuous** and is worth naming so nobody repeats it: the scratch repo had no `origin/main` ref, so the spine took `conservative fallback (origin/main unresolved)` and printed `node=true` for reasons having nothing to do with the new rule. The probe above has a real base ref. `jvm=false` is the second half of the claim: the arm is narrow, and no JVM roster entry was invented for an artefact with no JVM suite.

**Durable, so it cannot rot.** `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` — always-on in CI via `js-harness-self-tests` — gains four tests modelled on the freehand block beside them: the arm at artefact-root depth; the arm on future nested paths that do not exist yet (the `rf2-hic-009` carve-up

author: paadams
body:
Brings the module up to date after its first changes since 2018, and adds a new function for VM disk/datastore reporting.

## Why

On PowerShell 7 this module only *appeared* to work. `Get-WmiObject` no longer exists there, and the engine was silently proxying it through a Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility session — which returns *deserialized* objects, so `$os.ConvertToDateTime($os.LastBootUpTime)` failed at runtime:

```
ConvertToDateTime FAILED: Method invocation failed because
[Deserialized...Win32_OperatingSystem] does not contain a method named 'ConvertToDateTime'.
```

## What changed

**CIM migration.** `Get-WmiObject` is gone. One CIM session per computer, reused across all class queries — the old code queried `Win32_OperatingSystem` twice, once as a reachability probe and again for real. WSMan is tried first with a DCOM fallback, so hosts that only have the legacy RPC transport keep working.

**Correctness fixes:**

- `Get-PADiskInfo` returned `Size`/`FreeSpace` as preformatted strings, so `Sort-Object Size` sorted alphabetically and `Where-Object FreeSpace -lt 10` compared wrong. They're numbers now; the format view does the rounding.
- Warning messages rendered the literal text `.Exception.Message` — `"$_.Exception.Message"` doesn't expand a property inside a string.
- `Get-PAVMInfo` filtered `Get-View` by regex, so querying `SERVER1` also returned `SERVER10` and `SERVER1-DR`.
- `Get-PADatastoreStatistics` passed the datastore *name* to `Get-OMStat -Resource`, which PowerCLI types as `OMResource[]` and won't coerce from a string — **every call failed**. Names now resolve via `Get-OMResource`.
- `Get-PAHotfixStatus` gated on `Test-Connection`, reporting healthy servers as offline wherever ICMP is blocked.
- The three VMware functions had no error handling (one bad name aborted the pipeline) and their `-ErrorLogFilePath` parameter was declared but never used.
- Writing to the error log failed when the containing folder didn't exist.

**New: `Get-PAVMDiskInfo`.** One object per virtual disk, paired with its datastore's capacity/used/free/free-percent:

```
ComputerName Disk        SCSI Prov(GB) Used(GB) Format           Datastore    DSCap(GB) DSFree(GB) DSFree%
------------ ----        ---- -------- -------- ------           ---------    --------- ---------- -------
SERVER1      Hard disk 1 0:0     40.00    12.00 Thin             datastore_01  1,000.00     250.00    25.0
SERVER1      Hard disk 2 0:1    100.00   100.00 EagerZeroedThick datastore_02  2,000.00   1,000.00    50.0
```

**Packaging.** Version 2.1.0, explicit exports instead of wildcards, real description and gallery metadata, employer reference removed. Added LICENSE, CHANGELOG, `.gitignore`. README rewritten — it documented a `Get-PATools` command that has never existed.

## Notes for review

**Breaking changes** (documented in CHANGELOG): disk sizes are numbers not strings; `Get-PAHotfixStatus` no longer pings first. Renamed parameters (`-hotfix` → `-HotfixID`, `-ErrorLogFilePath` → `-ErrorLog`) keep the old names as aliases.

**PowerCLI is deliberately not in `RequiredModules`.** That would force everyone using the three Windows/CIM functions to install PowerCLI just to import the module. The VMware functions check their own prerequisites at runtime and fail with an actionable message instead.

**Design decisions worth a look:**

- `Get-PAVMDiskInfo` reads disks from the VM's device list rather than `Get-HardDisk`. `Get-HardDisk -VM` binds to the `VirtualMachine` interface, which can't be instantiated for a test; the device list has the same data, removes a vCenter call per VM, and is testable.
- `UsedGB` is a true per-disk figure summed from `LayoutEx`, not `Storage.PerDatastoreUsage` (which can only be attributed to a VM *and* a datastore). Snapshot deltas count towards their disk, so a thin disk with snapshots can report more used than provisioned.
- `StorageFormat` is derived from the backing's `ThinProvisioned`/`EagerlyScrub` flags, since PowerCLI 13 doesn't expose `StorageFormat` on the `HardDisk` interface. RDMs report `$null` rather than being mislabelled `Thick`.
- PSScriptAnalyzer config excludes formatter rules (`PSUseConsistentIndentation` et al) — they object to the module's deliberate column alignment and to the stock manifest template, and would bury real findings.

## Testing

147 Pester tests, PSScriptAnalyzer clean, manifest valid — verified on **both** Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.6. Windows functions smoke-tested live against localhost.

vSphere tests mock PowerCLI and self-skip where it isn't installed, so CI stays green without pulling it in. The reduction/format/layout helpers are unit-tested directly and run in CI regardless.

⚠️ **Not verified against a live vCenter or vROps.** The VMware changes are mock-driven, so property paths into `ExtensionData` are my best reading of the API rather than observed output. Worth one manual run of `Get-PAVMDiskInfo` and `Get-PADatastoreStatistics` against a real environment before trusting a bulk report.

⚠️ The CI workflow runs on runners where the execution policy is `Bypass`. On a locked-down Windows PowerShell 5.1 host, `PATools.ps1xml` fails to load because it contains a `ScriptProperty`/`ScriptMethod` — that path isn't covered.

author: anras573
body:
## Summary
- Adds `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;` next to the existing `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;` in `migrate()` (`electron/db.ts`), which every connection goes through via `openDb()`.
- `synchronous` previously stayed at its `FULL` default, fsyncing on every commit. During an agent turn the app writes frequently — `saveToolCall`, `updateToolCallStatus` (twice per tool call), `updateSessionStatus`, message inserts/updates — so each paid that fsync cost.
- `NORMAL` is the standard pairing with WAL: the database cannot be corrupted by power loss, worst case is losing the most recent transaction(s), which for this data (a tool-call status row) is acceptable.
- This is a per-connection pragma, not schema, so it belongs in `migrate()`/`openDb()` rather than a numbered migration.
- Adds a test in `electron/db.test.ts` asserting `PRAGMA synchronous` reports `1` (NORMAL) after `migrate()`.

Closes #179 (part of epic #175).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run typecheck` passes
- [x] `bun run test` — all 1456 tests pass, including the new synchronous-pragma test

author: maximilian-maag
body:
## Why

`deployment_environments.webhook_token` was pulling double duty — the value stored in that single column had to simultaneously match:
1. **Outbound** — the pipeline-trigger token that GitLab expects on the `POST /projects/:id/trigger/pipeline` body
2. **Inbound** — the shared secret that GitLab sends as `X-Gitlab-Token` when it delivers a Pipeline event to the portal

Those live in **two independent GitLab UI locations** (`Settings → CI/CD → Pipeline trigger tokens` vs. `Settings → Webhooks → Secret token`). Any rotation that touched one silently broke the other, and orders stuck at Provisioning until both sides were manually re-synced.

## What changes

- **Migration 0004**: `ALTER TABLE deployment_environments ADD COLUMN callback_secret TEXT NOT NULL` with a backfill `SET callback_secret = webhook_token WHERE NULL` — legacy installations keep working during rollout.
- **Backend**: new `callback-secret` route with `GET` (reveal) and `POST` (rotate). `createEnvironment` auto-generates a `ohc-cb-<64 hex>` value via `crypto.randomBytes(32)`; the operator can never set it directly. The webhook validator switches to `callback_secret`.
- **Frontend** (`EnvironmentsManager`): a new **Callback Secret** panel in the Edit modal with Reveal / Copy / Regenerate. `Webhook Token` gets a hint clarifying it's the outbound trigger token.
- **Docs**: `root.md`, `gitlab-opentofu-workflow.md`, and `handbook.tex` (rebuilt PDF, 95 pages) describe the two-token model and where each lives in GitLab.
- **Tests**: new route tests for reveal + rotate + auth; a webhook-route regression test that verifies rotating the outbound trigger token does NOT accidentally unlock the callback.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint --max-warnings 0` clean for backend + frontend
- 42/42 vitest passes across touched suites (environments service, callback-secret route, webhook route, pipeline-stacks)

## Rollout / Test plan

- [ ] Merge → Watchtower pulls new backend image → migration 0004 runs at boot, backfills existing envs
- [ ] Open **Admin → Environments → Edit → Callback Secret → Reveal current** — value visible and equals the previous webhook_token for the existing env
- [ ] Set GitLab Project Webhook Secret token to that value → send Test Pipeline event → HTTP 200
- [ ] Regenerate callback secret in portal → update GitLab webhook Secret → trigger a real order → order transitions Provisioning → Completed
- [ ] Rotate the outbound trigger token independently (GitLab Settings → CI/CD, then portal Webhook Token field) — callback still works throughout

author: bennyzrealty-sys
body:
Requirement 1 of the project, finally answerable now that Phase 4 records where attention was: **on open, offer the writer his way back to where he was working.**

Nothing is stored for this feature. It is four queries over tables that already exist — which is the argument for event sourcing, stated as code.

## The four destinations (`src/features/resume/destinations.ts`)

| Destination | Resolved from | Decision it needed |
|---|---|---|
| Last edited | most recently updated block with `revisionCount > 0` | the filter is what stops a fresh import from offering the importer's last paragraph as "where you were" |
| Last read | deepest block that accrued dwell last session | ADR-0026 — not a stored scroll offset |
| Longest dwelled | highest gated dwell last session | the ADR-0017 model, reused |
| Most rewritten | highest `revisionCount` within 7 days | without a window it is a monument: the paragraph fought over in March keeps winning in August |

The dwell half runs **one** query and ranks it twice — by accrued dwell for one destination, by `order` for the other, compared lexicographically because `order` is a string (ADR-0007). The block scan streams with `each` rather than collecting: its window can cover the whole document, and holding that array would put the manuscript in memory.

## The strip (`ResumeStrip.tsx`, ADR-0023)

- **Fixed order.** Slots with no answer are rendered and *disabled*, not removed — if an absent destination closed the gap, the other three would move between launches, and the point of a fixed order is that the strip can be operated without reading it.
- **Absent entirely until something resolves**, so a fresh install sees nothing rather than four dead buttons.
- **The learning is the default, never the position.** Five picks before anything is emphasised; ties break by the fixed order, because resolving them by recency would make the default oscillate between launches — the same instability one level down.
- **The strip focuses itself**, not its default slot, so Enter activates the default without a tab press while Tab still walks the four in order. Focusing the slot would make the default's *position* matter, which is the thing being kept stable.
- The pick is written **before** the document moves, and awaited: closing the app right after resuming is ordinary, and a fire-and-forget write gets aborted mid-transaction when it happens.
- Excerpts go through the segmenter's `preview` — `slice(0, 48)` on Malayalam severs a vowel sign from its base.

Pick counts live in `settings`, not `signals`: a pick is an explicit choice rather than an observation, and it has to survive the 90-day signal prune.

## ADR-0026 — pushing back on destination 2

`docs/SIGNALS.md` specified "furthest scroll position from last session". Building it surfaced two problems:

- **A scroll offset is not a place in the document.** It is a pixel measurement against a layout that depends on viewport width, the loaded font and the height cache. Restore it after a rotation and it lands at whatever text now occupies those pixels. Everything else here addresses *blocks* (ADR-0003) precisely because blocks survive relayout.
- **Scrolling to the end is not reading to the end.** A fling that comes to rest at the bottom sets "furthest scroll" to the last paragraph — ADR-0017's error in a less obvious disguise.

So it is the deepest block that accrued *gated* dwell. A session spent only flinging produces no "last read" at all, which is correct. The ADR names its own revisit trigger: a writer who revises *backwards* gets "deepest" where he means "where I stopped", and the switch to latest-by-timestamp needs no new data.

## Perf

80,022-word corpus, serial, three runs. Phase 4 in brackets.

| Metric | Budget | Phase 5 | Phase 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold open | < 1.5 s | 154–188 ms | [151–174] |
| Keystroke handler | < 16 ms | 0.78–0.83 ms median | [0.79–0.93] |
| Frame p95 while typing | < 33 ms | 16.8–16.9 ms | [16.9–17.0] |
| Scroll p95 | < 33 ms | 17.1–17.2 ms | [17.1–17.3] |
| Memory | < 150 MB | 3.8–4.2 MB | [3.8–4.0] |
| Search miss scan | < 250 ms | 73–91 ms | [71–79] |

Cold open's top end is ~8% higher. That is inside run-to-run noise, but it has a mechanism worth naming rather than waving away: the resume queries run at open, and after an import every block falls inside the seven-day rewrite window, so that scan streams the whole document. It is off the first-paint path — the strip renders nothing until it resolves — and if it grows, deferring the resolve to an idle callback is the fix. Recorded in `HANDOFF.md` as a watch item rather than pre-emptively optimised, so the committed code is the code that was measured.

## Tests

248 unit (+17) · 36 e2e (+7) · 6 perf. All passing; typecheck clean.

The e2e spec covers the parts that only exist in a real launch: that a fresh import offers nothing, that an edit then a relaunch offers the paragraph, that picking it moves a document opened at the top, that empty slots stay in place and disabled, that a session spent reading produces the dwell destinations, and that the default appears only on the fifth pick — and then responds to Enter.

Fixes recheck findings M18, M19, M20, L11 from `repo-sanity-recheck-2026-08-09.md`, tracked as `agents-config-9k9.215.12` under epic `agents-config-9k9.215`, plus a fifth false claim discovered in the same file during verification (AGENTS_PRIMER.md:21, added to scope by the epic coordinator), plus review round 1 (2 findings) and review round 2 (10 findings, all primer-vs-installer-code). **M19 — AGENTS_PRIMER.md:45,84-85, model enum "opus[1m], sonnet[1m], sonnet, haiku".**

**L11 — AGENTS_PRIMER.md:47, memory comment "project | user | none (default)".**
`memory` accepts `user`, `project`, `local` — no `none` value. Fixed to match the table below it.

**M18 — COMMANDS_PRIMER.md:77,140-142, plugin path `src/plugins/<plugin>/commands/`.**
False. Verified against `overlay.py` and `namespaces.py` (`PLUGIN_TOOL_SCOPED` uses `.{tool}/`; `SHARED` excludes `commands`). Fixed to `src/plugins/<plugin>/.<tool>/commands/`, matching RULES_PRIMER.md/SKILLS_PRIMER.md.

**Fifth claim — AGENTS_PRIMER.md:21, "not... the parent's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md context".**
False. Official docs' "What loads at startup": a non-fork subagent's context includes the full CLAUDE.md hierarchy; Explore/Plan are the only exception. Fixed.

## Review round 2 (global-consistency lens, 10 findings, all verified against cited installer code, all fixed, no rebuttal)

**r2f1 (mechanical)** — SKILLS_PRIMER.md:139,141 said the `disable-model-invocation` flag is read from source front matter *before* per-tool projection. Verified against `deploy_gate.py`'s `_judge()` docstring: it's read from the **deployed** front matter *after* projection, so a tool that strips the key (Codex, OpenCode) measures the body against the strict 2,000-token cap, not the looser 5,000-token one. **r2f2 (mechanical)** — RULES_PRIMER.md:181 said admission is judged on the merged bytes, so an append onto a record-less base deploys nothing. Verified against `deploy_gate.py`'s docstring and reassembly loop (lines ~25-33, ~204-244): admission is judged **per contributor**, and the destination is reassembled only from the survivors — a record-less base drops out, but a plugin addition with its own valid record still deploys. **r2f3 (mechanical)** — AGENTS_PRIMER.md:169,176 claimed shared agents (base and plugin `.agents/agents/`) reach every active tool. **r2f6 (mechanical)** — AGENTS_PRIMER.md's File Locations block indented `<agent-name>.md` as a direct sibling of `src/plugins/<plugin>/`'s two subdirectory lines, implying a plugin-root file path the installer never stages. body:
## What changed
- Replace the missing browser-session-cookie secret with a short-lived GitHub Actions OIDC identity for the protected preview hosted lifecycle.
- Validate issuer, audience, subject, repository, and exact workflow ref at the API boundary.
- Keep the workflow preview-only, explicit-consent, PKCE-protected, mutation-scoped, cleanup-safe, and receipt-redacted.
- Leave production automation identity configuration absent.

## Why
The lifecycle receipt needs a real authenticated resource-owner identity, but storing or extracting a browser session cookie would create unnecessary secret and operator burden. GitHub Actions OIDC gives the workflow a short-lived, non-exported identity with an exact allowlist.

## Impact
- No new long-lived secret is required.
- The preview API accepts only the configured GitHub Actions workflow identity for this automation path.
- Production remains disabled for this automation path.

## Validation
- Focused resource-owner, consent, grants, MCP-provider, and browser OIDC tests pass.
- API build, typecheck, lint, format, duplicate checks, redaction fail-closed check, and script syntax checks pass.
- One combined OAuth test encountered an unrelated Miniflare/Workerd SQLite readonly startup failure; CI is required to validate the full matrix under the repository Node 22 setup.

## Follow-up
After merge: deploy preview, run the protected hosted lifecycle with `confirm_preview=true`, inspect the redacted receipt, and only then close issue #524.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes OAuth resource-owner resolution and preview automation auth, but scope is tight (preview-only, explicit claim allowlist) and removes long-lived session secrets from CI.
> 
> **Overview**
> The protected preview **hosted OAuth lifecycle** no longer depends on a maintainer-copied `FANALYX_OIDC_SESSION_COOKIE` secret. The workflow grants **`id-token: write`**, the lifecycle script mints a GitHub Actions OIDC token, and consent, grant listing, and revocation use **`Authorization: Bearer`** instead of a session cookie.
> 
> The preview API adds a separate **`AUTOMATION_OIDC_*`** verification path (issuer, audience, JWKS, exact subject, repository, and `job_workflow_ref`) wired only in preview `wrangler.toml`. Human Clerk OIDC and browser sessions are unchanged; production does not configure automation OIDC.
> 
> Docs and receipt redaction checks are updated accordingly (including blocking `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN` in artifacts). A focused unit test locks the allowlist behavior.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 76239f039a794acea0731e6c3b226c55dacf9e62. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: selvaz
body:
## Riepilogo

Fase 4 di `docs/node-advisor-operational-plan.md` (§13, LP/LT-09) — la **prima fase che chiama davvero un LLM**. Ogni fase precedente (0-3) è Python deterministico, zero LLM.

- **`project/advisor/agent.py`** — `run_advisor_turn()`: **una sola** chiamata `Agent` con output strutturato (`AdvisorTurnResult`: `route "explain"|"propose"`, `message`, `proposed_views`), non un `Plan` LazyBridge a 10 step. Semplificazione deliberata rispetto allo schizzo §8.2, documentata come Decisione 5 dell'ADR: i dieci step descrivono un invariante (l'LLM propone tramite uno schema vincolato; tutto il resto è validazione/calcolo/persistenza deterministici; nessun tool dell'LLM può mai scrivere), non un numero di step imposto. `route="explain"` ritorna **prima** che `validate_view_set`/counterfactual/`create_proposal` vengano mai chiamati.
- **`_prepare_view_proposal_tools()`**: `NodeAdvisorReadTools` (tutti e 7, read-only per costruzione) + `DataHubTools`/`StatisticalAnalysisTools` come superficie di ricerca limitata. Nessun tool save/delete/apply esiste su questa superficie — **provato dal test**, non solo dichiarato per design.
- **`services.create_proposal()`** (rinominata da `create_fixture_proposal`, nessun altro chiamante esisteva): ora accetta `producer_kind`/`producer_id`/`model`, così il job fixture di Fase 3 e il percorso LLM di Fase 4 condividono un'unica pipeline con provenance diversa, invece di due copie della stessa logica.

## Sicurezza: test di injection senza bisogno di una vera API key

I test usano un LLM mockato per provare che una view candidata che punta a uno strumento di financing, o a uno strumento fuori dall'universo del nodo — cioè un output LLM **completamente compromesso**, come se un'injection fosse riuscita — viene comunque rifiutata dal validator deterministico, mai applicata silenziosamente.

## Verifica live

Un test opt-in (skippato senza `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) fa una vera chiamata LLM — **eseguito per davvero in questa sessione** contro l'API DeepSeek reale: NodeContext vero, tool reali, parsing dell'output strutturato reale, `route="explain"`, zero proposte create.

## Exit criteria (§13 Fase 4)

- [x] Domande informative non avviano il Plan di proposta (`route="explain"` ritorna prima di validate/counterfactual/create_proposal — provato)
- [x] "prepara ma non applicare" produce solo `pending_approval` (stesso pipeline di Fase 3, mai auto-approvato)
- [x] Injection test non amplia privilegi (nessun tool write esiste; view malevola comunque rifiutata dal validator)
- [x] Budget/timeout visibili — `max_turns=8` sull'Agent (§9.3 rimane un affinamento futuro, non bloccante per l'MVP)

## Verifica eseguita

- `pytest tests/test_advisor_agent.py -q`: 7 passed (incluso il live smoke test, eseguito per davvero)
- `pytest -q` completo: 472 passed — **zero regressioni**
- `ruff check src tests project/tree_studio.py project/advisor`: pulito
- `mypy src/lazyportfolio`: nessun problema, 39 file

## Nota sulla CI

`lazybridge`/`lazytools` non sono installati nella CI di questo repo (stesso gap già segnalato per la CI di LazyTools rispetto a `lazyportfolio`, PR Fase 2) — `test_advisor_agent.py` usa `pytest.importorskip` quindi skippa pulito lì invece di fallire. La verifica reale (inclusa quella live) è quella locale, dove l'intero ecosistema è installato in editable mode dallo stesso checkout.

## Fuori scope (per costruzione)

Reviewer esterno, hardening avanzato, red-team suite completa (Fase 5). Innesto dell'Investment Committee come secondo producer (Fase 6).

author: tsouth89
body:
## Summary
Closes #150. `clips.content_hash` carried a plain index, so deduplication rested
entirely on the `SELECT uuid FROM clips WHERE content_hash = ?` lookup
succeeding. That makes a failed lookup indistinguishable from a genuine miss:
any caller collapsing the error arm into `None` silently doubles the user's
history. #137 fixed the one caller; the schema still permitted the bad state for
the next one. Now the database refuses.

## The migration

`Database::enforce_content_hash_uniqueness` collapses existing duplicates and
then creates the unique index. **Newest row wins**, and **pinned state and
folder membership carry forward** from the rows being removed — losing a pin
because a duplicate happened to be newer would be silent data loss, and a pin is
cheap to keep.

Three ordering decisions carry the risk here:

- **It runs after the encrypted-storage and clip-format migrations**, not inside
  `migrate()`. Both of those rewrite `content_hash` for existing rows and can
  therefore *create* duplicates that did not exist when the schema was set up.
  Creating the unique index before them would fail the upgrade of exactly the
  installs that need it.
- **The unique index is created before the old one is dropped**, so a database
  that still holds duplicates fails there and rolls back with its old index
  intact. Per the issue: leaving the constraint off beats a half-migrated
  database.
- **Image files are deleted after the transaction commits**, never inside it. A
  rollback must not leave a surviving clip pointing at a file that is gone.
  Child rows in `clip_images`/`clip_formats` cascade (the pool sets
  `foreign_keys(true)`), but files on disk do not.

Startup **logs** a failure rather than panicking. A failure leaves the database
exactly as the previous version left it, which still works; refusing to start
over a hardening step would be the worse outcome.

## Tests

The four the issue asks for, plus one:

- a fresh database gets the unique index, and the old non-unique index is gone
- a database with no duplicates upgrades with nothing removed and no clip lost
- duplicates collapse to the newest row — with the pin and folder deliberately
  placed on the *oldest* row, the one that loses, so the test fails if they are
  not carried forward
- a duplicate insert after migration is rejected with a uniqueness violation
- child rows of a removed duplicate do not outlive it

## Not verified here

The issue's last step is upgrading over a real install with populated history.
I have not done that — it means running against your live clipboard database,
which is not mine to experiment on. The migration is covered by the tests above
and rolls back on failure, but a real-data upgrade is still worth doing
deliberately, ideally with `cubby.db.bak` fresh beforehand.

## Verification
- `cargo test --locked --all-targets`: 186 passed, 2 ignored
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- `pnpm run test`: 74 passed; `pnpm run release:check`
- `AGENTS.md` gotcha rewritten: the hazard is now a lost capture reported as a
  constraint error, not a corrupted history

  * Removed associated files for duplicate entries during cleanup.

body:
## The finding

W3.4 has recorded, across **four separate merges**, that reading Linear's canonical state category "needs a GraphQL query change that 400s the WHOLE query if wrong, and the test fake accepts any query, so no CI test in this repo can catch it — it needs one real call against a real tenant."

The first half is right. **The conclusion is wrong**, because it assumes validating a query document requires a tenant.

Measured 2026-08-09 against `api.linear.app/graphql`, negative-controlled FIRST (fabricated host ⇒ does not resolve; fabricated path on the real host ⇒ 404, so the answers are not blanket):

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `query { thisFieldDoesNotExist }` | HTTP 400 `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| the shipped `linearIssuesQuery`, verbatim | HTTP 401 `AUTHENTICATION_ERROR` |
| that query with `state { name type }` | HTTP 401 `AUTHENTICATION_ERROR` |

**Linear validates the document before it authenticates.** So "this query would 400" and "this query is well-formed" are distinguishable with no credentials at all. `scripts/w34-linear-schema-probe.py` re-runs it, reading the query out of `linear.go` rather than a copy.

## The vocabulary is not an enum — the asymmetry with #73

Jira's `/rest/api/2/statuscategory` enumerates exactly four, so #73 could say "there is no fifth to miss". Linear models `WorkflowState.type` as `String!`; measured across **1,132 schema types and 115 enums, not one** carries the issue-state vocabulary. It comes from the field's own description, read by unauthenticated introspection:

> One of `"triage"`, `"backlog"`, `"unstarted"`, `"started"`, `"completed"`, `"canceled"`, `"duplicate"`.

⚠ **That is seven. Linear's public docs list six.** `duplicate` is the one an implementation written from memory drops — #73's "no fifth to miss" hazard, arriving as a seventh.

## Decisions, stated rather than made silently

- **Name first**, so a recognised import is byte-for-byte what it was. This merge is purely additive.
- **`triage` and `duplicate` do NOT resolve** (#73's `undefined` rule). Track has no counterpart; answering them invents the meaning this change exists to stop inventing. Both are reported as arrived-and-unusable — a *third* distinct line from "no type present".
- ⚠ **`started` is coarser than the name mapping.** Linear files both "In Progress" and "In Review" under it, so a custom review state resolves to `in_progress`. This is where Linear differs from Jira, where #73 measured zero disagreement — and it is exactly why name-first is load-bearing rather than a preference. It is on the report, not hidden.

## Guards

Before this PR, `linearIssuesQuery` and `defaultLinearURL` appeared in **zero test files**, and every fake in the package answers any path and any method with the same body (positive-controlled: the same grep *does* find jira.go's assertions, so the instrument reads).

- **Wire contract** — query document, endpoint, POST, and the no-`Bearer` auth header `linear.go`'s own comment names and nothing asserted.
- **Rule 1** — the mapper's switch parsed from the AST, both directions against the pinned vocabulary.
- **Rule 2** — the measured vocabulary pinned by hand, because deleting a `case` moves the parse and the mapper together.
- **Job level, real Postgres** — the async runner + `linear_api` source, status column read back per identifier. `TestRunner_LinearAPI_EndToEnd` drives this route today and asserts only the job row's `{status, imported}`.

## Red first, then 12 positive controls

Red at **7 test functions, behaviourally** — the file compiles against today's code on purpose (#74's C1: a control that cannot tell "the guard caught it" from "nothing compiled" is not a control).

12 controls, each anchor-count-asserted before applying, each naming a test that must stay green, each file restored sha256-identical. **11 caught, 1 recorded as a demonstration rather than counted as a catch:**

- ⚠ **C1's must-stay-green IS the finding**: reverting the query leaves every fixture still sending `type` and every behavioural test still passing. The wire contract is the *only* guard that reds.
- ⚠ **C4 controls a test that passed on its first run** — the name-first precedence assertion.
- ⚠ **C11 isolates the job tests** — it reds only those while every source-level assertion stays green, so the job file is not the unit test twice (#74's C9, one layer over).
- ⚠ **C12 is a vacuity demo and STAYS GREEN by design**: it makes the wire assertion self-referential *and* reverts the query, and the test still passes. That is why the literal is hardcoded (#75's C6).

⚠ **Two controls corrected the harness itself, which is the part worth keeping:**
1. **C6's first form was a wrong edit, not a caught mutation.** It matched its anchor, edited real bytes, and left `triage` returning exactly what it returned before — reported "NOT CAUGHT" for a guard that was working. *An anchor assertion proves the edit applied; it says nothing about whether the replacement meant anything.*
2. **C7's restore corrupted `csv.go`.** Reverse substitution for a deletion control is `str.replace("", old, 1)`, which Python inserts at position 0 — it silently prepended the deleted case above the package comment. The sha assertion caught it; restore is now from original bytes.
3. **C8's obvious anchor matched 3×** (`case "backlog"` is also in both name mappers). The count assertion caught it before it mutated the wrong function.

## Gauntlet

`gofmt` clean · `go vet` clean · `go test -timeout 120s -race -count=1 ./...` 39 packages ok on real Postgres from zero (26 migrations) · semgrep 15 rules 0 findings · compose-secrets 0 findings · golangci-lint v2.12.2 0 issues.

1058 insertions, **2 deletions**, both lines replaced in place. No migration; 0026 still the highest.

## What this still does not prove, said rather than implied

That a **customer's** tenant populates the field, or what their states are called. That still needs a real tenant — W3.4 item (3). It is why every unrecognised state reports which path decided it: the first real import answers that out loud instead of hiding it.

author: talexdreamsoul
body:
Closes #733.

Two plaintext repository variables decided security-relevant behaviour in a `pull_request_target` job — one that runs **with repository secrets in scope on pull requests from forks**.

### The `*` bypass
`AI_REVIEW_ALLOWED_ASSOCIATIONS` accepted `'*'`, which skipped the author gate entirely.

That reads like a convenience setting ("let everyone use AI review") and is not one: under `pull_request_target` it hands **any fork author** a job holding `OPENAI_API_KEY`. It is now refused with an explanation rather than honoured.

### The endpoint
`OPENAI_BASE_URL` had **no validation at all** — `normalizeOpenAiBaseUrl` only strips a trailing slash, so the bearer token went wherever the variable pointed.

Now checked against a host allowlist, parsed with `new URL` and compared on `hostname`, because a prefix test still accepts `https://api.openai.com.evil.test`. `api.openai.com`, `api.deepseek.com` (already used elsewhere in this repo) and localhost are permitted.

### Both guards are mutation-verified
- restoring the wildcard → the first test fails, second still passes
- removing the allowlist → the second test fails, first still passes

A third test asserts the trigger is **still `pull_request_target`**. If that ever changes, the first two stop guarding secrets and should be revisited rather than passing vacuously.

**191/191** across `vitest.workspace-scripts.config.mjs`. An earlier run showed 2 failures — that was a race between restoring the mutated file and the suite starting, not a real result; the clean rerun is green.

## Summary

Reject a multipart byte-range part that would continue into a non-adjacent requested range. Previously, a malformed response such as `Content-Range: bytes 0-19/...` could fill requests for `0-9` and `100-109`, silently writing bytes 10-19 into the second buffer.

Adjacent ranges remain supported because the HTTP request preprocessor coalesces them intentionally.

Add a loopback HTTP regression test that sends the malformed multipart response and verifies that the transfer fails before the second range is written.

author: rexlunae
body:
Closes #409.

## What was wrong

Bulma 1.x builds every `is-light` chip out of two lightness tokens it declares for the light scheme only: a 90% background and a ~15% foreground. Its own `[data-theme="dark"]` block leaves both alone. So `tag is-info is-light` — the pill on the cron, MCP, memory, tools, channels, approvals, services, downloads and logs dialogs, 27 sites — renders as a near-white slab on a 7% shell, bright enough to pull the eye off whatever the dialog is actually saying.

`.has-text-grey` is a separate case: Bulma hard-codes it to `#69748c !important` with no dark variant at all. That is 4.0:1 on the shell and 3.5:1 on a raised panel — under AA for the small print it is mostly used on (field hints, timestamps, empty states), across 36 sites.

## The fix

Inverted the token pair under the dark theme rather than restyling the pills one at a time, so the markup stays on stock Bulma classes — which is what the issue asks for. Hue and saturation still come from the colour itself, so an info chip is still blue and a danger chip is still red; only the lightnesses swap ends.

Contrast was checked rather than eyeballed: 22% background against the 80% steps clears WCAG AA for every colour in the palette, with 5.9:1 at the worst pairing (warning). `.has-text-grey` now points at the scheme's weak text, which the theme already tunes for this background — 6.5:1.

Notifications needed a rule rather than a token: Bulma writes their 90% into `.notification.is-<colour>.is-light` literally, where an override of `--bulma-light-l` cannot reach it.

## Why the override lives where it does

On `[data-theme="dark"]`, not `:root`. A custom property is substituted where it is declared, so a `:root` declaration would bake in the light value and every descendant would inherit it straight past the themed element — the same trap the existing comment at the top of `styles.css` documents for the `--rc-*` aliases.

## Tests

Three, in `crates/rustyclaw-desktop/src/app/mod.rs`. The interesting one asserts that the vendored Bulma *still* leaves these tokens to the light scheme: if a future upgrade starts handling dark mode itself, our override becomes a second opinion on a settled question, and the test says so instead of leaving it to be found by eye. The other two check the override is present in the block carrying the attribute, and that the hard-coded notification rules are covered.

`cargo test -p rustyclaw-desktop`, fmt and clippy all clean.

author: arthsdev
body:
## Summary
Adds a status filter (Last 100/Pending/Verified/Resolved) to the
admin moderation dashboard, applied consistently to both the card
list and the map view from a single piece of page state.

## What's new

**Status filter**
- List: filters server-side via `GET /occurrences?status=X` (already
  supported by the backend)
- Map: filters client-side via the `OccurrenceMapFilters` prop
  `OccurrenceMap` already accepted since its original design — this
  is the first UI actually wiring it up
- Both share the same `statusFilter` state in `AdminPage`, so
  switching the filter updates both views together

**"Last 100" instead of "All"**
The unfiltered view was labeled "All" but only ever returns the first
100 occurrences (`size=100`, a known stopgap — see backlog). Relabeled
to "Last 100" for honesty, and paired with a backend change (separate
PR) flipping default sort to most-recent-first, so the label is
actually accurate.

**Map zoom fix**
`FitBoundsToMarkers` produced an excessively tight zoom when exactly
one marker was visible (a single-point bounds has no real area, so
Leaflet's fitBounds over-zoomed). Fixed with a dedicated `flyTo` at a
fixed reasonable zoom for the single-marker case.

**Cleanup**
Removed leftover `canEdit`/`canEditLookup` plumbing in `OccurrenceMap`
and `OccurrenceMapMarker` — superseded by `OccurrenceDetailModal`
handling the edit-permission check internally (previous PR).

## Considered and deferred
Real pagination (numbered pages, `GET /occurrences/{id}` for the
detail modal to stop depending on the loaded list) was discussed as
an alternative to this filter-based approach. Deferred: filtering
solves today's actual usability problem (finding occurrences by
status) at a fraction of the cost; pagination solves a data-volume
problem that doesn't exist yet at this project's current scale.
Revisit if/when occurrence volume grows past what a single filtered
fetch comfortably handles.

## Testing
Manual verification:
- Switching status filter updates list and map together
- Resolving/verifying an occurrence while its status filter is active
  removes it from both views automatically (existing cache
  invalidation covers this)
- Map zoom behaves correctly with 1, 2, and many markers
- No leftover TypeScript errors from the `canEdit` cleanup

## Depends on
Backend PR changing default sort order — without it, "Last 100" would
show the oldest occurrences instead of the most recent ones.

author: tutkli
body:
## Summary

- Closes [#1733](https://github.com/tutkli/forty-cdk/issues/1733). The published FESM bundles no longer carry the library's own JSDoc: `dist/forty-cdk/fesm2022/*.mjs` drops from 2.80 MB to 1.74 MB (61.9%), with `forty-cdk-core.mjs` at 533,641 → 263,486 bytes (49.4%). The emitted `.d.ts` are **byte-identical** to `main` — their JSDoc is the consumer-facing documentation and `stripInternal` already removes what should not ship.

- **The issue's option 1 cannot work, and that is worth recording.** `removeComments: true` on [tsconfig.lib.prod.json](projects/forty-cdk/tsconfig.lib.prod.json) is inert wherever it is written: ng-packagr pins `removeComments: false` in the mandatory `extraOptions` it hands `readConfiguration` (`ng-packagr/src/lib/ts/tsconfig.js:62`), and TypeScript's `extend(existingOptions, parsedConfig.options)` copies the **existing** options *last* (`typescript/lib/typescript.js:3147`), so the injected value wins over the project's tsconfig. Setting the flag and rebuilding produced a byte-identical `dist/`, which is how this was caught rather than shipped as a no-op.

- **So this takes the issue's alternative — a post-step.** [strip-fesm-comments.mjs](scripts/strip-fesm-comments.mjs) runs first in `postbuild`, before the nine gates, so every gate and `npm publish ./dist/forty-cdk` see the bytes that ship. It strips by **splicing the original text**, not by re-printing it, which is what ng-packagr's own comment (`can remove important annotations, such as /* @__PURE__ */`) is warning about:
  - **Annotations survive.** A comment carrying `@__PURE__`, `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__`, a legal notice, or the `sourceMappingURL` pointer is kept. The library emits none of the first kind today; the check is there so the day one appears it is not silently dropped.
  - **The `.mjs.map` stay valid.** Each stripped comment is replaced by the newlines it contained, so every line of code keeps its line number, and a comment with code after it on the same line is skipped so no column moves either. `class ForAspectRatio` sits on line 34 before and after, and each bundle's mapping-group count still equals its line count.

- **The splice is verified rather than trusted, per bundle.** Each file is re-parsed before and after and printed through a comment-free printer; the two prints must be identical, the line count must match, and a bundle whose walk found no comment at all fails — the step is idempotent, so "removed nothing" would otherwise be indistinguishable from "stopped finding anything", and every bundle ends with a `sourceMappingURL` pointer that makes one kept comment the floor. Stubbing the comment walk to return nothing fails all 59 bundles and writes none of them.

- **AC1's ≤60% target for `fesm2022/` is unreachable as written, and the measurement below shows why.** 4.43 MB of that 7.37 MB directory is `.mjs.map`, not JavaScript — ng-packagr pins `sourceMap: true` and `inlineSources: true` in the same mandatory block, so each bundle ships a map embedding the full TypeScript source. Comments are the JS half's problem and the JS half is where the 61.9% lands; the directory as a whole reaches 84.8%. Shrinking the maps is a separate decision (drop them, or drop `sourcesContent` and make them undebuggable) that this change deliberately does not take.

- Two ordinal phrases in [conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) now say "of the nine gates" rather than counting positions in `postbuild`, which the new step would otherwise shift by one.

### Measured before / after

Both builds clean, on `7df3319b`:

| | `main` | this PR | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dist/forty-cdk` | 10,097,984 B | 8,979,039 B | 88.9% |
| `dist/forty-cdk/fesm2022` | 7,369,821 B | 6,250,876 B | 84.8% |
|   └ `fesm2022/*.mjs` | 2,940,274 B | 1,821,329 B | **61.9%** |
|   └ `fesm2022/*.mjs.map` | 4,429,547 B | 4,429,547 B | 100% |
| `fesm2022/forty-cdk-core.mjs` | 533,641 B | 263,486 B | **49.4%** |
| `dist/forty-cdk/types` | 1,745,773 B | 1,745,773 B | 100% |
| `types/forty-cdk-core.d.ts` | 437,178 B | 437,178 B | 100% |

3,831 comments removed across 59 bundles, 59 kept (one `sourceMappingURL` each), in 2.1 s.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — lib, spec, harness and playground projects all clean.
- [x] `pnpm build` — ng-packagr clean, then `strip-fesm-comments` plus all nine `postbuild` gates green, with `check-emitted-types-compile.mjs` reporting TS2304 + TS2420.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 7464/7464 passing across 231 files, unchanged vs. `main` (no library source touched).
- [x] `pnpm build:docs` — the playground bundles and prerenders against the stripped `dist/forty-cdk`.
- [x] Liveness: stubbing `collectComments` to return `[]` fails all 59 bundles and leaves `dist/` unwritten.
- [x] Idempotence: a second `pnpm strip:fesm-comments` reports 0 removed / 59 kept and rewrites nothing.
- [x] `.d.ts` spot check: `forty-cdk-accordion.d.ts`, `forty-cdk-dialog.d.ts` and `forty-cdk-core.d.ts` are byte-identical to the `main` build (27 / 56 / 1108 JSDoc blocks intact).
- [ ] `pnpm test:e2e` — not run; the change touches no library source, no harness fixture and no E2E spec.

relit la liste des collections pour trancher :

```python
except LedgerError:
    listed = _request("GET", f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}{_API}/collections", token, None, timeout)
    names = {c.get("name") for c in listed.get("collections", [])}
    if collection not in names:
        raise
```

Cette garde `if collection not in names: raise` n'était exercée par **aucun test** du
dépôt. Le faux serveur HTTP de `tests/test_immudb.py` ne produit jamais l'état « le
POST échoue réellement ET la collection cible est absente de la liste de secours » —
il ne teste que le cas idempotent (collection déjà là). Un mutant qui neutralise la
garde (`if False: raise`, ou équivalent) fait passer les 1901 tests existants sans
qu'aucun ne rougisse. Sans elle, un échec réel de création de collection serait
silencieusement traité comme un succès — **sur le ledger d'audit lui-même**.

### Correctif

Aucune modification du code de production : la garde était déjà correcte, elle
manquait seulement de couverture de test (pinning). Deux tests ajoutés à
`tests/test_immudb.py`, avec une double injectée pour `_request` (monkeypatch, aucun
réseau réel) :

- `test_ensure_collection_relance_si_absente_de_la_liste_secours` — POST échoue
  (`LedgerError`) ET la collection cible n'est **pas** dans le GET de secours →
  l'exception doit remonter. Test de pinning de la garde.
- `test_ensure_collection_absorbe_si_presente_dans_la_liste_secours` — contrôle
  négatif complémentaire : POST échoue mais la collection cible **est** dans le GET
  de secours (2e appel idempotent) → aucune exception ne remonte.

### Cycle RED/GREEN (preuve, méthode PROOF)

- **RED** : garde neutralisée temporairement (`if collection not in names:` →
  `if False:  # CAND-008 RED probe`) dans `immudb.py`, puis
  `pytest tests/test_immudb.py -k "relance_si_absente or absorbe_si_presente" -v`
  → `1 failed, 1 passed` : le test de pinning échoue avec
  `Failed: DID NOT RAISE LedgerError` (le test complémentaire reste vert, comme
  attendu — il ne dépend pas de cette branche).
- **GREEN** : garde restaurée à l'identique (`git diff` sur `immudb.py` vide, vérifié),
  même commande → `2 passed`. `pytest tests/test_immudb.py -v` complet → `8 passed`
  (6 tests existants + 2 nouveaux).

### Suite complète (avant / après), flags mandatés

```
PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 PYTHONPATH="$(pwd)/src:.../TOOLS/lib" \
  python3 -m pytest tests -q --no-header --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
```

- **Avant** (baseline mesurée, pas la valeur citée dans le mandat qui datait du
  snapshot d'audit) : **1901 passed, 7 skipped**, 0 failed (exit 0).
- **Après** : **1903 passed, 7 skipped**, 0 failed (exit 0).
- Delta : **+2 passed, 0 régression, 0 nouveau skip.**

(Note technique : sous pytest 9.1.1 ici présent, `-q` supprime la ligne de résumé
finale — comportement de version vérifié en isolant chaque flag. Les comptes ci-dessus
proviennent d'une exécution identique sans `-q` pour lecture humaine ; le code de
sortie de la commande mandatée avec `-q` est 0 avant et après.)

`scripts/no_stub_scan.py tests/test_immudb.py` → OK, zéro violation.

### Portée

Fichier modifié : `tests/test_immudb.py` uniquement. Aucun changement au code de
production.

body:
Notifies whoever renders after a tick, without letting the model know a view exists.

- **`controller/Rendering`**: shows listeners a projection of the state (`S => V`), so rendering only ever sees what it needs. An update is notified only when it changes that projection; the last shown value is remembered, so each state is projected once.
- **`controller/TickNotification`**: `tickNotifying` runs one pipeline tick and notifies afterwards. The pipeline is untouched and stays a plain state-to-state function: the notification happens outside it.

body:
Implements the five human rulings recorded on `agents-config-9k9.215.7` (the
seven charter-vs-tree disagreements from the 2026-08-09 fresh-context recheck).
The charter is canonical, so none of these took a unilateral edit — each carries
a ruling made by the repository owner and quoted verbatim on the tracker item.

Charter prose only. Nothing else is in the diff.

## What changed

Each amendment follows the charter's existing convention: a dated
`*Amended YYYY-MM-DD:*` paragraph immediately after the decision it amends
(the 2026-08-07 `wayfinder` readmission is the precedent). No decision is
renumbered or rewritten.

| Ruling | Charter section | Amendment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 — caps: "Amend: record the 5k tier" | D16 | Records both tiers: 2k model-invoked, 5k user-invoked, with the raised ceiling stated as relief rather than permission |
| 3 — readmission: "Backfill the amendment" | D18 | Dated readmission of `improve-codebase-architecture`, user-invoked, Claude tree, with its grafts and the placement condition |
| 4 — park reasons: "Amend: record both axes" | D10 | Records the failure axis (PR-bound, mirrored by the `work` facade) and the grind-native scheduling axis |
| 6 — dead tracker IDs: "Mark as archive-era" | D13, D14, D18 | Each citation marked archive-era, resolvable in the private archive repository and not through `work` |
| 7 — no-prose-plans surface: "Repo-owned surface only" | AC5 | Names the repo-owned surface AC5 binds, and records the marketplace exposure — `superpowers` ships a `writing-plans` skill — as a known gap outside that jurisdiction |

Two of the seven rulings produce no charter edit and are deliberately absent
here: ruling 1 (home2 conform — the charter is unchanged; execution is
`agents-config-9k9.215.19`) and ruling 5 (extend spec-lint to match AC4 — code
work routed to `agents-config-9k9.215.8`).

## Round 2 — review disposition

Round 1 returned five mechanical findings. Findings f1/f2/f3 were one defect and
are fixed in `98449dd4`: the AC5 amendment stated the marketplace exposure as
account-scoped machine state ("one installed plugin (`superpowers`, primary
account only)"), which no observation of this repository can settle and which
goes stale the moment that account changes. The amendment now states the same
ruling as a standing property — marketplace plugins install outside the
repo-owned surface, the admission gate has no reach over them, and the
`superpowers` plugin ships a `writing-plans` skill — so every clause is
settleable without inspecting a particular machine. The ruling's three parts are
intact: AC5 binds the repo-owned surface; the exposure is known and outside its
jurisdiction; `superpowers`/`writing-plans` is the named instance.

Findings f4 (archive-era annotations) and f5 (readmission amendment) are
rebutted in the round-2 disposition ledger rather than changed.

Copilot's three comments triaged alongside. One fixed in `baff4269`: D14 read
"`wgclw.30` (event-sourced grind runtime; archive-era, …) is the one live M0
workstream", colliding "archive-era" and "live" in one sentence with each
adjective on the wrong noun. The runtime now leads the sentence and keeps the
live claim, and the archive-era note attaches to the ID it describes. The other
two — rewrite D16's base 2k sentence, drop `improve-codebase-architecture` from
D18's base skipped list — are rebutted: the charter's own convention preserves
base text under a dated amendment that supersedes it, which is why the
2026-08-07 `wayfinder` amendment sits beneath a list still naming `wayfinder`
as skipped. Rewriting base decisions was out of scope of the rulings.

## Verification

All five disagreements were re-verified against the current tree before
amending; none had been resolved in the interim.

- **Caps** — `surface_budget.py` carries `SKILL_BODY_TOKEN_CAP = 2_000` and
  `USER_INVOKED_SKILL_BODY_TOKEN_CAP = 5_000`.
- **Readmission** — `src/user/.claude/skills/improve-codebase-architecture/`
  is present with a complete admission record and `disable-model-invocation`.
- **Park axes** — `PARK_REASONS` in `packages/grind/src/grind/model.py` maps
  every reason to `failure` or `scheduling`; `.work/config.toml`'s
  `[park.reasons]` carries the five failure-axis reasons only, which is why the
  amendment calls the scheduling axis grind-native.
- **Dead IDs** — `work show` returns `E_NOT_FOUND` for all six of
  `abn9.8.33`, `abn9.8.49`, `j8pdq`, `wgclw.30`, `wgclw.24`, `wgclw.25`.
- **AC5 surface** — zero hits for the retired names under `src/`. The
  `superpowers` plugin ships a `writing-plans` skill, which is the claim the
  amendment makes and is a property of the plugin rather than of any install.

Gates, re-run standalone from this worktree root after the round-1 fix:
`make spec-lint` exit 0, `make doc-lint` exit 0. No `packages/**` code changed,
so no package suite applies.

## Consumer sweep (uncapped)

Whole-repo greps, no `head` caps, excluding only `.git`, `.venv`,
`node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.beads` and other worktrees. **No quoter was
edited** — the files below belong to other items.

**Skill-body caps.** Two child specs state the flat 2k without the tier, both
point-in-time documents that predate it (PR 474 / `9k9.149`):
`docs/specs/2026-07-22-installer-single-home-admission-s3.md:91` and
`docs/specs/2026-07-24-spec-contract-s5.md:25` (the same document states both
tiers correctly at `:220`). Already consistent with the amendment:
`.claude/skills/admit-request/SKILL.md:157-159` and
`docs/primers/SKILLS_PRIMER.md:139-141`.

**Park axes.** Every downstream artifact already carries both axes — the
amendment brings the charter to them, not the reverse:
`docs/specs/2026-07-25-executor-seam-s9-tier1.md:25`,
`docs/specs/2026-07-19-event-sourced-grind-runtime.md:179-200`, `CONTEXT.md:88-92`,
`packages/grind/AGENTS.md:174-181`, `packages/executor/src/executor/rules.py:58`.
`docs/specs/2026-07-22-workcli-completion-s2.md:45-46` lists failure-axis reasons
only, which remains correct for the facade.

**D18 / `improve-codebase-architecture`.** No stale quoter.
`src/user/.agents/skills/AGENTS.md:88` records it as a Claude-tree skill with its
provenance, and `docs/specs/2026-07-22-instruction-surface-teardown-s4.md:192`
cites its content as live — both consistent with the readmission.

**AC5.** No quoter contradicts the repo-owned reading.
`docs/specs/2026-07-24-review-contracts-s6.md:34` and
`docs/specs/2026-07-24-spec-contract-s5.md:4,162,185` all read on that surface.
One adjacent staleness, pre-existing and not induced here: the S6 line says the
retired skills are "held only under `archive/`", a tree that has since moved to
the private archive repository.

**Archive-era IDs.** No document quotes the charter's citations. The same
namespace appears as other specs' own bead headers
(`docs/specs/2026-07-19-event-sourced-grind-runtime.md:3`,
`docs/specs/2026-07-19-grind-dashboard-renderer.md:3`,
`docs/specs/2026-07-16-prgroom-runloop-state-derivation.md:5`), in the
grind-dashboard prototype fixtures, and in `scripts/track-backfill/applied.log`
— the same dead-namespace class, but each owned by its own document.

Closes `agents-config-9k9.215.7` on merge.

author: maronnjapan
body:
## 背景

OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.5.1.1 は、`claims` パラメータをサポートする OP に対して次を MUST として課しています。

> If the `acr` Claim is requested as an Essential Claim for the ID Token with a `value` or `values` parameter ... the Authorization Server MUST return an `acr` Claim Value that matches one of the requested values. ... **If this is an Essential Claim and the requirement cannot be met, then the Authorization Server MUST treat that outcome as a failed authentication attempt.**

本リポジトリは `claims.id_token.acr.values` を `AcrResolver` へ「要求値」として渡すところまでは実装済みでしたが、**resolver が返した `acr` が要求値に一致するかを検証していません**でした。`essential` フラグはパースされ型にも保持されていながら、どこからも参照されない dead field でした。

その結果、resolver が要求外の値を返しても、`undefined` を返して `acr` クレームが省略されても、ID Token はそのまま発行されていました。RP が `acr` の欠落を厳格に検査していなければ、**要求した認証強度を満たさないセッションを受け入れてしまう**状態です。

`tasks/p1-essential-acr-claim-unmet-issuance-guard.md` の実装で、study-material の方針 A（Token Endpoint での一致検証 = 黙って発行しない）を最小実装として入れます。認可エンドポイントで `unmet_authentication_requirements` を返す方針 B、追加認証を要求する方針 C は本 PR の範囲外で、`study-material/done/claims-essential-acr-unmet-authentication-failure.md` に検討として残ります。

## 実装内容

### packages/core

`resolveAcrAmr`（`token-response.ts`）に一致検証を追加しました。

- `claims.id_token.acr` を「要求値 + essential フラグ」へ正規化するヘルパー `extractAcrClaimRequest` を追加。§5.5.1.1 は "with a `value` or `values` parameter" と規定しているため、`values`（配列）だけでなく `value`（単数）も要求値として扱います
- Essential 要求（`essential: true` かつ要求値あり）に対し、解決された `acr` が `undefined` の場合・要求値のいずれとも一致しない場合は、RFC 6749 §5.2 の `invalid_grant` として `TokenError` を投げます。`error_description` に要求値は反映しません
- `acrResolver` が未設定の OP は acr を一切決められないため、Essential 要求は原理的に満たせません。この経路でも同じく発行を止めます
- Essential 要求の要求値は `acr_values` パラメータより優先して resolver へ渡します。`acr_values` は §3.1.2.1 の Note により Voluntary な要求にすぎず、Essential 要求こそが満たすべき制約だからです（優先しないと、両方を送った RP のリクエストが必ず失敗します）
- `essential` 省略 / `essential: false` の要求、`acr_values` パラメータのみの要求は従来どおりエラーになりません（§5.5.1 の一般則）
- `acr` / `amr` が直接指定される refresh_token grant の §12.1 保持経路は早期 return のままで影響を受けません

§5.5.1 の「Claim を返せなくてもエラーにしてはならない」という MUST NOT には `unless otherwise specified in the description of the specific claim` という但し書きがあり、`acr` はその例外にあたる旨を JSDoc とテストのコメントに明記しています。

### packages/cli

生成 OP の契約テストに `essentialAcrConformanceBlock()` を追加し、hono / web-standard（express・fastify・nextjs）両方の `conformance.test.ts` 生成コードへ配線しました。生成 OP の token ルートは既存の `catch` が `TokenError` を変換するため、ルート側の分岐追加は不要であることをテストで確認しています。

- Essential 要求を満たせないとき token エンドポイントが `invalid_grant` を返し、`Cache-Control: no-store` / `Pragma: no-cache` が付くこと
- Essential 要求を満たせるときは `acr` が要求値と一致した ID Token が発行されること
- Voluntary な不一致要求は従来どおり発行され、セッションの現在の `acr` が載ること

`samples/*` は 4 つとも再生成済みです。

### ドキュメント

- `study-material/done/claims-parameter-value-values-essential.md`: 「Essential でもエラーにしない」という一般則が `acr` / `sub` には適用されない例外であることを追記
- `study-material/ext-step-up-authentication-rfc9470.md`: `AcrResolver` のエラーパスの行を 🟡 → 🟢 に更新し、本実装と後続検討（方針 B / C）への参照を追加

### リリース

core の挙動変更（これまで発行されていたトークンが失敗しうる）のため core は minor、cli は patch の changeset を追加しました。あわせて RELEASE.md「peer range は『下限』を宣言する」に従い、experimental の core peer range 下限を `>=0.2.0` へ上げ、その patch changeset を追加しています。`tasks/experimental/done/jarm/promotion-review` は生成コードの footprint が変わったため再生成しました。

## テスト

- `pnpm --filter @maronn-openid-connect/core test` — 1166 passed
- `pnpm --filter @maronn-openid-connect/cli test` — 820 passed
- `pnpm --filter @maronn-openid-connect/experimental test` — 296 passed
- `pnpm typecheck`
- 各 sample の `conformance.test.ts`: hono-cloudflare 183 / express-flyio 112 / fastify-flyio 112 / nextjs-vercel 110 すべて passed
- `pnpm run test:ci-gate` / `test:supply-chain` / `test:release-contract` / `test:experimental-review`

なお `pnpm review:experimental --all --check` は par / token-exchange / device-authorization-grant のパケットが本 PR 以前から実装と一致しておらず、その 3 件は引き続き失敗します（本 PR の変更で壊れたものではないため、対象タスク外として触っていません）。本 PR で footprint が変わった jarm は再生成して一致させています。

author: mniewrzal
body:
## Problem

`Options.SoftCancel` exists so that canceling a stream does not cost the whole transport: the manager sends a `KindCancel` packet and keeps the connection for the next stream.

That only works if the cancel can actually be sent. `Stream.SendCancel` needs the stream's state and write mutexes and takes both with `TryLock` — deliberately, so that a wedged transport write can never block teardown. The consequence is that a stream which happens to be sending when the cancel arrives reports busy, and the manager hard cancels: transport destroyed, next call pays a dial and a handshake.

For clients whose streams send and receive concurrently, that race is both common and benign. Losing the connection over it is a poor trade.

## Change

* `Options.SoftCancelGrace` bounds how long a busy soft cancel will wait for the concurrent send to finish. Zero or negative preserves today's behavior.
* `Manager.sendCancel` implements the wait by retrying `SendCancel` with backoff (100µs, doubling to a 5ms cap) rather than blocking on the mutex. Blocking would give back exactly the property that lets a dead transport be torn down; polling keeps it. The loop also exits early if the manager terminates, since there is nothing left to preserve at that point.
* The outcome of each soft cancel attempt — `CancelClean`, `CancelBusy` or `CancelError` — is reported through a callback in the internal options, following the existing `statsCB` pattern. The ratio of kept to destroyed transports is the difference between a connection pool that works and one that never gets a hit, and it is not otherwise observable in production.

## Tests

`TestSoftCancel_Grace` parks a flush inside the transport, waits until the write is actually blocked, cancels the stream's context, and releases the write 50ms later. With no grace the manager reports busy; with a grace period the retry picks the stream up once the send lands and the cancel is delivered cleanly.

body:
## Background
Bead rev-wzrh: the dispatch loop read sqlite rows with `-separator $'\t'` + `IFS=$'\t' read`. Bash collapses consecutive IFS-whitespace tabs, so rows with a NULL branch shifted target_repo into the branch field, producing false "[af] skip: no repo mapping" fail-closed skips. Beads with target_repo set were stuck QUEUED for 19 days (jleechan-e7na/0jx6/vgs9/70lx, 2026-07-21 → 2026-08-09).

## Goals
Dispatch loop parses NULL-branch rows correctly; no false repo-mapping skips.

## Tenets
Minimal targeted fix; RED test before fix; no behavior change for non-NULL rows.

## High-level description
Switch the dispatch SELECT read to a non-whitespace '|' separator (non-whitespace IFS chars do not collapse), matching sibling loops in factory-overlay.sh.

## Testing
RED→GREEN: regression test added in commit 04889606 reproduces the field shift; fix commit 9088b529 turns it green. Repro one-liner: `printf 'a\t1\t\tr\n' | IFS=$'\t' read -r w x y z` → y=r, z=''.

## Low-level details
2 files changed (+219/-2): daemon/factory-af-tick.sh + regression test. Implemented by sonnet lane under sidekick-af-factory-code-fixes; pushed by main session. [claude-code/claude-fable-5 + claude-sonnet lane]

## User Stories
N/A — daemon-internal dispatch correctness; operator-visible effect is beads no longer silently stuck QUEUED.

**Evidence**: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/f2bad24f515c66aa1aa82057db948987

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small delimiter change in one dispatch loop, aligned with existing pipe-separated reads in factory-overlay.sh; behavior for rows with a non-empty branch is unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **dispatch deadlock** where QUEUED beads with a set `target_repo` but **no branch yet** were falsely skipped as unmapped.

> The `/af` dispatch loop in `factory-af-tick.sh` now reads sqlite rows with **`|`** instead of tab for both `sqlite3 -separator` and `while IFS= read`. Bash collapses consecutive tab IFS whitespace, so an empty `coalesce(branch,'')` field caused `target_repo` to shift into `branch` and left `bead_repo` empty, tripping the fail-closed repo check.
